Formed during a massive volcanic eruption 34.9 million years ago, these giant boulders, some reaching 40 feet high, create a labyrinthine 'city' that offers unique opportunities for exploration, photography, and amateur astronomy in one of the darkest skies in the region.

hikingTrails.name: Hydra Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible loop that winds through the heart of the most impressive rock formations.

hikingTrails.name: Prospector Trail
hikingTrails.description: A longer trail that circles the perimeter of the park, offering panoramic views of the surrounding Mimbres Valley.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park offers 52 campsites, including 22 sites with 30/50 amp electrical hookups and water, plus several primitive tent sites and a group camping area.
new mexico.fishingBoating: Not applicable; this is a high-desert park with no significant bodies of water for boating or fishing.

visitorCenter.name: City of Rocks Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides interpretive exhibits on the volcanic history of the area, park maps, and information on local flora and fauna.

new mexico.hours: Open 24 hours for registered campers; day use from sunrise to sunset.
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures, or Winter for clear night skies.
tips: Bring a telescope or binoculars as the park is a designated dark sky area.
Wear sturdy hiking shoes to navigate the uneven terrain around the boulders.
Visit during the early morning or late afternoon for the best lighting on the rock formations.

new mexico.name: Bottomless Lakes State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: New Mexico's first state park features a series of unique sinkhole lakes nestled against dramatic red bluffs.
new mexico.fullDescription: Established in 1933, Bottomless Lakes State Park is located along the Pecos River valley. The park is famous for its nine small, deep lakes formed by the collapse of underground salt deposits, creating sinkholes that range from 17 to 90 feet deep. The water appears deep blue or green due to the depth and aquatic vegetation, contrasting sharply with the surrounding arid desert landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Wetland Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through the marshy areas near the lakes, offering excellent opportunities for birding.

hikingTrails.name: Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail climbs the red bluffs surrounding the lakes, providing panoramic views of the entire park and the Pecos Valley.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park offers 32 developed campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as primitive camping areas. Reservations are highly recommended during peak season.
new mexico.fishingBoating: Lea Lake is open for non-motorized boating and fishing. The lake is stocked with rainbow trout during the winter months.

visitorCenter.name: Bottomless Lakes Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on the unique geology of the sinkhole lakes and local history.

new mexico.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new mexico.address: 545 A Bottomless Lakes Rd, Roswell, NM 88201
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and active bird migration.
tips: Bring polarized sunglasses to better see into the deep, clear water of the sinkholes.
The park is a popular spot for scuba diving; ensure you have proper certification and permits.
Stay on marked trails to protect the fragile desert ecosystem and avoid steep drop-offs.
nearbyAttractions: International UFO Museum and Research Center

new mexico.name: Cimarron Canyon State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: Nestled in the heart of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, this park offers stunning granite palisades and excellent trout fishing along the Cimarron River.
new mexico.fullDescription: Cimarron Canyon State Park is a scenic gem located within the Colin Neblett Wildlife Area. The park is defined by the dramatic Palisades, which are towering granite cliffs that rise 400 feet above the Cimarron River. The area is rich in history, having served as a vital route for travelers on the Santa Fe Trail. Today, it provides a rugged landscape for outdoor enthusiasts, featuring diverse ecosystems ranging from ponderosa pine forests to high-mountain meadows.

hikingTrails.name: Tolby Meadow Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that climbs through dense forests to reach a beautiful high-mountain meadow.

hikingTrails.name: Palisades Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb that rewards hikers with breathtaking panoramic views of the canyon and the iconic granite cliffs.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park features several campgrounds including Maverick, Ponderosa, and Cimarron, offering both tent and RV sites with basic amenities like fire rings and picnic tables.
new mexico.fishingBoating: The Cimarron River is a premier destination for fly fishing, known for its healthy populations of rainbow and brown trout.

visitorCenter.name: Cimarron Canyon Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on trail conditions, fishing regulations, and local wildlife safety.

new mexico.hours: Open 24 hours for camping; day use from sunrise to sunset.
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for pleasant weather and active wildlife.
tips: Bring polarized sunglasses to help spot trout in the river.
Be bear aware and store all food in bear-proof containers.
Check the weather forecast as mountain conditions can change rapidly.

new mexico.name: Elephant Butte Lake State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: New Mexico's largest state park, Elephant Butte Lake offers expansive water recreation and desert landscapes in the heart of the Rio Grande Valley.
new mexico.fullDescription: Elephant Butte Lake State Park is centered around the massive Elephant Butte Reservoir, created by the construction of the Elephant Butte Dam in 1916. The park serves as a premier destination for boating, fishing, and water sports in the high desert. Beyond the water, the park features rugged volcanic terrain and diverse desert flora, providing a unique backdrop for camping, hiking, and birdwatching throughout the year.
thingsToDo: Fishing for striped bass and walleye

hikingTrails.name: Desert Cove Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path offering scenic views of the lake and opportunities to spot local desert wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Lions Beach Trail
hikingTrails.description: A relaxing walk along the shoreline that provides easy access to swimming areas and picnic spots.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park offers over 200 developed campsites, many with electric and water hookups, as well as primitive camping areas along the shoreline.
new mexico.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat ramps and extensive shoreline access for fishing; common catches include striped bass, walleye, and catfish.

visitorCenter.name: Elephant Butte Lake State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, current lake levels, fishing regulations, and local wildlife exhibits.

new mexico.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
new mexico.entranceFees: $5.00 per vehicle per day for day-use entry.
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal water recreation conditions.
tips: Check current lake levels on the official website before planning your boating trip.
Bring plenty of sunscreen and water, as the desert sun is intense even in cooler months.
Reservations for campsites are highly recommended during summer weekends and holidays.
nearbyAttractions: Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge

new mexico.name: Hyde Memorial State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: Nestled in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Hyde Memorial State Park offers a high-altitude escape just minutes from Santa Fe.
new mexico.fullDescription: Hyde Memorial State Park is New Mexico's first state park, established in 1938. Located at an elevation of 8,500 feet, the park is surrounded by the Santa Fe National Forest and features stunning views of the surrounding peaks. The park is a popular destination for year-round recreation, including cross-country skiing in the winter and hiking through lush aspen and conifer forests during the warmer months.

hikingTrails.name: Big Tesuque Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through dense forest and offers beautiful views of the Tesuque Creek valley.

hikingTrails.name: Hyde Park Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path perfect for families, showcasing the park's diverse alpine flora and fauna.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park offers 7 developed campsites with electrical hookups and several tent-only sites, along with a group shelter area.
new mexico.fishingBoating: Fishing is not a primary activity at this park, though small streams are present in the surrounding national forest.

visitorCenter.name: Hyde Memorial Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on trail conditions, park maps, and local wildlife education.

new mexico.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new mexico.entranceFees: $5.00 daily vehicle fee for day use.
new mexico.address: 740 Hyde Park Rd, Santa Fe, NM 87501
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking, or winter for cross-country skiing.
tips: Bring layers as temperatures drop significantly at this high elevation.
Drink plenty of water to acclimate to the 8,500-foot altitude.
Visit in late September to see the spectacular golden aspen leaves.

new mexico.name: Sugarite Canyon State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: Nestled in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Sugarite Canyon State Park offers stunning alpine lakes and a rich history of coal mining.
new mexico.fullDescription: Sugarite Canyon State Park is located on the border of New Mexico and Colorado, featuring two beautiful lakes, Lake Maloya and Lake Alice. The park is renowned for its dramatic volcanic geology and the remnants of the historic Sugarite coal mining camp, which operated in the early 20th century. Visitors can explore the rugged terrain, enjoy high-altitude fishing, and observe diverse wildlife in this pristine mountain environment.

hikingTrails.name: Little Coal Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the historic mining area, offering glimpses of old foundations and beautiful canyon views.

hikingTrails.name: Ponderosa Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that rewards hikers with panoramic vistas of the surrounding Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park features two campgrounds, Soda Pocket and Prairie Dog, offering a mix of primitive and developed sites with some electric hookups available.
new mexico.fishingBoating: Lake Maloya is a premier destination for trout fishing; non-motorized boats and electric trolling motors are permitted.

visitorCenter.name: Sugarite Canyon Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local mining heritage.

new mexico.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for pleasant temperatures and wildlife viewing.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird and elk watching opportunities.
Check the weather forecast as mountain conditions can change rapidly.
Visit the historic coal camp ruins to learn about the area's industrial past.

new mexico.name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: Nestled at the base of the Sacramento Mountains, this park offers a stunning desert landscape and a glimpse into the history of 19th-century ranching.
new mexico.fullDescription: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park is located in the Tularosa Basin, providing a dramatic backdrop of the Sacramento Mountains. The park features the historic Frenchy's Cabin and the restored Oliver Lee Ranch house, which dates back to the late 1800s. Visitors can explore the unique Chihuahuan Desert ecosystem, characterized by rugged canyons, diverse flora, and spectacular views of the White Sands area.

hikingTrails.name: Dog Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that rewards hikers with panoramic views of the Tularosa Basin and the surrounding desert landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Riparian Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, educational walk through the lush vegetation near the canyon stream, perfect for spotting local wildlife.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park offers 44 developed campsites, including sites with water and electric hookups, as well as primitive tent sites and a dump station.
new mexico.fishingBoating: There is no fishing or boating available at this park.

visitorCenter.name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of the ranch, local geology, and the diverse plant and animal life of the Chihuahuan Desert.

new mexico.hours: Daily: 7:00 AM - 9:00 PM
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall, when temperatures are mild and desert wildflowers are in bloom.
tips: Bring plenty of water, as the desert climate is extremely dry.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to tackle the Dog Canyon Trail.
Check the weather forecast before hiking, as flash floods can occur in the canyons.
nearbyAttractions: New Mexico Museum of Space History

new mexico.name: Heron Lake State Park
new mexico.shortDescription: A serene high-altitude reservoir known for its quiet waters, sailing, and excellent kokanee salmon fishing.
new mexico.fullDescription: Heron Lake State Park is located in the high mountains of northern New Mexico at an elevation of 7,100 feet. The lake is a popular destination for those seeking tranquility, as it enforces a 'no-wake' policy for motorboats, making it ideal for sailing, kayaking, and canoeing. Surrounded by ponderosa pine forests and rugged terrain, the park offers a peaceful retreat with abundant opportunities for wildlife viewing and outdoor recreation.
thingsToDo: Fishing for kokanee salmon and trout

hikingTrails.name: Capulin Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the ponderosa pine forest and offers beautiful views of the lake.

hikingTrails.name: Heron Lake Shoreline Trail
hikingTrails.description: A longer trail that follows the perimeter of the lake, providing excellent access to secluded coves and fishing spots.

new mexico.campingInfo: The park features several developed campgrounds including Willow Creek, La Jara, and Blanco, offering a mix of primitive and electric hookup sites.
new mexico.fishingBoating: The lake is famous for kokanee salmon fishing; boat ramps are available at the main recreation areas.

visitorCenter.name: Heron Lake State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, local wildlife, and current lake conditions.

new mexico.hours: Open 24 hours for camping; day use from sunrise to sunset.
new mexico.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities; winter for snow sports.
tips: Bring a windbreaker as temperatures can drop significantly at this high elevation.
The lake is a no-wake zone, making it perfect for non-motorized watercraft.
Check the official website for current fire restrictions before planning your trip.

oregon.name: Silver Falls State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Known as the crown jewel of the Oregon State Parks system, this park features the spectacular Trail of Ten Falls.
oregon.fullDescription: Silver Falls State Park is Oregon's largest state park, encompassing over 9,000 acres of lush temperate rainforest. The park is world-renowned for its dramatic waterfalls, including the iconic South Falls, which plunges 177 feet over a basalt ledge. The geology of the area is defined by ancient lava flows that have been carved by the Silver Creek drainage over millennia, creating a unique canyon environment that supports diverse flora and fauna.
thingsToDo: Hiking the Trail of Ten Falls
Picnicking in the historic South Falls Day Use Area

hikingTrails.name: Trail of Ten Falls
hikingTrails.description: A world-class hike that takes you past ten stunning waterfalls, including several you can walk behind.

hikingTrails.name: Maple Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop through old-growth forest that offers beautiful views of the canyon and lush ferns.

oregon.campingInfo: The park offers a large campground with 48 electrical sites with water, 43 tent sites, and 14 rustic cabins. Reservations are highly recommended during peak season.
oregon.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Silver Creek, though the primary focus of the park is hiking and sightseeing rather than boating.

visitorCenter.name: South Falls Lodge and Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides historical information, park maps, and educational exhibits about the Civilian Conservation Corps.

oregon.address: 20024 Silver Falls Hwy SE, Sublimity, OR 97385
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for peak waterfall flow or Autumn for vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive before 9:00 AM on weekends to secure parking, as the lots fill up quickly.
Bring a waterproof jacket even in summer, as the mist from the waterfalls can be heavy.
Wear sturdy hiking boots with good traction, as the trails near the falls can be slippery.

oregon.name: Smith Rock State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Renowned globally as a premier destination for rock climbing, Smith Rock State Park features dramatic volcanic tuff cliffs and the winding Crooked River.
oregon.fullDescription: Smith Rock State Park is a geological marvel located in the high desert of Central Oregon. The park is famous for its sheer, vertical walls of welded tuff, which were formed by volcanic activity millions of years ago. It is widely considered the birthplace of modern American sport climbing, attracting climbers from around the world to test their skills on thousands of routes. Beyond climbing, the park offers stunning vistas of the Cascade Mountains and diverse wildlife habitats along the Crooked River.

hikingTrails.name: Misery Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep, challenging climb that rewards hikers with iconic panoramic views of the park and the Cascade peaks.

hikingTrails.name: River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic path that follows the Crooked River, perfect for spotting otters and nesting raptors.

oregon.campingInfo: The park offers a walk-in tent camping area known as the Bivouac Area, which is available on a first-come, first-served basis. No RV hookups are available.
oregon.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Crooked River, primarily for trout, though the river is not suitable for motorized boating.

visitorCenter.name: Smith Rock Welcome Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on climbing routes, trail maps, and park history.

oregon.address: 9241 NE Crooked River Dr, Terrebonne, OR 97760
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal climbing conditions.
tips: Arrive early, especially on weekends, as the parking lot fills up quickly.
Bring plenty of water, as there is very little shade in the high desert environment.
Respect all posted climbing closures, which are often in place to protect nesting raptors.
nearbyAttractions: Peter Skene Ogden State Scenic Viewpoint

oregon.name: Ecola State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Perched on the edge of the Pacific Ocean, Ecola State Park offers breathtaking views of rugged cliffs, hidden coves, and the historic Tillamook Rock Lighthouse.
oregon.fullDescription: Ecola State Park stretches along nine miles of coastline between Cannon Beach and Seaside. The park is renowned for its dramatic scenery, including the iconic Haystack Rock views and the offshore Tillamook Rock Lighthouse. Historically, the area was explored by Captain William Clark of the Lewis and Clark Expedition in 1806, who named the area 'Ecola' after the Chinook word for whale. The park's geology is defined by ancient basalt flows and active landslides that continue to shape the rugged coastline.

hikingTrails.name: Clatsop Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through old-growth Sitka spruce forests and offers stunning vistas of the Pacific Ocean.

hikingTrails.name: Tillamook Head Trail
hikingTrails.description: Part of the Oregon Coast Trail, this challenging path takes hikers through dense forest with significant elevation changes and historic markers.

oregon.campingInfo: Ecola State Park does not offer overnight camping or RV hookups; it is strictly a day-use park.
oregon.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted from the shoreline in designated areas; no boat ramps are available at this park.

visitorCenter.name: Ecola State Park Entrance Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and safety guidance for visitors.

oregon.address: 84318 Ecola Park Rd, Cannon Beach, OR 97110
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Summer for whale watching and clear coastal views.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly during peak season.
Bring binoculars for spotting whales and seabirds from the cliffside viewpoints.
Check the tide charts before heading down to the beach areas to avoid getting stranded.

oregon.name: Cape Lookout State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Nestled on a sand spit between the Pacific Ocean and Netarts Bay, this park offers stunning coastal views and diverse recreational opportunities.
oregon.fullDescription: Cape Lookout State Park is located on a narrow sand spit that separates the Pacific Ocean from Netarts Bay. The park is renowned for its dramatic headland, which juts two miles into the ocean, providing a prime vantage point for whale watching and observing the rugged Oregon coastline. The area is geologically significant, featuring ancient basalt formations and a rich history of coastal erosion and deposition that has shaped the unique landscape seen today.
thingsToDo: Camping in the forest or near the beach

hikingTrails.name: Cape Lookout Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the spine of the cape, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean and surrounding cliffs.

hikingTrails.name: Cape Lookout Beach Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle walk along the sandy beach that provides excellent opportunities for spotting marine life and enjoying the surf.

oregon.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with over 170 tent sites, 38 full-hookup RV sites, and 13 cozy yurts available for reservation.
oregon.fishingBoating: Fishing is popular along the beach and in Netarts Bay, though there is no boat ramp within the park itself.

visitorCenter.name: Cape Lookout Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and current weather conditions for hikers.

oregon.entranceFees: No daily entrance fee; parking is included with camping reservations or day-use access.
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for whale watching and mild weather.
tips: Bring binoculars for whale watching from the headland.
Check tide charts before heading out for beachcombing.
Dress in layers as coastal weather can change rapidly.

oregon.name: Fort Stevens State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Explore the historic remains of a coastal defense fort and the iconic shipwreck of the Peter Iredale on the rugged Oregon coast.
oregon.fullDescription: Fort Stevens State Park encompasses 4,300 acres of diverse landscape, including beaches, wetlands, and forests. Originally built in 1863 to defend the mouth of the Columbia River, the fort served as a military installation through World War II. Today, visitors can explore the historic military museum, walk through the concrete bunkers, and view the skeletal remains of the 1906 shipwreck, the Peter Iredale, which rests on the sandy shore.
thingsToDo: Tour the historic military museum and bunkers
Bike the extensive paved trail system
Go beachcombing along the Pacific shoreline

hikingTrails.name: South Jetty Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, accessible path that leads through coastal dunes and provides excellent views of the Columbia River mouth.

hikingTrails.name: Coffenbury Lake Loop
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that circles the freshwater lake, offering opportunities to spot waterfowl and enjoy the forest canopy.

oregon.campingInfo: The park features one of the largest campgrounds in the United States, offering over 470 campsites, including full hookup sites, tent sites, and several yurts and cabins available for reservation.
oregon.fishingBoating: Coffenbury Lake offers excellent fishing for rainbow trout and bass, with two boat ramps available for non-motorized or electric motor watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Stevens State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides historical exhibits, maps, and information about the military history of the fort and local ecology.

oregon.entranceFees: No daily entrance fee is required for day-use parking at this park.
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and beach access.
tips: Check the tide charts before visiting the Peter Iredale shipwreck to ensure it is accessible.
Bring layers as the coastal weather can change rapidly and become quite windy.
Book campsites well in advance, especially for summer weekends, as they fill up quickly.
nearbyAttractions: Lewis and Clark National Historical Park

oregon.name: Wallowa Lake State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Nestled at the southern end of the spectacular Wallowa Lake, this park offers breathtaking views of the surrounding 9,000-foot peaks.
oregon.fullDescription: Wallowa Lake State Park is located in the heart of the 'Little Switzerland of America.' The park is situated on the terminal moraine of a glacier, providing a unique geological landscape. Visitors can enjoy the crystal-clear waters of the lake, which is fed by snowmelt from the Wallowa Mountains, and explore the rich history of the Nez Perce people who once inhabited this valley.

hikingTrails.name: East Moraine Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail offering panoramic views of the lake and the surrounding glacial valley.

hikingTrails.name: Wallowa Lake Shoreline Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that follows the edge of the lake, perfect for bird watching and photography.

oregon.campingInfo: The park features 121 full-hookup sites, 88 tent sites with water nearby, and 2 yurts. Reservations are highly recommended during the summer months.
oregon.fishingBoating: The park features a public boat ramp and excellent fishing for Kokanee salmon and rainbow trout.

visitorCenter.name: Wallowa Lake Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, local history, and trail maps.

oregon.hours: Open year-round, 24 hours for registered campers; day-use areas open sunrise to sunset.
oregon.entranceFees: No daily vehicle entrance fee, but camping fees apply.
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: June through September for warm weather and full access to water activities.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities.
Book campsites well in advance as they fill up quickly in the summer.
Be prepared for rapidly changing weather conditions due to the high elevation.

oregon.name: Beverly Beach State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Nestled between the Pacific Ocean and the lush coastal forest, Beverly Beach State Park offers a stunning stretch of sandy beach and a popular, well-wooded campground.
oregon.fullDescription: Beverly Beach State Park is located on the central Oregon coast, just north of Newport. The park is famous for its expansive beach that stretches from Yaquina Head to Cape Foulweather, providing excellent opportunities for beachcombing and whale watching. The park is situated in a sheltered valley, protecting campers from the strong coastal winds while providing easy access to the beach via a pedestrian tunnel under Highway 101.
thingsToDo: Exploring tide pools at low tide

hikingTrails.name: Spencer Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail that winds through the lush coastal forest and along the creek, offering a peaceful escape from the beach.

hikingTrails.name: Cape Foulweather Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that provides elevated views of the Pacific Ocean and the rugged coastline near the park.

oregon.campingInfo: The park features one of the largest campgrounds in the Oregon State Parks system, offering over 200 sites including full hookups, electrical sites, and tent sites, along with several yurts.
oregon.fishingBoating: Surf fishing is popular along the beach, though no boat ramps are available within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Beverly Beach Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, camping registration, and local coastal safety tips.

oregon.hours: Day-use area open from sunrise to sunset daily.
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and whale watching opportunities.
tips: Check tide tables before heading out to explore the tide pools.
Book campsites well in advance, especially during summer weekends.
Bring layers as coastal weather can change rapidly even in summer.

oregon.name: Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park
oregon.shortDescription: Famous for its massive, shifting sand dunes, this park offers a unique desert-like landscape nestled against the lush Oregon coast.
oregon.fullDescription: Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park is one of the most popular parks in Oregon, renowned for its expansive sand dunes that stretch for miles along the Pacific coast. The park features two freshwater lakes, Woahink and Cleawox, which provide a stark contrast to the surrounding dunes. The area was named after Jessie M. Honeyman, a prominent figure in the Oregon roadside beautification movement. The dunes are part of the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area, offering visitors a rare opportunity to explore a vast, shifting landscape of sand that reaches heights of up to 500 feet.

hikingTrails.name: Cleawox Lake Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail that circles the scenic Cleawox Lake, offering beautiful views of the water and surrounding forest.

hikingTrails.name: Dune Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers up onto the ridges of the massive sand dunes, providing panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean and the inland lakes.

oregon.campingInfo: The park features one of the largest campgrounds in the Oregon State Parks system, offering over 350 campsites, including full hookup sites, tent sites, and group camping areas.
oregon.fishingBoating: Both Woahink and Cleawox lakes are popular for fishing, canoeing, and kayaking. Boat ramps are available for non-motorized and small motorized watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Honeyman Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, dune safety, and camping reservations.

oregon.entranceFees: Day-use parking permit is $5.00 per vehicle.
oregon.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather for sandboarding and swimming.
tips: Bring plenty of water and sunscreen as the dunes provide little shade.
Book your campsite well in advance during summer months as it fills up quickly.
Rent sandboards at local shops in Florence before heading to the park.

utah.name: Goblin Valley State Park
utah.shortDescription: Utah park known for thousands of mushroom-shaped hoodoos, called goblins, that visitors can walk among.
utah.fullDescription: Goblin Valley State Park in Emery County is known for thousands of hoodoos, locally called goblins, formed where an erosion-resistant layer of rock tops softer sandstone. Visitors can hike freely among them in the Valley of Goblins. It is an International Dark Sky Park with a campground and yurts and is near the Little Wild Horse Canyon trailhead in the San Rafael Swell.
utah.campingInfo: The park has a 24-site campground, a group site and two yurts with central restroom and shower facilities, all bookable up to 4 months in advance.
utah.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Goblin Valley State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

utah.hours: Park: 6 a.m. – 10 p.m. every day; Visitor Center: 9 a.m. – 5 p.m.
utah.entranceFees: Day-use: $20 per private vehicle; $10 per motorcycle, bicycle or pedestrian (valid until 10 p.m. the day after purchase)
utah.address: 18630 Goblin Valley Rd, Green River, UT 84525
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall are the most comfortable times to visit, since summer brings hot, sunny conditions with temperatures in the 90s and 100s °F.
tips: In hot weather, hike early in the day and carry at least 32 ounces of water per person per hour, plus salty snacks or electrolytes.
Check the flash flood forecast before entering any canyon. Avoid hiking canyons or camping in washes if there is any chance of rain. A daily weather report is posted at the Visitor Center.

Drone flights require a $15/day permit issued in person at the Visitor Center. Flights are allowed only over Valley 1 from the Observation Point platform, and are not allowed on weekends or holidays from March 1 to October 31.

utah.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
utah.shortDescription: Utah mesa-top park near Moab with a famous overlook of the Colorado River and Canyonlands.
utah.fullDescription: Dead Horse Point State Park, opened in 1959, covers 5,362 acres of high desert at 5,900 feet near Moab. Its overlooks look down on the Colorado River and out to Canyonlands National Park. It has a visitor center, two campgrounds with yurts, rim trails and 17 miles of mountain bike trails.

hikingTrails.name: West Rim Trail
hikingTrails.description: Listed as a moderate 2.5-mile hike among the best hikes in Dead Horse Point State Park.

hikingTrails.name: Dead Horse Point Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A very short, easy walk to the Dead Horse Point overlook.

hikingTrails.name: Intrepid
hikingTrails.description: The easiest and shortest loop of the Intrepid Trail System, which offers hiking and biking trails.

utah.campingInfo: The park has campgrounds with modern amenities plus Wingate and Moenkopi yurts, and only the Moenkopi Yurts are pet friendly.
utah.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Dead Horse Point State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

utah.hours: Park open year-round 6:00 am – 10:00 pm; Visitor Center open daily 7 a.m. – 5 p.m. (closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day)
utah.entranceFees: $20 day-use per private vehicle (up to 8 people); $2 per person after the first 8 in high-capacity vehicles
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall generally offer milder conditions for hiking this high-desert park, and sunrise and sunset are especially memorable for the canyon views.
tips: The park closes at 10 p.m. and day-use fees only cover access until then. Only campers, yurt guests, ranger-led activities or permitted companies can stay later for stargazing.
Trails are primitive and marked with cairns, rock lines and wood. Don't move, stack or knock down rocks.
National Park passes aren't accepted here because it's a state park.

utah.name: Antelope Island State Park
utah.shortDescription: Largest island in the Great Salt Lake, with free-roaming bison, beaches and a historic ranch.
utah.fullDescription: Antelope Island State Park protects the largest of the Great Salt Lake's ten islands, 42 square miles near Salt Lake City, reached by causeway. Its wildlife includes American bison, pronghorn, bighorn sheep and millions of waterfowl. Bridger Bay on the north end has a beach, swimming area, campground and marina, and the historic Fielding Garr Ranch stands by a freshwater spring.

hikingTrails.name: Frary Peak Trail
hikingTrails.description: Frary Peak is one of the spots in the island's backcountry trail network where hikers can take in stunning views.

hikingTrails.name: Buffalo Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: Buffalo Point is recommended as a spot for watching the sunset.

hikingTrails.name: White Rock Loop
hikingTrails.description: White Rock Loop is a backcountry trail that hikers can reach via the backcountry trailhead and Bone Road trail.

utah.campingInfo: The park offers several primitive campsites, and its listed lodging options include RV sites, tent pads and a cottage.
utah.fishingBoating: The main boat ramp is currently closed due to low water levels, though kayaking is listed as a park activity.

visitorCenter.name: Antelope Island State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

utah.hours: Open year-round 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Visitor Center 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
utah.entranceFees: $15 per vehicle (up to 8 people); pedestrians $3 per person
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Fall brings the annual Bison Roundup, and the park is open year-round with millions of birds gathering along its shores, making it rewarding for birding and wildlife viewing.
tips: Uber and Lyft do not pick up from the park, so rent a car to avoid being stranded.
Drones are prohibited March through November and allowed only by permit December through February. Day-of permits are available at the visitor center.
Bridger Bay Beach is the best place to swim or float in Great Salt Lake and has restrooms and showers.

utah.name: Snow Canyon State Park
utah.shortDescription: A stunning desert landscape featuring towering sandstone cliffs, lava tubes, and vibrant red rock formations in the heart of Utah's Red Rock Country.
utah.fullDescription: Snow Canyon State Park is located in the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve and offers a dramatic landscape of Navajo sandstone cliffs, extinct volcanic cones, and lava tubes. Formed by the erosion of the Santa Clara volcano and the shifting sands of the ancient desert, the park provides a unique geological experience. Visitors can explore the park's diverse terrain, which ranges from white and red sandstone to black basalt lava flows, offering a stark and beautiful contrast that has attracted hikers, photographers, and geologists for decades.

hikingTrails.name: Jenny's Canyon
hikingTrails.description: A short, flat trail leading to a narrow, slot-like canyon with beautiful red rock walls.

hikingTrails.name: Lava Flow Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through rugged black lava fields and leads to several accessible lava tubes.

utah.campingInfo: The park features the Snow Canyon Campground with 26 sites, including options for RVs up to 40 feet and tent camping, equipped with water and electrical hookups.
utah.fishingBoating: There are no lakes or rivers within the park suitable for boating or fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Snow Canyon Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides educational exhibits on the park's geology, flora, and fauna, along with ranger assistance for trail conditions.

utah.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
utah.entranceFees: $10.00 per vehicle daily entrance fee for Utah residents, $15.00 for non-residents.
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal hiking conditions.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the desert heat can be intense even in cooler months.
Visit early in the morning to avoid peak crowds and midday heat.
Check the park website for seasonal closures of certain trails due to desert tortoise protection.

utah.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
utah.shortDescription: Experience a stunning landscape of shifting, salmon-colored sand dunes nestled between red sandstone cliffs in southern Utah.
utah.fullDescription: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park features expansive dunes created by the erosion of Navajo Sandstone cliffs. The unique pink hue comes from iron oxides in the sand. The dunes are constantly shifting due to wind patterns, creating a dynamic environment that is popular for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts, photographers, and hikers.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, interpretive trail that offers a great introduction to the local flora and the geology of the dunes.

hikingTrails.name: Dune Field Trek
hikingTrails.description: A self-guided trek across the open sand dunes providing panoramic views of the surrounding red rock cliffs.

utah.campingInfo: The park offers a modern campground with 22 sites, including full hookups for RVs, as well as primitive tent sites and a group camping area.
utah.fishingBoating: There are no lakes or rivers within the park, so fishing and boating are not available.
wildlife: Coral Pink Sand Dunes Tiger Beetle

visitorCenter.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, geology, and sandboarding rentals.

utah.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures, as summer days can be extremely hot.
tips: Rent a sandboard at the visitor center for a fun way to navigate the dunes.
Visit during sunrise or sunset when the light makes the sand appear most vibrant.
Bring plenty of water and sun protection, as there is very little shade in the dune field.

utah.name: Wasatch Mountain State Park
utah.shortDescription: Nestled in the scenic Heber Valley, Wasatch Mountain State Park offers year-round outdoor recreation ranging from championship golf to rugged mountain trails.
utah.fullDescription: Established in 1961, Wasatch Mountain State Park is one of Utah's most popular destinations, encompassing over 21,000 acres of diverse terrain. The park features a rich history of early pioneer settlement and provides a habitat for a wide variety of wildlife. Visitors can explore the mountainous landscape, which transitions from lush valleys to high-alpine ridges, offering spectacular views of the Wasatch Range.
thingsToDo: Golfing at the 36-hole Wasatch Mountain Golf Course
Mountain biking on extensive trail networks
Horseback riding on designated equestrian paths
Snowmobiling and cross-country skiing in winter

hikingTrails.name: Pine Creek Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, family-friendly loop that winds through wooded areas and offers great opportunities for bird watching.

hikingTrails.name: Dutch Hollow Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular trail for hikers and mountain bikers that climbs through scenic canyons with panoramic views of the Heber Valley.

utah.campingInfo: The park offers the Pine Creek Campground with 128 sites, including full hookups for RVs, tent sites, and group camping areas. Reservations are highly recommended during peak summer months.
utah.fishingBoating: While the park itself is not centered on water, it is located just minutes from Deer Creek Reservoir, which offers excellent boating, fishing, and water sports.

visitorCenter.name: Wasatch Mountain State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about local flora and fauna.

utah.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
utah.entranceFees: $15.00 daily vehicle entrance fee for up to 8 people.
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking and golf; winter for snow sports.
tips: Book your golf tee times well in advance as the courses are very popular.
Bring binoculars for wildlife viewing, especially during dawn and dusk when elk are most active.
Check the park website for seasonal trail closures due to mud or snow conditions.

utah.name: Jordanelle State Park
utah.shortDescription: A premier water recreation destination nestled in the mountains near Heber City, offering boating, fishing, and camping.
utah.fullDescription: Jordanelle State Park is located on the shores of the Jordanelle Reservoir, a massive water project completed in the 1990s. The park is divided into three main areas: Hailstone, Rock Cliff, and Ross Creek. It features diverse geological formations and provides a critical habitat for various wildlife while serving as a hub for outdoor enthusiasts seeking relief from the summer heat or winter snow sports.

hikingTrails.name: Perimeter Trail
hikingTrails.description: A long, scenic trail that circles much of the reservoir, offering panoramic views of the water and surrounding Wasatch Mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Rock Cliff Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through the riparian area of the Provo River, perfect for bird watching and spotting local wildlife.

utah.campingInfo: The park offers multiple campgrounds including Hailstone and Rock Cliff, featuring full hookups, tent sites, and several cabins available for reservation.
utah.fishingBoating: The reservoir is a popular spot for smallmouth bass, largemouth bass, and rainbow trout. Multiple boat ramps are available at the Hailstone area.

visitorCenter.name: Hailstone Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park regulations, fishing licenses, and educational exhibits about the reservoir's history.

utah.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
utah.entranceFees: $20.00 daily vehicle entrance fee for up to 8 people.
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities.
tips: Make camping reservations well in advance during summer months as sites fill up quickly.
Check the water temperature and weather conditions before heading out on the reservoir.
Visit the Rock Cliff area for a quieter, more nature-focused experience compared to the busy Hailstone area.

utah.name: Kodachrome Basin State Park
utah.shortDescription: Kodachrome Basin State Park is a geological wonderland known for its towering sandstone chimneys and vibrant, multi-colored rock formations.
utah.fullDescription: Named by the National Geographic Society for its vivid colors and photogenic landscapes, Kodachrome Basin features 67 monolithic stone spires that rise from the desert floor. The park's unique geology is attributed to ancient geysers that filled with sediment and hardened, leaving behind these striking sedimentary pipes as the surrounding softer rock eroded away. The area offers a serene escape with dramatic vistas, high-desert flora, and a rich history of exploration in the Grand Staircase-Escalante region.

hikingTrails.name: Panorama Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that offers expansive views of the basin and passes by several unique rock formations like Ballerina Spire.

hikingTrails.name: Angels Palace Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail climbs to a ridge providing a bird's-eye view of the park's iconic sandstone chimneys and surrounding cliffs.

utah.campingInfo: The park offers two campgrounds, Basin and Arch, featuring sites with full hookups, tent pads, fire pits, and modern restrooms with showers.
utah.fishingBoating: There are no lakes or rivers within the park suitable for fishing or boating.

visitorCenter.name: Kodachrome Basin Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park geology, trail maps, souvenirs, and assistance from park rangers.

utah.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; Visitor Center hours vary by season.
utah.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal hiking conditions.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the high desert climate is very dry.
Visit during the early morning or late afternoon for the best light to photograph the vibrant rock colors.
The park is a certified International Dark Sky Park, so stay after sunset for incredible stargazing.

washington.name: Deception Pass State Park
washington.shortDescription: Washington park around Deception Pass, the narrow strait between Whidbey and Fidalgo islands under a historic bridge.
washington.fullDescription: Deception Pass State Park covers 3,854 acres around Deception Pass, the strait between Whidbey and Fidalgo islands, crossed by the Deception Pass Bridge. With over two million visitors a year it is one of Washington's most visited state parks. It has campgrounds, beaches, tidepools, part of the Pacific Northwest Trail, boat launches at Cornet Bay and an interpretive center at Bowman Bay.

hikingTrails.name: Sand Dunes Interpretive Trail
hikingTrails.description: A paved ADA loop with interpretive panels about the seaside vegetation unique to the area.

hikingTrails.name: Goose Rock
hikingTrails.description: A wide, well-built trail climbs above North Beach toward the bridge and then crosses under it.

hikingTrails.name: Lighthouse Point Loop
hikingTrails.description: A loop at Bowman Bay; storms washed away part of the trail between it and Lottie Point Loop, and you may walk around that section on the beach.

washington.campingInfo: The park offers camping, including winter camping and accessible campsites.
washington.fishingBoating: Crabbing and both fresh and saltwater fishing are popular and need a recreational license, but Pass Lake is closed because of toxic algae and the Bowman Bay boat launch is closed to trailered vessels.

visitorCenter.name: Deception Pass State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

washington.hours: Summer: 6:30 a.m. - Dusk; Winter: 8:00 a.m. - Dusk
washington.entranceFees: Discover Pass required: $10 one-day or $45 annual
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall gives the longest hours (6:30 a.m. to dusk), and the park's interpretive center is open April to September.
tips: Pass Lake is closed to fishing, people and pets due to toxic algae until further notice.
From November 2 to 13, 2026, the lower Bowman Bay parking lot is closed. Use the Upper Bowman Bay lot, where parking may be limited.
Vehicles over 25 feet, including trailers, motorhomes and buses, can't enter the West Beach parking area. Buses can drop off at West Beach and park at the East Cranberry Lake lot.

washington.name: Palouse Falls State Park
washington.shortDescription: Small Washington park at Palouse Falls, a 200-foot waterfall plunging into a 377-foot-deep canyon.
washington.fullDescription: Palouse Falls State Park covers 94 acres on the Palouse River about four miles above its confluence with the Snake River in southeast Washington. The falls drop about 200 feet into a canyon 377 feet deep, with a smaller upper fall upstream. A viewpoint is a short walk from the parking area, campground and picnic area.

hikingTrails.name: Palouse Falls Overlook
hikingTrails.description: A short overlook route with about 26 feet of elevation gain that takes roughly 0.5 to 1 hour to complete.

washington.campingInfo: No camping in the park.
washington.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Palouse Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

washington.hours: Summer: 6:30 a.m. to dusk; Winter: 8 a.m. to dusk
washington.entranceFees: Discover Pass required: $10 one-day or $45 annual
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Spring is a good time to visit, when wildflowers bloom in the canyon, but check the weather first because extreme conditions are possible, and come on a weekday to avoid long parking waits.
tips: Parking is extremely limited, so expect long waits on weekends and holidays. Trailers and RVs are not allowed.
Most of the park has no cell service and it is far from amenities and first responders, so bring plenty of water and plan ahead.
All trails into the canyon and to the base of the falls are permanently closed. Stay within the designated viewing areas and trails.

washington.name: Cape Disappointment State Park
washington.shortDescription: Washington park where the Columbia River meets the Pacific, with two lighthouses and the Lewis and Clark center.
washington.fullDescription: Cape Disappointment State Park, formerly Fort Canby State Park, covers 2,023 acres southwest of Ilwaco at the mouth of the Columbia River. Its sites include Fort Canby, North Head and Cape Disappointment lighthouses, and the Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center on a cliff above the river's meeting with the ocean. It offers camping, yurts and historic vacation homes.

hikingTrails.name: Cape Disappointment Lighthouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: Per WTA, the round trip from the trailhead to the lighthouse is 2.4 miles with about 500 feet of elevation gain.

hikingTrails.name: Northhead Lighthouse Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: One of the popular fall hiking trails in Cape Disappointment State Park.

hikingTrails.name: North Head Discovery Trail
hikingTrails.description: One of the popular fall hiking trails in Cape Disappointment State Park.

washington.campingInfo: The campground has standard, partial hookup, full hookup, and five primitive hiker/biker campsites, plus yurts and historic vacation homes, and accommodates RVs and combinations of 45 feet or less.
washington.fishingBoating: The park has one boat ramp and 135 feet of dock on Baker Bay in the Columbia River, but the boat launch is closed Oct 1-31, 2026 for paving.

visitorCenter.name: Cape Disappointment State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

washington.hours: 6:30 a.m. - Dusk year round
washington.entranceFees: Discover Pass required: $10 one-day or $45 annual; watercraft launch $7/day
washington.bestTimeToVisit: May through September is best, when the North Head Lighthouse is open to visitors (through Sept. 30), though the park is open year round and offers winter camping.
tips: The parking lots at North Head, the Lewis & Clark Interpretive Center and Beards Hollow will not accommodate RVs.
Swimming in the ocean on the Long Beach Peninsula is not advised because of beach hazards.
The Cape D Store is closed in 2026 and into 2027 for construction of a new contact station, so bring your own supplies such as firewood, ice and groceries.

washington.name: Mount Spokane State Park
washington.shortDescription: Mount Spokane State Park is a massive 13,919-acre park featuring stunning mountain vistas, extensive trail networks, and year-round recreational opportunities.
washington.fullDescription: Located in the Selkirk Mountains, Mount Spokane State Park is one of the largest state parks in Washington. It offers a diverse landscape of sub-alpine meadows, old-growth forests, and dramatic granite peaks. Historically significant for its Civilian Conservation Corps structures, the park provides a rugged escape for hikers, mountain bikers, and winter sports enthusiasts alike. The summit offers panoramic views that can stretch as far as the Canadian border on clear days.

hikingTrails.name: Summit Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steady climb that leads visitors to the historic Vista House at the summit, offering breathtaking 360-degree views.

hikingTrails.name: Burping Brook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic path that winds through lush forest areas and crosses several small, tranquil streams.

washington.campingInfo: The park offers primitive camping at the Lower Kit Carson Loop Road area, which includes sites suitable for tents and small RVs, though no hookups are provided.
washington.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the park's smaller ponds and streams, though the park is primarily known for its mountain terrain rather than large-scale boating.

visitorCenter.name: Mount Spokane Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, trail condition updates, and information on park history and seasonal activities.

washington.hours: 6:30 AM to dusk daily
washington.entranceFees: A Washington State Discover Pass is required for vehicle access ($10 daily or $30 annually).
washington.address: 26107 N. Mt. Spokane Park Dr., Mead, WA 99021
washington.bestTimeToVisit: July through September for hiking; December through March for winter sports.
tips: Check the official website for current road conditions before driving up, as mountain weather changes rapidly.
Bring a Discover Pass, as it is required for vehicle access to all Washington state parks.
Visit the historic Vista House during summer weekends to learn about the park's CCC history.

washington.name: Fort Worden State Park
washington.shortDescription: A historic former military base turned state park, Fort Worden offers stunning views of the Olympic Mountains and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
washington.fullDescription: Fort Worden State Park is a 432-acre park with over two miles of saltwater shoreline. Originally built as a coastal defense fort in the early 1900s, it features well-preserved concrete bunkers and Victorian-era officer homes. The park is rich in history and natural beauty, providing visitors with a unique blend of military architecture and coastal wilderness.

hikingTrails.name: Point Wilson Lighthouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, scenic walk along the beach leading to the iconic Point Wilson Lighthouse.

hikingTrails.name: Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the high bluffs, offering panoramic views of the water and the Olympic Peninsula.

washington.campingInfo: The park features 80 tent sites and 50 full-hookup RV sites, along with several historic houses available for vacation rentals.
washington.fishingBoating: The park offers excellent saltwater fishing opportunities from the beach and a boat launch nearby in Port Townsend.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Worden State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, maps, and event scheduling for the various arts and educational programs held on-site.

washington.hours: 6:30 AM - 10:00 PM daily
washington.entranceFees: A Discover Pass is required for vehicle access, costing $10 for a day pass or $30 for an annual pass.
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and outdoor activities.
tips: Bring a flashlight to safely explore the dark, underground bunkers.
Check the tide charts before heading out for beachcombing.
Book campsites well in advance as they fill up quickly during summer months.

washington.name: Moran State Park
washington.shortDescription: Located on Orcas Island, Moran State Park is a crown jewel of the San Juan Islands, featuring lush forests, freshwater lakes, and the panoramic summit of Mount Constitution.
washington.fullDescription: Moran State Park encompasses over 5,000 acres of diverse terrain on Orcas Island. Established in 1921 through the donation of land by Robert Moran, the park features a complex network of trails, five freshwater lakes, and the historic stone observation tower atop Mount Constitution, which offers breathtaking 360-degree views of the San Juan archipelago and beyond.
thingsToDo: Swimming and paddleboarding in Cascade Lake
Visiting the Mount Constitution observation tower

hikingTrails.name: Mount Constitution Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steady climb through old-growth forest leading to the highest point in the San Juan Islands.

hikingTrails.name: Cascade Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, scenic walk that leads to a beautiful waterfall tucked away in the forest.

washington.campingInfo: The park offers 151 campsites across five campgrounds, including sites for tents and RVs, as well as several environmental campsites and group camps.
washington.fishingBoating: Cascade Lake offers excellent trout fishing and a boat launch for non-motorized watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Moran State Park Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping permits.

washington.hours: 6:30 AM to 10:00 PM daily
washington.entranceFees: A Discover Pass is required for vehicle access ($10 daily or $30 annually).
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and trail conditions.
tips: Book campsites well in advance as they fill up quickly during summer months.
Bring binoculars for spotting wildlife and distant mountain ranges from the summit.
Check the ferry schedule for Orcas Island before planning your trip.

washington.name: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park
washington.shortDescription: A stunning geological wonder featuring the massive Dry Falls cataract and a chain of desert lakes perfect for outdoor recreation.
washington.fullDescription: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park is a 4,027-acre camping park located in the Channeled Scablands of eastern Washington. The park is famous for Dry Falls, a 3.5-mile-wide, 400-foot-high precipice that was once the site of a massive waterfall during the last Ice Age. The area offers a unique desert landscape with basalt cliffs, glacial flood remnants, and a series of interconnected lakes created by the catastrophic Missoula Floods.
thingsToDo: Golfing at the Sun Lakes Park Resort course

hikingTrails.name: Dry Falls Interpretive Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, paved path leading to an overlook with spectacular views of the ancient waterfall basin.

hikingTrails.name: Umatilla Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A loop trail that circles the massive Umatilla Rock formation, offering close-up views of basalt columns and flood-scoured terrain.

washington.campingInfo: The park offers extensive camping facilities including 173 standard sites, 28 full-hookup sites, and several cabins available for reservation.
washington.fishingBoating: The park provides boat ramps on Park Lake and Deep Lake, with excellent opportunities for trout fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Dry Falls Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the Ice Age floods, local geology, and the history of the Grand Coulee.

washington.hours: 6:30 AM to dusk daily
washington.entranceFees: A Washington State Discover Pass is required for vehicle access ($10 daily or $30 annually).
washington.address: 34875 Park Lake Rd NE, Coulee City, WA 99115
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming desert wildflowers.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the desert climate can be very dry and hot in the summer.
Visit the Dry Falls Visitor Center first to understand the geological significance of the area.
Check for burn bans before planning a campfire during the summer months.

washington.name: Wallace Falls State Park
washington.shortDescription: A stunning park featuring a series of nine waterfalls along the Wallace River, nestled in the lush forests of the Cascade Mountains.
washington.fullDescription: Wallace Falls State Park is a 1,380-acre park located near Gold Bar, Washington. It is renowned for its spectacular waterfall system, which drops over 600 feet in total. The park offers a dense, old-growth forest environment with moss-covered trees and ferns, providing a quintessential Pacific Northwest hiking experience. The geology of the area is defined by the steep terrain of the Wallace River valley, carved by glacial activity and river erosion over millennia.

hikingTrails.name: Wallace Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: This popular trail leads hikers past the lower, middle, and upper falls, offering breathtaking views of the cascading water.

hikingTrails.name: Greg Ball Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic, forested trail that connects to the main falls trail, named in honor of a local trail builder.

washington.campingInfo: The park offers five cabins available for reservation, which are heated and include electricity. There are no tent or RV campsites available within the park boundaries.
washington.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Wallace River in accordance with state regulations, though there are no boat ramps within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Wallace Falls Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and safety guidance for visitors.

washington.hours: 8:00 AM to dusk daily
washington.entranceFees: A Washington State Discover Pass is required for vehicle access ($10 daily or $30 annual).
washington.address: 14503 Wallace Lake Rd, Gold Bar, WA 98251
washington.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and early summer for peak waterfall flow, or autumn for vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly.
Bring a rain jacket even in summer, as the mist from the falls can be heavy.
Ensure you have a Discover Pass displayed in your vehicle to avoid fines.

wyoming.name: Glendo State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Wyoming park around Glendo Reservoir on the North Platte River, with 45 miles of bike trails and 500+ campsites.
wyoming.fullDescription: Glendo State Park surrounds Glendo Reservoir on the North Platte River near the town of Glendo, about 20 miles southeast of Douglas. It has 45 miles of mountain bike trails, more than 500 campsites, and fishing and water sports on a reservoir that has produced several state-record fish.

hikingTrails.name: Sunset Point
hikingTrails.description: An out-and-back hike high above Glendo Reservoir to Sunset Point.

wyoming.campingInfo: The park has over 500 campsites spread across 19 campgrounds.
wyoming.fishingBoating: Glendo Reservoir has one of the best walleye fisheries in Wyoming, and six boat ramps provide seasonal water access, though water levels vary significantly through the year.

visitorCenter.name: Glendo State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

wyoming.hours: Open year-round. Day-use permits are required 6AM–10PM and camping permits 10PM–6AM. Fee booths are staffed daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
wyoming.entranceFees: 2026: $7 per vehicle per day for Wyoming residents. The nonresident fee is not stated in the sources.
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall (Memorial Day to Labor Day) is best for boating and camping when water access is seasonal, though trails and recreation are open year-round.
tips: Water levels vary significantly through the year, so check reservoir capacity and boat-ramp status before your trip.
Outside Memorial Day–Labor Day, fee booths are unstaffed, so pay by cash, check or credit card at the canisters and kiosks.
Park headquarters is about 2 miles past the main fee booth on Glendo Park Road, on the left just past the Marina.

wyoming.name: Hot Springs State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Thermopolis park known for 135°F mineral hot springs and free soaking at the State Bath House.
wyoming.fullDescription: Hot Springs State Park in Thermopolis is known for hot springs that flow at a constant 135°F. The State Bath House offers free bathing in water cooled to 104°F. The park also has travertine terraces formed by the mineral springs, a suspension footbridge over the Bighorn River, flower gardens and a small state bison herd.
thingsToDo: Free soaking at the State Bath House

hikingTrails.name: T Hill and Rim Loop
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists it among the trails in Hot Springs State Park with scenic mountain peak views.

hikingTrails.name: Monument Hill Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists it among the trails in Hot Springs State Park with scenic mountain peak views.

hikingTrails.name: Spirit Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists it among the trails in Hot Springs State Park with scenic mountain peak views.

wyoming.fishingBoating: The park offers fishing and a boat ramp along the Big Horn River.

visitorCenter.name: Hot Springs State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

wyoming.hours: Grounds 6 a.m.–10 p.m., open year-round. Bath House summer hours are Mon–Sat 8 a.m.–7 p.m. and Sun noon–7 p.m. Winter hours are Mon–Sat 8 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Sun noon–5:30 p.m. The Bath House is closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.
wyoming.entranceFees: Free; no charge to enter, and the State Bath House is a free public facility.
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Summer brings colorful flower gardens and longer Bath House hours, while late fall and winter offer close-up views of the bison herd during daily feedings.
tips: In late fall and winter, the park's bison are usually fed a daily supplement around 8:30 a.m., which is a good chance to see them up close. The park asks that bison be viewed only from a safe position.
The three large group picnic shelters are reservable and heavily used. Contact park headquarters early to reserve one, and ask whether your group needs a park liquor permit.
The free State Bath House keeps its water at 104°F for therapeutic bathing. It is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

wyoming.name: Curt Gowdy State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Wyoming park between Cheyenne and Laramie, known for its trail system, fishing reservoirs and Hidden Falls.
wyoming.fullDescription: Curt Gowdy State Park covers 3,395 acres on Happy Jack Road, halfway between Cheyenne and Laramie. Opened in 1971 as Granite State Park, it was renamed in 1972 for Wyoming-born sportscaster Curt Gowdy. It is known for over 35 miles of trails for biking, hiking and horseback riding, its fishing reservoirs, the Hidden Falls area and the historic Hynds Lodge.

hikingTrails.name: Mo' Rocka Trail
hikingTrails.description: Visit Cheyenne rates this trail advanced and says it takes around 45 minutes.

hikingTrails.name: Hidden Falls
hikingTrails.description: The park calls this one of its busiest trails, and the Hidden Falls Trailhead has improvements including a new restroom, an accessible picnic shelter and formalized parking.

hikingTrails.name: Stone Temple Circuit
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists it as a popular fall hiking trail in Curt Gowdy State Park.

wyoming.campingInfo: All campsites are by reservation only, and the Aspen Grove campground is next to a free public horse corral for visitors camping with horses.
wyoming.fishingBoating: Granite Reservoir offers rainbow trout and kokanee salmon fishing plus water sports, while Crystal Reservoir has shoreline fishing and boating with a 15 horsepower limit.

visitorCenter.name: Curt Gowdy State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

wyoming.hours: Park open 365 days, 24 hrs (with camping permit); visitor center hours vary seasonally
wyoming.entranceFees: Wyoming residents $7 per day per vehicle (2026 official schedule); non-residents $12 per vehicle per cheyenne.org
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is generally best for hiking, biking and fishing at this roughly 7,000-foot park, though the official page lists year-round activities, including winter sports.
tips: Reserve ahead, because all campsites are by reservation only.
North Crow Reservoir is an unimproved, day-use-only fishing area with no picnic tables, water supply or comfort stations, so bring what you need.
Expect crowds at Hidden Falls, one of the park's busiest trails, which now has formalized trailhead parking.

wyoming.name: Keyhole State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Located on the western edge of the Black Hills, Keyhole State Park offers stunning reservoir views and exceptional outdoor recreation opportunities.
wyoming.fullDescription: Keyhole State Park is situated along the shores of the Keyhole Reservoir, which was created by the construction of the Keyhole Dam on the Belle Fourche River. The park is renowned for its diverse landscape, ranging from open ponderosa pine forests to rugged sandstone cliffs. It serves as a premier destination for water sports, fishing, and wildlife viewing, providing a peaceful retreat for visitors exploring the northeastern corner of Wyoming.
thingsToDo: Fishing for walleye and smallmouth bass

hikingTrails.name: Wind Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through the pine trees and offers beautiful views of the reservoir shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Arch Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads hikers through unique sandstone formations and provides elevated vantage points over the water.

wyoming.campingInfo: The park features multiple campgrounds including Homestead, Antelope, and Tatanka, offering a mix of tent sites and RV sites with electrical hookups.
wyoming.fishingBoating: The reservoir is a popular spot for fishing walleye, northern pike, and smallmouth bass; multiple boat ramps are available for public use.

visitorCenter.name: Keyhole State Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping permits and regulations.

wyoming.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
wyoming.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $6.00 for Wyoming residents and $11.00 for non-residents.
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water activities and pleasant weather.
tips: Bring plenty of sunscreen and water as the reservoir area can be very exposed to the sun.
Check the wind forecast before heading out on the water, as the reservoir can get choppy.
Make camping reservations well in advance during the summer months as sites fill up quickly.

wyoming.name: Boysen State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Located at the mouth of the spectacular Wind River Canyon, Boysen State Park offers expansive water recreation and stunning desert landscapes.
wyoming.fullDescription: Boysen State Park surrounds the massive Boysen Reservoir, which was created by the construction of the Boysen Dam on the Wind River. The park features diverse terrain ranging from high desert plains to dramatic red rock canyons, providing a unique geological backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts. It is a premier destination for water sports, fishing, and wildlife viewing in central Wyoming.

hikingTrails.name: Wind River Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail offering panoramic views of the Wind River and the surrounding canyon walls.

hikingTrails.name: Tough Creek Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path winding through the desert landscape, perfect for spotting local flora and fauna.

wyoming.campingInfo: The park features 11 developed campgrounds with over 150 campsites, many of which offer lake views and basic amenities like fire rings and picnic tables.
wyoming.fishingBoating: The reservoir is famous for its walleye, perch, and trout fishing, with multiple boat ramps available for public use.

visitorCenter.name: Boysen State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping permits and regulations.

wyoming.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping and recreation
wyoming.entranceFees: Daily vehicle fee is $7.00 for Wyoming residents and $12.00 for non-residents.
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water temperatures and weather.
tips: Bring plenty of sunscreen and water as the high desert sun can be intense.
Check the wind forecast before heading out on the water, as it can pick up quickly.
Keep a camera ready for the bighorn sheep often seen near the canyon entrance.

wyoming.name: Buffalo Bill State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Located just outside the east entrance of Yellowstone National Park, this scenic park offers stunning views of the Absaroka Mountains and the expansive Buffalo Bill Reservoir.
wyoming.fullDescription: Buffalo Bill State Park is situated in the scenic Shoshone River valley, featuring the massive Buffalo Bill Reservoir created by the historic Buffalo Bill Dam. The park provides a gateway to the high country of Wyoming, offering visitors a unique blend of water-based recreation and rugged mountain landscapes. The area is rich in history, named after the legendary William 'Buffalo Bill' Cody, who founded the nearby town of Cody. The geology is dominated by volcanic formations and the dramatic canyon walls of the Shoshone River.
thingsToDo: Boating and sailing on the reservoir

hikingTrails.name: Buffalo Bill Reservoir Trail
hikingTrails.description: A relatively flat trail that follows the shoreline of the reservoir, offering excellent opportunities for bird watching and photography.

hikingTrails.name: Cedar Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail climbs into the foothills, providing panoramic views of the reservoir and the surrounding Absaroka Range.

wyoming.campingInfo: The park features two main campgrounds, North Fork and Lakeview, offering a total of 97 campsites. Many sites provide electrical hookups, and all are equipped with picnic tables and fire rings.
wyoming.fishingBoating: The reservoir is a premier destination for trout fishing, including brown, rainbow, and cutthroat trout. Two boat ramps are available for public use.

visitorCenter.name: Buffalo Bill State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, local wildlife, and recreational opportunities, along with educational exhibits about the dam.

wyoming.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
wyoming.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $7.00 for Wyoming residents and $13.00 for non-residents.
wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: June through September for optimal weather and water activities.
tips: Be prepared for high winds that can develop quickly on the reservoir.
Bring binoculars for spotting bighorn sheep on the nearby canyon walls.
Always store food properly to avoid attracting local wildlife.
nearbyAttractions: Buffalo Bill Center of the West

wyoming.name: Sinks Canyon State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: Located in the Wind River Mountains, this park is famous for the mysterious 'Sinks' where the Popo Agie River disappears into a limestone cavern.
wyoming.fullDescription: Sinks Canyon State Park offers a unique geological experience where the Popo Agie River flows into a large cavern at the base of a 600-foot limestone cliff, only to reappear a quarter-mile downstream in a crystal-clear pool teeming with trout. The canyon provides a dramatic landscape of sheer rock walls, lush riparian zones, and diverse wildlife habitats, serving as a gateway to the Shoshone National Forest.

hikingTrails.name: Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads hikers to the beautiful Popo Agie Falls, offering great views of the canyon floor.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: An accessible loop trail perfect for families, featuring interpretive signs about the local flora and geology.

wyoming.campingInfo: The park features several campgrounds including Popo Agie, Sawmill, and Boulder Flat, offering tent and RV sites with fire rings and picnic tables.
wyoming.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Popo Agie River, though the 'Rise' area is a protected sanctuary where fishing is prohibited.

visitorCenter.name: Sinks Canyon Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the geology of the canyon, local history, and wildlife, plus a gift shop.

wyoming.entranceFees: Free entrance for day use; camping fees apply.
tips: Bring quarters to purchase fish food at the visitor center to feed the trout at the Rise.
Be bear aware and store all food properly in bear-resistant containers.
Visit in the early morning or late evening for the best chances to spot moose and deer.

wyoming.name: Bear River State Park
wyoming.shortDescription: A beautiful riverside park in Evanston, Wyoming, known for its resident elk and bison herds and scenic walking trails.
wyoming.fullDescription: Bear River State Park is a unique urban oasis located along the banks of the Bear River. It serves as a gateway to Wyoming, featuring a visitor center with educational exhibits about the region's history and wildlife. The park is famous for its captive herd of elk and bison, which visitors can view from designated observation areas. The park's landscape includes lush riparian zones, open meadows, and miles of paved and natural trails that connect to the city of Evanston's trail system.
thingsToDo: Wildlife viewing of elk and bison
Hiking and cycling on paved trails
