Educational programs at the visitor center

hikingTrails.name: Bear River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A mostly flat, paved trail that follows the winding path of the Bear River, offering excellent bird-watching opportunities.

hikingTrails.name: Bison Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail that circles the wildlife enclosure, providing consistent views of the park's resident bison and elk herds.

wyoming.campingInfo: Bear River State Park does not offer overnight camping or RV hookups; however, it provides excellent day-use facilities and picnic shelters.
wyoming.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Bear River within park boundaries; please ensure you have a valid Wyoming fishing license.

visitorCenter.name: Bear River State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive displays on local wildlife, geology, and the history of the Bear River valley.

wyoming.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal wildlife viewing and trail conditions.
tips: Bring binoculars for better views of the elk and bison herds.
The park connects to the Evanston city trail system, perfect for longer bike rides.
Visit during the early morning or late evening for the best chance to see active wildlife.

illinois.name: Starved Rock State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Illinois River park known for its 18 sandstone canyons, seasonal waterfalls and river overlooks.
illinois.fullDescription: Starved Rock covers 2,630 acres on the south bank of the Illinois River near Utica and is the most visited state park in Illinois. Its sandstone canyons were carved by glacial floodwaters; French, LaSalle, Ottawa and St. Louis Canyons have the longest-lasting waterfalls. Over 13 miles of trails lead to the canyons and to river overlooks such as Lover's Leap and Eagle Cliff.

hikingTrails.name: Starved Rock and Sandstone Point Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A 4.2-mile loop near Oglesby that is generally considered moderately challenging and takes about 1.5 hours on average.

illinois.campingInfo: The park campground has 133 Class-A Premium campsites, and its gates are open from 8:30 a.m. until 10 p.m. daily.
illinois.fishingBoating: The park's activities page lists catfish, bullhead, white bass, sauger and walleye for fishing and says boats may be launched from the west end of the park.

visitorCenter.name: Starved Rock State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

illinois.hours: Trails 7 a.m. until sunset; visitor center 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily
illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall are good times to see the park's sandstone canyons and waterfalls, but check the posted late-fall and winter deer hunting closures before you go.
tips: Throughout 2026, a major trail improvement project may close some trails or limit access, so check current trail availability online before visiting.

During deer hunting seasons (Nov 20-22, Dec 3-6, Dec 11-13, Dec 31-Jan 3 and Jan 15-17, 2027), areas including the Starved Rock Nature Preserve, the Hennepin Canyon Parking Lot and, for some dates, the campground are closed to the public except for hunters.
Groups of 20 or more need advance written permission, and activity permits should be submitted at least 21 days ahead.

illinois.name: Matthiessen State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Illinois park near Starved Rock with a stream-cut sandstone canyon, the Upper and Lower Dells and waterfalls.
illinois.fullDescription: Matthiessen State Park, a few miles south of Starved Rock, is centered on a stream that runs from Matthiessen Lake to the Vermilion River through sandstone canyons. The Upper Dells start at Lake Falls and end at 45-foot Cascade Falls, where the Lower Dells begin. The 1,938-acre park was once the private estate of industrialist Frederick Matthiessen.

hikingTrails.name: Matthiessen State Park River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A loop trail near Oglesby that AllTrails describes as an easy route taking an average of 41 minutes to complete.

hikingTrails.name: Matthiessen State Park Lake Loop
hikingTrails.description: An easy hike with 95 ft of elevation gain that takes about 0.5–1 hour to complete.

illinois.campingInfo: The official park page lists camping among park activities, and the park's activities page references equestrian camping.
illinois.fishingBoating: Bank fishing is allowed at Matthiessen Lake on the north side of the park off Route 71, following state fishing regulations.

visitorCenter.name: Matthiessen State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Spring through early fall is a good time to explore the canyons, waterfalls and rock formations of the Dells. Check closure dates before visiting in late fall and winter, when the park closes to the public for deer hunting seasons.
tips: The park is closed to the public (except hunters) during deer seasons: Nov 20–22 and Dec 3–6 (shotgun), and Dec 11–13 (muzzleloader). During the CWD firearm seasons (Dec 31–Jan 3 and Jan 15–17, 2027), park trails stay open but Matthiessen Nature Preserve is closed.

The Lake Falls bridge/trail is closed to all hikers until further notice, with a posted detour. The restroom building at the Dells parking lot is closed for repairs, and porta-potties are available instead.

Stay on marked trails, since going off-trail is illegal. Swimming, rock climbing/rappelling, drones and alcohol are all prohibited. Bikes are not allowed on Dells Area trails and are permitted only in the Vermillion River Area.

illinois.name: Giant City State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Southern Illinois park known for its 'Giant City Streets' of huge sandstone bluffs and a 1930s CCC-built lodge.
illinois.fullDescription: Giant City State Park covers about 4,000 acres in Jackson and Union counties in Southern Illinois. It has a lodge and cabins built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, now with a restaurant, and a prehistoric stone fort site listed on the National Register. The park is a National Natural Landmark.

hikingTrails.name: Giant City Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: The park's especially popular trail, home of the "Giant City Streets," huge sandstone bluffs formed 12,000 years ago.

hikingTrails.name: Red Cedar Trail
hikingTrails.description: Listed as one of the park's most popular hiking trails.

hikingTrails.name: Trillium Trail
hikingTrails.description: Listed as one of the park's most popular hiking trails.

illinois.campingInfo: The park has 85 Class A campsites reservable online at ExploreMoreIL, a Class C area with 14 walk-in campsites, a youth group camping area, and an equestrian campground.
illinois.fishingBoating: Ponds throughout the park offer bank fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Giant City State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

illinois.hours: Park 7 a.m. - 10 p.m.; trails 7 a.m. - dusk; Visitor Center 8 a.m. - 3:30 p.m.
illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Spring is a good time to visit because the park is known for hundreds of species of wildflowers. Fall is also pleasant for hiking among its more than 75 tree varieties and sandstone bluffs. Note that the lodge closes from mid-December to early February.
tips: Trails are open only from 7 a.m. to dusk, even though the park itself stays open until 10 p.m.
The lodge and cabins are seasonal, open from the first Friday in February to mid-December. Call 618-457-4921 for reservations.
Rock climbing and rappelling are permitted only in two designated locations. The Giant City Stables operate only from March 15 to November 15.

illinois.name: Cave-in-Rock State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Perched on the banks of the Ohio River, this park is famous for its historic 55-foot-wide limestone cavern once used by river pirates.
illinois.fullDescription: Cave-in-Rock State Park is located in Hardin County, Illinois, overlooking the Ohio River. The park is named for the 55-foot-wide cave carved into the limestone bluff by water erosion. Historically, the cave served as a notorious hideout for river pirates and outlaws in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Today, the park offers scenic views of the river, rugged bluffs, and a peaceful environment for outdoor recreation.

hikingTrails.name: Pirate's Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the limestone bluffs, offering panoramic views of the Ohio River.

hikingTrails.name: Cave Access Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading directly from the parking area to the entrance of the historic cave.

illinois.campingInfo: The park features a campground with 34 sites, including some with electricity, as well as a playground and shower facilities.
illinois.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Ohio River shoreline; however, there is no boat ramp located directly within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Cave-in-Rock Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and camping registration.

illinois.address: 1 New State Park Rd, Cave-In-Rock, IL 62919
illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and vibrant foliage.
tips: Bring a flashlight to explore the depths of the cave safely.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the limestone near the river can be slippery.
Check the river levels before visiting, as high water can occasionally restrict access to the cave entrance.

illinois.name: Pere Marquette State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Illinois' largest state park, offering stunning views of the Illinois River and famous for its winter bald eagle population.
illinois.fullDescription: Located near the confluence of the Illinois and Mississippi Rivers, Pere Marquette State Park is a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts. The park is named after Father Jacques Marquette, who arrived in the area in 1673. Its rugged landscape features massive limestone bluffs, deep ravines, and lush forests, providing a diverse habitat for wildlife and spectacular vistas for visitors.
thingsToDo: Picnicking in the historic stone shelters

hikingTrails.name: Goat Cliff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the base of the limestone bluffs and offers excellent opportunities to spot local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Dogwood Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that is particularly beautiful during the spring when the dogwood trees are in full bloom.

illinois.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 80 sites, including electrical hookups, shower facilities, and a youth tent area.
illinois.fishingBoating: The park provides a boat ramp for access to the Illinois River, which is popular for fishing bass, crappie, and catfish.

visitorCenter.name: Pere Marquette Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the history of the Illinois River, local geology, and the annual bald eagle migration.

illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Winter for eagle watching or Autumn for fall foliage.
tips: Visit in January or February for the best chance to see bald eagles.
Bring binoculars for bird watching along the river bluffs.
Check the visitor center for scheduled guided nature hikes.

illinois.name: Illinois Beach State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Illinois Beach State Park is the only remaining beach ridge shoreline left in the state, offering unique dunes and sandy beaches along Lake Michigan.
illinois.fullDescription: Spanning over 4,000 acres, Illinois Beach State Park features a diverse landscape of sandy beaches, dunes, marshes, and forests. It is the only remaining beach ridge shoreline left in the state, providing a critical habitat for rare plants and animals. The park is divided into two units, North and South, and offers a unique glimpse into the natural history of the Lake Michigan shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Dead River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the dunes and offers views of the Dead River and surrounding wetlands.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses the unique beach ridge topography, showcasing the diverse plant life of the region.

illinois.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 241 sites, many equipped with electricity, showers, and sanitary facilities for both tents and RVs.
illinois.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Lake Michigan shoreline and in the park's ponds; however, there are no boat ramps within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Illinois Beach State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides educational exhibits on the park's unique geology, local flora, and fauna, along with ranger assistance.

illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities and bird migration.
tips: Visit during the weekdays to avoid large crowds on the beach.
Bring insect repellent, especially when hiking near the marshy areas.
Check the official website for current beach swimming advisories before arriving.

illinois.name: Mississippi Palisades State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Perched high above the Mississippi River, this park features dramatic limestone bluffs and breathtaking views of the river valley.
illinois.fullDescription: Mississippi Palisades State Park is a 2,500-acre park located in Carroll County, Illinois. The park is defined by its rugged limestone bluffs, deep ravines, and ancient rock formations carved by the Mississippi River over millennia. It serves as a significant geological site and a haven for diverse wildlife, offering visitors a unique landscape that contrasts sharply with the surrounding flat prairie terrain of Illinois.

hikingTrails.name: Sentinel Trail
hikingTrails.description: A relatively flat trail that offers spectacular views of the Mississippi River and the famous Sentinel rock formation.

hikingTrails.name: Oak Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through dense hardwood forests and provides access to several scenic overlooks along the bluff edge.

illinois.campingInfo: The park offers 241 campsites, including both tent and RV sites. Amenities include electricity, showers, and flush toilets, with some sites available for reservation.
illinois.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the river banks, and there is a boat ramp available for access to the Mississippi River.

visitorCenter.name: Mississippi Palisades Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, educational displays about the local geology, and information on park history.

illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for fall foliage or Spring for bird migration.
tips: Visit during the fall to see the vibrant colors of the trees against the limestone bluffs.
Bring binoculars as the park is a prime location for spotting bald eagles in the winter.
Stay on marked trails to avoid dangerous drop-offs near the cliff edges.

illinois.name: Rock Cut State Park
illinois.shortDescription: Located in northern Illinois, Rock Cut State Park offers over 3,000 acres of rolling hills, lush forests, and two beautiful lakes for outdoor recreation.
illinois.fullDescription: Rock Cut State Park is a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts in Winnebago County. The park features Pierce Lake and Olson Lake, which provide excellent opportunities for fishing, boating, and ice skating. The landscape is characterized by diverse habitats including upland forests, prairie remnants, and wetlands, making it a haven for birdwatchers and nature photographers. Historically, the area was shaped by glacial activity, resulting in the unique topography that visitors enjoy today.
thingsToDo: Fishing and boating on Pierce Lake
Hiking and mountain biking on extensive trails
Winter sports including cross-country skiing and ice fishing
Camping in wooded or open sites
Horseback riding on designated equestrian trails

hikingTrails.name: Pierce Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that circles the perimeter of Pierce Lake, offering frequent views of the water and local waterfowl.

hikingTrails.name: Red Oak Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through mature oak-hickory forests and provides a great opportunity to see spring wildflowers.

illinois.campingInfo: The park offers over 200 campsites, including Class A sites with electricity and showers, as well as primitive equestrian camping areas.
illinois.fishingBoating: Pierce Lake allows motorized boats with a 10-horsepower limit and offers a public boat launch; Olson Lake is restricted to non-motorized watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Rock Cut State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about local flora and fauna.

illinois.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Check the official website for seasonal lake closures or ice thickness reports before visiting.
Bring binoculars as the park is a designated Important Bird Area.
Mountain bikers should check the trail status board at the entrance for current conditions.

indiana.name: Brown County State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Indiana's largest state park, 15,776 wooded acres in the hills near Nashville, with a historic lodge.
indiana.fullDescription: Brown County State Park in southern Indiana is the state's largest, at 15,776 acres, and draws about 1.2 million visitors a year. Its Abe Martin Lodge dates from 1932 and has a restaurant and an indoor water park, with family and rustic cabins and campgrounds nearby.

hikingTrails.name: CCC Trail (Trail 2)
hikingTrails.description: A trail built by the Civilian Conservation Corps with impressive stone bridges, stairways and retaining walls that starts and ends behind the lodge.

hikingTrails.name: Ogle Hollow Nature Preserve Trail (Trail 5)
hikingTrails.description: A self-guided trail that follows a slope wooded with yellowwood trees and loops through the Ogle Hollow Nature Preserve.

hikingTrails.name: Ogle Lake Trail (Trail 7)
hikingTrails.description: A hilly, wooded hike along the shores of Ogle Lake.

indiana.campingInfo: The park offers 401 electric, 28 non-electric and 60 rally campsites, plus a separate horsemen's campground off State Road 135 South with 118 electric and 86 non-electric sites.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing and ice fishing are offered in the park, which has two lakes for fishing, including Ogle Lake and Strahl Lake.

visitorCenter.name: Brown County State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

indiana.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
indiana.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle with Indiana plates; $15 out-of-state plates
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is the classic time to visit, as Indiana's largest park is a traditional fall color hot spot with nearly 20 miles of tree-lined roads and scenic vistas, though the park is popular year-round.
tips: All RVs and vehicles towing trailers must use the West Gate on State Road 46, because the North Gate has a historic covered bridge with a 9-foot height clearance and a 3-ton weight limit.
GPS directions may not send you to the correct entrance, so use the official mapping addresses or coordinates for the West Gate, North Gate or Horse Camp.
Pool hours may change in summer because of weather and staffing, so call the property office for exact times before your visit.

indiana.name: Turkey Run State Park
indiana.shortDescription: West-central Indiana park of sandstone gorges along Sugar Creek, with a suspension bridge and a 1919 inn.
indiana.fullDescription: Turkey Run, Indiana's second state park (1916), sits along Sugar Creek in Parke County. It includes the Rocky Hollow Falls Canyon Nature Preserve, a suspension bridge across the creek, the historic Lusk Home and Mill Site, the Richard Lieber Log Cabin and the Turkey Run Inn, built in 1919.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 3
hikingTrails.description: Known as the ladders trail, it offers unusual hiking between the steep walls of Rocky and Bear hollows, and portions may be impassable during high water.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 10
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads to 'Camel's Back' for a fine scenic view and passes many unusual formations caused by erosion.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 11
hikingTrails.description: A short hike high above Turkey Run Hollow leads to the Lieber Memorial and Log Church.

indiana.campingInfo: The park's campground has 213 electric sites, plus youth tent areas, a camp store and a dumping station.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing is a listed park activity, and a third-party guide says anglers can fish Sugar Creek for bass and bluegill with a state fishing license.

visitorCenter.name: Turkey Run State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

indiana.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
indiana.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle with Indiana plates; $15 out-of-state plates
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is when the ravine drainages are relatively free of water, which makes the streambed trails most passable, and arriving early helps avoid the busiest hours.
tips: All trails use ravine streambeds in places and can be slick or impassable during high water, so treat flooded sections as closed and use alternate trails.
The ladders on Trail 3 can be hazardous for visitors with some medical conditions or disabilities, and hikers with small children or pets should use alternate trails.
Pool hours may change because of weather and staffing, so contact the property office for exact times before your visit.

indiana.name: Clifty Falls State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Indiana park on the Ohio River near Madison with a creek canyon and four waterfalls of 60 to 83 feet.
indiana.fullDescription: Clifty Falls State Park covers 1,416 acres in Jefferson County near Madison. Clifty Creek Canyon runs the length of the park, and its waterfalls include Big and Little Clifty Falls (60 ft each), Hoffman Falls (78 ft) and Tunnel Falls (83 ft). Ten trails range from easy to very rugged, and the Clifty Inn and a campground offer overnight stays.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 4
hikingTrails.description: Starts at the Hoffman Falls parking lot, reaches a falls overlook after a short distance, and follows the canyon to Lilly Memorial, where there is a long, steep staircase.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 7
hikingTrails.description: Starts at Clifty Shelter and passes Little Clifty Falls along rocky footing to Lookout Point, then returns via the upper Little Clifty Creek gorge.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 5
hikingTrails.description: Descends a long, steep staircase from Lilly Memorial and follows the canyon past the tunnel entrances and Oak Grove to Tunnel Falls.

indiana.campingInfo: The park campground has 106 electric and 63 non-electric sites, plus youth tent areas and a dumping station, with campground reservations available.
indiana.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Clifty Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

indiana.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
indiana.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle with Indiana plates; $15 out-of-state plates
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Winter and spring are best for seeing the park's waterfalls at their most impressive, though Clifty Canyon offers hiking year-round.
tips: Brough's Tunnel is closed indefinitely after a rockslide. Trail 5 remains open, but avoid both tunnel entrances.
Trail 2 is mostly the stone bed of Clifty Creek and may be impassable during high water. Areas above and below all waterfalls are always off limits.
Trails in Clifty Canyon close after sunset, so plan canyon hikes for daylight.
nearbyAttractions: Madison riverfront on the Ohio River

indiana.name: Indiana Dunes State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Located along the southern shore of Lake Michigan, this park features massive sand dunes, expansive beaches, and diverse ecosystems.
indiana.fullDescription: Indiana Dunes State Park consists of 2,182 acres of primitive, beautiful, historic, and unique landscape. It is located in Porter County, Indiana, and features more than three miles of beautiful beach along Lake Michigan. The park is surrounded by the Indiana Dunes National Park and offers a unique look at the geological history of the Great Lakes region, including the famous '3 Dune Challenge' which traverses the three tallest dunes in the park.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 8
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers over the three tallest dunes in the park, offering panoramic views of Lake Michigan.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 9
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the dunes and wooded areas, providing a great look at the park's diverse flora.

indiana.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 140 sites, including full hookups for RVs and modern restrooms with showers.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Lake Michigan shoreline, though no boat launch is available within the state park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Indiana Dunes State Park Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The Nature Center provides educational exhibits about the dunes' ecology, history, and local wildlife, along with ranger-led programs.

indiana.entranceFees: $7.00 for Indiana residents and $12.00 for out-of-state vehicles per day.
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities and hiking.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring plenty of water and sunscreen for the exposed dune hikes.
Check the park website for current beach water quality reports before swimming.

indiana.name: Pokagon State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Located in the lake country of northeast Indiana, Pokagon State Park offers beautiful glacial landscapes and year-round recreational activities.
indiana.fullDescription: Pokagon State Park is nestled between Lake James and Snow Lake, offering a unique glacial landscape characterized by rolling hills and kettle lakes. Established in 1925, the park is named after the Potawatomi chiefs Leopold and Simon Pokagon. It is famous for its diverse ecosystems, including wetlands, forests, and meadows, and is home to the historic Potawatomi Inn.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Lake James
Wildlife viewing at the nature center

hikingTrails.name: Trail 3
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through diverse forest habitats and offers scenic views of the glacial kettle holes.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 4
hikingTrails.description: A beautiful loop that takes hikers through the park's wetland areas and hardwood forests.

indiana.campingInfo: The park features over 200 electric campsites and several non-electric sites, along with the historic Potawatomi Inn which offers lodge rooms and cabins.
indiana.fishingBoating: The park provides boat ramps for access to Lake James and Snow Lake, with fishing opportunities for bass, bluegill, and perch.

visitorCenter.name: Pokagon Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on local geology, wildlife, and the history of the Potawatomi people.

indiana.entranceFees: $7.00 per vehicle for Indiana residents, $9.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for wildflowers or winter for the famous toboggan run.
tips: Visit the toboggan run early on weekends as it reaches capacity quickly.
Bring binoculars for bird watching near the wetlands.
Check the park website for seasonal programs and guided nature hikes.

indiana.name: Spring Mill State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Experience a unique blend of history and nature at Spring Mill, featuring a restored pioneer village and fascinating limestone caves.
indiana.fullDescription: Spring Mill State Park is a unique destination that combines natural beauty with historical preservation. The park is home to a fully restored 1863 pioneer village, complete with a working water-powered grist mill. Geologically, the park is famous for its extensive karst topography, featuring numerous sinkholes and the impressive Donaldson Cave system, which offers a glimpse into the subterranean world of Indiana.
thingsToDo: Explore the Twin Caves boat tour
Visit the Virgil I. Grissom Memorial

hikingTrails.name: Trail 3
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the woods and offers beautiful views of the park's unique karst landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 4
hikingTrails.description: A challenging hike that takes visitors through the rugged terrain surrounding the cave entrances.

indiana.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 187 electric sites and 36 primitive sites, along with modern restrooms, showers, and a camp store.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted on the 30-acre Spring Mill Lake; boat rentals are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Spring Mill Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The nature center provides educational exhibits on the park's geology, cave systems, and local wildlife.

indiana.entranceFees: $7.00 for Indiana residents and $9.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book your cave boat tour early as they fill up quickly during peak season.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to explore the more rugged trails.
Visit the grist mill during the week to avoid weekend crowds.

indiana.name: McCormick's Creek State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Indiana's first state park, featuring a stunning limestone canyon, scenic waterfalls, and historic structures.
indiana.fullDescription: Established in 1916, McCormick's Creek State Park is Indiana's oldest state park. It is renowned for its dramatic limestone canyon carved by the waters of McCormick's Creek, which flows into the White River. The park features diverse geological formations, including sinkholes and caves, and is home to the historic Canyon Inn, which was originally built as a sanitarium in the late 19th century.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 3
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers through the heart of the canyon, offering close-up views of the limestone walls and the creek.

hikingTrails.name: Trail 5
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the forest and provides access to the Wolf Cave nature preserve area.

indiana.campingInfo: The park offers over 180 electric campsites, a youth tent area, and the historic Canyon Inn which provides full-service lodging and dining.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the White River, which borders the park; however, there are no boat ramps located directly within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: McCormick's Creek Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the park's geology, local wildlife, and history, along with a resident naturalist.

indiana.entranceFees: $7.00 for Indiana residents and $9.00 for out-of-state vehicles per day.
indiana.address: 250 McCormick Creek Park Rd, Spencer, IN 47460
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for waterfall viewing or Autumn for fall foliage.
tips: Visit the waterfall after a rainfall for the most impressive flow.
Check the Canyon Inn schedule for seasonal dining hours.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the canyon trails can be slippery and rocky.

indiana.name: Fort Harrison State Park
indiana.shortDescription: Located on the northeast side of Indianapolis, this urban oasis offers 1,700 acres of beautiful woods, rolling hills, and the scenic Fall Creek.
indiana.fullDescription: Fort Harrison State Park, often called 'Fort Ben' by locals, is a former military base turned state park. It features a unique blend of history and nature, with remnants of its military past integrated into the landscape. The park is characterized by its mature hardwood forests, steep ravines, and the meandering Fall Creek, providing a peaceful retreat from the surrounding urban environment of Indianapolis.
thingsToDo: Horseback riding at the saddle barn
Golfing at The Fort Golf Resort

hikingTrails.name: Harrison Trace Trail
hikingTrails.description: A paved multi-use trail that loops around the park, offering great views of the lake and surrounding forest.

hikingTrails.name: Lawrence Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A rugged dirt trail that winds through deep ravines and dense woodlands, perfect for hikers seeking a challenge.

indiana.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options including equestrian campsites and modern facilities, though it is primarily known for its day-use amenities and the historic Garrison event center.
indiana.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Fall Creek and the park's lake; however, no motorized boats are allowed on the water.

visitorCenter.name: The Garrison
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational programs about the local ecosystem.

indiana.entranceFees: $7.00 per vehicle for Indiana residents, $9.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
indiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for the vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit during the weekdays to avoid heavy crowds on the popular hiking trails.
Check the park website for seasonal events and guided nature hikes.
Bring binoculars as the park is a prime location for bird watching near the creek.

iowa.name: Backbone State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Iowa's oldest state park (1920), named for the Devil's Backbone, a narrow rock ridge above the Maquoketa River.
iowa.fullDescription: Backbone State Park near Strawberry Point was dedicated in 1920 as Iowa's first state park. It is named for a steep bedrock ridge carved by a loop of the Maquoketa River. The Civilian Conservation Corps built Backbone Lake's dam and most of the park's trails and buildings in the 1930s.

hikingTrails.name: Backbone Trail
hikingTrails.description: Built by the CCC in 1933–1934, this loop follows the top of the narrow Backbone Ridge and passes some of the park's most popular rock-climbing spots.

hikingTrails.name: West Lake and East Lake Trail Loop
hikingTrails.description: This loop combines the park's East Lake and West Lake trails, which are part of the 21-mile multi-use system and are also used by mountain bikers.

hikingTrails.name: Barred Owl Trail
hikingTrails.description: Barred Owl is one of the park's multi-use trails that the official page recommends to mountain bikers.

iowa.campingInfo: Campers can choose electric and non-electric sites with showers and a dump station at South Lake Campground or non-electric sites with pit latrines at Six Pine Campground, and all campsites require a reservation.
iowa.fishingBoating: Anglers can fish for trout in a clear stream fed by Richmond Springs, and boaters on Backbone Lake can use rentals and a boat ramp, with only electric motors allowed.

visitorCenter.name: Backbone State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

iowa.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Visit from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend for full services, or until mid-October for the CCC museum and fall color in the oak and maple forest; winter brings snowmobile and cross-country ski trails.
tips: Campgrounds are 100% reservable and require a reservation, so book campsites and cabins in advance through the online reservation system.
Rock climbers and rappellers must register at the park office before climbing.
Check the beach monitoring dashboard or call 515-725-3434 for current beach advisories; both are updated on Fridays during the monitoring season.

iowa.name: Ledges State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Iowa park near Boone with a 100-foot-deep sandstone gorge carved by Pea's Creek.
iowa.fullDescription: Ledges State Park, four miles south of Boone, contains a sandstone gorge cut by Pea's Creek, a tributary of the Des Moines River, up to 100 feet deep with concretions jutting from the cliffs. Woodlands of basswood, maple, oak and hickory mix with prairie, and the Des Moines River runs along the west side.

hikingTrails.name: Lost Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A shaded, crushed-limestone path at the southern end of the park leads to a small lake, and its first 0.4 miles are fully accessible, which allows an out-and-back hike of nearly 1 mile.

hikingTrails.name: Ledges Prairie Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails rates this trail an easy hike with about 13 feet of elevation gain, taking roughly 0.5 to 1 hour.

hikingTrails.name: Ledges Table Rock Trail and Inspiration Point
hikingTrails.description: A moderate trail in Ledges State Park, part of a trail system that climbs steep slopes to scenic overlooks of the Pea's Creek canyon.

iowa.campingInfo: The renovated campground has electric, full hook-up and primitive hike-in sites; reservations are required for all sites, are accepted March through November, and the campground is closed December through February.
iowa.fishingBoating: Canoeing and fishing are possible on the Des Moines River, which runs along the west side of the park.

visitorCenter.name: Ledges State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

iowa.entranceFees: Free (Iowa state parks charge no entrance fee)
iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is ideal: the campground is open March through November, families can streamwalk in ankle-deep Peas Creek in warm weather, and the Friends of the Ledges concession runs on weekend evenings from Memorial Day through Labor Day.
tips: All campsites require an advance reservation through the online reservation system. Reservations are accepted March through November, and the campground is closed December through February.
Check the Park Alerts & Notices page for current closures before you go. Low-lying areas of the park are regularly flooded by the Des Moines River.
Trails within the canyon have steps and steep terrain. For an accessible option, use the Lost Lake Trail, whose first 0.4 miles are accessible.

iowa.name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Iowa park with more caves than any other in the state, linked by trails, including Dancehall Cave.
iowa.fullDescription: Maquoketa Caves State Park lies northwest of Maquoketa in Jackson County, in Iowa's unglaciated Driftless Area. It has more caves than any other Iowa state park, plus limestone arches and chimneys, linked by a trail system with overlooks. Dancehall Cave and a natural bridge are among the best known, and part of the park is a National Register historic district.

hikingTrails.name: Caves Loop
hikingTrails.description: A wooded, shaded trail that briefly meanders alongside Raccoon Creek.

iowa.campingInfo: The park has a newly upgraded campground among pine trees plus primitive hike-in sites; all sites require a reservation, which is accepted March through November, and the campground is closed December through February.
iowa.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Maquoketa Caves State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

iowa.hours: Iowa state parks open 4 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. daily. Caves are closed Nov 15 to Apr 1. The visitor center is typically open 9 am to 5 pm Sat–Sun, Memorial Day through Labor Day.
iowa.entranceFees: Check the official park website for current fees.
iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through fall, between April and mid-November, when the caves are open; summer weekends also offer the interpretive center and nature programs.
tips: Status as of Oct 2026: closed for the season Oct 19, 2026 – Apr 15, 2027 (DNR alert). Check the official page before going.
Bring hiking shoes and a flashlight for exploring the caves.
The trails are not accessible because of steep inclines, rocky terrain and staircases.
Check Park Alerts before you go. The caves close every year from Nov 15 to Apr 1 for hibernating bats.

iowa.name: Pikes Peak State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Perched high above the confluence of the Mississippi and Wisconsin Rivers, Pikes Peak State Park offers some of the most spectacular views in the Midwest.
iowa.fullDescription: Pikes Peak State Park is renowned for its 500-foot bluffs overlooking the Mississippi River. The park features ancient Native American burial mounds, fossil-rich limestone formations, and lush hardwood forests. It serves as a premier destination for bird watching, photography, and exploring the unique geological history of the Driftless Area.

hikingTrails.name: Bridal Veil Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible boardwalk trail that leads to a beautiful waterfall and lush fern-covered cliffs.

hikingTrails.name: Point Ann Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through dense forest and offers elevated vantage points of the Mississippi River valley.

iowa.campingInfo: The park offers 77 campsites, including 60 with electrical hookups, modern restrooms, showers, and a dump station.
iowa.fishingBoating: Fishing is available along the Mississippi River shoreline; however, there is no boat ramp located directly within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Pikes Peak State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interpretive displays about the geology, history, and wildlife of the Mississippi River valley.

iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for fall foliage or spring for eagle migration.
tips: Visit the overlook early in the morning to avoid crowds and catch the best light for photography.
Bring binoculars as the park is a prime location for spotting bald eagles.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as some trails can be steep and rocky.

iowa.name: Mines of Spain State Recreation Area
iowa.shortDescription: A stunning 1,437-acre recreation area located along the Mississippi River, featuring rugged bluffs, diverse forests, and rich historical significance.
iowa.fullDescription: The Mines of Spain State Recreation Area is a National Historic Landmark that offers a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural history. Once the site of Julien Dubuque's lead mining operations in the late 18th century, the park now preserves diverse ecosystems including prairies, woodlands, and limestone bluffs. Visitors can explore the E.B. Lyons Interpretive Center to learn about the area's geology, flora, and the legacy of the Meskwaki people and early European settlers.
thingsToDo: Educational programs at the interpretive center

hikingTrails.name: Catfish Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the creek, offering beautiful views of the water and surrounding forest canopy.

hikingTrails.name: Julien Dubuque Monument Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading to the historic monument dedicated to the founder of Dubuque, providing panoramic views of the Mississippi River.

iowa.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within the Mines of Spain State Recreation Area; however, several private campgrounds are located in the nearby Dubuque area.
iowa.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the banks of the Mississippi River and Catfish Creek; however, there are no boat ramps located within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: E.B. Lyons Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's natural history, geology, and the history of lead mining in the region.
visitorCenter.hours: Monday-Friday: 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM, Saturday-Sunday: 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM

iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities along the river bluffs.
Check the interpretive center schedule for guided nature walks and historical talks.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as some trails feature steep, rocky terrain.

iowa.name: Bellevue State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Perched high above the Mississippi River, Bellevue State Park offers breathtaking panoramic views and unique limestone bluffs.
iowa.fullDescription: Bellevue State Park is divided into two distinct areas: the Nelson Unit and the Dyas Unit. The park is renowned for its dramatic limestone bluffs that rise 300 feet above the Mississippi River, providing some of the most spectacular vistas in Iowa. The area is rich in geological history, featuring ancient rock formations and diverse ecosystems including hardwood forests and prairie remnants.

hikingTrails.name: Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the edge of the limestone bluffs, offering stunning views of the Mississippi River valley.

hikingTrails.name: Forest Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through mature hardwood forests, perfect for spotting local songbirds and wildflowers.

iowa.campingInfo: The park offers 46 campsites, many with electrical hookups, along with modern restrooms and shower facilities. Reservations are recommended during peak summer months.
iowa.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the Mississippi River nearby, though the park itself is primarily focused on hiking and nature observation.

visitorCenter.name: Bellevue State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational displays about the local ecosystem.

iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities along the river.
Visit the Butterfly Garden during mid-summer for the best floral displays.
Check the official DNR website for seasonal trail closures due to weather.

iowa.name: Waubonsie State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Waubonsie State Park offers breathtaking views of the Loess Hills and the Missouri River valley, featuring unique geological formations and diverse ecosystems.
iowa.fullDescription: Located in the southwest corner of Iowa, Waubonsie State Park is renowned for its dramatic Loess Hills landscape. These unique wind-deposited silt formations create a rugged, rolling terrain that is unlike anywhere else in the state. The park is rich in history, serving as a significant site for Native American tribes and later as a landmark for pioneers traveling westward. Visitors can explore a variety of habitats, including native prairies, oak-hickory forests, and deep ravines that provide a sanctuary for diverse wildlife.
thingsToDo: Hiking the scenic Loess Hills trails
Horseback riding on designated equestrian trails
Picnicking in the shaded woodland areas
Camping in the scenic ridge-top sites

hikingTrails.name: Sunset Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the ridge line, offering panoramic views of the Missouri River valley and spectacular sunset vistas.

hikingTrails.name: Waubonsie Trail
hikingTrails.description: A winding path that takes hikers through dense forests and deep ravines, showcasing the unique geology of the Loess Hills.

iowa.campingInfo: The park features both modern and non-electric campsites, as well as equestrian camping facilities with stalls available for rent.
iowa.fishingBoating: Small ponds are available for fishing, though the park is primarily focused on hiking and equestrian activities.

visitorCenter.name: Waubonsie Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, trail information, and assistance with camping reservations.

iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for the vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Bring binoculars to take full advantage of the bird watching opportunities.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the Loess Hills terrain can be steep and uneven.
Check the official website for trail closures during wet weather to protect the fragile soil.
nearbyAttractions: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail

iowa.name: Lake Macbride State Park
iowa.shortDescription: Lake Macbride State Park is a premier outdoor destination in Iowa, offering expansive water recreation and scenic woodland trails.
iowa.fullDescription: Located near Solon, Lake Macbride State Park features a massive 812-acre lake that serves as the centerpiece for water-based recreation in the region. The park is characterized by its rolling hills, diverse hardwood forests, and abundant wildlife. It was developed in the 1930s and has since become a vital hub for boating, fishing, and hiking, providing a peaceful escape for visitors looking to enjoy Iowa's natural landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Macbride Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the shoreline, offering beautiful views of the lake and surrounding forest.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through mature hardwood trees, perfect for families and bird enthusiasts.

iowa.campingInfo: The park offers two modern campgrounds with electrical hookups, shower facilities, and flush toilets, as well as several non-electric sites.
iowa.fishingBoating: The lake features multiple boat ramps and a full-service marina offering boat rentals, including pontoons and kayaks.

visitorCenter.name: Lake Macbride Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, camping reservations, and local wildlife education.

iowa.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water activities and foliage.
tips: Visit during the week to avoid heavy weekend crowds at the beach.
Bring binoculars as the park is a fantastic spot for birdwatching.
Check the Iowa DNR website for current water quality alerts before swimming.
nearbyAttractions: University of Iowa Museum of Natural History

kansas.name: Kanopolis State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Kansas' first state park, Kanopolis offers rugged sandstone bluffs, rolling hills, and the expansive Kanopolis Reservoir.
kansas.fullDescription: Established in 1955, Kanopolis State Park is located in the Smoky Hills region of Kansas. The park surrounds the 3,500-acre Kanopolis Reservoir, which was the first federal reservoir in Kansas. The landscape is defined by dramatic sandstone canyons, prairie grasslands, and diverse wildlife habitats, making it a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts interested in geology and history.
thingsToDo: Horseback riding on designated equestrian paths

hikingTrails.name: Horsethief Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through sandstone canyons and offers panoramic views of the reservoir.

hikingTrails.name: Buffalo Track Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses through unique geological formations and provides excellent opportunities for bird watching.

kansas.campingInfo: The park features over 200 primitive and utility campsites, including sites with water and electric hookups. Several cabins are available for rent year-round.
kansas.fishingBoating: The reservoir features multiple boat ramps and is highly regarded for its walleye, wiper, and channel catfish populations.

visitorCenter.name: Kanopolis State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping reservations and permits.

kansas.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
kansas.entranceFees: $5.00 daily vehicle permit required for all motor vehicles.
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and migratory bird sightings.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the trails can be exposed to direct sun.
Check the official website for current lake levels before planning water activities.
The park is popular on weekends, so arrive early to secure a prime spot.

kansas.name: Wilson State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Nestled in the Smoky Hills, Wilson State Park offers stunning views of Wilson Reservoir and rugged sandstone bluffs.
kansas.fullDescription: Wilson State Park is widely considered the most beautiful state park in Kansas. Located on the shores of Wilson Reservoir, the park features dramatic sandstone formations, rolling hills, and diverse ecosystems. It is a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts, offering world-class fishing, boating, and mountain biking trails that wind through the unique landscape of the Smoky Hills region.
thingsToDo: Fishing for striped bass and walleye
Mountain biking on the Switchgrass Trail

hikingTrails.name: Switchgrass Trail
hikingTrails.description: A nationally recognized mountain biking and hiking trail that traverses rugged terrain and offers panoramic views of the reservoir.

hikingTrails.name: Cedar Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic, shorter loop trail perfect for families that winds through cedar groves and provides access to the shoreline.

kansas.campingInfo: The park offers over 100 utility campsites with water and electricity, as well as numerous primitive camping sites. Reservations are highly recommended during peak season.
kansas.fishingBoating: Wilson Reservoir is famous for its striped bass, walleye, and channel catfish. Multiple boat ramps are available throughout the park.

visitorCenter.name: Wilson State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, fishing regulations, and park permits.

kansas.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
kansas.entranceFees: $5.00 daily vehicle permit required for all motor vehicles.
kansas.address: 3 State Park Rd, Sylvan Grove, KS 67481
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal bird migration viewing.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the trails can be exposed to direct sun.
Check the official website for current lake levels and boat ramp status.
The Switchgrass Trail is popular with mountain bikers, so hikers should stay alert.

kansas.name: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park features 332 acres of spectacular Niobrara Chalk formations in Logan County, Kansas.
kansas.fullDescription: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park is Kansas' newest state park, showcasing a massive expanse of Niobrara Chalk formations that date back to the Cretaceous period. The park offers visitors a unique opportunity to explore towering spires and deep canyons that were once part of an ancient inland sea. Managed in partnership with The Nature Conservancy, the park emphasizes conservation while providing accessible trails for public enjoyment.

hikingTrails.name: Life on the Rocks Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the heart of the chalk formations, offering close-up views of the unique geological structures.

hikingTrails.name: Rim Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path along the upper rim that provides panoramic views of the badlands and the surrounding prairie landscape.

kansas.campingInfo: There is no camping allowed within the boundaries of Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park to protect the fragile ecosystem.
kansas.fishingBoating: Not applicable; there are no bodies of water suitable for fishing or boating within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Little Jerusalem Information Kiosk
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, safety information, and educational displays about the geology and history of the chalk formations.

kansas.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal hiking conditions.
tips: Stay on marked trails at all times to protect the fragile chalk formations.
Bring plenty of water and sun protection as there is very little shade in the park.
Check the official website for potential closures due to wet weather, as the chalk becomes slippery and unstable.

kansas.name: Mushroom Rock State Park
kansas.shortDescription: One of the smallest state parks in Kansas, featuring unique, giant mushroom-shaped rock formations.
kansas.fullDescription: Mushroom Rock State Park is a 5-acre park located in Ellsworth County, Kansas. It is famous for its large, mushroom-shaped sandstone formations that were once part of the Dakota Formation. These unique geological structures were created by erosion, leaving behind harder rock caps atop softer pedestals. The park offers a glimpse into the prehistoric landscape of the Great Plains and is a popular spot for photography and geology enthusiasts.

hikingTrails.name: Mushroom Rock Loop
hikingTrails.description: A short, flat trail that winds around the primary rock formations, perfect for families and casual walkers.

hikingTrails.name: Pioneer Trail
hikingTrails.description: A level, interpretive trail outlining the geological history of the unique Dakota sandstone formations.

kansas.campingInfo: There is no camping available at Mushroom Rock State Park. The park is strictly for day-use only.
kansas.fishingBoating: There is no water access or fishing available at this park.

visitorCenter.name: Kanopolis State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Mushroom Rock is managed by the staff at Kanopolis State Park, who provide information and maintenance for the site.

kansas.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal lighting for photography.
tips: Bring a camera as the rock formations are highly photogenic.
The park is very small, so plan for a 30-60 minute visit.
There is no drinking water on-site, so bring your own supplies.

kansas.name: Lake Scott State Park
kansas.shortDescription: An oasis in the high plains of western Kansas, Lake Scott State Park features dramatic canyons, natural springs, and rich historical significance.
kansas.fullDescription: Lake Scott State Park is a unique geological and historical treasure located in western Kansas. The park is situated in a canyon carved by Ladder Creek, providing a stark contrast to the surrounding flat prairie landscape. It is home to the El Cuartejo Pueblo, the northernmost Indian pueblo in the United States, and served as a hideout for the legendary outlaw Dick Yeager. The park's diverse ecosystem includes limestone bluffs, wooded canyons, and a 100-acre spring-fed lake.
thingsToDo: Fishing and boating on the 100-acre lake
Exploring the historic El Cuartejo Pueblo ruins
Swimming at the designated beach area

hikingTrails.name: Lake Scott Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the wooded areas near the lake, offering excellent opportunities to spot local flora and fauna.

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers along the limestone bluffs, providing panoramic views of the canyon and the surrounding prairie.

kansas.campingInfo: The park offers 55 utility campsites with water and electricity, as well as numerous primitive camping sites. Reservations are recommended during peak summer months.
kansas.fishingBoating: The lake is well-stocked with bass, bluegill, crappie, and channel catfish. Boat ramps are available for public use.

visitorCenter.name: Lake Scott State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and fishing permits.

kansas.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
kansas.entranceFees: $5.00 daily vehicle permit required for all visitors.
kansas.address: 101 W Scott Lake Dr, Scott City, KS 67871
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and migratory bird sightings.
tips: Bring binoculars for bird watching as the park is a major stop for migratory species.
Visit the El Cuartejo Pueblo ruins early in the morning to avoid the midday heat.
Check the official website for current fire bans before planning a campfire.

kansas.name: Clinton State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Clinton Reservoir, this park offers extensive outdoor recreation including boating, fishing, and miles of scenic trails.
kansas.fullDescription: Clinton State Park is situated on the north shore of the 7,000-acre Clinton Reservoir in Douglas County, Kansas. Established in the 1970s, the park provides a diverse landscape of rolling hills, tallgrass prairie, and hardwood forests. It serves as a premier destination for water sports enthusiasts and hikers alike, featuring a complex trail system that winds through varied terrain and offers stunning views of the lake.

hikingTrails.name: North Shore Trails
hikingTrails.description: A series of interconnected loops that wind through dense forests and offer challenging terrain for hikers and mountain bikers.

hikingTrails.name: Prairie Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through native tallgrass prairie, perfect for observing local wildflowers and bird species.

kansas.campingInfo: The park features over 200 utility campsites with water and electricity, as well as numerous primitive camping sites and several reservable cabins.
kansas.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat ramps and a full-service marina nearby. Fishing is excellent for walleye, crappie, channel catfish, and white bass.

visitorCenter.name: Clinton State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, camping permits, and local trail maps.

kansas.hours: 24 hours daily
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and migratory bird sightings.
tips: Purchase a Kansas State Park vehicle permit online before arrival to save time.
Check the water levels of the reservoir before planning a boating trip.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the summer months when hiking the wooded trails.
nearbyAttractions: University of Kansas Natural History Museum

kansas.name: Tuttle Creek State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Located in the scenic Flint Hills, Tuttle Creek State Park offers expansive water recreation and diverse outdoor activities near Manhattan, Kansas.
kansas.fullDescription: Tuttle Creek State Park is situated on the shores of the 12,500-acre Tuttle Creek Reservoir. The park is divided into several units, including the River Pond, Fancy Creek, and Randolph areas, providing a variety of landscapes from wooded valleys to open prairie. It serves as a premier destination for boating, fishing, and equestrian activities, reflecting the natural beauty of the Kansas Flint Hills.

hikingTrails.name: Fancy Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A rugged trail that winds through limestone bluffs and offers panoramic views of the reservoir.

hikingTrails.name: River Pond Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic path perfect for birdwatching and observing local flora near the water.

kansas.campingInfo: The park features over 100 utility campsites with water and electricity, as well as numerous primitive camping areas and several rental cabins available for reservation.
kansas.fishingBoating: The reservoir is a popular destination for anglers targeting crappie, saugeye, and catfish; multiple boat ramps are available throughout the park units.

visitorCenter.name: Tuttle Creek State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The office provides park permits, camping registration, and information on local trail conditions and fishing regulations.

kansas.hours: Open 24 hours daily for registered campers; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
kansas.entranceFees: $5.00 daily vehicle permit required for all motor vehicles entering the park.
kansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal bird migration viewing.
tips: Check the official website for current water levels before planning boating activities.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months, especially when hiking near wooded areas.
Make camping reservations well in advance for holiday weekends as sites fill up quickly.

kansas.name: Milford State Park
kansas.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Kansas' largest lake, Milford State Park offers expansive water recreation and diverse wildlife habitats.
kansas.fullDescription: Milford State Park is situated on the shores of the 15,730-acre Milford Reservoir. The park features a diverse landscape of rolling hills, tallgrass prairie, and wooded areas. It serves as a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts, offering extensive opportunities for boating, fishing, and wildlife viewing. The area is rich in history and provides a scenic escape for those looking to enjoy the natural beauty of the Flint Hills region.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through wooded areas and offers beautiful views of the reservoir.

hikingTrails.name: Prairie View Trail
hikingTrails.description: An accessible path through native tallgrass prairie, perfect for birdwatching and spotting local flora.

kansas.campingInfo: The park offers over 100 utility campsites with water and electricity, as well as numerous primitive camping sites. Reservations are recommended during peak season.
kansas.fishingBoating: Milford Reservoir is renowned for its excellent fishing, particularly for walleye, channel catfish, and smallmouth bass. Multiple boat ramps are available throughout the park.

visitorCenter.name: Milford State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, camping permits, and local wildlife educational materials.

kansas.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
tips: Check the water levels before planning a boating trip.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months.
Visit during the winter for excellent bald eagle viewing opportunities.

michigan.name: Tahquamenon Falls State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Upper Peninsula park on the Tahquamenon River, known for its 50-foot Upper Falls and the cascading Lower Falls.
michigan.fullDescription: Tahquamenon Falls State Park covers 46,179 acres near Paradise and is Michigan's second-largest state park. The Tahquamenon River drops 50 feet at the Upper Falls, then runs through the rapids and cascades of the Lower Falls before reaching Lake Superior's Whitefish Bay. A paved path leads to the Upper Falls, and rowboats can be rented to reach the Lower Falls.

hikingTrails.name: North Country Trail
hikingTrails.description: The North Country Trail runs 16 miles within the park, including a route between the Upper and Lower Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Giant Pines Loop
hikingTrails.description: Part of the park's hiking trail system in the Upper Falls area, this loop is groomed for cross-country skiing in winter.

hikingTrails.name: Lantern Loop
hikingTrails.description: A short loop in the Upper Falls area that is part of the hiking trail system and is groomed for cross-country skiing in winter.

michigan.campingInfo: The park has the 188-site Lower Falls Modern Campground (Hemlock loop open year-round), the 72-site Rivermouth Modern Campground and the Rivermouth Rustic Campground; reserve at 800-447-2757 or online.
michigan.fishingBoating: Anglers on the Tahquamenon River catch brown trout, walleye, muskie, northern pike, yellow perch and smallmouth bass; there is an accessible paved boat launch near Rivermouth Campground, and rowboats can be rented at the Lower Falls from Memorial Day weekend to mid-October as conditions allow.

visitorCenter.name: Tahquamenon Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

michigan.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
michigan.entranceFees: Recreation Passport required for vehicles: $15 for Michigan plates (annual); non-Michigan vehicles $12 daily or $42 annual
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring runoff brings the Upper Falls to peak volume, summer through mid-October offers shuttle service and rowboat rentals, and winter draws visitors to see colored ice at the falls and ski or snowshoe the groomed and marked trails.
tips: Hunter Shuttle Service runs a fee-based shuttle between the Upper and Lower Falls from noon to 8 p.m., on weekends through June 21 and daily June 22 through Labor Day; book online or call or text 906-291-3422.
Drones are permitted with restrictions but are prohibited on or above the viewing platforms.
Parking is limited at the Rivermouth boat launch, and pets must stay on a 6-foot leash on all trails and viewing platforms.

michigan.name: Ludington State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Lake Michigan park between the big lake and Hamlin Lake, home to the 1876 Big Sable Point Lighthouse.
michigan.fullDescription: Ludington State Park covers 4,800 acres two miles north of Ludington, between Lake Michigan and Hamlin Lake, crossed by the Big Sable River. It is home to the 112-foot Big Sable Point Lighthouse from 1876. The park has 21.5 miles of hiking trails, ski and canoe trails, and four campgrounds with 360 sites.

hikingTrails.name: Lighthouse Path
hikingTrails.description: This sand-and-gravel path, open to hikers and bikers, leads 1.8 miles one-way to the Big Sable Point Lighthouse and has little shade.

hikingTrails.name: Lost Lake-Island Trail loop
hikingTrails.description: This very popular loop connects to the loops of the Beechwood Modern Campground near Hamlin Lake.

michigan.campingInfo: The park has three campgrounds, including the 147-site Beechwood Modern Campground near Hamlin Lake, plus mini cabins, all reservable at 800-447-2757 or online.
michigan.fishingBoating: Anglers can fish spring and fall runs of salmon, lake trout, steelhead and brown trout along the Lake Michigan shoreline and in the Big Sable River, and a boating access site with trailer parking serves Hamlin Lake.

visitorCenter.name: Ludington State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

michigan.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
michigan.entranceFees: Recreation Passport required for vehicles: $15 for Michigan plates (annual); non-Michigan vehicles $12 daily or $42 annual
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is best for the Lake Michigan and Hamlin Lake beaches and paddling, while spring and fall bring the salmon and trout runs, and lighthouse tours run May through October.
tips: The Skyline Trail, all intersecting trails, and the park amphitheater and its access road are closed for reconstruction through mid-2027.
Most of the Lake Michigan shoreline is closed to pets to protect piping plover habitat. Use the pet-friendly beach between the beach house and the Big Sable River, with pets on a 6-foot leash.
The Lighthouse Path offers little shade and can be challenging in warm weather, so plan accordingly. Large vehicles are not recommended on Piney Ridge Road.
nearbyAttractions: Ludington's North Breakwater Light at Stearns Park Beach

michigan.name: Holland State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Michigan's most visited state park: Lake Michigan beach and dunes by the Holland Harbor Light, 'Big Red'.
michigan.fullDescription: Holland State Park covers 142 acres west of Holland, with units on Lake Michigan and Lake Macatawa beside the channel joining them. It draws 1.5 to 2 million visitors a year to its sandy beach, dunes and views of the Holland Harbor Light, known as Big Red. Each unit has a campground; the Lake Macatawa unit also has a boat launch.

hikingTrails.name: Lakeshore Trail
hikingTrails.description: A paved route that parallels Lakeshore Drive and runs continuously from Grand Haven State Park to Holland State Park.

michigan.campingInfo: The park has two modern campgrounds, Holland Modern Beach Campground (98 paved sites) and Lake Macatawa Campground (211 sites), plus two camper cabins, all reservable at 800-447-2757 or online.
michigan.fishingBoating: Fishing is popular along the channel walkway on Lake Michigan and Ottawa County's boardwalk on Lake Macatawa, and while there is no boat launch in the park, the Lake Macatawa boating access site with a fish cleaning station is 1 mile east on Ottawa Beach Road.

visitorCenter.name: Holland State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

michigan.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
michigan.entranceFees: Recreation Passport required for vehicles: $15 for Michigan plates (annual); non-Michigan vehicles $12 daily or $42 annual
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is the best time to enjoy the park's sugar sand beaches, buoyed swim areas, seasonal naturalist programs and sunsets over Lake Michigan by the "Big Red" lighthouse.
tips: The Woodstock loop of the Lake Macatawa Campground (sites 117-211) will be closed for the majority of the 2027 season for construction of a new toilet and shower building, but sites 1-116 will be open.
Watch the beach flag warning system. Red flags mean the water is unsafe and no one should swim in or enter the water.
Alcohol is prohibited anywhere in the park, and pets are allowed only at the designated dog beach along Lake Macatawa on a 6-foot leash.

michigan.name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Michigan's largest state park, the Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park encompasses 60,000 acres of old-growth forest, rugged mountains, and stunning Lake Superior shoreline.
michigan.fullDescription: Known locally as the 'Porkies,' this park is one of the few remaining large wilderness areas in the Midwest. It features towering virgin timber, secluded waterfalls, and the dramatic Escarpment trail overlooking the Lake of the Clouds. The park's geology is defined by ancient volcanic activity and glacial carving, creating a rugged landscape that offers a true backcountry experience.

hikingTrails.name: Escarpment Trail
hikingTrails.description: This iconic trail offers breathtaking panoramic views of the Lake of the Clouds and the Carp River valley from high cliff ridges.

hikingTrails.name: Presque Isle River Waterfalls Loop
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that follows the river, showcasing several spectacular waterfalls and unique rock formations carved by the rushing water.

michigan.campingInfo: The park offers modern campgrounds at Union Bay, rustic cabins, yurts, and extensive backcountry campsites accessible only by hiking.
michigan.fishingBoating: Excellent trout fishing in the Presque Isle and Carp rivers; non-motorized boating is permitted on inland lakes.

visitorCenter.name: Porcupine Mountains Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits on the park's natural history, geology, and local mining heritage, along with ranger assistance.

michigan.hours: Open 24 hours daily for recreational use
michigan.entranceFees: Requires a Michigan Recreation Passport for vehicle entry.
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to early October for peak fall foliage or July for warm hiking weather.
tips: Always carry bear spray and practice proper food storage when backpacking.
Check the weather frequently as conditions near Lake Superior can change rapidly.
Visit the Lake of the Clouds overlook early in the morning to avoid large crowds.

michigan.name: Mackinac Island State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Established in 1895, Mackinac Island State Park covers over 80 percent of the island and offers breathtaking views of Lake Huron and historic geological formations.
michigan.fullDescription: Mackinac Island State Park was the second national park in the United States, established in 1875, before being transferred to the state of Michigan in 1895. The park is renowned for its unique limestone rock formations, such as Arch Rock, and its strict prohibition of motor vehicles, preserving a turn-of-the-century atmosphere. Visitors can explore dense forests, high bluffs, and miles of trails that showcase the island's rich geological history and strategic military importance during the 18th and 19th centuries.

hikingTrails.name: Arch Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading to the iconic limestone arch overlooking the turquoise waters of Lake Huron.

hikingTrails.name: Sugar Loaf Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the interior of the island, bringing hikers to the base of the massive 75-foot tall Sugar Loaf rock formation.

michigan.campingInfo: Camping is not permitted within the boundaries of Mackinac Island State Park; visitors typically stay at the island's historic hotels, bed and breakfasts, or private cottages.
michigan.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted from the shoreline in designated areas; no boat ramps are available within the park, but public marinas are located in the harbor.

visitorCenter.name: Mackinac Island State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, historical information, and guidance on park regulations and trail conditions.

michigan.entranceFees: Free entrance to the state park grounds; fees apply for specific historic sites like Fort Mackinac.
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for pleasant weather and full access to all island amenities.
tips: Rent a bicycle upon arrival to easily navigate the island's extensive trail system.
Pack comfortable walking shoes as the island is best explored on foot or by bike.
Visit during the shoulder seasons of May or September to avoid the peak summer crowds.

michigan.name: Warren Dunes State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Warren Dunes State Park features massive sand dunes rising 260 feet above the shores of Lake Michigan, offering spectacular views and expansive sandy beaches.
michigan.fullDescription: Located along the eastern shore of Lake Michigan, Warren Dunes State Park encompasses over 1,900 acres of diverse landscape. The park is famous for its towering sand dunes, including Tower Hill, which provides a challenging climb and panoramic vistas of the lake. The area was shaped by glacial activity and wind patterns, creating a unique ecosystem that supports rare plants and wildlife. Visitors can explore miles of hiking trails, swim in the refreshing waters of Lake Michigan, or enjoy hang gliding from the designated dunes.

hikingTrails.name: Tower Hill Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb up the park's most famous dune, offering unparalleled views of the Lake Michigan shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Blue Jay Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the wooded areas behind the dunes, providing a quieter experience away from the beach.

michigan.campingInfo: The park offers 185 modern campsites with electrical hookups, as well as a rustic group camping area. Reservations are highly recommended during the summer months.
michigan.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Lake Michigan shoreline, though there are no boat ramps located directly within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Warren Dunes State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, park rules, and educational materials about the dune ecosystem.

michigan.entranceFees: Requires a Michigan Recreation Passport for entry.
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities, or autumn for fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring plenty of water and wear sturdy footwear if you plan to climb the dunes.
Check the Michigan DNR website for current beach safety and water quality alerts.

michigan.name: Saugatuck Dunes State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Saugatuck Dunes State Park features 1,000 acres of rugged landscape, including 2.5 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline and towering sand dunes.
michigan.fullDescription: Located between Saugatuck and Holland, this park offers a unique natural experience with dunes reaching heights of over 200 feet. The area is characterized by its diverse topography, including sandy beaches, forested dunes, and interdunal wetlands. It is a popular destination for hikers and nature enthusiasts looking to explore the pristine, undeveloped coastline of Lake Michigan.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Trail
