hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that winds through the dunes and leads directly to the sandy shores of Lake Michigan.

hikingTrails.name: Living Dunes Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers an immersive experience through the shifting sand dunes and mature hardwood forests.

michigan.campingInfo: There is no modern campground at Saugatuck Dunes State Park; however, the park is located near several private campgrounds in the Saugatuck and Holland area.
michigan.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Lake Michigan shoreline, though there are no boat launches located within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Saugatuck Dunes State Park Entrance Station
visitorCenter.info: The entrance station provides park information, trail maps, and parking permits for visitors.

michigan.entranceFees: A Michigan Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry.
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking and beach activities.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking shoes as the sand can be challenging to walk on.
Bring plenty of water, as there are no water stations along the trails.
Visit during the weekday to avoid heavy weekend crowds at the beach.

michigan.name: Wilderness State Park
michigan.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Lake Michigan, this park offers over 10,000 acres of pristine wilderness, sandy beaches, and dense forests.
michigan.fullDescription: Wilderness State Park features over 26 miles of beautiful Lake Michigan shoreline. The park is characterized by its diverse landscape, including conifer swamps, hardwood forests, and expansive dunes. It is a premier destination for stargazing, as it is designated as an International Dark Sky Park, offering unparalleled views of the night sky.

hikingTrails.name: Red Pine Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through a beautiful stand of red pine trees, perfect for a quick nature walk.

hikingTrails.name: Nebwaw Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers scenic views of the shoreline and traverses through diverse forest ecosystems.

michigan.campingInfo: The park offers several campgrounds including the Lakeshore Campground and the Pines Campground, featuring both modern and rustic sites, as well as several rustic cabins available for rent.
michigan.fishingBoating: The park offers excellent fishing opportunities for smallmouth bass and perch along the Lake Michigan shoreline, with boat launch access available nearby.

visitorCenter.name: Wilderness State Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping reservations.

michigan.entranceFees: Requires a Michigan Recreation Passport for vehicle entry.
michigan.address: 903 Wilderness Park Dr, Carp Lake, MI 49718
michigan.bestTimeToVisit: Summer for swimming and beach activities, or autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Bring bug spray during the summer months as the wooded areas can have mosquitoes.
Visit the beach at night for some of the best stargazing in the Midwest.
Check the Michigan DNR website for seasonal road closures before visiting in winter.

minnesota.name: Tettegouche State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Experience the rugged beauty of the North Shore with dramatic cliffs, cascading waterfalls, and the iconic suspension bridge over the Baptism River.
minnesota.fullDescription: Tettegouche State Park is a premier destination on Minnesota's North Shore of Lake Superior. Established in 1979, the park features the spectacular High Falls of the Baptism River, the highest waterfall entirely within Minnesota. The landscape is defined by ancient volcanic rock formations, dense hardwood forests, and miles of rugged shoreline. Visitors can explore the park's rich history, including the Tettegouche Camp, which was once a private retreat for wealthy industrialists in the early 20th century.
thingsToDo: Bird watching for raptors and songbirds
Photography of the Baptism River waterfalls

hikingTrails.name: Shovel Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: A stunning trail that leads to the edge of massive basalt cliffs overlooking Lake Superior with panoramic views.

hikingTrails.name: High Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A well-maintained path that takes hikers through a beautiful forest to the base of the majestic High Falls.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park offers 28 drive-in campsites, 22 cart-in sites, and several rustic camper cabins available for reservation year-round.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is popular in the Baptism River for trout and along the Lake Superior shoreline; no boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Tettegouche Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the geology, history, and ecology of the North Shore, along with a gift shop and information desk.

minnesota.hours: Park grounds open daily from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM
minnesota.entranceFees: Daily vehicle permit is $7.00 or an annual state park permit is $35.00.
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to early October for spectacular fall foliage colors.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails can be rocky and uneven.
Check the park website for seasonal trail closures due to mud or ice.
Bring binoculars for spotting raptors near the cliff edges.
nearbyAttractions: George H. Crosby Manitou State Park

minnesota.name: Itasca State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Home to the headwaters of the Mississippi River, Itasca State Park is Minnesota's oldest state park and a premier destination for nature lovers.
minnesota.fullDescription: Established in 1891, Itasca State Park encompasses over 32,000 acres of pristine wilderness, including the iconic headwaters where the Mississippi River begins its 2,552-mile journey to the Gulf of Mexico. The park features a diverse landscape of towering old-growth red and white pines, glacial lakes, and abundant wildlife, offering a glimpse into the Minnesota landscape as it appeared before European settlement.
thingsToDo: Wade across the Mississippi River headwaters
Take a guided boat tour on Lake Itasca
Visit the Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center

hikingTrails.name: Headwaters Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading directly to the Mississippi River headwaters marker.

hikingTrails.name: Preacher's Grove Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic walk through a grove of majestic, centuries-old red pines.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park offers several campgrounds including Bear Paw, Pine Ridge, and Douglas Lodge, featuring over 200 sites with electric hookups, showers, and seasonal availability.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Lake Itasca offers excellent fishing for walleye, northern pike, and panfish; boat rentals are available at the Headwaters Marina.

visitorCenter.name: Jacob V. Brower Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the park's history, geology, and the Mississippi River, along with a gift shop and information desk.

minnesota.hours: Park grounds open daily 8:00 AM - 10:00 PM
minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit
minnesota.address: 36750 Main Park Drive, Park Rapids, MN 56470
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking and water activities, or winter for snow sports.
tips: Bring water shoes if you plan to wade across the Mississippi headwaters.
Visit during the week to avoid heavy crowds at the headwaters area.
Check the DNR website for seasonal road closures on the Wilderness Drive.

minnesota.name: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Perched on the rugged North Shore of Lake Superior, this iconic park features a historic 1910 lighthouse and dramatic cliffside views.
minnesota.fullDescription: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park is one of Minnesota's most scenic destinations, famous for its historic lighthouse built in 1910 following a devastating 1905 storm. The park offers miles of hiking trails that wind through birch and aspen forests, leading to rocky beaches and breathtaking vistas of the world's largest freshwater lake. The geology is defined by ancient volcanic basalt flows, creating the rugged shoreline that makes this area a photographer's paradise.
thingsToDo: Tour the historic lighthouse and fog signal building
Hiking along the Superior Hiking Trail
Picnicking on the rocky Lake Superior shoreline
Photography of the iconic lighthouse silhouette

hikingTrails.name: Corundum Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the shoreline, offering excellent views of the lake and access to rocky beaches.

hikingTrails.name: Day Hill Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads to a high overlook providing a panoramic view of the lighthouse and the vast expanse of Lake Superior.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park features 20 cart-in campsites located near the shore, providing a unique, semi-primitive camping experience with stunning lake views.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Lake Superior; however, there is no boat launch within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Split Rock Lighthouse Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Managed by the Minnesota Historical Society, the center features exhibits on the history of the lighthouse, the 1905 storm, and maritime life.

minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit.
minnesota.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd, Two Harbors, MN 55616
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late summer and early autumn for fall foliage and pleasant temperatures.
tips: Bring sturdy hiking boots as the terrain is rocky and uneven.
Check the weather forecast frequently, as North Shore conditions change rapidly.
Visit during the golden hour for the best photography opportunities of the lighthouse.

minnesota.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Known as the gateway to the North Shore, Gooseberry Falls State Park features spectacular waterfalls, river gorges, and stunning Lake Superior views.
minnesota.fullDescription: Established in 1937, Gooseberry Falls State Park is a crown jewel of the Minnesota state park system. The park is defined by the Gooseberry River, which cascades over a series of dramatic waterfalls and through a deep, rocky gorge before emptying into Lake Superior. The area is rich in Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) history, with many stone structures and buildings still standing today. Geologically, the park showcases ancient lava flows that formed the rugged basalt cliffs characteristic of the North Shore.

hikingTrails.name: Fifth Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers past the upper and lower falls and into the quieter, forested sections of the river.

hikingTrails.name: River View Trail
hikingTrails.description: An accessible path that provides excellent vantage points of the main falls and the river gorge.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park offers 70 drive-in campsites, many with electrical hookups, and several cart-in sites for a more secluded experience.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Gooseberry River for trout, though boating is not allowed on the river due to the falls and rapids.

visitorCenter.name: Gateway Memorial Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interpretive displays on the park's geology, history, and local wildlife, along with a gift shop and information desk.

minnesota.entranceFees: A valid Minnesota State Park vehicle permit is required ($7 daily or $35 annual).
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for peak waterfall flow or autumn for spectacular fall foliage.
tips: Visit early in the morning or on weekdays to avoid heavy crowds at the main falls.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the rocks near the river can be slippery.
Check the park website for seasonal trail closures due to ice or mud.

minnesota.name: Interstate State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Located along the scenic St. Croix River, Interstate State Park is famous for its dramatic basalt rock formations and deep glacial potholes.
minnesota.fullDescription: Interstate State Park, established in 1895, is the oldest state park in Minnesota. It is renowned for the Dalles of the St. Croix, a deep gorge carved by glacial meltwater that features some of the deepest potholes in the world. The park offers a unique look into geological history with its exposed volcanic basalt flows and diverse riverine ecosystem.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking the St. Croix River

hikingTrails.name: River Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the edge of the St. Croix River, offering stunning views of the gorge and the unique rock formations.

hikingTrails.name: Pothole Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, interpretive trail that leads visitors through the park's most famous collection of glacial potholes.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park features 37 drive-in campsites, many with electrical hookups, and several walk-in sites. Reservations are highly recommended during peak summer months.
minnesota.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat launch for access to the St. Croix River, which is excellent for smallmouth bass and walleye fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Interstate State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides educational exhibits on the geology of the St. Croix River valley and the history of the park.

minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit.
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking and water activities.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain near the gorge can be uneven and rocky.
Check the park website for seasonal rock climbing permit requirements.
Visit during the fall to see the spectacular foliage along the St. Croix River valley.

minnesota.name: Minneopa State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Famous for its stunning double waterfall and historic Seppmann Mill, Minneopa State Park offers a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural history.
minnesota.fullDescription: Minneopa State Park, located near Mankato, is named after the Dakota word meaning 'water falling twice.' The park features the spectacular Minneopa Falls, which drops 40 feet into a deep gorge. Beyond the falls, the park includes a restored prairie landscape where a herd of American bison roams, providing visitors with a glimpse of the Minnesota landscape as it appeared before European settlement.

hikingTrails.name: Waterfall Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible trail that leads visitors to the scenic overlook of the double waterfall.

hikingTrails.name: Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers along the edge of the gorge, offering dramatic views of the Minneopa Creek valley.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park offers 61 campsites, including 38 with electrical hookups, suitable for tents and RVs. There are also group camping areas available by reservation.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Minnesota River, which borders the park, though there are no boat ramps within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Minneopa State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and educational displays about the local geology and the bison restoration project.

minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit.
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for the waterfall flow or Autumn for the prairie colors.
tips: Check the park website for bison drive closures before arriving.
Wear sturdy shoes if you plan to hike the gorge trails as they can be slippery.
Bring a camera for the waterfall, as it is one of the most photographed spots in Southern Minnesota.

minnesota.name: Blue Mounds State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Famous for its dramatic Sioux Quartzite cliffs and a roaming herd of American bison, Blue Mounds offers a unique prairie landscape in southwestern Minnesota.
minnesota.fullDescription: Blue Mounds State Park is defined by its massive outcroppings of Sioux Quartzite, which rise 100 feet above the surrounding prairie. The park preserves a significant portion of native tallgrass prairie, providing a glimpse into the landscape as it appeared before European settlement. Visitors can explore the unique geology, view the bison herd managed by the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, and enjoy panoramic views from the cliff tops.

hikingTrails.name: Cliffline Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the top of the quartzite cliffs, offering spectacular views of the prairie below and the surrounding landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Prairie Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through restored tallgrass prairie, perfect for spotting wildflowers and native birds.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park features 73 drive-in campsites, many with electrical hookups, as well as walk-in sites and a group camp area. Reservations are highly recommended during peak summer months.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is available at the park's swimming pond, which is stocked with trout seasonally. No motorized boats are allowed.

visitorCenter.name: Blue Mounds Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the geology of the Sioux Quartzite, the history of the bison herd, and local prairie ecology.

minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for wildflowers or autumn for cooler hiking temperatures and bison activity.
tips: Check the park website for bison tour schedules as the herd is managed in a restricted area.
Bring binoculars for wildlife viewing, especially if you want to spot the bison from a distance.
The quartzite rocks can be slippery when wet; wear sturdy hiking boots with good grip.

minnesota.name: Jay Cooke State Park
minnesota.shortDescription: Experience the dramatic beauty of the St. Louis River as it carves through ancient rock formations in this historic Minnesota state park.
minnesota.fullDescription: Jay Cooke State Park is renowned for its spectacular scenery, featuring the turbulent St. Louis River flowing through a deep, rocky gorge. Established in 1915, the park preserves a unique geological landscape where the river cuts through tilted slate and greywacke rock. Visitors can explore the iconic swinging bridge, hike through diverse forests, and learn about the park's history as a former fur trade route and the legacy of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

hikingTrails.name: Superior Hiking Trail
hikingTrails.description: A segment of the famous long-distance trail that offers rugged terrain and stunning overlooks of the river valley.

hikingTrails.name: Swinging Bridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading to the park's famous suspension bridge, providing excellent views of the river rapids.

minnesota.campingInfo: The park offers 79 drive-in campsites, including 21 with electrical hookups, as well as five camper cabins and a group camp area.
minnesota.fishingBoating: Fishing is popular along the St. Louis River for smallmouth bass and walleye; however, the river is generally not suitable for motorized boating due to rapids.

visitorCenter.name: Jay Cooke State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interpretive exhibits on the park's geology, history, and natural resources, along with a gift shop and ranger assistance.

minnesota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit or $35.00 annual permit
minnesota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for high water levels or autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit the swinging bridge early in the morning to avoid crowds.
Check the DNR website for trail conditions before heading out, especially after heavy rain.
Bring sturdy hiking boots as the terrain near the river can be rocky and uneven.

missouri.name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Lake of the Ozarks park known for the stone ruins of an early-1900s castle, plus caves, sinkholes and bluffs.
missouri.fullDescription: Ha Ha Tonka State Park covers 3,751 acres on the Niangua arm of the Lake of the Ozarks near Camdenton. Its best-known feature is the ruins of Ha Ha Tonka, an early 20th-century stone mansion modeled on European castles. Fifteen miles of trails lead to the castle, caves, sinkholes and natural bridges of this karst landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Castle Trail
hikingTrails.description: A family-friendly trail leading to the castle ruins and a lake overlook, and one of the park's most popular routes.

hikingTrails.name: Spring Trail
hikingTrails.description: About 0.40 mile of this trail is paved and accessible to visitors with physical limitations, and that section follows the Lake of the Ozarks shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Lake View Bend Trail
hikingTrails.description: A park trail used for the park's 'Wednesday Walkabout' hike event.

missouri.campingInfo: Camping is limited to a special-use camping area, and the park file lists backcountry camping rules.
missouri.fishingBoating: The park offers fishing, boating and kayaking on the Niangua arm of the Lake of the Ozarks, and kayak rentals are available on-site, but there are no marina slips.

visitorCenter.name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

missouri.hours: Park: 7 a.m. to sunset, daily; Park Office/Visitor Center: 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, April through October
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring through fall (April–October) is a good time to visit, when the park office/visitor center keeps daily hours and the trails, boardwalks, castle-ruins overlooks and lake views are at their most enjoyable.
tips: Parts of the castle ruins have been closed off because of mortar and stone failure, but you can see the ruins from an observation point across from the park office.
The park office telephone is monitored for messages only from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, though park staff are usually in the park daily.
For an accessible option, about 0.40 mile of the Spring Trail is paved for visitors with physical limitations.

missouri.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Missouri Ozarks park where the East Fork Black River squeezes through hard volcanic rock, forming natural pools.
missouri.fullDescription: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park covers 9,432 acres on the East Fork Black River in Reynolds County, in the St. Francois Mountains. A 'shut-in' is a spot where hard rock narrows the river, creating chutes and pools. A paved walkway leads to an overlook of the shut-ins, and the Ozark Trail and an equestrian loop pass through.

hikingTrails.name: Shut-Ins Trail
hikingTrails.description: A loop trail that AllTrails lists among the park's popular hikes and calls moderately challenging; a hiker's post notes it begins with a boardwalk portion.

hikingTrails.name: Goggins Mountain Equestrian Trail
hikingTrails.description: A ten-mile loop trail in the park, according to Wikipedia.

hikingTrails.name: Scour Trail
hikingTrails.description: St. Louis Magazine lists hiking the Scour Trail among its top things to do at the park.

missouri.campingInfo: The park has a campground with reservations available online or toll free at 877-ICampMO (877-422-6766), and backcountry camping requires registration.
missouri.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the park, and smallmouth bass are the commonly caught fish.

visitorCenter.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

missouri.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
missouri.entranceFees: Free (no entrance fee at Missouri state parks)
missouri.address: 148 Taum Sauk Trail, Middle Brook, MO 63656-9601
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is the classic time to swim in the shut-ins of the East Fork Black River when water levels are not dangerously high, while spring and fall suit hiking in the rugged St. Francois Mountains.
tips: Parking at the park is limited, so check the park's Limited Parking Notification before you go.
Rappelling and rock climbing require a permit from the park.
Book campsites well in advance and check river levels before swimming, since the shut-ins are used only when water levels are not dangerously high.
nearbyAttractions: Bell Mountain Wilderness Area (Mark Twain National Forest)

missouri.name: Table Rock State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Small Missouri park on Table Rock Lake beside Branson, with a marina and campgrounds.
missouri.fullDescription: Table Rock State Park covers 356 acres on Table Rock Lake along the south side of Branson. Its facilities include a marina, campgrounds, and trails for hiking and bicycling.

hikingTrails.name: Lake View Bend Trail
hikingTrails.description: Lake View Bend Trail is a park trail used for the park's 'Wednesday Walkabout' guided hike event.

missouri.campingInfo: Basic, electric and sewer/electric/water campsites wind along the lakeshore among oak and hickory trees, and visitors can also stay in one of six premium yurts.
missouri.fishingBoating: State Park Marina rents everything from ski boats to paddleboards, and commonly caught fish include bass, sunfish, catfish, crappie, and rainbow and brown trout.

visitorCenter.name: Table Rock State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

missouri.hours: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, year-round
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is best for the lake-based boating, swimming and fishing the park is known for, while cooler spring and fall days suit hiking and biking.
tips: The open picnic shelter can be reserved by contacting the park office.
There is no designated beach, but swimming is allowed in several areas of the park.
Maximum boat trailer parking length is 55 feet.

missouri.name: Castlewood State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Nestled along the Meramec River, Castlewood State Park is a premier destination for mountain biking, hiking, and river recreation near St. Louis.
missouri.fullDescription: Castlewood State Park is renowned for its dramatic limestone bluffs overlooking the Meramec River. Historically a popular resort area in the early 20th century, the park now offers a rugged landscape characterized by deep ravines, lush forests, and extensive trail systems. The geology of the area features exposed Ordovician-age limestone, providing a scenic backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts.
thingsToDo: Hiking along the Meramec River bluffs
Fishing for smallmouth bass and catfish

hikingTrails.name: River Scene Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the river bluffs, offering spectacular views of the Meramec River and the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Stinging Nettle Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular loop for hikers and mountain bikers that traverses through dense hardwood forests and rocky terrain.

missouri.campingInfo: Castlewood State Park does not offer overnight camping or cabin rentals; it is strictly a day-use park.
missouri.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Meramec River banks. There is no formal boat ramp for motorized watercraft, but the river is popular for kayaking and canoeing.

visitorCenter.name: Castlewood State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, trail information, and assistance from park rangers regarding park regulations.

missouri.hours: 7:00 AM - Sunset daily
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: The park is extremely popular on weekends; arrive early to secure parking.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails can be rocky and uneven.
Check the official website for trail closure notices during wet weather to protect the trails.

missouri.name: Echo Bluff State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Nestled along the Current River, Echo Bluff State Park features towering limestone bluffs and pristine natural beauty in the heart of the Ozarks.
missouri.fullDescription: Echo Bluff State Park is a premier destination in the Missouri Ozarks, centered around the dramatic, towering Echo Bluff that rises above the crystal-clear waters of the Current River. The park offers a blend of modern amenities and rugged outdoor experiences, including the historic lodge, extensive trail systems, and access to one of the most scenic rivers in the state. The geology of the area is defined by karst topography, featuring springs, caves, and dramatic rock formations that have been carved by the river over millennia.
thingsToDo: Float trips on the Current River

hikingTrails.name: Bluff Top Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers spectacular panoramic views of the Current River valley from the top of the limestone bluffs.

hikingTrails.name: Siloam Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through lush forest areas, perfect for birdwatching and observing local flora.

missouri.campingInfo: The park offers full-service campsites with electric and water hookups, as well as primitive tent sites and the modern Betty Lea Lodge for overnight stays.
missouri.fishingBoating: The Current River is a popular destination for fly fishing and smallmouth bass fishing; boat access is available for canoes and kayaks.

visitorCenter.name: Echo Bluff State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides information on park history, local geology, and current trail conditions, along with a gift shop.

missouri.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
missouri.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; fees apply for camping and lodging.
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book your campsite or lodge room well in advance as they fill up quickly during peak season.
Bring water shoes if you plan on wading or floating in the Current River.
Check the park website for seasonal river level alerts before planning water activities.

missouri.name: Roaring River State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Nestled in a deep, narrow valley in the Ozark Mountains, Roaring River State Park is one of Missouri's most popular parks, famous for its trout hatchery and stunning natural springs.
missouri.fullDescription: Roaring River State Park is located in the heart of the Missouri Ozarks. The park is centered around a massive spring that discharges over 20 million gallons of water daily, feeding the Roaring River. The area has a rich history dating back to the 19th century, including remnants of old mills and CCC-era stone structures. The rugged landscape features steep limestone bluffs, lush forests, and diverse ecosystems, making it a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts and anglers alike.

hikingTrails.name: Deer Leap Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but steep climb that rewards hikers with a breathtaking panoramic view of the valley and the river below.

hikingTrails.name: Fire Tower Trail
hikingTrails.description: This challenging trail leads hikers to the historic fire tower site, offering a rigorous workout and dense forest scenery.

missouri.campingInfo: The park offers multiple campgrounds ranging from basic tent sites to full-hookup RV sites, along with the historic Emory Melton Inn and Conference Center for those preferring lodge accommodations.
missouri.fishingBoating: The park is world-renowned for its trout fishing; the river is divided into zones for fly fishing and bait fishing. No private boats are allowed on the spring-fed river.

visitorCenter.name: Roaring River State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, fishing regulations, and local geology, along with a gift shop.

missouri.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
missouri.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; fishing requires a daily tag and valid Missouri fishing license.
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild weather and peak fishing conditions.
tips: Purchase your trout tag at the park store before heading to the water.
Visit during the week to avoid heavy weekend crowds at the spring.
Bring sturdy hiking boots if you plan to tackle the steeper trails like Fire Tower.

missouri.name: Sam A. Baker State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Nestled in the St. Francois Mountains, this park offers a serene escape along the St. Francis River with lush forests and historic CCC-built structures.
missouri.fullDescription: Sam A. Baker State Park is one of Missouri's oldest and most beloved state parks. It features the rugged beauty of the St. Francois Mountains and the clear, spring-fed waters of the St. Francis River and Big Creek. The park is renowned for its Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) history, with many stone and timber structures still in use today. Visitors can explore diverse ecosystems ranging from oak-hickory forests to glades, providing a rich habitat for wildlife and a scenic backdrop for outdoor recreation.
thingsToDo: Swimming in the St. Francis River

hikingTrails.name: Mudlick Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that traverses the rugged terrain of the Mudlick Mountain Natural Area, offering spectacular ridge-top views.

hikingTrails.name: Shut-ins Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads visitors through a unique geological area where the river flows through narrow rock channels.

missouri.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options including basic, electric, and sewer/electric/water sites. There are also rustic cabins and a modern motel available for reservation.
missouri.fishingBoating: Fishing is popular along the St. Francis River and Big Creek. While there are no boat rentals, visitors are welcome to bring their own canoes or kayaks for paddling.

visitorCenter.name: Sam A. Baker Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's natural history, the CCC legacy, and local flora and fauna.

missouri.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Check the river levels before planning a swimming or floating trip.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to tackle the Mudlick Trail.
Book campsites well in advance during peak summer months.

missouri.name: Onondaga Cave State Park
missouri.shortDescription: Experience the breathtaking underground beauty of one of Missouri's most spectacular caves, featuring massive stalactites and flowstones.
missouri.fullDescription: Onondaga Cave State Park is a National Natural Landmark that offers visitors a chance to explore a subterranean wonderland. The park is centered around the Onondaga Cave, which features a stunning array of dripstone formations, including stalactites, stalagmites, and rimstone dams. Above ground, the park encompasses the scenic Meramec River, providing opportunities for hiking, fishing, and floating through the lush Ozark landscape.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on the Meramec River

hikingTrails.name: Vilander Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers scenic views of the Meramec River valley from high atop the bluffs.

hikingTrails.name: Deer Run Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through hardwood forests, perfect for spotting local wildlife.

missouri.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options, including basic, electric, and sewer/electric/water sites, as well as several rustic camping cabins.
missouri.fishingBoating: The Meramec River provides excellent fishing for smallmouth bass and sunfish, with a boat ramp available for easy river access.

visitorCenter.name: Onondaga Cave Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center serves as the hub for cave tour tickets, educational exhibits on cave geology, and park information.

missouri.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily
missouri.entranceFees: Free park entry; cave tour fees apply.
missouri.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book your cave tour tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly during peak season.
Bring a light jacket, as the cave maintains a constant temperature of 57 degrees Fahrenheit year-round.
Wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes for the cave tour as paths can be damp and uneven.

nebraska.name: Eugene T. Mahoney State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: A premier year-round destination in Nebraska featuring an aquatic center, ice skating, and scenic views of the Platte River.
nebraska.fullDescription: Eugene T. Mahoney State Park is one of Nebraska's most popular parks, situated on the bluffs overlooking the Platte River. It offers a unique blend of modern amenities and natural beauty, including the Peter Kiewit Lodge, an indoor aquatic center, and an observation tower that provides panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. The park is named after a former Nebraska state senator and is a hub for family-oriented recreation.

hikingTrails.name: Platte River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the river bluffs, offering excellent views of the water and local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through the park's forested areas, perfect for birdwatching and a quiet nature walk.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of lodging options including modern cabins, RV campsites with full hookups, and tent camping areas.
nebraska.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the park's stocked ponds; no motorized boating is permitted on the ponds.

visitorCenter.name: Mahoney State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, activity permits, and assistance with lodging reservations.

nebraska.hours: Open daily from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park entry permit is required for all vehicles.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for outdoor activities, or winter for ice skating.
tips: Purchase your park entry permit online in advance to save time at the gate.
Visit the observation tower early in the morning for the best photography lighting.
Check the park website for seasonal aquatic center and ice rink schedules.
nearbyAttractions: Lee G. Simmons Conservation Park and Wildlife Safari

nebraska.name: Chadron State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Nebraska's first state park, nestled in the scenic Pine Ridge escarpment, offering rugged landscapes and historic charm.
nebraska.fullDescription: Established in 1921, Chadron State Park is located in the heart of the Pine Ridge escarpment. The park features unique geological formations, ponderosa pine forests, and deep canyons. It serves as a gateway to the Nebraska National Forest and provides a rich history of Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) architecture, with many original cabins still in use today.

hikingTrails.name: Steamboat Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that offers panoramic views of the Pine Ridge escarpment and the surrounding ponderosa pine forest.

hikingTrails.name: Black Hills Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb that rewards hikers with breathtaking vistas of the distant Black Hills on clear days.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers 22 modern cabins, 52 electrical campsites, and numerous tent sites, along with a group camp facility.
nebraska.fishingBoating: The park features a small pond stocked with trout, perfect for youth fishing and relaxing afternoons.

visitorCenter.name: Chadron State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park permits, trail maps, and information on local history and CCC exhibits.

nebraska.hours: Open year-round, 24 hours a day for camping; day use from sunrise to sunset.
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park Entry Permit is required for all vehicles.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal weather and full facility access.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent wildlife viewing, especially at dawn and dusk.
Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular during summer months.
Check the weather forecast, as Pine Ridge can experience rapid temperature changes.

nebraska.name: Fort Robinson State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Located in the scenic Pine Ridge region, Fort Robinson State Park offers a unique blend of Old West history and expansive outdoor recreation.
nebraska.fullDescription: Fort Robinson State Park is a historic site that served as a U.S. Army fort from 1874 to 1948. Today, it spans over 22,000 acres of dramatic Pine Ridge escarpments, offering visitors a chance to explore preserved military buildings, museums, and rugged landscapes that once played a pivotal role in the Indian Wars.

hikingTrails.name: Red Cloud Buttes Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the iconic Pine Ridge buttes, offering panoramic views of the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Soldier Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path following the creek, perfect for birdwatching and observing local wildlife in a riparian habitat.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers extensive lodging options, including historic officer quarters, cabins, and modern RV campsites with full hookups.
nebraska.fishingBoating: The park features several stocked ponds and access to Soldier Creek, which is popular for trout fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Robinson History Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the fort's military history, the Cheyenne Outbreak, and the local geology of the Pine Ridge.

nebraska.hours: Open daily, 24 hours for registered guests; visitor facilities operate seasonally.
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park Entry Permit is required for all vehicles.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal weather and full facility operations.
tips: Book lodging well in advance as historic cabins fill up quickly during summer months.
Bring binoculars for spotting bighorn sheep on the nearby cliffs.
Check the schedule for the summer rodeo events held at the park arena.

nebraska.name: Platte River State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Nestled between Lincoln and Omaha, Platte River State Park offers a scenic retreat with wooded hills, modern cabins, and diverse recreational activities.
nebraska.fullDescription: Platte River State Park is situated on the bluffs overlooking the Platte River. The park is well-known for its unique glamping opportunities, modern cabins, and the scenic Jenny Newman Observation Tower, which provides panoramic views of the river valley. The area features a mix of hardwood forests and rolling hills, providing a beautiful backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts interested in hiking, archery, and water activities.

hikingTrails.name: Stone Creek Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the wooded hills and leads to a picturesque waterfall feature.

hikingTrails.name: Riverview Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the ridge line, offering stunning elevated views of the Platte River valley below.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of lodging options including modern cabins, camper cabins, and glamping tents. There are no traditional tent or RV campsites available for public reservation.
nebraska.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the park's stocked ponds. No boat ramps are available for the Platte River within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Platte River State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, activity permits, and cabin check-in services.

nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park vehicle permit is required for entry.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular and fill up quickly.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months due to the wooded terrain.
Check the official website for seasonal activity schedules like the pool and archery range.

nebraska.name: Ponca State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Perched on the bluffs overlooking the Missouri River, Ponca State Park is a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts in northeast Nebraska.
nebraska.fullDescription: Ponca State Park encompasses over 2,400 acres of heavily wooded hills and river bottomlands. It serves as the gateway to the Missouri National Recreational River, offering a unique blend of rugged topography, diverse ecosystems, and rich history related to the Lewis and Clark expedition.
thingsToDo: Educational programs at the Resource and Education Center

hikingTrails.name: Old Oak Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through mature hardwood forests and offers glimpses of the Missouri River valley.

hikingTrails.name: Bloodroot Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging hike featuring significant elevation changes and rewarding panoramic views from the bluffs.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers modern campgrounds with electrical hookups, primitive tent sites, and a variety of climate-controlled rental cabins.
nebraska.fishingBoating: Public boat ramp access to the Missouri River is available, providing excellent opportunities for catfish and sauger fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Missouri National Recreational River Resource and Education Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on the Missouri River ecosystem, local history, and the Lewis and Clark expedition.

nebraska.hours: Open daily, 24 hours for registered campers; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park Entry Permit is required for all vehicles.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and fall for the vibrant autumn foliage.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities along the river.
Check the park website for seasonal educational programs and guided hikes.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the bluff trails can be steep and uneven.
nearbyAttractions: Lewis and Clark State Recreation Area

nebraska.name: Niobrara State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Located at the confluence of the Niobrara and Missouri Rivers, this park offers stunning vistas and diverse outdoor recreation in northeastern Nebraska.
nebraska.fullDescription: Niobrara State Park is situated in the scenic bluffs where the Niobrara and Missouri Rivers meet. The park features a unique landscape of rolling hills, dense forests, and open prairies. Historically significant as a crossroads for explorers and indigenous tribes, the park now serves as a premier destination for nature lovers, offering a blend of modern amenities and rugged wilderness experiences.
thingsToDo: Fishing in the Niobrara and Missouri Rivers

hikingTrails.name: River Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the high bluffs providing panoramic views of the river confluence below.

hikingTrails.name: Prairie Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through restored native prairie grasses, perfect for spotting wildflowers and butterflies.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers 51 modern campsites with electrical hookups, as well as 19 fully furnished cabins available for rent year-round.
nebraska.fishingBoating: The park features boat ramps providing access to both the Niobrara and Missouri Rivers, popular for catfish and walleye fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Niobrara State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, local information, and assistance with cabin and campsite reservations.

nebraska.hours: Open daily, 24 hours for registered campers; day use from sunrise to sunset.
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska Park Entry Permit is required for all vehicles entering the park.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal weather and wildlife viewing.
tips: Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities near the river.
Book cabins well in advance as they are popular during summer months.
Check the park website for seasonal pool hours before planning your visit.

nebraska.name: Smith Falls State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Home to Nebraska's tallest waterfall, Smith Falls State Park offers a stunning natural oasis along the Niobrara National Scenic River.
nebraska.fullDescription: Smith Falls State Park is a geological gem featuring the tallest waterfall in Nebraska, cascading 63 feet over a ledge of sandstone. The park is situated along the Niobrara National Scenic River, providing a unique microclimate where eastern, western, and northern plant species converge. Visitors can explore the lush canyon, walk across the historic bridge, and enjoy the serene beauty of the Niobrara River valley.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on the Niobrara River

hikingTrails.name: Smith Falls Boardwalk
hikingTrails.description: A scenic, accessible boardwalk that leads visitors directly to the base of the majestic Smith Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Niobrara River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A winding trail that follows the riverbank, offering excellent views of the canyon walls and local flora.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers tent camping sites with fire rings and picnic tables, as well as limited RV sites. Reservations are highly recommended during peak summer months.
nebraska.fishingBoating: The Niobrara River is popular for canoeing, kayaking, and tubing. Fishing is permitted in the river with a valid Nebraska fishing license.

visitorCenter.name: Smith Falls Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping permits.

nebraska.entranceFees: $6.00 daily vehicle permit for Nebraska residents; $12.00 for non-residents.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal weather and river activities.
tips: Bring water shoes for wading near the waterfall base.
Book your campsite well in advance as they fill up quickly during summer weekends.
Pack insect repellent, especially if visiting during the humid summer months.

nebraska.name: Indian Cave State Park
nebraska.shortDescription: Nestled on the banks of the Missouri River, this park is famous for its massive sandstone cave and stunning hardwood forest vistas.
nebraska.fullDescription: Indian Cave State Park encompasses over 3,000 acres of rugged, forested terrain along the Missouri River. The park is named for the large sandstone cave featuring prehistoric petroglyphs carved into the walls. Visitors can explore the diverse ecosystem of the Loess Hills, which provides a unique landscape of steep ridges and deep ravines, offering some of the most scenic hiking and camping opportunities in Nebraska.

hikingTrails.name: Indian Cave Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but steep trail that leads visitors directly to the historic sandstone cave and its ancient petroglyphs.

hikingTrails.name: Hardwood Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop through dense oak-hickory forests that offers panoramic views of the Missouri River valley.

nebraska.campingInfo: The park offers extensive camping facilities including modern RV sites with electrical hookups, primitive tent sites, and several rustic cabins available for rent.
nebraska.fishingBoating: The park features access to the Missouri River for fishing and non-motorized boating, though no formal boat ramp is available within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Indian Cave State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, trail information, and educational displays regarding the history of the cave and local geology.

nebraska.hours: Open daily from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM
nebraska.entranceFees: A valid Nebraska State Park entry permit is required for all vehicles.
nebraska.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn is the best time to visit to witness the spectacular fall foliage across the Loess Hills.
tips: Bring insect repellent, especially during the summer months when ticks and mosquitoes are active.
Check the official website for seasonal road closures due to heavy rain or flooding.
Visit during the early morning hours for the best chance to spot wild turkeys and deer.

north dakota.name: Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: North Dakota park near Mandan with a rebuilt Mandan earth-lodge village and Custer's reconstructed house.
north dakota.fullDescription: Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park lies 7 miles south of Mandan on the Missouri River. It holds the reconstructed On-A-Slant Mandan village, inhabited from the late 1500s to about 1781, and rebuilt military buildings of the fort, including the Custer House and blockhouses.

hikingTrails.name: Scouts Trail System
hikingTrails.description: A non-motorized, multi-use series of loops and connecting trails, mostly hard-packed single-track with manageable grades and only a few steeper sections, open to hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding and mountain biking.

hikingTrails.name: Little Soldier Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: Starting at the Valley picnic shelter and meeting the Young Hawk Interpretive Trail, this segment offers excellent vistas of On-A-Slant Village, the Missouri and Heart rivers and the city of Bismarck.

hikingTrails.name: Young Hawk Interpretive Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail starts and ends at the Valley picnic shelter and has numbered posts keyed to a trail guide, available at the Visitor Center, describing the area's history, plants and wildlife.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park has 51 modern campsites, 15 modern group campsites, 15 primitive campsites, 1 primitive group tent campsite, 4 primitive horse campsites and two seasonal camping cabins along the Missouri River, with campsites bookable 95 days in advance online or at 800-807-4723.
north dakota.fishingBoating: Anglers can fish along the shorelines of both the Missouri and Heart Rivers, and the park lists a kayak launch among its amenities.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

north dakota.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle per day; $35 annual vehicle permit
north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is ideal, since the Custer House living history tours and On-A-Slant Village tours run Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, while October brings the Haunted Fort event.
tips: Tours of the Custer House and On-A-Slant Village require an Interpretive Tour Pass ($8 adult, $5 student K-12), sold at the Visitor Center or Commissary. Tours operate Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, and large groups should call 701-667-6340 in advance.
Campsites can be booked 95 days in advance online or by calling 800-807-4723. Camping cabins require a two-night minimum, do not allow pets and do not provide bedding or towels.
Equestrians need a horse pass ($6/horse daily or $30/horse annual) in addition to the park entrance fee, and may ride only on trails designated for horse use.
nearbyAttractions: Five Nations Arts (former Northern Pacific Railway station, Main Street, Mandan)

north dakota.name: Lake Metigoshe State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Turtle Mountains lake park on the Canadian border near Bottineau, for water sports in summer and snow sports in winter.
north dakota.fullDescription: Lake Metigoshe State Park occupies about 1,500 acres on Lake Metigoshe in the Turtle Mountains, 14 miles northeast of Bottineau, next to Manitoba's Turtle Mountain Provincial Park. The lake has northern pike, walleye and perch; winter brings snowmobiling, cross-country skiing and ice fishing.

hikingTrails.name: Old Oak Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: North Dakota's first National Recreation Trail, this self-guided interpretive hiking trail was built by the Youth Conservation Corps in 1974 and takes about two hours to hike.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Metigoshe Cub Loop
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails describes it as an easy hike with 9 feet of elevation gain that takes about 0.5 to 1 hour to complete.

hikingTrails.name: Hemerick Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail runs through the wooded Turtle Mountains, and the park's White Pelican cabin is located along it.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park has 84 modern campsites with electricity and water ($25-30 per night), 39 primitive campsites ($15 per night) and 3 modern group campsites, plus cabins, a yurt and group dorms, with reservations available online or by calling 800-807-4723.
north dakota.fishingBoating: The park has a boat ramp, four fishing docks, and canoe, kayak, paddleboard and pontoon rentals, and Lake Metigoshe is fished for northern pike, walleye and perch, including ice fishing in winter.

visitorCenter.name: Lake Metigoshe State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

north dakota.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle per day; $35 annual vehicle permit
north dakota.address: 2 Lake Metigoshe State Pk, Bottineau, ND 58318
north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Lake Metigoshe is a year-round destination: summer suits paddling, swimming and fishing, while winter brings cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, sledding and ice fishing.
tips: Campsites can be booked 95 days in advance, either online or by calling 800-807-4723.
The backcountry Osprey Cabin is reached only by a 2-mile hike or a 1.5-mile paddle and short portage. Water must be packed in, and bedding and towels are not provided at any park cabin.
A free all-terrain wheelchair is available for visitors with mobility challenges. Reserve it in advance by calling 701-263-4651.

north dakota.name: Cross Ranch State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Missouri River park in North Dakota with cottonwood bottomlands, next to a nature preserve with a bison herd.
north dakota.fullDescription: Cross Ranch State Park covers 569 acres on the west bank of the Missouri River nine miles south of Washburn. It borders The Nature Conservancy's 6,000-acre Cross Ranch Nature Preserve, home to a herd of over 200 bison. Together they offer 16 miles of trails, and the park has campsites, cabins and yurts.

hikingTrails.name: Matah "River" Trail
hikingTrails.description: Starting at the Visitor Center, this loop circles the park's main use areas, with interpretive signs along the river describing the area's history, wildlife and geology.

hikingTrails.name: Ma-ak-oti "Old Village" Trail
hikingTrails.description: This two-section trail winds through prairie bluffs and wooded channels with vistas of the Missouri River and includes steep stairs without handrails on portions.

hikingTrails.name: TNC Self-Guided Prairie Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail crosses preserve prairie and wooded draws within the Nature Conservancy bison pasture, with a guidebook at the trailhead covering wildlife, plants and history.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park has two campgrounds with 35 standard electric sites ($25-30 per night) and 22 primitive sites ($15 per night), plus cabins and yurts, and campsites can be booked 95 days in advance online or at 800-807-4723.
north dakota.fishingBoating: A boat ramp provides access to a free-flowing stretch of the Missouri River where anglers find walleye, trout, catfish, salmon, pike and bass, and the park rents canoes and kayaks and offers a nine-mile shuttle run from Washburn to the Sanger boat landing.

visitorCenter.name: Cross Ranch State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

north dakota.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
north dakota.entranceFees: $7 per vehicle per day; $35 annual vehicle permit
north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: The park is open year-round: warmer months suit hiking, biking and paddling the Missouri River, while winter brings groomed cross-country ski trails and snowshoeing.
tips: Bison are present on the TNC Self-Guided Prairie Trail, so keep a safe distance and remember they are wild animals.
The Ma-ak-oti Trail has steep stairs without handrails, and some areas may be muddy or impassable due to seasonal water fluctuations.
All vehicles entering a state park, including those of overnight guests, need a valid daily or annual vehicle entrance permit.
nearbyAttractions: Washburn (start of the park's nine-mile Missouri River kayak/canoe run)

north dakota.name: Icelandic State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Lake Renwick, Icelandic State Park offers a serene escape with rich cultural history and beautiful woodland trails.
north dakota.fullDescription: Icelandic State Park is situated on the north shore of Lake Renwick in Cavalier County. The park preserves the heritage of early Icelandic settlers in the region and features the Gunlogson State Nature Preserve, which protects a unique riparian forest. Visitors can explore the Pioneer Heritage Center, which houses exhibits on local history, and enjoy the diverse ecosystems ranging from prairie to mature hardwood forests.
thingsToDo: Fishing for northern pike and walleye
Bird watching in the nature preserve

hikingTrails.name: Gunlogson Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the lush hardwood forest of the Gunlogson State Nature Preserve.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Renwick Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the shoreline of Lake Renwick, offering excellent views of the water and local waterfowl.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park offers modern campsites with electrical hookups, as well as primitive tent sites and a group camping area.
north dakota.fishingBoating: The park features a boat ramp on Lake Renwick and is a popular spot for shore fishing and non-motorized boating.

visitorCenter.name: Pioneer Heritage Center
visitorCenter.info: Features historical exhibits, artifacts from Icelandic settlers, and information about the local natural environment.

north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal weather and bird migration.
tips: Bring insect repellent during the summer months as the wooded areas can have mosquitoes.
Visit the Pioneer Heritage Center early in your trip to understand the historical context of the area.
Check the park website for seasonal swimming beach closures or water quality updates.

north dakota.name: Grahams Island State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Devils Lake, Grahams Island State Park is a premier destination for world-class fishing and outdoor recreation in North Dakota.
north dakota.fullDescription: Grahams Island State Park is situated on a large island in Devils Lake, connected to the mainland by a causeway. The park is renowned for its exceptional perch and walleye fishing, attracting anglers from across the country. The landscape features rolling hills, wooded areas, and expansive views of the lake, providing a serene environment for camping, hiking, and birdwatching.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path winding through the wooded areas of the island, perfect for spotting local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Lakeside Loop
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers scenic views of Devils Lake and follows the shoreline for much of the journey.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park offers modern campsites with electrical hookups, as well as primitive tent sites. Cabin rentals are also available for those seeking a more comfortable stay.
north dakota.fishingBoating: The park features a high-quality boat ramp and fish cleaning station, making it a top-tier location for boaters and anglers.

visitorCenter.name: Grahams Island Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on fishing regulations, trail maps, and camping reservations.

north dakota.hours: Open 24 hours for registered campers; day use from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM
north dakota.address: 152 S Grahams Island Rd, Devils Lake, ND 58301
north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal fishing and camping conditions.
tips: Check current lake levels before arrival as they can fluctuate.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months.
Book campsites well in advance, especially for summer weekends.
nearbyAttractions: White Horse Hill National Game Preserve

north dakota.name: Turtle River State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Nestled in the scenic Turtle River valley, this park offers a lush, wooded escape featuring diverse recreational activities and historic Civilian Conservation Corps structures.
north dakota.fullDescription: Turtle River State Park is located in the scenic Turtle River valley, providing a unique landscape of wooded hills and river bottomlands that contrast with the surrounding flat plains of the Red River Valley. Developed in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), the park retains much of its historic charm through its rustic log buildings and stone bridges. The park is a popular destination for outdoor enthusiasts seeking hiking, mountain biking, and winter sports, while also serving as a peaceful retreat for families and nature lovers.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path winding through the dense forest canopy, perfect for birdwatching and spotting local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: River Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the meandering path of the Turtle River, offering scenic views of the water and the historic CCC-built stone structures.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park offers modern campsites with electrical hookups, as well as primitive tent sites. Several rustic cabins are available for rent, providing a cozy experience in the heart of the woods.
north dakota.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Turtle River, which is stocked with trout. No motorized boats are allowed due to the shallow nature of the river.

visitorCenter.name: Turtle River State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, camping reservations, and historical exhibits regarding the CCC era.

north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking, or winter for cross-country skiing.
tips: Bring insect repellent during the summer months as the wooded areas can be buggy.
Visit during the autumn to see the vibrant fall foliage along the river valley.
Check the official website for seasonal road conditions before planning a winter visit.

north dakota.name: Lake Sakakawea State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Located on the shores of one of the largest man-made reservoirs in the United States, this park is a premier destination for water recreation and outdoor adventure.
north dakota.fullDescription: Lake Sakakawea State Park is situated at the south end of the massive Lake Sakakawea, created by the Garrison Dam. The park offers expansive views of the reservoir and serves as a gateway to the North Country National Scenic Trail. Its geology is defined by the rolling prairie hills and the vast, deep waters of the Missouri River system, providing a unique habitat for diverse wildlife and a playground for boating enthusiasts.
thingsToDo: Fishing for walleye and northern pike
Hiking the North Country National Scenic Trail
Camping in modern or primitive sites

hikingTrails.name: North Country National Scenic Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic segment of the national trail that winds through prairie grasses and offers elevated views of the lake.

hikingTrails.name: Park Perimeter Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that circles the main recreation area, perfect for families and bird watching.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park features over 200 campsites, including modern sites with full electrical and water hookups, as well as primitive tent sites and several rental cabins.
north dakota.fishingBoating: The park features a world-class marina with multiple boat ramps, fuel docks, and fish cleaning stations.

visitorCenter.name: Lake Sakakawea State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping reservations.

north dakota.hours: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM
north dakota.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle permit required for entry.
north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water temperatures and hiking conditions.
tips: Bring plenty of sunscreen as there is limited shade in the open prairie areas.
Check the wind forecast before heading out on the water, as the lake can get choppy.
Make camping reservations well in advance during the peak summer months.
nearbyAttractions: Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site

north dakota.name: Fort Stevenson State Park
north dakota.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Lake Sakakawea, this park offers premier fishing, boating, and a rich history centered around the 19th-century military fort.
north dakota.fullDescription: Fort Stevenson State Park is situated on the north shore of Lake Sakakawea, one of the largest man-made reservoirs in the United States. The park is named after the historic military post established in 1867 to protect the overland route between Fort Totten and Fort Buford. Today, visitors can explore the interpretive center which details the history of the fort and the Missouri River valley. The park is a hub for outdoor recreation, featuring extensive marina facilities, modern camping, and miles of trails that wind through the rolling prairie landscape.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Lake Sakakawea
Camping in modern sites or cabins

hikingTrails.name: Deapolis Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that offers beautiful views of the lake and opportunities to spot local prairie wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Fort Stevenson Loop
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the historic areas of the park, providing educational markers about the original fort site.

north dakota.campingInfo: The park offers over 100 campsites with electrical and water hookups, as well as several modern camping cabins available for rent.
north dakota.fishingBoating: The park features a full-service marina, boat ramps, and is widely considered one of the best walleye fishing spots in North Dakota.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Stevenson Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of the military fort, the Missouri River, and the construction of the Garrison Dam.

north dakota.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities and pleasant hiking weather.
tips: Check the lake water levels before planning a boating trip as they can fluctuate.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months, especially near the shoreline.
Visit the interpretive center early in your stay to better understand the historical significance of the area.

ohio.name: Hocking Hills State Park
ohio.shortDescription: Hocking Hills State Park is a world-renowned destination featuring dramatic sandstone cliffs, deep gorges, and cascading waterfalls in southeastern Ohio.
ohio.fullDescription: Hocking Hills State Park is defined by its unique Black Hand Sandstone geology, which has been carved over millennia by water and ice into spectacular caves, recess shelters, and gorges. The park encompasses several distinct areas including Old Man's Cave, Ash Cave, and Cedar Falls, each offering a unique glimpse into the region's rich natural history and diverse forest ecosystems.

hikingTrails.name: Old Man's Cave to Cedar Falls
hikingTrails.description: This scenic trail follows the gorge floor, passing through tunnels and past impressive rock formations and waterfalls.

hikingTrails.name: Ash Cave Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, accessible path leading to the massive recess cave and the tallest waterfall in the park.

ohio.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with over 150 electric sites, full-hookup sites, and primitive sites, along with several camper cabins available for reservation.
ohio.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park, though boating is not available within the main gorge areas.

visitorCenter.name: Hocking Hills State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features interactive exhibits on the park's geology, history, and wildlife, along with a gift shop and information desk.

ohio.entranceFees: Admission to Hocking Hills State Park is free for all visitors.
ohio.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for waterfalls or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit on weekdays to avoid heavy weekend crowds.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as trails can be slippery near waterfalls.
Download offline maps as cell service is limited in the deep gorges.

ohio.name: John Bryan State Park
ohio.shortDescription: John Bryan State Park features a remarkable limestone gorge carved by the Little Miami River, offering stunning scenery and diverse recreational opportunities.
ohio.fullDescription: John Bryan State Park is a 752-acre park located in Greene County, Ohio. It is widely considered the most scenic state park in western Ohio, characterized by the dramatic Clifton Gorge, which is a National Natural Landmark. The park's geology is defined by massive limestone cliffs and the rushing waters of the Little Miami State and National Scenic River. The area was once home to the Miami people and later became a site for early industrial mills. Today, it provides a lush habitat for diverse flora and fauna, including rare wildflowers and towering hardwood trees.

hikingTrails.name: North Rim Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the top of the gorge, providing spectacular elevated views of the Little Miami River below.

hikingTrails.name: South Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that winds along the riverbank, allowing hikers to get up close to the limestone rock formations.

ohio.campingInfo: The park offers a campground with 100 sites, including both electric and non-electric options, suitable for tents and RVs. Amenities include showers, flush toilets, and a dump station.
ohio.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Little Miami River, which is known for smallmouth bass and rock bass. No boat ramps are available due to the shallow, rocky nature of the river.

visitorCenter.name: John Bryan State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, trail information, and educational materials about the gorge's geology.

ohio.entranceFees: Admission to John Bryan State Park is free.
ohio.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit during the spring to see the spectacular display of trillium and other wildflowers.
The gorge can be slippery; wear sturdy hiking boots with good traction.
Combine your visit with a trip to the adjacent Clifton Gorge State Nature Preserve for more trails.

ohio.name: Maumee Bay State Park
ohio.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Lake Erie, Maumee Bay State Park offers a unique blend of recreational facilities and diverse natural habitats.
ohio.fullDescription: Maumee Bay State Park is situated on the shores of Lake Erie, featuring 1,336 acres of diverse landscape including marshes, meadows, and woodlands. The park is a premier destination for birdwatchers, as it sits along a major migratory path. The area was once part of the Great Black Swamp, and today it provides essential habitat for wildlife while offering visitors modern amenities like a resort lodge, golf course, and sandy beaches.
thingsToDo: Swimming at the Lake Erie beach

hikingTrails.name: Trautman Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic boardwalk trail that winds through marshes and woodlands, offering excellent opportunities to spot migratory birds.

hikingTrails.name: Mouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, multi-use trail that traverses through meadows and forest edges, perfect for a leisurely walk or bike ride.

ohio.campingInfo: The park features a modern campground with 256 sites, all equipped with electrical hookups, showers, flush toilets, and laundry facilities.
ohio.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the inland lake and along the Lake Erie shoreline. A boat ramp is available for access to Lake Erie.

visitorCenter.name: Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The Nature Center features interactive exhibits about the Great Black Swamp, local wildlife, and the ecology of Lake Erie.

ohio.entranceFees: Free admission to the park; fees apply for camping, golf, and lodge rentals.
ohio.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for bird migration, Summer for beach activities.
tips: Bring binoculars as the park is a world-renowned birding destination.
Check the Lake Erie water quality reports online before planning a swim.
Visit during the weekday to avoid crowds at the beach and golf course.
nearbyAttractions: National Museum of the Great Lakes

ohio.name: Mohican State Park
ohio.shortDescription: Nestled in the heart of Ohio's scenic Mohican River valley, this park offers breathtaking views, rugged gorges, and lush forests.
ohio.fullDescription: Mohican State Park is a premier destination in Ohio, renowned for its dramatic landscape carved by the Clear Fork of the Mohican River. The park features steep, hemlock-lined gorges and expansive hardwood forests that provide a stunning backdrop for outdoor recreation. Historically significant, the area was once home to the Delaware Indians and later became a hub for early settlers. Today, it is celebrated for its diverse ecosystem, including rare plant species and abundant wildlife, making it a favorite for nature enthusiasts and adventure seekers alike.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on the Mohican River

hikingTrails.name: Gorge Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers spectacular views of the deep gorge and the river below, winding through beautiful hemlock groves.

hikingTrails.name: Hemlock Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that follows the riverbank, providing excellent opportunities to observe the park's unique geological formations.

ohio.campingInfo: The park features a large, modern campground with over 100 sites, including full hookups, electric-only sites, and primitive tent sites, along with seasonal cabin rentals.
ohio.fishingBoating: The Mohican River is a popular destination for trout fishing, and the park provides access points for canoes and kayaks.

visitorCenter.name: Mohican State Park Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The nature center provides educational exhibits on local flora, fauna, and the geological history of the Mohican River valley.

ohio.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Mohican State Park.
ohio.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for the vibrant fall foliage or spring for blooming wildflowers.
tips: Visit during the weekdays to avoid heavy weekend crowds.
Bring waterproof footwear if you plan on exploring the creek beds.
Check the official website for seasonal river water levels before planning a kayaking trip.

ohio.name: Geneva State Park
ohio.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Lake Erie, Geneva State Park offers beautiful beaches, extensive trails, and a full-service marina.
ohio.fullDescription: Geneva State Park is a premier destination on the shores of Lake Erie in Ashtabula County. The park features a diverse landscape of meadows, woodlands, and sandy beaches. Historically, the area was shaped by the glacial activity that formed the Great Lakes, and today it serves as a vital recreational hub for boating, fishing, and birdwatching. The park is well-known for its expansive marina and its proximity to the Geneva-on-the-Lake resort area.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Lake Erie

hikingTrails.name: Breakwater Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, scenic path that offers excellent views of the Lake Erie shoreline and the marina.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the park's forested areas, providing opportunities to spot local wildlife and enjoy the changing seasons.
