arkansas.shortDescription: Perched atop Rich Mountain, this park offers breathtaking views of the Ouachita Mountains and a historic lodge experience.
arkansas.fullDescription: Queen Wilhelmina State Park is located on the second-highest peak in Arkansas, Rich Mountain. Named after the Queen of the Netherlands, the park features the historic Queen Wilhelmina Lodge, which provides a unique mountain retreat experience. The area is renowned for its stunning vistas, diverse flora, and the scenic Talimena National Scenic Byway that winds through the surrounding Ouachita National Forest.
thingsToDo: Dining at the Queen Wilhelmina Lodge
Exploring the Talimena National Scenic Byway

hikingTrails.name: Lover's Leap Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads to a dramatic rock outcropping offering panoramic views of the valley below.

hikingTrails.name: Ouachita National Recreation Trail
hikingTrails.description: A long-distance trail that passes through the park, offering rugged terrain and deep forest immersion for experienced hikers.

arkansas.campingInfo: The park features 41 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as a modern lodge with 40 guest rooms for those seeking indoor accommodations.
arkansas.fishingBoating: While there is no lake within the park, nearby streams and lakes in the Ouachita National Forest offer excellent fishing opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Queen Wilhelmina Lodge Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and local wildlife exhibits.

arkansas.hours: Park grounds are open 24 hours; Lodge and Visitor Center hours vary by season.
arkansas.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for fall foliage or Spring for blooming wildflowers.
tips: Bring a jacket as temperatures are significantly cooler on the mountain summit.
Check the weather before driving the Talimena Scenic Byway as fog can reduce visibility.
Book lodge rooms well in advance during peak foliage season.

arkansas.name: Bull Shoals-White River State Park
arkansas.shortDescription: Nestled along the banks of the White River and the shores of Bull Shoals Lake, this park is a premier destination for world-class trout fishing and outdoor recreation.
arkansas.fullDescription: Bull Shoals-White River State Park offers a unique blend of river and lake experiences. The park is situated at the base of the Bull Shoals Dam, where the cold, clear waters of the White River provide an ideal habitat for trophy trout. The surrounding Ozark landscape features rugged hills, lush forests, and expansive water views, making it a haven for anglers, boaters, and nature enthusiasts alike.

hikingTrails.name: Big Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the forest and offers elevated views of the White River.

hikingTrails.name: Lakeside Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path along the shoreline of Bull Shoals Lake, perfect for a relaxing walk.

arkansas.campingInfo: The park features 103 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as several tent-only sites and modern bathhouses.
arkansas.fishingBoating: The park provides multiple boat ramps for both the lake and the river, along with a full-service marina offering boat rentals and supplies.

visitorCenter.name: Bull Shoals-White River State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of the dam, local geology, and the aquatic life of the White River.

arkansas.address: 153 Dam Overlook Lane, Bull Shoals, AR 72619
arkansas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild weather and peak fishing conditions.
tips: Check the water release schedule from the dam before planning your fishing trip.
Bring polarized sunglasses to better spot trout in the clear river water.
Visit during the early morning hours to see the most wildlife activity.

delaware.name: Cape Henlopen State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Delaware park at the mouth of Delaware Bay, with ocean and bay beaches and World War II Fort Miles.
delaware.fullDescription: Cape Henlopen State Park covers 5,450 acres on Cape Henlopen near Lewes. William Penn set its beaches aside for public use in 1682, making it one of the first public lands in what became the United States. It has lifeguarded swimming beaches in summer, WWII-era Fort Miles with an observation tower, and Gordons Pond.

hikingTrails.name: Gordons Pond Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular, easy biking, hiking, running and bird-watching trail that crosses the park's salt marshes.

hikingTrails.name: Junction and Breakwater Trail
hikingTrails.description: It appears on the park's official 'Gordons Pond, J&B and Wolfe Neck Trail Map' and is listed by AllTrails among popular trails in the park.

delaware.campingInfo: The park offers RV camping, cabins and tent camping at its campground, which is set among the pine-covered dunes.
delaware.fishingBoating: Anglers can fish from the fishing pier on Delaware Bay or surf-fish from designated beach areas, and the park has a bait and tackle store and paddlesport rentals.

visitorCenter.name: Cape Henlopen State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

delaware.hours: Open daily from 8 a.m. until sunset
delaware.entranceFees: $10/day for Delaware-registered vehicles; $20/day for non-Delaware-registered vehicles; walking/biking free
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is best for the guarded ocean beaches, which have lifeguards from Memorial Day Saturday to Labor Day Monday; spring and fall suit birding at the Point and in the shorebird habitat.
tips: The Seaside Nature Center is closed October 19-27, so plan aquarium and touch-tank visits around that closure.
You can borrow a bike for free at the Seaside Nature Center to explore the park's extensive bike trails.
Most of Beach Plum Nature Preserve is off-limits for wildlife conservation. Only a small surf-fishing area and a pedestrian-only trail are open to the public.

delaware.name: Delaware Seashore State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Delaware barrier-island park between the Atlantic and Rehoboth and Indian River bays, near Dewey Beach.
delaware.fullDescription: Delaware Seashore State Park covers 2,722 acres near Dewey Beach, between the Atlantic Ocean and Rehoboth and Indian River bays, with 6 miles of shoreline. Created in 1965, it has two ocean swimming areas with bathhouses, surf fishing, a marina at Indian River Inlet, and camping.

hikingTrails.name: Burton Island Trail
hikingTrails.description: This nature trail on Burton Island offers views of salt marshes and bay islands and has its own trailhead.

hikingTrails.name: Assawoman Canal Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail in Ocean View is a separate recreation area overseen by Delaware Seashore State Park management, and a PDF map is available.

delaware.campingInfo: The park has two waterfront campgrounds for RV and tent camping, plus bayfront cottages and a four-bedroom house.
delaware.fishingBoating: Anglers can surf fish along the ocean, including from surf fishing vehicle areas, or fish at Indian River Inlet, and boaters can use the park's boat ramp and the Indian River Marina.

visitorCenter.name: Delaware Seashore State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

delaware.hours: Open daily from 8 a.m. until sunset
delaware.entranceFees: $10/day for DE-registered vehicles; $20/day for non-DE-registered vehicles; walking/biking free
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Visit from Memorial Day Saturday through Labor Day Monday if you want guarded swimming beaches, or come in spring or fall for birding, fishing and paddling the inland bays.
tips: From September 15, 2026 to March 15, 2027, a sand bypass system will close portions of the beaches on the north and south sides of the Indian River Inlet. Avoid the construction zones.
The Delaware Seashore park office is closed for pass and permit sales, so buy passes and permits another way before you arrive.
Driving on the beach to surf fish requires a surf fishing permit, and daily entrance fees apply from March 1 to November 30.

delaware.name: Lums Pond State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Delaware park around Lums Pond, a 19th-century reservoir built to feed the C&D Canal locks.
delaware.fullDescription: Lums Pond State Park covers 1,790 acres near Bear and surrounds Lums Pond, built on St. Georges Creek to supply water to the locks of the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal in the early 1800s. Rowboats, kayaks, canoes and pedal boats can be rented, and the pond holds largemouth bass, crappie and stocked hybrid striped bass.

hikingTrails.name: Little Jersey Trail
hikingTrails.description: An 8-mile trail described as enjoyable for all skill levels that provides access to the Lums Pond Woods Nature Preserve.

hikingTrails.name: Swamp Forest Trail
hikingTrails.description: Described by the park as a more challenging trail for experienced bikers.

hikingTrails.name: Mile Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short forest walk with scenic views of Lums Pond.

delaware.campingInfo: The newly renovated year-round campground offers spacious RV sites with three-point hookups as well as tent sites, and new cabins are under construction.
delaware.fishingBoating: Visitors can fish or paddle on Delaware's largest freshwater pond, which has a boat ramp and fishing pier, using rented kayaks, canoes or pedalboats or their own boats; the pond holds carp, pickerel, crappie, catfish, largemouth bass and stocked hybrid striped bass.

visitorCenter.name: Lums Pond State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

delaware.entranceFees: DE registered vehicle: $5/day; Non-DE registered vehicle: $10/day; Walking/biking: Free
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is a great time to visit for foliage around the pond, while late spring through summer suits paddling and the Go Ape course, which is open March through November.
tips: New cabin construction runs 7 a.m.-4 p.m. Monday through Friday through March 2027, so expect vehicle and equipment traffic, noise and detours in the campground.
The Whale Wallow Nature Center is open year-round, but only Wednesday through Sunday from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m.
The vehicle entrance fee is charged daily from March 1 to November 30. Walkers and bikers enter free.

delaware.name: Trap Pond State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Home to one of the northernmost natural stands of bald cypress trees in the United States, Trap Pond offers a serene escape into a unique wetland ecosystem.
delaware.fullDescription: Trap Pond State Park was established in 1951 and encompasses a large portion of the original bald cypress swamp that once covered much of the region. The park features a 90-acre pond created in the late 1700s to power a sawmill. Today, it serves as a vital habitat for diverse wildlife and provides recreational opportunities centered around its tranquil waters and towering, moss-draped cypress trees.

hikingTrails.name: Cypress Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers through the heart of the bald cypress swamp with excellent views of the water.

hikingTrails.name: Bob Trail
hikingTrails.description: A longer trail that winds through diverse forest habitats and offers a more immersive experience in the park's natural landscape.

delaware.campingInfo: The park offers 130 campsites, including sites with full hookups for RVs, as well as several rustic camping cabins available for rent.
delaware.fishingBoating: The park features a boat ramp for private vessels and offers seasonal rentals for canoes, kayaks, and pedal boats.

visitorCenter.name: Bald Cypress Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits about the swamp ecosystem, local history, and the unique flora and fauna of the area.

delaware.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $4.00 for Delaware residents and $8.00 for out-of-state visitors.
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and peak bird migration activity.
tips: Rent a kayak or canoe to explore the cypress swamp from the water for the best views.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer summer months.
Visit during the early morning hours to increase your chances of spotting wildlife.

delaware.name: Brandywine Creek State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Nestled along the scenic Brandywine Creek, this park offers rolling hills, historic stone walls, and lush forests just minutes from Wilmington.
delaware.fullDescription: Brandywine Creek State Park features a landscape shaped by centuries of agricultural use and the natural flow of the Brandywine River. The park is renowned for its steep slopes, tulip poplar forests, and expansive meadows that provide critical habitat for diverse wildlife. Visitors can explore the remnants of historic farmsteads and enjoy the tranquil beauty of the Piedmont region.

hikingTrails.name: Tulip Tree Woods Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path winding through a mature forest featuring impressive tulip poplar trees.

hikingTrails.name: Rocky Run Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the scenic Rocky Run stream, offering varied terrain and beautiful woodland views.

delaware.campingInfo: Brandywine Creek State Park does not offer overnight camping or cabin rentals.
delaware.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Brandywine Creek with a valid Delaware fishing license; no boat ramps are available.

visitorCenter.name: Brandywine Creek Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The nature center provides educational exhibits about the local ecosystem and park history.

delaware.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $4.00 for Delaware residents and $8.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as some trails can be muddy after rain.
Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities in the meadows.
Check the official website for seasonal hunting closures before planning your hike.

delaware.name: Killens Pond State Park
delaware.shortDescription: Killens Pond State Park is a scenic destination featuring a 66-acre millpond, a popular water park, and extensive trails through lush woodlands.
delaware.fullDescription: Located in the heart of Kent County, Killens Pond State Park centers around a historic millpond created in the late 18th century. The park offers a diverse landscape of hardwood forests, wetlands, and open fields. It is widely recognized for its family-friendly amenities, including a large water park, boat rentals, and a well-maintained campground, making it a premier outdoor recreation hub in Delaware.
thingsToDo: Swimming at the Killens Pond Water Park
Kayaking and canoeing on the millpond

hikingTrails.name: Pondside Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that winds along the edge of the millpond, offering excellent views of the water and local waterfowl.

hikingTrails.name: Deep Woods Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers through dense hardwood forests and provides a quiet, immersive nature experience away from the main park areas.

delaware.campingInfo: The park features 59 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as several camping cabins available for rent, all nestled in a wooded setting.
delaware.fishingBoating: The 66-acre pond is open for fishing and boating. Boat rentals including kayaks, canoes, and pedal boats are available seasonally at the boat house.

visitorCenter.name: Killens Pond Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The Nature Center features interactive exhibits about the local ecosystem, pond life, and the history of the millpond.

delaware.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $4.00 for Delaware residents and $8.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Summer for water activities and blooming flora.
tips: Visit the water park early on weekends as it reaches capacity quickly during peak summer days.
Bring insect repellent if you plan to hike the woodland trails during the warmer months.
Check the official website for seasonal boat rental availability before arriving.

delaware.name: White Clay Creek State Park
delaware.shortDescription: A sprawling natural sanctuary featuring lush woodlands, scenic creek valleys, and an extensive network of multi-use trails.
delaware.fullDescription: White Clay Creek State Park encompasses over 3,600 acres of diverse landscape, ranging from steep, wooded ravines to open meadows. The park is named for the creek that winds through its center, which is a designated National Wild and Scenic River. Historically, the area was home to various mills and agricultural operations, and today it serves as a vital corridor for wildlife and outdoor recreation enthusiasts.

hikingTrails.name: David English Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic path that follows the creek, perfect for families and casual walkers.

hikingTrails.name: Bryan's Field Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses through open fields and dense forest, offering excellent opportunities to spot local wildlife.

delaware.campingInfo: The park offers the Wedgewood Campground, which features sites for tents and RVs, including electric and water hookups.
delaware.fishingBoating: The creek is a popular destination for trout fishing; a valid Delaware fishing license and trout stamp are required.

visitorCenter.name: Carpenter Recreation Area Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park maps, trail information, and educational displays about the local ecosystem.

delaware.entranceFees: $4.00 for Delaware residents and $8.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Check the park website for seasonal hunting closures on certain trails.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months, especially near the creek.
Visit the disc golf course early on weekends to avoid crowds.
nearbyAttractions: Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area

delaware.name: Alapocas Run State Park
delaware.shortDescription: A scenic urban oasis featuring dramatic rock cliffs, lush woodlands, and the historic Blue Ball Barn.
delaware.fullDescription: Alapocas Run State Park is a unique natural area located in the heart of Wilmington, Delaware. The park is defined by the deep, rocky valley carved by Alapocas Run, which features impressive granite cliffs that are popular with rock climbers. The park also houses the Blue Ball Barn, a historic dairy barn that now serves as a cultural center and museum showcasing Delaware's history and folk art.
thingsToDo: Rock climbing on the granite cliffs
Exploring the Northern Delaware Greenway Trail

hikingTrails.name: Northern Delaware Greenway Trail
hikingTrails.description: A paved, multi-use trail that winds through the park's woodlands and connects to other regional greenway segments.

hikingTrails.name: Alapocas Woods Trail
hikingTrails.description: A natural surface trail that takes hikers along the creek and beneath the towering rock formations.

delaware.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available at Alapocas Run State Park.
delaware.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Alapocas Run, though the creek is generally too shallow for boating.

visitorCenter.name: Blue Ball Barn
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center features exhibits on Delaware's history, local art, and information about the park's natural resources.

delaware.entranceFees: Daily vehicle entrance fee is $4.00 for Delaware residents and $8.00 for out-of-state vehicles.
delaware.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Check the park website for rock climbing permit requirements before visiting.
Visit the Blue Ball Barn during operating hours to see the impressive folk art collection.
The park is very popular on weekends; arrive early to secure parking near the main trailheads.

florida.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
florida.shortDescription: The first undersea state park in the nation, famous for its vibrant coral reefs and colorful marine life.
florida.fullDescription: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, located in Key Largo, Florida, is a spectacular marine sanctuary covering approximately 70 nautical square miles of Atlantic Ocean. It was the first underwater park established in the United States. The park is renowned for its living coral reefs, colorful marine life, and mangrove swamps. Visitors can snorkel, scuba dive, take glass-bottom boat tours, or kayak through quiet mangrove channels.
thingsToDo: Snorkeling and scuba diving on the coral reef
Kayaking and canoeing through mangrove canals
Viewing the giant saltwater aquariums at the visitor center

hikingTrails.name: Mangrove Wilderness Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat wooden boardwalk winding deep into a dense mangrove swamp, featuring interpretive signs explaining the unique coastal swamp ecosystem.

hikingTrails.name: Wild Tamarind Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short loop path showcasing native hardwood hammock trees, wild tamarind, and beautiful tropical butterflies.

florida.campingInfo: The park features 47 modern campsites with full RV hookups (water, sewer, and electricity), modern restrooms with hot showers, and a laundry station.
florida.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park in accordance with Florida state laws. Boating is highly active. Snorkel boats and kayak rentals are available on-site at the park marina.

visitorCenter.name: John Pennekamp Visitor Center & Aquarium
visitorCenter.info: Features massive 30,000-gallon saltwater aquariums, historical marine displays, and a theater showing educational films about the coral reef.

florida.bestTimeToVisit: December to May for calm ocean waters, clear snorkeling visibility, and comfortable weather.
tips: Booking reef snorkel or glass-bottom boat tours online in advance is highly recommended, as they sell out daily.
Use reef-safe sunscreen to help protect the delicate, living coral reefs.
Rent a kayak to paddle through the quiet mangrove loops; it's one of the best ways to spot juvenile barracudas and wading herons.
nearbyAttractions: Key Largo Hammock State Botanical Site

georgia.name: Tallulah Gorge State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Georgia park around a 1,000-foot-deep gorge with six waterfalls and a suspension bridge.
georgia.fullDescription: Tallulah Gorge State Park covers 2,689 acres at Tallulah Falls in northeast Georgia. The Tallulah River runs through a gorge about 1,000 feet deep, dropping 500 feet in a mile over six waterfalls. Trails follow the rim to overlooks and a suspension bridge, and free permits from the Interpretive Center allow hiking to the gorge floor.

hikingTrails.name: Gorge Floor (Sliding Rock) Trail
hikingTrails.description: This very strenuous trail, which includes 1,000 stairs, needs a free same-day permit issued after a safety briefing and is limited to 100 permits per day.

hikingTrails.name: Stoneplace Trail
hikingTrails.description: The Stoneplace Trail leaves park property and enters an adjacent Wildlife Management Area, so hikers and bikers are encouraged to wear reflective orange.

hikingTrails.name: Rails to Trails path
hikingTrails.description: This paved path follows an old railroad bed and is suited to strollers and bicycles.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers 52 tent, trailer and RV campsites, a pioneer campground and 2 backcountry Adirondack shelters.
georgia.fishingBoating: Fishing and paddling are offered at the park's 63-acre lake, but kayaking at the Terrora Day Use Area is unavailable until construction of a new ADA kayak launch is finished.

visitorCenter.name: Tallulah Gorge State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

georgia.hours: Park 8 a.m. to dark; office 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
georgia.entranceFees: $10 daily ParkPass per vehicle (parking fee required; annual passes available)
georgia.address: 338 Jane Hurt Yarn Drive, Tallulah Falls, GA 30573
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is a great time to visit for leaf watching and the scheduled aesthetic and whitewater water releases, but if you want to hike the gorge floor, choose a non-release day.
tips: Gorge floor permits are free but limited to 100 per day and cannot be reserved. They are issued at the Interpretive Center after safety briefings at 8 a.m., 10 a.m. and 12 p.m., and on busy days they often run out early in the morning.

Hiking and climbing in the gorge are not allowed on water release dates, including aesthetic releases on October 21, 23 and 31 and November release weekends. Call ahead, because weather and water flow can also restrict access.
Pets are not allowed on the gorge floor, the Sliding Rock trail or the Hurricane Falls staircase to the suspension bridge. Leashed pets are welcome on rim trails.

georgia.name: Cloudland Canyon State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Georgia park on Lookout Mountain's west edge, overlooking a deep canyon with two waterfalls.
georgia.fullDescription: Cloudland Canyon State Park covers 3,485 acres near Trenton on the western edge of Lookout Mountain, where Sitton Gulch Creek has cut a gorge with elevations from 800 to over 1,800 feet. A strenuous stair trail descends to Cherokee Falls and Hemlock Falls at the canyon bottom. The park has cottages, campsites and backcountry sites.

hikingTrails.name: Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short round-trip trail that starts at the Main Overlook and offers views over the canyon.

hikingTrails.name: Waterfalls Trail
hikingTrails.description: This round-trip trail descends into the canyon on about 600 stairsteps each way to Cherokee Falls and Hemlock Falls.

hikingTrails.name: West Rim Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: This loop starts at the Daniels Creek Bridge and offers panoramic views of the canyon, Trenton and neighboring Sand Mountain.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers 75 tent, trailer and RV campsites, 30 walk-in campsites, 13 backcountry campsites and 4 pioneer campsites, plus 10 yurts and 18 cottages.
georgia.fishingBoating: The park has a fishing pond, but fishing is not allowed in Daniels and Sitton Gulch creeks in the canyon.

visitorCenter.name: Cloudland Canyon State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

georgia.hours: Park 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.; office 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
georgia.entranceFees: Parking fee required: $10 daily ParkPass per vehicle (annual ParkPass $70)
georgia.address: 122 Cloudland Canyon Park Road, Rising Fawn, GA 30738
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is a highlight for leaf watching on the Cumberland Plateau, and spring is good for waterfall flow, since the creeks feeding the falls can run low or dry in summer and early fall.
tips: Road work is underway at the park entrance, so expect one-lane traffic with flaggers during the day.
The Visitor Center is under construction. Follow the red and white signs to the temporary Visitor Center at the Group Lodge.
Parking is not included with overnight reservations, but overnight guests pay the daily ParkPass fee only once per vehicle for their whole stay.

georgia.name: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge
georgia.shortDescription: North Georgia park home to 729-foot Amicalola Falls, with a lodge and the trail to the Appalachian Trail's start.
georgia.fullDescription: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge covers 829 acres near Dawsonville. Its name comes from a Cherokee word meaning 'tumbling waters', and its 729-foot Amicalola Falls is called the highest in Georgia. An 8-mile trail from the park leads to Springer Mountain, the southern end of the Appalachian Trail. The park has a lodge, restaurant and cabins.

hikingTrails.name: Lodge Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, easy loop trail in Amicalola Falls State Park listed by Discover Georgia Outdoors.

hikingTrails.name: Appalachian Approach Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail begins at the base of Amicalola Falls and leads to Springer Mountain, the southern terminus of the Appalachian Trail.

georgia.campingInfo: The park's campground has 18 wooded campsites for tent camping and RVs, plus lodge rooms, cabins and glamping.
georgia.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

georgia.hours: Park 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.; visitor center 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
georgia.entranceFees: $10 GA State Park Pass per vehicle
georgia.address: 418 Amicalola Falls Lodge Drive, Dawsonville, GA 30534
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is a great time to visit for North Georgia's fall colors, when the park offers ranger-led hikes from the Visitor Center to the 729-foot waterfall.
tips: All vehicles entering the park require a $10 GA State Park Pass.
Black bears live in the area and have an excellent sense of smell, so store food and scented items securely.
Guests of the backcountry Len Foote Hike Inn check in at the park before hiking about 5 miles to the inn.
nearbyAttractions: Edge of the World on Amicalola Creek

georgia.name: Providence Canyon State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Known as Georgia's Little Grand Canyon, this park features massive gullies created by poor 19th-century farming practices.
georgia.fullDescription: Providence Canyon State Park is a geological wonder located in Stewart County, Georgia. The deep, colorful gullies were formed primarily due to erosion caused by poor farming practices in the 1800s. Today, the park offers stunning views of layered soil in shades of pink, orange, red, and purple, providing a unique landscape that contrasts sharply with the surrounding pine forests.

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers along the rim of the canyon before descending to the floor to explore the unique erosion patterns.

hikingTrails.name: White Blaze Trail
hikingTrails.description: A longer, more challenging trek that circles the entire canyon area, offering diverse terrain and expansive views.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers 6 walk-in campsites for tent camping. There are no RV hookups available at this location.
georgia.fishingBoating: Fishing is not permitted within the canyon area; however, nearby Florence Marina State Park offers extensive fishing and boating on Lake Walter F. George.

visitorCenter.name: Providence Canyon Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of the canyon's formation and local geology.

georgia.hours: 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming wildflowers.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the canyon floor can be muddy.
Bring plenty of water, especially if hiking the longer trails.
Visit during the week to avoid weekend crowds.

georgia.name: Sweetwater Creek State Park
georgia.shortDescription: A stunning park featuring the ruins of a Civil War-era textile mill and beautiful rapids along Sweetwater Creek.
georgia.fullDescription: Located just a short drive from downtown Atlanta, Sweetwater Creek State Park is a peaceful retreat known for its rich history and diverse landscape. The park is home to the ruins of the New Manchester Manufacturing Company, a textile mill burned during the Civil War. Visitors can explore the rugged terrain, which includes rocky bluffs, deep forests, and the rushing waters of the creek, providing a unique geological experience in the Georgia Piedmont.

hikingTrails.name: Red Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads hikers directly to the historic mill ruins and offers scenic views of the creek rapids.

hikingTrails.name: White Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that takes visitors through diverse forest terrain and offers elevated views of the park.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers several yurts for rent, as well as primitive campsites for tent camping. No full RV hookups are available.
georgia.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the reservoir and creek. Kayak and canoe rentals are available seasonally at the visitor center.

visitorCenter.name: Sweetwater Creek Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: A LEED-certified building featuring exhibits on the park's history, local wildlife, and a gift shop.

georgia.hours: 7:00 AM until dark daily
georgia.address: 1750 Mt Vernon Rd, Lithia Springs, GA 30122
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and beautiful foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lots fill up quickly.
Wear sturdy hiking shoes if you plan to visit the mill ruins, as the terrain is rocky.
Check the park website for guided historical tour schedules.

georgia.name: Fort Mountain State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Perched atop the Cohutta Mountains, this park is famous for its mysterious 855-foot-long ancient stone wall and breathtaking panoramic views.
georgia.fullDescription: Fort Mountain State Park is located in the Chattahoochee National Forest and is renowned for its mysterious ancient stone wall, which stretches 855 feet along the mountain ridge. The park offers a diverse landscape of hardwood forests, blueberry thickets, and mountain streams. Visitors can explore the rich history of the area, including the CCC-built stone fire tower, while enjoying the rugged beauty of the Southern Appalachian Mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Stone Wall Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads visitors to the mysterious ancient stone wall and offers scenic views of the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Cool Springs Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through lush forest areas, perfect for families and bird watching.

georgia.campingInfo: The park features 70 campsites for tents, trailers, and RVs, as well as 15 fully equipped cottages available for rent.
georgia.fishingBoating: The park features a 17-acre lake where visitors can enjoy fishing for bass and bream, as well as pedal boat and canoe rentals.

visitorCenter.name: Fort Mountain State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the stone wall.

georgia.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
georgia.address: 181 Fort Mountain Park Rd, Chatsworth, GA 30705
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for spectacular fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends during the fall as the parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring sturdy hiking boots as the terrain can be rocky and uneven.
Check the official website for seasonal swimming beach hours before planning your trip.

georgia.name: Vogel State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Nestled at the base of Blood Mountain in the Blue Ridge Mountains, Vogel State Park is one of Georgia's oldest and most beloved parks.
georgia.fullDescription: Established in 1931, Vogel State Park is located in the heart of the Chattahoochee National Forest. It features a 22-acre lake fed by mountain springs, offering a stunning backdrop for outdoor recreation. The park is famous for its Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) history, with a museum dedicated to the men who built the park during the Great Depression. The geology is defined by the rugged terrain of the Blue Ridge Mountains, providing visitors with dramatic vistas and lush forest landscapes.

hikingTrails.name: Trahlyta Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that circles the lake, offering beautiful views of the water and the surrounding mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Bear Hair Gap Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that climbs the ridge above the park, providing a challenging hike with rewarding panoramic views.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers 102 tent, trailer, and RV campsites, as well as 35 cottages available for rent, providing a variety of lodging options for visitors.
georgia.fishingBoating: Lake Trahlyta is open for fishing and non-motorized boating; pedal boat and kayak rentals are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Vogel State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and houses the CCC Museum exhibits.

georgia.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
georgia.address: 405 Vogel State Park Rd, Blairsville, GA 30512
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for the spectacular fall foliage or summer for swimming.
tips: Arrive early on weekends during the fall, as the park reaches capacity quickly.
Bring a camera for the stunning views of the lake from the dam.
Check the official website for seasonal events and guided ranger programs.

georgia.name: F.D. Roosevelt State Park
georgia.shortDescription: Georgia's largest state park, featuring the historic Pine Mountain Range and the scenic Liberty Bell Pool.
georgia.fullDescription: Located on the Pine Mountain Range, F.D. Roosevelt State Park is a sprawling 9,049-acre park that served as a retreat for President Franklin D. Roosevelt. The park offers breathtaking views of the rolling hills and dense forests of West Georgia. It is home to the famous Dowdell's Knob, a favorite overlook of the President, and provides a rich history of the Civilian Conservation Corps, who built many of the park's stone structures in the 1930s.
thingsToDo: Swimming in the Liberty Bell Pool

hikingTrails.name: Pine Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A premier trail that traverses the ridge of Pine Mountain, offering stunning vistas and access to waterfalls.

hikingTrails.name: Mountain Creek Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through lush forests and along the banks of Mountain Creek, perfect for birdwatching.

georgia.campingInfo: The park offers 111 campsites for tents, trailers, and RVs, as well as 21 fully equipped cottages for overnight stays.
georgia.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the park's lakes; however, no boat rentals are available, and only electric motors are allowed on private boats.

visitorCenter.name: Park Office and Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, trail information, and historical exhibits regarding President Roosevelt's time in the area.

georgia.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
georgia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit Dowdell's Knob at sunset for the best views in the park.
Check the park website for seasonal pool hours before planning a swim.
Bring sturdy hiking boots if you plan to tackle the longer sections of the Pine Mountain Trail.
nearbyAttractions: The Little White House Historic Site

kentucky.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Kentucky park named for 68-foot Cumberland Falls, one of the few places a moonbow is often seen.
kentucky.fullDescription: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park covers 1,657 acres southwest of Corbin, inside the Daniel Boone National Forest. Its main feature is 68-foot Cumberland Falls on the Cumberland River, one of the few places in the Western Hemisphere where a moonbow can often be seen on full-moon nights. About 20 miles of trails, a lodge and cabins are on site.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Falls Trail #9
hikingTrails.description: An out-and-back hike with a spur, listed by the park as one of its top five things to do.

hikingTrails.name: Cumberland Falls Trail #6
hikingTrails.description: The most popular route to the falls, beginning in front of Dupont Lodge with an excellent view of the river and Gatliff Bridge and a total descent of 200 ft.

hikingTrails.name: Cumberland River Trail #2
hikingTrails.description: Starts at the far end of the picnic area, follows the river upstream for 2 miles, then intersects the Moonbow Trail and ends at the falls parking area.

kentucky.campingInfo: Clifty Campground has 11 primitive sites and Ridgeline Campground has 40 sites with electric and water hookups, plus a service building with showers, restrooms, a grocery and a dump station.
kentucky.fishingBoating: The Cumberland River offers bass, catfish, panfish and roughfish, and a Kentucky fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

kentucky.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
kentucky.entranceFees: No entrance fee (per TripAdvisor; not stated on official page)
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is best: spring wildflowers bloom on Anvil Branch Trail, the stables and pool run Memorial Day to Labor Day, and a clear full-moon night gives a chance to see the moonbow.
tips: Pets are not permitted on the McCreary County side of the park because it is a dedicated Kentucky State Nature Preserve.
Dupont Lodge and Riverview Restaurant have been closed for renovations since December 1, 2025. Cabins, the falls, gift shop, welcome center and trails remain open.
Guided horseback rides are for ages 6 and up, cost $27 per person, and start on the hour from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. in season. Call ahead for weekend rides in May, September and October.
nearbyAttractions: Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area

kentucky.name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Kentucky park built around a 78-foot sandstone arch, next to the Red River Gorge.
kentucky.fullDescription: Natural Bridge State Resort Park lies on the Middle Fork of the Red River near Slade, next to the Red River Gorge and surrounded by the Daniel Boone National Forest. Its sandstone arch spans 78 feet and stands 65 feet high; Lover's Leap and Fat Man's Squeeze are other well-known spots. About 1,200 of its roughly 2,300 acres are a state nature preserve.

hikingTrails.name: Balanced Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: Over 600 steps lead to Natural Bridge, passing the on-park cave entrance and a large weathered sandstone balanced rock (trail currently closed part way).

hikingTrails.name: The Original Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail from Hemlock Lodge reaches the Natural Bridge arch and is described as deceptively strenuous and challenging.

hikingTrails.name: Hood's Branch Trail
hikingTrails.description: The official park page lists this trail as one of the best places in the park to spot birds.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park has two campgrounds, including Whittleton Campground, with improved and primitive sites and two service buildings with showers and restrooms.
kentucky.fishingBoating: Mill Creek Lake holds bass, bluegill, crappie, rainbow trout and catfish, has a launch ramp for fishing boats (electric trolling motors only), and requires a Kentucky fishing license.

visitorCenter.name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

kentucky.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
kentucky.entranceFees: Check the official park website for current fees.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: May and June are best for birding, and October brings fall foliage while the sky lift still runs through the last weekend of October.
tips: Dogs are not allowed on the park's hiking trails because of its Nature Preserve status, except the pet-friendly Whittleton Trail, which is accessed via Whittleton Campground.
Trail maps are available at Hemlock Lodge, and free fishing equipment can be borrowed through the park's loaner program.
The sky lift runs daily from the first weekend of April through the last weekend in October; call (606) 663-2922 for pricing.

kentucky.name: Dale Hollow Lake State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Kentucky resort park on Dale Hollow Lake's Frogue Peninsula, with an 18-hole golf course and lake overlooks.
kentucky.fullDescription: Dale Hollow Lake State Resort Park covers 3,400 acres on the Frogue Peninsula, on the north shore of the 27,600-acre Dale Hollow Reservoir. The park has an 18-hole golf course, about 12 miles of multi-use trails including the 1.8-mile Eagle Point Trail to Eagle Point Overlook, and the Island View Restaurant.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: The park's most important birding trail leads to Eagle Point Overlook, a good spot to view raptors and waterbirds.

hikingTrails.name: Boom Ridge-Eagle Point Connector Trail
hikingTrails.description: This connector trail offers less shrub-scrub habitat and more mixed forest habitat than Eagle Point Trail.

hikingTrails.name: Wolf Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A spur off the Boom Ridge Trail that follows an old logging road along a ridge top.

kentucky.campingInfo: The campground has 145 sites, 24 of them set aside for campers with horses, plus camping cabins with bunk beds and AC.
kentucky.fishingBoating: The park marina has nearly 200 slips, a fuel dock and day boat rentals, a concrete launch ramp is available, and fishing is year-round with a Kentucky Fishing License required.

visitorCenter.name: Dale Hollow Lake State Resort Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

kentucky.hours: Check the official park website for current hours.
kentucky.entranceFees: Check the official park website for current fees.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: April through October, when lodge rooms and cabins are available daily, suits boating and fishing, while December through February offers the best eagle sightings around the lake.
tips: No fishing pole? Ask at the lodge desk about the free fishing equipment loaner program.
Guided wild tours of Cindy Cave run Memorial Day through Labor Day ($10 per person, $8 for children 9 and under), and self-guided tours are prohibited.
WiFi is not available in the campground, and the lodge pool is for lodge guests only.

kentucky.name: Carter Caves State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of eastern Kentucky, this park is famous for its extensive cave systems and natural bridges.
kentucky.fullDescription: Carter Caves State Resort Park is a geological wonderland featuring one of the highest concentrations of caves in Kentucky. The park offers a unique blend of outdoor adventure and comfortable resort amenities, including the Lewis Caveland Lodge. Visitors can explore subterranean passages, hike through rugged sandstone cliffs, and marvel at the natural arches that define the landscape of the Appalachian foothills.

hikingTrails.name: 4C's Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that traverses the entire park, offering views of natural bridges and deep ravines.

hikingTrails.name: Natural Bridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path leading to one of the park's most iconic natural sandstone arches.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park features a campground with 29 sites equipped with water and electricity, plus primitive tent sites and 10 rental cottages.
kentucky.fishingBoating: Smoky Valley Lake offers excellent fishing for bass and bluegill, with seasonal canoe and pedal boat rentals available.

visitorCenter.name: Carter Caves Welcome Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on cave tour schedules, trail maps, and educational exhibits about local geology.

kentucky.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; fees apply for cave tours and recreational activities.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book cave tours in advance as they sell out quickly during peak season.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain can be rocky and slippery.
Bring a light jacket even in summer, as cave temperatures remain around 55 degrees Fahrenheit.

kentucky.name: Greenbo Lake State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of northeastern Kentucky, Greenbo Lake State Resort Park offers a serene escape centered around a beautiful 225-acre lake.
kentucky.fullDescription: Greenbo Lake State Resort Park is a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts, featuring a 225-acre lake that provides excellent fishing and boating opportunities. The park is situated within a lush, forested landscape that showcases the natural beauty of the Appalachian foothills. Visitors can explore miles of scenic trails, enjoy the full-service lodge, or participate in various recreational activities. The park's history is deeply connected to the region's coal mining past, and it serves as a peaceful retreat for families and nature lovers alike.
thingsToDo: Fishing for bass, bluegill, and catfish
Swimming at the seasonal outdoor pool
Playing a round of miniature golf

hikingTrails.name: Jesse Stuart Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through beautiful hardwood forests and offers glimpses of the local wildlife and diverse flora.

hikingTrails.name: Claylick Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path perfect for families, providing scenic views of the lake and surrounding hillsides.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park features a campground with 50 sites, including water and electric hookups, as well as a central service building with showers and restrooms.
kentucky.fishingBoating: The lake allows motorized boats and offers a boat ramp for public use, along with seasonal rentals for paddle boats and canoes.

visitorCenter.name: Greenbo Lake Lodge
visitorCenter.info: The lodge serves as the main hub for guest services, information, and park activities.

kentucky.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Bring your own fishing gear as the lake is well-stocked and popular with anglers.
Check the park website for seasonal lodge events and dining hours.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to explore the more rugged sections of the trail system.

kentucky.name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Experience the historic charm of Federal Hill, the inspiration for Stephen Foster's famous song, located in the heart of Bardstown.
kentucky.fullDescription: My Old Kentucky Home State Park centers around the historic Federal Hill mansion, built between 1795 and 1818. The site is famously associated with Stephen Foster, who visited his cousins here and was inspired to write the state song of Kentucky. The park offers a deep dive into 19th-century plantation life, architecture, and the cultural history of the Bluegrass region.

hikingTrails.name: Cedar Hill Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle walking path that winds through the wooded areas of the park, offering peaceful views of the landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Park Perimeter Loop
hikingTrails.description: This trail circles the outer edges of the park, providing a mix of open fields and shaded forest sections.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park features a well-maintained campground with 39 sites, offering water and electrical hookups, a dump station, and modern bathhouses.
kentucky.fishingBoating: Fishing is not permitted within the park boundaries; however, nearby lakes offer excellent fishing opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: My Old Kentucky Home Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides tickets for mansion tours, historical exhibits, and information on park events.

kentucky.entranceFees: Free park admission; mansion tours require a paid ticket.
kentucky.address: 501 E Stephen Foster Ave, Bardstown, KY 40004
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and beautiful foliage.
tips: Book your mansion tour in advance as they fill up quickly during peak season.
Visit during the summer months to catch the outdoor musical production.
Bring comfortable walking shoes for the historic grounds and trails.
nearbyAttractions: Oscar Getz Museum of Whiskey History

kentucky.name: Pine Mountain State Resort Park
kentucky.shortDescription: Kentucky's first state park, Pine Mountain offers breathtaking views of the Cumberland Mountains and a rich history of Appalachian culture.
kentucky.fullDescription: Established in 1924, Pine Mountain State Resort Park is nestled in the heart of the Appalachian Mountains. The park is famous for its rugged terrain, ancient rock formations, and the historic Wasioto Winds Golf Course. Visitors can explore the Chained Rock formation, which offers a panoramic view of the valley below, and enjoy the serene atmosphere of the surrounding hardwood forests.
thingsToDo: Dining at the Mountain View Restaurant

hikingTrails.name: Chained Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail leading to a massive boulder chained to the cliffside, offering spectacular views of Pineville.

hikingTrails.name: Hemlock Garden Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, relaxing walk through a lush forest area featuring native hemlock trees and diverse wildflowers.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park features 29 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as a full-service lodge with 30 rooms and several cottages.
kentucky.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in nearby waterways; however, the park itself is primarily focused on hiking and mountain recreation.

visitorCenter.name: Pine Mountain State Resort Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, trail information, and details on park events and lodging reservations.

kentucky.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Visit the Chained Rock at sunset for the best lighting and views.
Check the park website for seasonal golf course rates at Wasioto Winds.
Bring binoculars as the park is a prime location for bird watching.
nearbyAttractions: Dr. Thomas Walker State Historic Site

kentucky.name: John James Audubon State Park
kentucky.shortDescription: A beautiful tribute to the famous naturalist and artist, this park features a world-class museum and extensive nature trails.
kentucky.fullDescription: John James Audubon State Park honors the life and work of the renowned bird artist who lived in Henderson, Kentucky. The park is situated on rolling hills overlooking the Ohio River and features a museum housing one of the world's largest collections of Audubon's original art. The landscape is characterized by mature hardwood forests, serene lakes, and diverse habitats that support a wide variety of bird species, reflecting the natural beauty that inspired Audubon's masterpieces.

hikingTrails.name: Warbler Road Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through the forest, perfect for spotting migratory birds.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Glen Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers more elevation changes and leads hikers through dense woodland areas.

kentucky.campingInfo: The park offers a campground with 45 sites featuring water and electric hookups, as well as modern bathhouses and a dump station.
kentucky.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the park's lakes, which are stocked with bass and bluegill. No motorized boats are allowed.

visitorCenter.name: Audubon Museum and Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features extensive exhibits on the life of John James Audubon, his art, and local natural history.

kentucky.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds; museum admission fees apply.
kentucky.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for optimal bird migration viewing and comfortable hiking temperatures.
tips: Bring binoculars for bird watching as the park is a major stop for migratory species.
Check the museum schedule before visiting as hours can vary seasonally.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to explore the more rugged sections of the trail system.

louisiana.name: Chicot State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Spanning over 6,400 acres of rolling hills and water, Chicot State Park is Louisiana's largest state park and a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.
louisiana.fullDescription: Chicot State Park is located near Ville Platte, Louisiana, and features a massive 2,000-acre man-made lake filled with largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill, and redear sunfish. The park is characterized by its diverse landscape of beech-magnolia forests and bottomland hardwoods, providing a sanctuary for a wide variety of wildlife. Established in the 1940s, the park offers a rich history of Civilian Conservation Corps development and remains a central hub for camping, hiking, and water-based recreation in the region.
thingsToDo: Fishing and boating on Chicot Lake
Camping in modern cabins or RV sites

hikingTrails.name: Chicot State Park Trail
hikingTrails.description: A long-distance trail that loops around the lake, offering hikers a chance to experience the diverse forest ecosystems and scenic water views.

hikingTrails.name: Arboretum Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path through the Louisiana State Arboretum, showcasing native trees and plants with educational signage along the way.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options including premium campsites with water and electrical hookups, primitive tent sites, and several comfortable cabins overlooking the lake.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat launches and a boathouse. Fishing is excellent for bass and panfish; a valid Louisiana fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Chicot State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, fishing regulations, and educational exhibits about the local flora and fauna.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; free for seniors 62+ and children 3 and under.
louisiana.address: 3469 Chicot Park Rd, Ville Platte, LA 70586
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and peak bird migration.
tips: Bring insect repellent as the wooded areas can have mosquitoes.
Book your campsite or cabin well in advance, especially for weekends.
Visit the Louisiana State Arboretum located within the park boundaries for a unique botanical experience.

louisiana.name: Fontainebleau State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Located on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, this park offers stunning views and the historic ruins of a 19th-century sugar mill.
louisiana.fullDescription: Fontainebleau State Park is situated on the site of a sugar plantation established in 1829 by Bernard de Marigny de Mandeville. The park encompasses 2,800 acres of diverse ecosystems, including pine forests, marshes, and hardwood forests. Visitors can explore the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the old sugar mill and enjoy panoramic views of Lake Pontchartrain from the sandy beach.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the park's diverse forest habitats and offers excellent opportunities for wildlife viewing.

hikingTrails.name: Old Rail Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, paved trail that connects the park to the surrounding community, perfect for cycling and walking.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 126 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as several premium cabins located along the lakefront.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat launch for access to Lake Pontchartrain and excellent pier fishing opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Fontainebleau State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, local flora and fauna, and assistance with camping reservations.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; children under 3 and seniors 62+ are free.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and active bird migration.
tips: Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer months.
Visit the sugar mill ruins at sunset for the best photography lighting.
Check the official website for seasonal swimming advisories at the beach.

louisiana.name: Grand Isle State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Grand Isle State Park offers a unique coastal experience where visitors can enjoy the Gulf of Mexico's pristine beaches and world-class saltwater fishing.
louisiana.fullDescription: Located on a barrier island at the end of Louisiana Highway 1, Grand Isle State Park is the only state-owned beach in Louisiana. The park provides a sanctuary for migratory birds and offers visitors a chance to explore the unique ecosystem of the Gulf Coast. With its history shaped by hurricanes and the resilience of the local community, the park serves as a vital recreational hub for swimming, birding, and fishing.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, scenic trail that winds through the coastal dunes and provides excellent opportunities for bird watching.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Walk
hikingTrails.description: A relaxing walk along the shoreline of the Gulf of Mexico, perfect for finding seashells and enjoying the ocean breeze.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 49 premium campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as a designated tent camping area near the beach.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park features a 400-foot fishing pier and excellent surf fishing opportunities for speckled trout, redfish, and flounder.

visitorCenter.name: Grand Isle State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, local wildlife, and current beach conditions.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; children 3 and under and seniors 62+ are free.
louisiana.address: 1 Admiral Craik Dr, Grand Isle, LA 70358
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and peak bird migration.
tips: Bring plenty of sunscreen and insect repellent as the coastal sun and mosquitoes can be intense.
Check the official website for beach closure notices due to high tides or weather events.
Visit during the spring migration to see hundreds of species of birds passing through the island.

louisiana.name: Bogue Chitto State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of Washington Parish, Bogue Chitto State Park offers a diverse landscape ranging from cypress-tupelo swamps to upland forests.
louisiana.fullDescription: Bogue Chitto State Park is a 1,786-acre site that showcases the natural beauty of Louisiana's Florida Parishes. The park is defined by the Bogue Chitto River, which winds through the property, creating dramatic bluffs and sandy beaches. Visitors can explore a variety of ecosystems, including hardwood forests and lush wetlands, making it a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts seeking both adventure and tranquility.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on the Bogue Chitto River
Hiking and mountain biking on the Gorge Run Trail

hikingTrails.name: Gorge Run Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the park's unique hilly terrain and offers views of the river bluffs.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop perfect for families, showcasing the diverse flora and fauna of the local hardwood forest.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 81 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 13 premium cabins available for overnight stays.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat launch for easy access to the Bogue Chitto River and several fishing ponds stocked with freshwater fish.

visitorCenter.name: Bogue Chitto State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local ecosystem.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; free for seniors 62+ and children under 3.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal outdoor activity conditions.
tips: Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer months.
Book your campsite or cabin well in advance as they fill up quickly on weekends.
Check the river levels before planning a kayaking trip to ensure safe conditions.

louisiana.name: Bayou Segnette State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Located just across the Mississippi River from New Orleans, this park offers a unique blend of swampy wetlands and modern recreational facilities.
louisiana.fullDescription: Bayou Segnette State Park provides access to both freshwater and saltwater environments, making it a premier destination for anglers and nature enthusiasts. The park features a wave pool, boat launches, and a variety of habitats ranging from cypress swamps to marshlands, showcasing the diverse ecosystem of coastal Louisiana.

hikingTrails.name: Nutria Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the swampy terrain, offering excellent opportunities to spot local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible loop perfect for families looking to experience the park's diverse flora.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park offers 98 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 16 vacation cabins located on the water.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park features a public boat launch providing access to Bayou Segnette and the surrounding waterways for both freshwater and saltwater fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Bayou Segnette Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local wetlands.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; children under 3 and seniors 62+ are free.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for milder temperatures and active wildlife.
tips: Bring plenty of insect repellent, especially during warmer months.
Check the wave pool schedule in advance as it is seasonal.
Early morning is the best time to spot alligators and migratory birds.
nearbyAttractions: Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve

louisiana.name: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: A premier destination for water sports and outdoor recreation, featuring a massive 2,700-acre reservoir in Northeast Louisiana.
louisiana.fullDescription: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park offers a unique blend of modern recreational facilities and natural beauty. The park is centered around a 2,700-acre man-made reservoir that provides excellent opportunities for boating, fishing, and water skiing. The area is rich in history, located near the ancient Poverty Point World Heritage Site, and features diverse wetlands and pine forests that provide a habitat for a variety of wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail that winds through the wooded areas of the park, perfect for spotting local birds and wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Reservoir Perimeter Trail
hikingTrails.description: Offers scenic views of the water and access to various fishing spots along the shoreline.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 54 premium campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 8 deluxe cabins overlooking the reservoir.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park features a world-class boat launch and a marina. Fishing is excellent for largemouth bass, crappie, and bluegill.

visitorCenter.name: Poverty Point Reservoir Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, fishing regulations, and local history, along with a gift shop.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; free for seniors 62+ and children 3 and under.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal fishing conditions.
tips: Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer months.
Check the official website for current fishing tournament schedules that may affect boat ramp availability.
Book your cabin or campsite well in advance as they fill up quickly on weekends.

louisiana.name: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Nestled in the heart of the Atchafalaya Basin, this park offers a gateway to the unique beauty of Louisiana's swamp and bayou landscapes.
louisiana.fullDescription: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park is located on the edge of the Atchafalaya Basin, the nation's largest river swamp. The park provides visitors with a chance to explore the diverse ecosystem of the bayou, featuring elevated boardwalks, cypress-tupelo forests, and extensive waterways. Historically, the area was once part of the Atchafalaya spillway, and today it serves as a premier destination for those looking to experience the authentic Cajun wilderness through boating, fishing, and wildlife observation.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking through bayou trails
Fishing for bass, crappie, and bream
Bird watching in the Atchafalaya Basin

hikingTrails.name: The Boardwalk Trail
hikingTrails.description: An accessible, elevated wooden path that winds through the cypress swamp, offering excellent views of the water and local flora.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A winding trail that takes hikers deeper into the hardwood forest, providing opportunities to spot deer and various bird species.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 48 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 18 waterfront cabins that offer a comfortable stay directly on the bayou.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat launch for motorized boats and provides rentals for canoes and kayaks to navigate the scenic bayou waterways.

visitorCenter.name: Lake Fausse Pointe Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides educational exhibits on the Atchafalaya Basin ecosystem, park maps, and assistance from knowledgeable park rangers.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; children under 3 and seniors 62+ are free.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Fall and Spring, when temperatures are mild and mosquito activity is lower.
tips: Bring plenty of insect repellent, as the swamp environment can be buggy.
Rent a canoe or kayak from the park office to explore the water trails properly.
Check the water levels before your trip, as high water can occasionally impact trail accessibility.

louisiana.name: Palmetto Island State Park
louisiana.shortDescription: Nestled along the Vermilion River, this park offers a lush, tropical escape featuring native palmetto trees and diverse wetland ecosystems.
louisiana.fullDescription: Palmetto Island State Park is a unique natural area in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana, characterized by its dense stands of dwarf palmetto trees and mature hardwood forests. The park provides visitors with an immersive experience in the Louisiana bayou landscape, featuring a boat launch, hiking trails, and a water playground. The geology is defined by the meandering Vermilion River, which creates a rich habitat for diverse wildlife and provides excellent opportunities for paddling and fishing.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on the Vermilion River

hikingTrails.name: Palmetto Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the heart of the park's signature palmetto groves and hardwood forest.

hikingTrails.name: River Trail
hikingTrails.description: Follows the banks of the Vermilion River, offering excellent views of the water and opportunities to spot local wildlife.

louisiana.campingInfo: The park features 96 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as six modern cabins available for rent, nestled in a quiet, wooded setting.
louisiana.fishingBoating: The park features a boat launch providing access to the Vermilion River, popular for freshwater fishing and recreational boating.
wildlife: Various species of snakes and turtles

visitorCenter.name: Palmetto Island Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides information on park history, local ecology, and trail maps, along with a small gift shop.

louisiana.entranceFees: $3.00 per person; free for seniors 62+ and children 3 and under.
louisiana.bestTimeToVisit: Fall and Spring, when temperatures are mild and the humidity is lower.
tips: Bring plenty of insect repellent, especially during the warmer months.
Check the water playground schedule before visiting if you are traveling with children.
Early morning is the best time to spot alligators and other wildlife along the river.

maryland.name: Assateague State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Maryland barrier-island park on Assateague Island's north end, with ocean beach and wild horses.
maryland.fullDescription: Assateague State Park sits at the north end of Assateague Island in Worcester County, between the Atlantic and Sinepuxent Bay, reached by the Verrazano Bridge and bordered by Assateague Island National Seashore. Feral horses roam freely on the beach, marshes and campground. The campground has 350 sites, and the restored 18th-century Rackliffe House holds a heritage center.
maryland.campingInfo: The campground has 342 campsites and 3 Youth Group sites, each with a fire ring and picnic table, and most sites can be reserved from the last week of April through the last weekend of October at 1-888-432-2267 or parkreservations.maryland.gov.
maryland.fishingBoating: The park's two miles of ocean beaches offer fishing (not permitted in the guarded swim sector), and the bayside lets visitors explore secluded coves by canoe or kayak.

visitorCenter.name: Assateague State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

maryland.hours: Day use area: 7 a.m. to sunset, year-round
maryland.entranceFees: $5.00 per vehicle after Labor Day to the Friday before Memorial Day; $5.00 per person Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through October suits this oceanfront barrier-island park: lifeguards are on duty Memorial Day to Labor Day, and campsites can be reserved through the last weekend of October.
tips: Stay at least 40 feet (a bus length) from the wild horses. Do not stop or park along roadways, and secure all food, because the horses bite, kick and can carry rabies.
When the contact booth is unstaffed off-season, entry uses a self-registration honor system, and payment is cash only in the provided envelope.
Lifeguards are on duty only from Memorial Day to Labor Day, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Surfing, kayaking and fishing are not allowed in the flagged swim sector.

maryland.name: Cunningham Falls State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Catoctin Mountain park with 78-foot Cunningham Falls, Maryland's largest cascading waterfall, and a lake.
maryland.fullDescription: Cunningham Falls State Park lies west of Thurmont on Catoctin Mountain. It is home to 78-foot Cunningham Falls, the largest cascading waterfall in Maryland, a 43-acre man-made lake, and the ruins of a historic Catoctin iron furnace. A boardwalk trail leads to the falls.

hikingTrails.name: Cunningham Falls Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: This is the park's most popular trail and leads to Cunningham Falls, the largest cascading waterfall in Maryland.

hikingTrails.name: Cunningham Falls Lower Trail and Cliff Trail Loop
hikingTrails.description: This loop near Thurmont reaches Maryland's tallest waterfall and has both easy and rugged terrain.

hikingTrails.name: Catoctin Trail
hikingTrails.description: The longest trail in the park area, the Catoctin Trail runs 27 miles starting from Gambrill.

maryland.campingInfo: Campsites and camper cabins are available from April until October at the William Houck Area and Manor Area campgrounds.
maryland.fishingBoating: The lake offers fishing, canoeing, boat rentals and a boat launch (no gasoline motors), and there is an accessible fishing pier in the William Houck Area.

visitorCenter.name: Cunningham Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

maryland.hours: 8 a.m. to sunset, April–October; 10 a.m. to sunset, November–March
maryland.entranceFees: Off-peak (after Labor Day weekend to the Friday of Memorial Day weekend) and Manor Area: $3/vehicle MD residents, $5/vehicle non-residents. Houck Area, Memorial Day–Labor Day: per person, $3 MD/$5 non-MD on weekdays and $5 MD/$7 non-MD on weekends and holidays.
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall weekdays are ideal, because summer weekends and holidays often fill the park to capacity. The Maple Syrup Festival runs the 1st and 2nd weekends in March.
tips: On warm spring and summer weekends and holidays, the Lake, Beach and Falls Area may close when full. Arrive early, and if your group is in several vehicles, arrive at the same time, since late cars are turned away even if others are already inside.
Cell service is limited, so do not rely on cell phones for communication in the park.
Campsites M1–M31 are at the Manor Area Campground, 6709 Cunningham Falls Park Rd, not at the main park address. Camping permits are also provided there.

maryland.name: Patapsco Valley State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Maryland's largest state park, stretching 32 miles along the Patapsco River near Baltimore.
maryland.fullDescription: Patapsco Valley State Park runs 32 miles along the Patapsco River south and west of Baltimore and covers over 14,000 acres, making it Maryland's largest state park; it dates from 1906. Its areas include McKeldin, with multi-use trails and a disc golf course, and Avalon, with the Swinging Bridge and a visitor center in an old mill building.

hikingTrails.name: Grist Mill Trail
hikingTrails.description: The official park page offers a Grist Mill Trail self-guided hike.

hikingTrails.name: Medicine Tree Trail
hikingTrails.description: The official park page lists the Medicine Tree Trail among its suggested activities.

maryland.campingInfo: Camping is offered, with campgrounds in the Hilton and Hollofield Areas, and reservations can be made at 1-888-432-CAMP or parkreservations.maryland.gov.
maryland.fishingBoating: The park offers fishing and canoeing along the Patapsco River, and fishing and boat launch use are permitted outside regular park hours.

visitorCenter.name: Patapsco Valley State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

maryland.hours: 9 a.m. to sunset
maryland.entranceFees: Apr–Oct: weekdays $2/vehicle MD residents, $4/vehicle out-of-state; weekends & holidays $3/person in-state, $5/person out-of-state
maryland.address: 8020 Baltimore National Pike, Ellicott City, MD 21043
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Fall is a great time to visit for foliage and owl-spotting, and weekdays or early mornings help you avoid weekend capacity closures.
tips: Arrive early on weekends and summer holidays, because the Avalon, Hollofield and Daniels areas often close when they reach capacity.
Bring a park map with you.
Pets are prohibited in the Hilton Area campground and the Pickall Area, so check the pet policy before you bring a dog.

maryland.name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Deep Creek Lake State Park offers a stunning mountain retreat featuring Maryland's largest freshwater lake and extensive recreational opportunities.
maryland.fullDescription: Located in Garrett County, Deep Creek Lake State Park encompasses over 1,800 acres of forest and shoreline. The park provides access to the 3,900-acre Deep Creek Lake, which was originally created in the 1920s for hydroelectric power. The area is characterized by its rolling Appalachian mountain terrain, diverse hardwood forests, and rich biodiversity, making it a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts year-round.

hikingTrails.name: Meadow Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers a scenic trek through dense forest and provides glimpses of local wildlife and native flora.

hikingTrails.name: Indian Turnip Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, family-friendly loop that winds through the park's wooded areas, perfect for birdwatching.

maryland.campingInfo: The park features 112 campsites, including 26 sites with electric hookups, and offers modern bathhouses with hot showers.
maryland.fishingBoating: The park provides a public boat launch and a designated fishing area; a valid Maryland fishing license is required.
