visitorCenter.name: Discovery Center
visitorCenter.info: The Discovery Center features interactive exhibits on the natural history, geology, and cultural heritage of the Deep Creek Lake area.

maryland.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
maryland.entranceFees: $3.00 per vehicle for Maryland residents, $5.00 per vehicle for out-of-state visitors.
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Summer for water activities or Autumn for spectacular fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the park often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Check the water quality reports on the official website before swimming.
Bring bug spray, especially if you plan on hiking the wooded trails.

maryland.name: Swallow Falls State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Home to Maryland's highest free-falling waterfall, Swallow Falls State Park features breathtaking scenery along the Youghiogheny River.
maryland.fullDescription: Swallow Falls State Park is located nine miles north of Oakland, Maryland, and is home to Muddy Creek Falls, a spectacular 53-foot waterfall. The park's landscape is defined by the Youghiogheny River, which flows through rocky gorges and ancient hemlock forests. The area is geologically significant for its rugged terrain and provides a glimpse into the natural beauty of the Allegheny Mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds along the edge of the Youghiogheny River and provides excellent views of Muddy Creek Falls and Swallow Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Tolliver Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that leads visitors to the smaller but picturesque Tolliver Falls, perfect for families.

maryland.campingInfo: The park offers 65 campsites, including some with electric hookups, nestled within a beautiful old-growth hemlock forest. Reservations are highly recommended during peak season.
maryland.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Youghiogheny River, which is a popular spot for trout fishing. No boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Swallow Falls Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: The station provides park maps, safety information, and educational displays about the local ecosystem.

maryland.hours: 8:00 AM to Sunset daily
maryland.entranceFees: $3.00 per vehicle for Maryland residents and $5.00 per vehicle for out-of-state visitors.
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for high water levels or autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails near the river can be slippery and rocky.
Visit on a weekday to avoid heavy crowds during the summer months.
Pack a camera, as the waterfall views are some of the best in the state.

maryland.name: Sandy Point State Park
maryland.shortDescription: A premier outdoor recreation area located on the northwestern shore of the Chesapeake Bay, offering stunning views of the Bay Bridge.
maryland.fullDescription: Sandy Point State Park is a 786-acre Maryland State Park located along the northwestern shore of the Chesapeake Bay. The park provides a variety of recreational activities, including swimming, fishing, crabbing, and boating. Its strategic location offers visitors unparalleled views of the iconic William Preston Lane Jr. Memorial Bridge, commonly known as the Chesapeake Bay Bridge. The park's diverse landscape includes sandy beaches, marshlands, and forest areas, making it a vital habitat for local wildlife and a popular destination for nature enthusiasts.
thingsToDo: Fishing and crabbing from the jetties

hikingTrails.name: Symbi Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, scenic nature trail that winds through the wooded areas of the park, perfect for a quick walk.

hikingTrails.name: Shoreline Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat path that follows the coastline, offering excellent opportunities for bird watching and bay views.

maryland.campingInfo: Sandy Point State Park does not offer overnight camping or cabin rentals.
maryland.fishingBoating: The park features a large boat ramp facility with multiple lanes and a dedicated fishing area on the jetties.

visitorCenter.name: Sandy Point Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: The ranger station provides park information, maps, and assistance with facility rentals and park regulations.

maryland.hours: 7:00 AM to Sunset daily
maryland.entranceFees: Fees range from $4.00 to $7.00 per person depending on residency and season; check the official website for current pricing.
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for swimming and outdoor activities.
tips: The park reaches capacity quickly on summer weekends; arrive early in the morning.
Check the official website for real-time park closure updates during peak season.
Bring your own fishing gear and bait if you plan to fish from the jetties.

maryland.name: Elk Neck State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Located on a peninsula between the Elk and Northeast Rivers, this park offers stunning views of the Chesapeake Bay and diverse recreational opportunities.
maryland.fullDescription: Elk Neck State Park is situated on a peninsula in Cecil County, Maryland, where the Elk and Northeast Rivers meet the Chesapeake Bay. The park's unique geology features sandy shorelines, marshlands, and wooded bluffs. It is home to the historic Turkey Point Lighthouse, which has guided mariners since 1833. The park provides a rich habitat for diverse wildlife and offers visitors a chance to explore the natural beauty of the upper Chesapeake region.

hikingTrails.name: Turkey Point Lighthouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic, mostly flat trail that leads visitors through a wooded area to the historic Turkey Point Lighthouse with panoramic views of the bay.

hikingTrails.name: Beaver Marsh Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through diverse forest habitats and offers excellent opportunities for observing local wildlife and wetland ecosystems.

maryland.campingInfo: The park features several camping loops with over 250 campsites, including options for tent camping, RVs with electric hookups, and rustic cabins available for rent.
maryland.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat launch ramp on the Northeast River and designated areas for shoreline fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Elk Neck State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides maps, trail information, and assistance with camping reservations and park regulations.

maryland.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
maryland.entranceFees: $3.00 per vehicle for Maryland residents and $5.00 per vehicle for out-of-state visitors.
maryland.address: 4395 Turkey Point Rd, North East, MD 21901
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild weather and migratory bird watching.
tips: Visit the Turkey Point Lighthouse early in the morning to avoid crowds and enjoy the best lighting for photography.
Check the park website for seasonal swimming beach closures before planning your trip.
Bring insect repellent, especially if you plan to hike the marsh trails during the summer months.
nearbyAttractions: Fair Hill Natural Resources Management Area

maryland.name: Rocky Gap State Park
maryland.shortDescription: Nestled in the mountains of Allegany County, Rocky Gap State Park features a stunning 243-acre lake and rugged mountain scenery.
maryland.fullDescription: Rocky Gap State Park is located in Allegany County, Maryland, and encompasses over 3,000 acres of public land. The park is defined by the dramatic Rocky Gap Run, which cuts through a narrow gorge, and the expansive Lake Habeeb, known for its exceptionally clear water. The area is geologically significant, featuring the Evitts Mountain and the rugged terrain of the Appalachian region, providing a diverse habitat for wildlife and a scenic backdrop for outdoor recreation.
thingsToDo: Boating and kayaking on Lake Habeeb

hikingTrails.name: Evitts Homesite Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail that winds through the forest and offers a glimpse into the historical homesteading of the region.

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail provides hikers with elevated views of the rugged gorge and the surrounding mountain landscape.

maryland.campingInfo: The park offers a large campground with 278 campsites, including sites with electric hookups and several mini-cabins available for rent.
maryland.fishingBoating: Lake Habeeb is a popular fishing destination stocked with trout; boat rentals including kayaks and canoes are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Rocky Gap Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with camping reservations.

maryland.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
maryland.entranceFees: $3.00 per vehicle for Maryland residents; $5.00 per vehicle for out-of-state visitors.
maryland.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities and fall foliage viewing.
tips: Lake Habeeb is famous for its clear water, so bring goggles for swimming.
Make camping reservations well in advance during the summer months as sites fill up quickly.
Check the official website for seasonal swimming beach hours and lifeguard availability.

mississippi.name: Tishomingo State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Mississippi park in the Appalachian foothills on the Natchez Trace, known for Bear Creek Canyon's sandstone outcrops.
mississippi.fullDescription: Tishomingo State Park lies about 45 miles northeast of Tupelo at Milepost 304 of the Natchez Trace Parkway. Its main feature is Bear Creek Canyon and its large sandstone outcrops. Seven trails of up to 3 miles pass springs, waterfalls, cliffs and rock walls, and the park has CCC-era facilities, cabins and campsites.

hikingTrails.name: CCC Camp Trail
hikingTrails.description: An easy hiking route that winds through Tishomingo State Park.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park offers an RV campground, a tent campground, cabins/cottages and a group camp, with overnight camping reservable through MDWFP.
mississippi.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in Bear Creek and in 45-acre Haynes Lake, which is stocked with catfish, bream and bass and has a boat launch; a seasonal 6.25-mile canoe float trip runs down Bear Creek.

visitorCenter.name: Tishomingo State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

mississippi.hours: 8 AM to 5 PM, seven days a week
mississippi.entranceFees: $2.00 per person; age 5 and under free
mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall are ideal: spring brings wildflowers along the trails and the seasonal Bear Creek float trip, and fall offers mild weather among the hardwood forests.
tips: The Bear Creek canoe float trip is seasonal and requires an advance reservation through the park office at (662) 438-6914. It costs $40, allows a maximum of two people per canoe, and participants must report to the Park Office at 9:00 am.
Swimming is not allowed in Haynes Lake or Bear Creek. Use the park's swimming pool instead.
A Mississippi fishing license is required for ages 16 to 65 and can be purchased at the park office.

mississippi.name: Percy Quin State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Mississippi park near McComb on Lake Tangipahoa, with cabins, a lodge and an 18-hole golf course.
mississippi.fullDescription: Percy Quin State Park lies about 7 miles southwest of McComb off I-55 and surrounds 490-acre Lake Tangipahoa, an impoundment of the Tangipahoa River. It has campsites, cabins, villas and a lodge, a 4-mile nature trail and the 18-hole Quail Hollow golf course.

hikingTrails.name: Percy Quin State Park Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: An out-and-back trail with about 265 ft of elevation gain that takes about 2–2.5 hours to complete.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park offers an RV campground, a tent campground and cabins/cottages, with reservations available for day use and overnight camping.
mississippi.fishingBoating: The 490-acre Lake Tangipahoa has a boat launch (fee; daily or annual permits), a covered 36-slip marina, a fish cleaning station, and allows water and jet skiing.

visitorCenter.name: Percy Quin State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

mississippi.hours: 8 AM to 5 PM, seven days a week
mississippi.entranceFees: $2.00 per person; age 5 and under free
mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall usually bring milder weather for hiking and lake activities in southern Mississippi, while summer is hot but suits water skiing and swimming.
tips: Register at the ranger station/gate house when checking in to park facilities.
The boat launch on Lake Tangipahoa requires a fee, with daily or annual permits available.
Use of the five tennis courts is included with the $2.00 day-use entry fee. Call the park office to reserve one of the four picnic pavilions.

mississippi.name: J.P. Coleman State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Mississippi park on the Tennessee River and Pickwick Lake north of Iuka, known for smallmouth bass fishing.
mississippi.fullDescription: J.P. Coleman State Park lies ten miles north of Iuka on the banks of the Tennessee River and 47,500-acre Pickwick Lake, and is named for former Mississippi governor James P. Coleman. The lake is known for smallmouth bass. The park has campsites, cabins, cottages, a motel, a swimming pool and miniature golf.
mississippi.campingInfo: The park offers RV and tent campgrounds plus cabins/cottages, and you check in for camping at the visitor center in the J.P. Coleman Lodge.
mississippi.fishingBoating: Pickwick Lake, a 47,500-acre freshwater lake, offers fishing, boating and water skiing, and the park has a boat launch ramp with trailer parking and a marina with fuel sales.

visitorCenter.name: J.P. Coleman State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

mississippi.hours: 8 AM to 5 PM, seven days a week
mississippi.entranceFees: $2.00 per person; ages 5 and under free
mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early fall is best for water sports and the seasonal swimming pool and miniature golf, while cooler months suit quieter fishing and camping.
tips: The marina fuel dock runs 24/7 with a card reader, but it sells only unleaded non-ethanol fuel and no diesel.
The pool is open seasonally Thursday through Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. It has no lifeguards, armbands are required, and children under 16 need an adult.
Register at the visitor center in the J.P. Coleman Lodge to use park facilities and to check in for lodging and camping.

mississippi.name: Clarkco State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of East Mississippi, Clarkco State Park offers a serene escape with lush pine forests and a beautiful 65-acre lake.
mississippi.fullDescription: Clarkco State Park is a hidden gem located in the pine-forested hills of Clarke County. Established in 1938, the park features a 65-acre lake that serves as the centerpiece for outdoor recreation. The park's landscape is characterized by towering loblolly pines and hardwoods, providing a tranquil environment for visitors to enjoy nature, history, and outdoor activities. It is a popular destination for families and outdoor enthusiasts looking for a peaceful retreat in the heart of Mississippi.
thingsToDo: Camping in RV or tent sites

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the dense pine forest, offering great opportunities for bird watching and spotting local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Perimeter Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the shoreline of the lake, providing scenic water views and access to various fishing spots.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park offers 43 RV campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as primitive tent sites. Additionally, there are 20 cabins available for rent overlooking the lake.
mississippi.fishingBoating: The 65-acre lake is stocked with bass, bream, and catfish. Boat ramps are available for private boats, and electric trolling motors are permitted.

visitorCenter.name: Clarkco State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The main office provides park information, camping registration, and assistance with facility rentals.

mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and beautiful foliage.
tips: Make cabin reservations well in advance as they fill up quickly during peak seasons.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer summer months.
Check the official website for current fishing regulations and permit requirements.

mississippi.name: Roosevelt State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Located in the Bienville National Forest, Roosevelt State Park offers a scenic escape with beautiful pine forests and the tranquil Shadow Lake.
mississippi.fullDescription: Roosevelt State Park is situated in the heart of Mississippi, offering a diverse landscape of rolling hills and lush forests. Named after President Franklin D. Roosevelt, the park was developed during the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps. It features the 114-acre Shadow Lake, which serves as a centerpiece for water-based recreation, and provides a peaceful retreat for nature enthusiasts, families, and outdoor adventurers alike.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the pine forest, offering great opportunities for bird watching and spotting local flora.

hikingTrails.name: Lakeview Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the perimeter of Shadow Lake, providing scenic water views and varied terrain.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park offers 109 RV campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 15 vacation cabins overlooking the lake.
mississippi.fishingBoating: Shadow Lake is well-stocked for fishing, and the park provides a boat ramp for private watercraft; boat rentals are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Roosevelt State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The main office provides park information, check-in services for campers, and maps of the trail system.

mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and beautiful foliage.
tips: Make cabin reservations well in advance as they are popular year-round.
Bring insect repellent during the warmer months.
Check the official website for seasonal pool operating hours.

mississippi.name: Paul B. Johnson State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Nestled in the heart of the Pine Belt, Paul B. Johnson State Park offers a serene escape with beautiful forests and the sparkling Geiger Lake.
mississippi.fullDescription: Paul B. Johnson State Park is located in the middle of Mississippi's pine forest region. The park is characterized by majestic longleaf and loblolly pines, delicate dogwoods, and ancient oaks. The centerpiece of the park is the 225-acre Geiger Lake, which provides excellent opportunities for fishing and water recreation. Established to provide outdoor recreation for the Hattiesburg area, the park features diverse ecosystems that support a wide variety of wildlife and native flora.
thingsToDo: Swimming at the designated beach area

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the dense pine forest, offering great opportunities to spot local bird species.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Perimeter Path
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the shoreline of Geiger Lake, providing scenic water views and access to various fishing spots.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park features 125 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 25 modern cabins available for rent overlooking the lake.
mississippi.fishingBoating: Geiger Lake is well-stocked with bass, bream, and catfish. Boat ramps are available for public use, and private boats are permitted.

visitorCenter.name: Park Office and Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The main office provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping and cabin reservations.

mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and beautiful foliage.
tips: Bring insect repellent during the warmer months as the pine forest can be humid.
Book your cabin or campsite well in advance, especially for summer weekends.
Check the official website for current fishing regulations before heading to the lake.

mississippi.name: Hugh White State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Grenada Lake, Hugh White State Park offers premier fishing, boating, and outdoor recreation in the heart of Mississippi.
mississippi.fullDescription: Hugh White State Park is situated on the banks of the 35,000-acre Grenada Lake, one of the largest reservoirs in the state. The park is renowned for its exceptional crappie fishing and serves as a hub for water-based recreation. Surrounded by lush forests and rolling hills, the park provides a serene escape for nature lovers, offering well-maintained facilities for camping, picnicking, and wildlife observation.

hikingTrails.name: Lakeview Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds along the shoreline of Grenada Lake, offering excellent birdwatching opportunities.

hikingTrails.name: Forest Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers through the dense hardwood forests surrounding the park, featuring native flora and fauna.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park features 75 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as several vacation cabins overlooking the lake.
mississippi.fishingBoating: The park offers multiple boat ramps for easy access to Grenada Lake, which is nationally recognized for its trophy crappie fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Hugh White Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on fishing regulations, boat ramp access, and campsite reservations.

mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and peak fishing seasons.
tips: Check the current lake levels before planning your boating trip.
Bring insect repellent during the warmer summer months.
Make cabin reservations well in advance as they fill up quickly during fishing tournaments.

mississippi.name: Tombigbee State Park
mississippi.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of northeast Mississippi, Tombigbee State Park offers a serene escape with beautiful lake views and lush forest trails.
mississippi.fullDescription: Tombigbee State Park is located just outside of Tupelo and provides a scenic retreat centered around a 100-acre lake. Established in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park features historic stone structures and offers a glimpse into the natural beauty of the region. The park's geology is characterized by the rolling hills of the Tombigbee River valley, providing diverse habitats for local wildlife and excellent opportunities for outdoor recreation.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the hardwood forest, offering great opportunities for birdwatching.

hikingTrails.name: Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses the higher elevations of the park, providing scenic overlooks of the lake below.

mississippi.campingInfo: The park features 20 RV campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as several rustic cabins available for rent overlooking the lake.
mississippi.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat ramp for private watercraft and allows fishing in the lake with a valid Mississippi fishing license.

visitorCenter.name: Tombigbee State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The main office provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping and cabin reservations.

mississippi.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Bring your own fishing gear as the lake is well-stocked with bass and bream.
Check the official website for seasonal disc golf tournament closures.
Reservations for cabins are highly recommended during peak summer months.

north carolina.name: Jockey's Ridge State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Home to the tallest living sand dune on the Atlantic coast, Jockey's Ridge offers breathtaking views of the Outer Banks and unique recreational opportunities.
north carolina.fullDescription: Jockey's Ridge State Park is a geological marvel located in Nags Head, North Carolina. It features the tallest active sand dune system in the eastern United States. The park's landscape is constantly shifting due to the powerful winds coming off the Atlantic Ocean and the Roanoke Sound. Historically, the area has been a hub for aviation pioneers, including the Wright brothers who frequented the dunes for their early gliding experiments. Today, the park serves as a protected environment for coastal flora and fauna while providing a premier destination for hang gliding, kite flying, and hiking.

hikingTrails.name: Tracks in the Sand Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible boardwalk trail that provides an introduction to the dune ecosystem.

hikingTrails.name: Soundside Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through the maritime thicket and leads to the shores of the Roanoke Sound.

north carolina.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping permitted within the boundaries of Jockey's Ridge State Park.
north carolina.fishingBoating: While there is no boat ramp, the park offers access to the Roanoke Sound for non-motorized watercraft like kayaks and paddleboards.

visitorCenter.name: Jockey's Ridge Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on dune ecology, local history, and the science of wind and sand.

north carolina.hours: 8:00 AM to sunset daily
north carolina.entranceFees: Admission to the park is free of charge.
north carolina.address: 300 W. Carolista Drive, Nags Head, NC 27959
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for milder temperatures and consistent winds for kite flying.
tips: Bring plenty of water as the sand can get extremely hot during summer months.
Wear sturdy footwear or be prepared to hike barefoot, as the sand can reach temperatures over 100 degrees.
Visit during the late afternoon for spectacular sunset views over the Roanoke Sound.

north carolina.name: Stone Mountain State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Stone Mountain State Park is a premier destination in North Carolina, famous for its massive 600-foot granite dome and stunning cascading waterfalls.
north carolina.fullDescription: Stone Mountain State Park encompasses over 14,000 acres of rugged terrain in the Blue Ridge Mountains. The park is anchored by a spectacular granite pluton that rises 600 feet above the surrounding landscape. Formed millions of years ago, this geological wonder offers panoramic views of the Blue Ridge Escarpment. The park also features historic homesteads, including the mid-19th century Hutchinson Homestead, providing a glimpse into early mountain life.
thingsToDo: Rock climbing on the granite dome

hikingTrails.name: Stone Mountain Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that takes hikers to the summit of the granite dome and past the beautiful Stone Mountain Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Widow's Creek Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading to a picturesque waterfall that is perfect for a quick nature walk.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park offers 88 campsites, including sites for tents, trailers, and RVs, as well as group camping and backpack camping options.
north carolina.fishingBoating: The park offers excellent trout fishing in designated mountain streams; a valid North Carolina fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Stone Mountain State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's geology, natural history, and the cultural heritage of the mountain settlers.

north carolina.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (varies by season)
north carolina.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Stone Mountain State Park.
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring sturdy hiking boots for the steep sections of the loop trail.
Check the official website for rock climbing permit requirements.

north carolina.name: Chimney Rock State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: A stunning mountain destination in North Carolina featuring a 315-foot granite monolith that offers breathtaking panoramic views of Hickory Nut Gorge.
north carolina.fullDescription: Chimney Rock State Park is a premier North Carolina destination known for its dramatic rock formations and the iconic 315-foot Chimney Rock itself. The park encompasses over 8,000 acres of rugged mountain terrain, including the impressive Hickory Nut Falls, which drops 404 feet. Formed by ancient volcanic activity and shaped by millions of years of erosion, the park provides a unique geological window into the Blue Ridge Mountains. Visitors can explore a network of trails that lead to high-elevation vistas, lush forests, and diverse ecosystems.
thingsToDo: Hiking to the top of Chimney Rock

hikingTrails.name: Outcroppings Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb featuring many stairs that leads directly to the Chimney Rock monolith and the Opera Box.

hikingTrails.name: Hickory Nut Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic, wooded trail that leads to the base of one of the tallest waterfalls east of the Mississippi River.

north carolina.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within the boundaries of Chimney Rock State Park, but numerous private campgrounds and lodging options are available in the surrounding Hickory Nut Gorge area.
north carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing and boating are not permitted within the state park boundaries, though Lake Lure nearby offers extensive water recreation opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Chimney Rock Welcome Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local geology and wildlife.

north carolina.hours: Daily: 8:30 AM - 5:30 PM (Seasonal variations apply)
north carolina.entranceFees: Admission fees are required for entry to the park; please check the official website for current pricing as it varies by age and group size.
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for blooming wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking shoes as the trails involve many stairs and uneven terrain.
Arrive early in the day during peak season to avoid parking congestion.
Bring plenty of water, especially during the warmer summer months.

north carolina.name: Hanging Rock State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Hanging Rock State Park offers stunning mountain vistas, cascading waterfalls, and miles of rugged hiking trails in the Sauratown Mountains.
north carolina.fullDescription: Established in 1936, Hanging Rock State Park is a premier destination in North Carolina's Sauratown Mountains. The park features quartzite rock formations that rise dramatically above the surrounding Piedmont landscape. Visitors can explore over 20 miles of trails, swim in a mountain lake, or enjoy the park's rich biodiversity and geological history, which dates back millions of years.

hikingTrails.name: Hanging Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular trail leading to the iconic Hanging Rock cliff, offering panoramic views of the surrounding mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Moore's Wall Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: This challenging loop features a fire tower at the summit with 360-degree views and passes by several scenic rock outcrops.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park offers a family campground with 73 sites, including options for tents and trailers, as well as primitive group campsites and vacation cabins.
north carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the 12-acre lake and the Dan River; however, private boats are not allowed on the lake.

visitorCenter.name: Hanging Rock Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits on the park's geology, flora, and fauna, along with a gift shop and information desk.

north carolina.hours: Daily: 7:00 AM - 9:00 PM
north carolina.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Hanging Rock State Park.
north carolina.address: 1790 Hanging Rock Park Rd, Danbury, NC 27016
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends, as parking lots fill up quickly during peak season.
Wear sturdy hiking boots, as the trails are rocky and uneven.
Bring plenty of water, especially during the summer months when humidity is high.

north carolina.name: Pilot Mountain State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Famous for its iconic quartzite pinnacle rising above the Piedmont, Pilot Mountain offers breathtaking views and diverse outdoor recreation.
north carolina.fullDescription: Pilot Mountain State Park is centered around the Big Pinnacle, a unique geological formation that rises 1,400 feet above the surrounding landscape. Once a landmark for Native Americans and early settlers, the park was established in 1968 to protect this natural wonder. The park spans over 3,700 acres, featuring a rugged terrain that connects the mountain section to the Yadkin River, providing a variety of ecosystems and recreational opportunities.

hikingTrails.name: Jomeokee Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail circles the base of the Big Pinnacle, offering spectacular views of the rock face and the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Grindstone Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that takes hikers from the visitor center area up to the summit parking lot, passing through lush forest.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park features a family campground with 42 sites, including options for tents and RVs, equipped with fire rings, picnic tables, and access to bathhouses.
north carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Yadkin River section of the park, and there is a canoe access area for paddlers to enjoy the river.

visitorCenter.name: Pilot Mountain Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits on the park's geology, history, and local flora and fauna, along with helpful park rangers.

north carolina.hours: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily (varies seasonally)
north carolina.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Pilot Mountain State Park.
north carolina.address: 1792 Pilot Knob Park Rd, Pinnacle, NC 27043
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends, as the summit parking lot often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Bring plenty of water, especially if hiking the steeper trails during summer months.
Check the official website for current rock climbing closures or trail maintenance alerts.

north carolina.name: Mount Mitchell State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Home to the highest peak east of the Mississippi River, Mount Mitchell State Park offers breathtaking panoramic views and a unique high-elevation spruce-fir forest.
north carolina.fullDescription: Established in 1915 as North Carolina's first state park, Mount Mitchell rises 6,684 feet above sea level. The park protects a rare southern Appalachian spruce-fir forest, an ecosystem more common in Canada than the southern United States. Visitors can explore the summit observation deck, which provides 360-degree views of the Blue Ridge Mountains, and learn about the mountain's history, including the legacy of Elisha Mitchell, for whom the peak is named.
thingsToDo: Hiking to the summit observation deck
Photography of the Blue Ridge Mountains

hikingTrails.name: Summit Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, paved path leading from the parking area to the observation deck at the highest point.

hikingTrails.name: Balsam Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A loop trail that winds through the beautiful spruce-fir forest, offering a peaceful walk through the high-altitude ecosystem.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park features a small, primitive tent-only campground with 9 sites available by reservation, typically open from May through October.
north carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park, though boating is not available due to the high-elevation terrain.

visitorCenter.name: Mount Mitchell Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the natural history, geology, and human history of the Black Mountains, along with a gift shop and information desk.

north carolina.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (seasonal variations apply)
north carolina.entranceFees: Admission to Mount Mitchell State Park is free.
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and visibility.
tips: Bring a jacket, as temperatures at the summit are often 10-20 degrees cooler than in the surrounding valleys.
Check the park website for road closures during winter months due to ice and snow.
Arrive early on weekends, as parking at the summit can fill up quickly during peak season.

north carolina.name: Grandfather Mountain State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Grandfather Mountain State Park features some of the most rugged and spectacular terrain in the Blue Ridge Mountains, offering high-elevation hiking and breathtaking vistas.
north carolina.fullDescription: Grandfather Mountain State Park encompasses 2,456 acres of high-elevation wilderness, including the iconic Calloway Peak, the highest point in the Blue Ridge Mountains at 5,946 feet. The park is renowned for its complex geology, featuring ancient rock formations and diverse ecosystems that support rare plant and animal species. Visitors can explore a network of challenging trails that traverse rocky cliffs, dense forests, and alpine meadows, providing a true backcountry experience.

hikingTrails.name: Profile Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that leads hikers through diverse forest types to the ridgeline, offering stunning views of the Profile rock formation.

hikingTrails.name: Grandfather Trail
hikingTrails.description: A technical trail featuring ladders and cables that traverses the rugged spine of the mountain, connecting several peaks.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park offers 13 primitive, backcountry campsites located along the trails. Permits are required for all overnight stays, and there are no amenities like water or toilets at these sites.
north carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas in accordance with North Carolina Wildlife Resources Commission regulations; no boating facilities are available.

visitorCenter.name: Grandfather Mountain State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides trail maps, backcountry permits, and information regarding park regulations and safety.

north carolina.hours: Open daily from sunrise to sunset
north carolina.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Grandfather Mountain State Park, though backcountry camping permits require a small fee.
north carolina.address: 9872 NC Highway 105 South, Banner Elk, NC 28604
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for mild temperatures and clear views.
tips: Always check the weather forecast, as conditions at high elevations can change rapidly.
Bring plenty of water, as there are no reliable water sources along the backcountry trails.
Wear sturdy, broken-in hiking boots due to the rocky and uneven terrain.

north carolina.name: Carolina Beach State Park
north carolina.shortDescription: Located on the banks of the Cape Fear River, this park is famous for its rare Venus flytraps and diverse coastal habitats.
north carolina.fullDescription: Carolina Beach State Park offers a unique blend of coastal environments, including sand dunes, salt marshes, and pine forests. It is internationally recognized for being one of the few places where the rare Venus flytrap grows naturally in the wild. The park's history dates back to the Civil War, with remnants of Sugarloaf, a massive sand dune used as a strategic lookout point, still visible today.
thingsToDo: Hiking through rare carnivorous plant habitats
Boating and fishing on the Cape Fear River

hikingTrails.name: Flytrap Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible loop that takes visitors through the habitat of the rare Venus flytrap.

hikingTrails.name: Sugarloaf Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through maritime forest and leads to the historic Sugarloaf sand dune overlooking the river.

north carolina.campingInfo: The park features 83 campsites, including sites with full hookups for RVs and tent-only sites, all nestled within a beautiful coastal forest.
north carolina.fishingBoating: The park provides a public boat ramp with access to the Cape Fear River and the Intracoastal Waterway, along with excellent pier fishing opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Carolina Beach State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits on the park's unique carnivorous plants and local coastal ecology.

north carolina.hours: 8:00 AM - Sunset daily
north carolina.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Carolina Beach State Park.
north carolina.address: 1010 State Park Rd, Carolina Beach, NC 28428
north carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming wildflowers.
tips: Visit in the spring to see the Venus flytraps in their prime blooming season.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer months near the marsh areas.
Check the park website for guided ranger programs regarding the carnivorous plants.

oklahoma.name: Beavers Bend State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Nestled in the scenic Ouachita Mountains, Beavers Bend State Park offers a lush retreat featuring towering pines, crystal-clear waters, and abundant outdoor recreation.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Located in southeastern Oklahoma, Beavers Bend State Park is a premier destination known for its dramatic landscape of pine-covered hills and the pristine Mountain Fork River. The park was developed in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps, and many of the original stone structures remain today. It serves as a gateway to Broken Bow Lake, providing visitors with a unique blend of rugged wilderness and accessible amenities, making it a favorite for nature enthusiasts and families alike.
thingsToDo: Fly fishing on the Mountain Fork River
Boating and water sports on Broken Bow Lake
Train rides on the Beavers Bend Depot and Trail Rides
Golfing at the Cedar Creek Golf Course

hikingTrails.name: Friends Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that offers beautiful views of the Mountain Fork River and unique rock formations.

hikingTrails.name: Cedar Bluff Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the forest and provides elevated views overlooking the river valley.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park features multiple campgrounds with over 300 campsites ranging from primitive to full RV hookups, plus 47 cabins available for rent.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: The Mountain Fork River is famous for trout fishing, while Broken Bow Lake offers excellent opportunities for bass fishing, boating, and jet skiing.

visitorCenter.name: Forest Heritage Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of forestry in Oklahoma, including dioramas and historical tools.

oklahoma.hours: Open 24 hours daily for park access
oklahoma.entranceFees: No general entrance fee, though specific activities like boat rentals or golf have associated costs.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book cabins well in advance as they fill up months ahead of time.
Bring water shoes if you plan to wade in the Mountain Fork River.
Check the park website for seasonal burn bans before planning a campfire.

oklahoma.name: Robbers Cave State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Nestled in the scenic Sans Bois Mountains, this park is famous for its rugged sandstone cliffs and history as a hideout for outlaws like Jesse James.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Robbers Cave State Park spans over 8,000 acres of forested hills and rocky bluffs. Historically significant as a refuge for notorious outlaws, the park offers a unique blend of geological wonder and frontier history. Visitors can explore the famous cave, hike through dense hardwood forests, and enjoy the serene waters of Lake Carlton and Coon Creek.

hikingTrails.name: Robbers Cave Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but steep climb leading directly to the historic cave entrance with panoramic views of the valley.

hikingTrails.name: Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that traverses the rugged ridges of the Sans Bois Mountains, offering excellent vantage points.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park features multiple campgrounds with RV hookups, tent sites, and a lodge. There are also several cabins available for rent, including some with modern amenities.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Lake Carlton, Coon Creek, and Wayne Wallace Reservoir. Boat ramps are available for non-motorized and small motorized watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Robbers Cave Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides educational exhibits on local geology, history, and wildlife, along with park maps and information.

oklahoma.hours: Open 24 hours daily for day-use and camping
oklahoma.entranceFees: No daily vehicle entrance fee; camping and cabin fees apply.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain around the cave is rocky and uneven.
Bring a flashlight if you plan to explore the interior of the cave.
Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular during peak seasons.

oklahoma.name: Gloss Mountain State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Famous for its sparkling selenite crystals, Gloss Mountain offers dramatic mesa views and unique geological formations in Major County.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Gloss Mountain State Park, also known as the Glass Mountains, is a geological wonder located in northwestern Oklahoma. The mountains are named for the high concentration of selenite crystals found in the gypsum-capped mesas, which shimmer like glass in the sunlight. The park features a steep trail leading to the top of Cathedral Mountain, providing panoramic views of the surrounding red-bed plains and the unique landscape shaped by erosion over millions of years.
thingsToDo: Hiking to the top of Cathedral Mountain

hikingTrails.name: Cathedral Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb featuring stairs that leads visitors to the summit of the mesa for expansive views of the surrounding countryside.

hikingTrails.name: Base Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path around the base of the mountains, perfect for viewing the selenite crystals up close.

oklahoma.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available at Gloss Mountain State Park. The park is strictly for day-use activities.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: There are no fishing or boating opportunities at this park as it is a dry, mesa-based landscape.

visitorCenter.name: Gloss Mountain Information Kiosk
visitorCenter.info: The park provides informational signage regarding the geology and history of the area at the trailhead.

oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall, when temperatures are mild and the sun makes the crystals sparkle without extreme heat.
tips: Bring plenty of water as there are no water facilities on the trail.
Wear sturdy hiking boots due to the loose, rocky terrain.
Visit during the golden hour for the best photography of the shimmering crystals.

oklahoma.name: Roman Nose State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Nestled in a beautiful canyon, Roman Nose State Park offers stunning gypsum rock cliffs, natural springs, and a serene lake perfect for outdoor recreation.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Roman Nose State Park is one of the original seven Oklahoma state parks, named after a Cheyenne chief. The park is famous for its dramatic gypsum rock cliffs, lush canyons, and natural springs that feed into the park's lakes. It offers a unique geological landscape in the heart of Blaine County, providing visitors with opportunities to explore rugged terrain, enjoy water activities, and experience the rich history of the region.
thingsToDo: Swimming in the pool or lake

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Vista Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the canyon, offering spectacular views of the gypsum cliffs and native vegetation.

hikingTrails.name: Three Springs Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that leads visitors to the park's famous natural springs, perfect for a relaxing walk.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park features modern RV sites with full hookups, tent campsites, and the historic Roman Nose Lodge which offers comfortable guest rooms.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: The park features two lakes, Lake Watonga and Boecher Lake, which are stocked with trout in the winter and offer excellent bass and catfish fishing year-round.

visitorCenter.name: Roman Nose State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping and lodge reservations.

oklahoma.hours: Open 24 hours daily for day-use and camping
oklahoma.entranceFees: No daily entrance fee; camping and lodge fees apply.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and beautiful foliage.
tips: Bring your camera for the stunning sunset views over the gypsum cliffs.
Check the seasonal trout stocking schedule if you plan to fish.
Book lodge rooms well in advance as they fill up quickly during peak season.

oklahoma.name: Lake Murray State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Oklahoma's first and largest state park, featuring a stunning 5,700-acre lake surrounded by rolling hills and dense forests.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Established in 1933, Lake Murray State Park is a historic destination encompassing 12,500 acres. The park is centered around the crystal-clear Lake Murray, which is renowned for its depth and water clarity. The area is rich in history, featuring the Tucker Tower, which was built by the Works Progress Administration in the 1930s and now serves as a nature center. The park's geology is characterized by the Arbuckle Mountains' foothills, providing diverse terrain for outdoor recreation.
thingsToDo: Golfing at Lake Murray Golf Course

hikingTrails.name: Buckhorn Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through the forest and offers beautiful views of the lake shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Anadarche Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail perfect for families, showcasing native flora and local wildlife habitats.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park offers a wide variety of camping options, including over 300 campsites ranging from primitive tent sites to full RV hookups, as well as cabin rentals at the Lake Murray Lodge.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat ramps, a full-service marina with boat rentals, and excellent fishing opportunities for largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and channel catfish.

visitorCenter.name: Tucker Tower Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's history, local geology, and native wildlife, along with an observation deck overlooking the lake.

oklahoma.entranceFees: No daily vehicle entrance fee; camping and facility fees vary by site type.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Visit the Tucker Tower early in the day to avoid crowds and get the best photos.
Bring your own watercraft or rent one at the marina for the best lake experience.
Check the official website for seasonal burn bans before planning a campfire.

oklahoma.name: Greenleaf State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of eastern Oklahoma, Greenleaf State Park offers a serene escape with crystal-clear waters and lush forest trails.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Established in 1938, Greenleaf State Park is one of Oklahoma's original seven state parks. The park surrounds the 930-acre Greenleaf Lake, which is renowned for its clear water and excellent fishing. The area is characterized by its rugged, hilly terrain and dense hardwood forests, providing a picturesque backdrop for outdoor recreation. The park features historic stone structures built by the WPA, adding a layer of cultural significance to its natural beauty.

hikingTrails.name: Ankle Express Trail
hikingTrails.description: A winding trail that offers beautiful views of the lake and passes through diverse forest ecosystems.

hikingTrails.name: Greenleaf Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging, long-distance trail that circles the lake, perfect for experienced hikers seeking solitude and rugged terrain.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options, including RV sites with full hookups, tent sites, and several charming cabins available for rent.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: The park features a boat ramp, a fishing dock, and a marina where visitors can enjoy boating and fishing for largemouth bass, channel catfish, and sunfish.

visitorCenter.name: Greenleaf State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with cabin and campsite reservations.

oklahoma.hours: Open 24 hours daily for registered campers; day use from sunrise to sunset.
oklahoma.entranceFees: No daily vehicle entrance fee; camping and cabin fees vary by site type.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Bring insect repellent during the warmer months.
Book cabins well in advance as they are very popular.
Check the official website for current lake water levels before planning water activities.

oklahoma.name: Natural Falls State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Home to a stunning 77-foot waterfall, this park offers a serene escape into the lush, forested landscape of the Ozark Highlands.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Natural Falls State Park is located in the scenic Ozark Highlands region of northeastern Oklahoma. The park is famous for its 77-foot waterfall, which cascades through a narrow, rock-lined canyon. The area features a unique microclimate that supports a variety of ferns and mosses, creating a lush, temperate rainforest-like environment. Historically, the site was a popular destination for locals and was featured in the movie 'Where the Red Fern Grows'.

hikingTrails.name: Dripping Springs Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads visitors down into the canyon floor, offering spectacular views of the waterfall and the surrounding rock formations.

hikingTrails.name: Red Fern Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through the hardwood forest, perfect for a quick nature walk and spotting local wildlife.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park offers 44 RV sites with water and electric hookups, as well as several tent campsites. There are also yurts available for rent for a unique glamping experience.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: Fishing is not permitted within the waterfall area to protect the delicate ecosystem, but nearby lakes offer ample fishing opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Natural Falls Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center provides information on park history, trail maps, and local flora and fauna.

oklahoma.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee, but camping and yurt rental fees apply.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking shoes as the trail to the waterfall base can be slippery.
Bring a camera with a tripod to capture the best long-exposure shots of the waterfall.
Visit during the week to avoid weekend crowds and enjoy a quieter experience.

oklahoma.name: Sequoyah State Park
oklahoma.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Fort Gibson Lake, Sequoyah State Park is Oklahoma's largest state park, offering extensive outdoor recreation and scenic waterfront views.
oklahoma.fullDescription: Sequoyah State Park, named after the famous Cherokee scholar who developed the Cherokee syllabary, spans over 3,000 acres along the banks of Fort Gibson Lake. The park features diverse terrain ranging from dense woodlands to open meadows, providing a habitat for a wide variety of wildlife. It is a premier destination for water sports, equestrian activities, and family camping, serving as a hub for outdoor enthusiasts in eastern Oklahoma.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Fort Gibson Lake
Horseback riding at the Sequoyah Riding Stables
Golfing at the Sequoyah Bay Golf Course
Wildlife viewing at the Nature Center
Swimming at the designated beach areas

hikingTrails.name: Three Forks Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail that winds through wooded areas and offers excellent opportunities for birdwatching.

hikingTrails.name: Sequoyah Lakeview Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the shoreline of Fort Gibson Lake, providing panoramic water views and access to secluded coves.

oklahoma.campingInfo: The park offers a wide range of camping options, including over 200 RV sites with full or partial hookups, numerous tent sites, and several climate-controlled cabins available for rent.
oklahoma.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat ramps providing access to Fort Gibson Lake, which is well-known for its excellent bass, crappie, and catfish fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Sequoyah State Park Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The nature center features educational exhibits on local flora and fauna, as well as live animal displays and information on park history.

oklahoma.hours: Open 24 hours daily for camping; day-use areas open from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM
oklahoma.entranceFees: No daily vehicle entrance fee is charged for entry into Sequoyah State Park.
oklahoma.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Make cabin reservations well in advance as they fill up quickly during peak summer months.
Bring binoculars to the Nature Center for better wildlife spotting along the lake.
Check the official website for current lake levels before planning water-based activities.

south carolina.name: Hunting Island State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Hunting Island is South Carolina's most popular state park, featuring five miles of pristine beach, a historic lighthouse, and a lush maritime forest.
south carolina.fullDescription: Hunting Island State Park is a 5,000-acre barrier island located near Beaufort, South Carolina. It is home to the only lighthouse in the state that is publicly accessible, which was originally built in 1859 and rebuilt in 1875. The park features a diverse ecosystem including salt marshes, maritime forests, and a vast sandy coastline that attracts thousands of visitors annually for its natural beauty and unique coastal geology.
thingsToDo: Climb the historic Hunting Island Lighthouse
Go beachcombing for shark teeth and shells
Explore the nature center and exhibits
Bird watching in the maritime forest

hikingTrails.name: Lighthouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, scenic walk through the maritime forest that leads directly to the historic lighthouse.

hikingTrails.name: Maritime Forest Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through the dense forest canopy, offering excellent opportunities to spot local wildlife and native plants.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park offers over 100 campsites equipped with water and electrical hookups, suitable for both tents and RVs, located just a short walk from the beach.
south carolina.fishingBoating: The park features a popular fishing pier extending into the Atlantic Ocean and offers opportunities for surf fishing along the beach.

visitorCenter.name: Hunting Island Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The nature center provides educational exhibits about the island's barrier island ecosystem, local marine life, and the history of the lighthouse.

south carolina.hours: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily (extended to 9:00 PM during daylight savings)
south carolina.entranceFees: $8.00 for adults, $5.00 for SC seniors, $4.00 for children ages 6-15, free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.address: 2555 Sea Island Pkwy, St Helena Island, SC 29920
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and fewer crowds.
tips: Arrive early during summer weekends as the park often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Bring insect repellent, especially if you plan to hike the forest trails.
Check the tide charts before heading out to the beach for the best shelling opportunities.

south carolina.name: Table Rock State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains, Table Rock State Park offers stunning granite mountain views and pristine mountain lakes.
south carolina.fullDescription: Table Rock State Park encompasses over 3,000 acres of rugged mountain terrain in the South Carolina Upstate. The park is famous for the massive granite dome of Table Rock Mountain, which rises above the surrounding forest. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, the park features historic cabins and lodge structures that reflect the rustic architectural style of the era. Visitors can explore diverse ecosystems ranging from hardwood forests to mountain streams and waterfalls.

hikingTrails.name: Table Rock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb to the summit of Table Rock Mountain offering panoramic views of the Blue Ridge Escarpment.

hikingTrails.name: Carrick Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that follows the creek, passing several small waterfalls and lush forest vegetation.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park offers 94 campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as several historic cabins available for rent.
south carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Lake Oolenoy and Lake Pinnacle. Non-motorized boats and electric trolling motors are allowed on the lakes.

visitorCenter.name: Table Rock State Park Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides educational exhibits on local geology, flora, and fauna, along with park maps and ranger assistance.

south carolina.entranceFees: $6.00 for adults, $3.75 for SC seniors, $3.50 for children ages 6-15, free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lots for popular trails fill up quickly.
Wear sturdy hiking boots, as the trails are rocky and can be slippery.
Check the weather forecast before attempting the summit trail, as conditions change rapidly at higher elevations.

south carolina.name: Devils Fork State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Devils Fork State Park offers unparalleled access to the pristine, spring-fed waters of Lake Jocassee.
south carolina.fullDescription: Devils Fork State Park is the only public access point to the 7,500-acre Lake Jocassee, a deep, clear mountain lake surrounded by steep, forested slopes. The park is renowned for its unique geology, including rare flora like the Oconee Bell, and its status as a premier destination for scuba diving, trout fishing, and boating. The area was once part of the Cherokee Nation and remains a place of significant natural beauty and historical intrigue.
thingsToDo: Scuba diving in the clear lake waters

hikingTrails.name: Oconee Bell Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail that winds through lush forest, famous for blooming Oconee Bells in the spring.

hikingTrails.name: Bear Cove Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers scenic views of the lake and passes through diverse hardwood forests.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park features 59 paved campsites with water and electrical hookups, as well as 20 lakeside villas available for rent.
south carolina.fishingBoating: The park features two boat ramps for easy lake access and is a premier location for brown and rainbow trout fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Devils Fork State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park activities, lake safety, and local history, along with a small gift shop.

south carolina.entranceFees: $8.00 for adults, $5.00 for SC seniors, $4.00 for children ages 6-15, free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the park often reaches capacity during peak summer months.
Bring a polarized pair of sunglasses to better enjoy the crystal-clear views of the lake.
Check the water temperature before swimming, as Lake Jocassee remains cool even in summer.

south carolina.name: Myrtle Beach State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: A serene coastal oasis nestled along the Atlantic Ocean, offering pristine beaches and lush maritime forests in the heart of Myrtle Beach.
south carolina.fullDescription: Established in 1936 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, Myrtle Beach State Park was the first state park in South Carolina. It protects a rare stretch of undeveloped coastline, featuring a maritime forest of oaks and magnolias that provides a stark, beautiful contrast to the surrounding urban development. The park is renowned for its fishing pier, diverse birdwatching opportunities, and miles of quiet, sandy beaches.

hikingTrails.name: Sculptured Oak Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, interpretive loop that winds through the maritime forest, showcasing native flora and fauna.

hikingTrails.name: Yaupon Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A peaceful trail that traverses through dense thickets of yaupon holly and coastal vegetation.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park features 278 campsites, many with water and electrical hookups, capable of accommodating RVs and tents, located just a short walk from the beach.
south carolina.fishingBoating: The park features a popular fishing pier with a bait and tackle shop; fishing is permitted from the pier and along the beach (outside of designated swimming areas).

visitorCenter.name: Myrtle Beach State Park Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits on local marine life, sea turtle conservation, and the park's history.

south carolina.entranceFees: $8.00 for adults, $5.00 for SC seniors, $4.00 for children ages 6-15, free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.address: 4401 South Kings Hwy, Myrtle Beach, SC 29575
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and fewer crowds.
tips: Visit the pier early in the morning to catch the sunrise and avoid peak heat.
Check the park's event calendar for guided sea turtle nest walks during summer months.
Bring insect repellent if you plan to hike the nature trails, especially in the warmer months.

south carolina.name: Caesars Head State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Perched atop the Blue Ridge Escarpment, Caesars Head offers breathtaking panoramic views and access to the rugged Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area.
south carolina.fullDescription: Caesars Head State Park is a premier destination in the South Carolina Upstate, famous for its dramatic granite rock outcropping that provides sweeping views of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The park serves as the gateway to the 13,000-acre Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area, a protected corridor of diverse ecosystems, waterfalls, and challenging terrain. Geologically, the area is defined by the Blue Ridge Escarpment, where the Piedmont plateau abruptly rises to meet the mountains, creating unique microclimates and spectacular vistas.

hikingTrails.name: Raven Cliff Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular trail that leads to a suspension bridge overlooking the 420-foot Raven Cliff Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Caesars Head Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path leading directly to the famous overlook at the top of the granite dome.

south carolina.campingInfo: Primitive backcountry camping is available within the Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area by permit only; there are no drive-up campsites at the park.
south carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the Middle Saluda River within the wilderness area; no boating facilities are available.

visitorCenter.name: Caesars Head Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The center provides trail maps, educational exhibits on local geology and wildlife, and information on the Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area.

south carolina.hours: Daily: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Extended hours during summer)
south carolina.entranceFees: $8.00 for adults, $5.00 for SC seniors, $4.00 for children ages 6-15, and free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for fall foliage or Spring for wildflower blooms.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly during peak season.
Bring binoculars for bird watching, especially for spotting migrating raptors.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails can be rocky and uneven.

south carolina.name: Jones Gap State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Nestled in the Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area, Jones Gap State Park offers rugged terrain, pristine trout streams, and breathtaking waterfall hikes.
south carolina.fullDescription: Jones Gap State Park is a premier destination for hikers and nature enthusiasts, serving as a gateway to the Mountain Bridge Wilderness Area. The park is defined by the Middle Saluda River, which cuts through a deep, rocky gorge, creating a unique microclimate that supports diverse flora and fauna. Historically, the area was a vital passage for early settlers and traders traveling between the Upstate and the mountains. Today, it is renowned for its challenging trails, scenic waterfalls, and status as a protected natural sanctuary.
thingsToDo: Trout fishing in the Middle Saluda River

hikingTrails.name: Jones Gap Trail
hikingTrails.description: This historic trail follows the Middle Saluda River, offering beautiful views of the gorge and access to several swimming holes.

hikingTrails.name: Rainbow Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that rewards hikers with a spectacular view of the 100-foot Rainbow Falls cascading over a rock face.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park features 17 primitive walk-in campsites located along the river, accessible only by hiking in. No RV hookups are available.
south carolina.fishingBoating: The Middle Saluda River is a designated State Scenic River and offers excellent trout fishing; a valid South Carolina fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Jones Gap Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides trail maps, fishing information, and educational exhibits about the local ecosystem.

south carolina.hours: Daily: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Extended to 9:00 PM during Daylight Savings)
south carolina.entranceFees: $6.00 for adults, $3.75 for SC seniors, $3.50 for children ages 6-15, and free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly due to limited capacity.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails are rocky and can be slippery near waterfalls.
Check the park website for trail closures before heading out, especially after heavy rain.

south carolina.name: Edisto Beach State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Edisto Beach State Park offers a unique coastal experience featuring one of the longest networks of ADA-accessible hiking and biking trails in South Carolina.
south carolina.fullDescription: Located on Edisto Island, this park is rich in history and natural beauty. It features a massive shell midden created by Native Americans thousands of years ago and offers stunning views of the Atlantic Ocean and salt marshes. The park's geology is defined by its maritime forest, which provides a habitat for diverse wildlife and protects the coastline from erosion.
thingsToDo: Beachcombing for shark teeth and shells
Educational programs at the Environmental Learning Center

hikingTrails.name: Spanish Mount Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads visitors through a lush maritime forest to a historic Native American shell midden.

hikingTrails.name: Scott Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail winds through salt marshes and provides excellent opportunities for spotting coastal birds and local wildlife.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park features two campgrounds with full hookups, including water and electricity, as well as several rustic cabins available for rent.
south carolina.fishingBoating: The park offers excellent saltwater fishing opportunities from the beach and designated areas, though there is no boat ramp inside the park.

visitorCenter.name: Edisto Beach State Park Environmental Learning Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features interactive exhibits about the local ecosystem, history, and the importance of sea turtle conservation.

south carolina.entranceFees: $8.00 for adults, $5.00 for SC seniors, $4.00 for children ages 6-15, and free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.address: 8377 State Cabin Rd, Edisto Island, SC 29438
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and fewer crowds.
tips: Visit during low tide to find the best shark teeth and fossils on the beach.
Bring insect repellent, especially if you plan to hike the marsh trails.
Book campsites well in advance as they fill up quickly during peak season.

south carolina.name: Paris Mountain State Park
south carolina.shortDescription: Located just minutes from downtown Greenville, this park offers a peaceful mountain escape with scenic lakes and rugged hiking trails.
south carolina.fullDescription: Paris Mountain State Park was developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) during the Great Depression. The park features a series of mountain lakes, including Lake Placid and Mountain Lake, which provide a serene backdrop for recreation. Its geology is defined by the Blue Ridge Escarpment, offering steep terrain and lush hardwood forests that provide a habitat for diverse flora and fauna.
thingsToDo: Canoeing and kayaking on Lake Placid

hikingTrails.name: Lake Placid Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic path that circles the main lake, perfect for families and casual walkers.

hikingTrails.name: Sulphur Springs Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular loop that climbs through hardwood forests and passes by historic CCC structures.

south carolina.campingInfo: The park offers 39 paved campsites for tents and RVs, each equipped with water and electrical hookups, as well as 13 rustic tent-only sites.
south carolina.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Lake Placid and Mountain Lake with a valid South Carolina fishing license. Canoes and kayaks are available for rent seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Paris Mountain State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The center provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local ecosystem.

south carolina.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (extended hours in summer)
south carolina.entranceFees: $6.00 for adults, $3.75 for SC seniors, $3.50 for children ages 6-15, free for children 5 and under.
south carolina.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers or Autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as the park often reaches capacity and closes the gates.
Download the trail map before arriving as cell service can be spotty in the mountains.
Bring bug spray during the warmer months, especially if you plan to hike near the lakes.

tennessee.name: Fall Creek Falls State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: One of Tennessee's largest and most visited state parks, featuring the spectacular 256-foot Fall Creek Falls.
tennessee.fullDescription: Fall Creek Falls State Park encompasses more than 29,800 acres on the Cumberland Plateau. It is renowned for its diverse landscape of cascades, gorges, waterfalls, and virgin hardwood forests. The park's centerpiece is the 256-foot Fall Creek Falls, one of the highest free-fall waterfalls in the eastern United States. The area was developed by the WPA and CCC in the 1930s and offers a rich history alongside its geological wonders.

hikingTrails.name: Fall Creek Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but steep descent to the base of the iconic 256-foot waterfall.

hikingTrails.name: Cable Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging, steep trail that requires using cables to navigate the rocky terrain to the base of the falls.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park offers 222 campsites across several campgrounds, including sites with full hookups for RVs and primitive tent sites. Cabins and a lodge are also available for overnight stays.
tennessee.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Fall Creek Lake and the surrounding streams. Boat rentals, including pedal boats and kayaks, are available seasonally at the boat dock.

visitorCenter.name: Betty Dunn Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits about the park's geology, flora, and fauna, along with information on park programs.

tennessee.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee for the park; however, some activities like swimming and golf require a fee.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for waterfall flow or Autumn for vibrant foliage.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as parking at the main waterfall overlook fills up quickly.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to descend to the base of the falls.
Check the park website for seasonal swimming pool and golf course availability.

tennessee.name: Burgess Falls State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Burgess Falls State Park is renowned for its natural beauty and a series of four stunning waterfalls that cascade down the Falling Water River.
tennessee.fullDescription: Located on the Eastern Highland Rim, Burgess Falls State Park features a dramatic 136-foot waterfall as its centerpiece. The park was once a site for a hydroelectric power plant in the early 20th century, and remnants of the old dam can still be seen today. The rugged terrain offers deep gorges, limestone bluffs, and a diverse forest ecosystem, making it a premier destination for hikers and nature photographers.

hikingTrails.name: River Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the Falling Water River and provides spectacular views of the four waterfalls, including the main 136-foot drop.

hikingTrails.name: Ridge Top Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that winds through the forest along the ridge, offering a quieter experience away from the main waterfall crowds.

tennessee.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available at Burgess Falls State Park. Nearby camping can be found at Edgar Evins State Park.
tennessee.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Falling Water River with a valid Tennessee fishing license. No boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Burgess Falls Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The center provides information on park history, local geology, and trail maps, along with educational exhibits.

tennessee.hours: 8:00 AM to Sunset daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Burgess Falls State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and early summer for the most impressive waterfall flow and lush greenery.
tips: The trail to the base of the waterfall is steep and can be slippery; wear sturdy hiking boots.
Visit on a weekday to avoid heavy weekend crowds at the main overlook.
