Check the official website for trail closures, as the river trail is occasionally closed due to high water levels.

tennessee.name: Rock Island State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: A scenic 883-acre park located at the confluence of the Caney Fork, Collins, and Rocky rivers, famous for its rugged beauty and historic cotton mill.
tennessee.fullDescription: Rock Island State Park is situated on the headwaters of Center Hill Lake. The park is known for its dramatic limestone bluffs, deep gorges, and the historic 19th-century cotton textile mill. The park's geology is defined by the Caney Fork River, which has carved a deep canyon through the landscape, creating the iconic Great Falls and Blue Hole areas. It serves as a premier destination for whitewater enthusiasts and hikers alike.

hikingTrails.name: Upstream Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the Caney Fork River and offers excellent views of the gorge and the historic mill ruins.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging hike that leads to a scenic overlook of the river and provides opportunities to spot nesting eagles.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park features 60 campsites equipped with water and electrical hookups, suitable for both tents and RVs, along with a bathhouse facility.
tennessee.fishingBoating: The park offers a boat ramp for access to Center Hill Lake and excellent fishing for bass, catfish, and walleye in the river and lake.

visitorCenter.name: Rock Island State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park maps, information on trail conditions, and educational exhibits about the park's history and geology.

tennessee.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee for Rock Island State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Check the water release schedule for the Caney Fork River before planning any water activities.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain near the gorge can be rocky and slippery.
Visit during the week to avoid heavy weekend crowds at the swimming areas.

tennessee.name: Roan Mountain State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains, this 2,000-acre park offers stunning vistas, lush forests, and the famous rhododendron gardens.
tennessee.fullDescription: Roan Mountain State Park is located at the base of the majestic Roan Mountain, which rises to over 6,000 feet. The park is characterized by its rich biodiversity, including the world's largest natural stand of Catawba rhododendrons. Visitors can explore the historic Miller Farmstead, which provides a glimpse into 19th-century Appalachian life, or enjoy the cool waters of the Doe River that winds through the park.
thingsToDo: Trout fishing in the Doe River

hikingTrails.name: Tom Gray Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, scenic loop that follows the Doe River and is perfect for families.

hikingTrails.name: Cloudland Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers beautiful forest views and connects to the higher elevations of the mountain.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park features 107 campsites equipped with water and electrical hookups, as well as 30 rustic cabins available for year-round rental.
tennessee.fishingBoating: The Doe River is a popular spot for trout fishing; a valid Tennessee fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Roan Mountain State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about local flora and fauna.

tennessee.hours: 8:00 AM - Sunset daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee for Roan Mountain State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Mid-June for the peak rhododendron bloom or October for fall foliage.
tips: Bring a jacket as temperatures at this elevation are significantly cooler than in the valley.
Check the park website for the annual Rhododendron Festival dates.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to explore the more rugged trails.

tennessee.name: Cumberland Mountain State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Nestled on the Cumberland Plateau, this park features a beautiful man-made lake and historic CCC-era stone structures.
tennessee.fullDescription: Cumberland Mountain State Park was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in the 1930s as part of a New Deal project. The park is centered around Byrd Lake, a picturesque reservoir created by a massive stone dam. The park is renowned for its rustic architecture, including cabins and a restaurant built from native Crab Orchard stone, reflecting the natural beauty of the Cumberland Plateau.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Byrd Lake
Golfing at the Bear Trace at Cumberland Mountain

hikingTrails.name: Byrd Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, scenic loop that circles the entire perimeter of Byrd Lake, offering great views of the water and the historic dam.

hikingTrails.name: Overnight Trail
hikingTrails.description: A longer trek that winds through the lush forests of the park, providing a more immersive experience in the plateau's ecosystem.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park offers 38 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as 38 rustic and modern cabins available for rent.
tennessee.fishingBoating: Byrd Lake allows fishing for bass, bluegill, and catfish. Boat rentals including pedal boats and canoes are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Park Office and Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and assistance with cabin and campsite reservations.

tennessee.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee for Cumberland Mountain State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book your cabin or campsite well in advance as they are very popular.
Visit the on-site restaurant for a meal with a view of the lake.
Bring binoculars for bird watching near the lake shore.

tennessee.name: Montgomery Bell State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Located just west of Nashville, this historic park offers lush forests, three pristine lakes, and a championship golf course.
tennessee.fullDescription: Montgomery Bell State Park encompasses 3,800 acres of forest and rolling hills. Historically significant as the site of the first Cumberland Presbyterian Church, the park features a diverse landscape of hardwood forests and three lakes. It is a premier destination for outdoor recreation, offering extensive trail systems, a full-service lodge, and a renowned golf course.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on Lake Acorn

hikingTrails.name: Montgomery Bell Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that traverses the entire park, offering hikers a deep immersion into the local hardwood forest.

hikingTrails.name: Wildcat Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path perfect for families, winding through wooded areas and providing excellent bird-watching opportunities.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park features 94 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as a modern lodge and several cabins available for rent.
tennessee.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted on all three lakes with a valid Tennessee fishing license; boat rentals are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Montgomery Bell State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, park information, and assistance with camping and facility reservations.

tennessee.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
tennessee.entranceFees: No daily entrance fee; park access is free to the public.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Book your campsite or cabin well in advance, especially for weekend stays.
Bring bug spray during the summer months as the wooded areas can be humid.
Check the official website for seasonal golf course maintenance schedules.

tennessee.name: Radnor Lake State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Radnor Lake State Park is a pristine 1,368-acre natural area in the heart of Nashville, dedicated to wildlife observation and environmental education.
tennessee.fullDescription: Established in 1914 as a private nature preserve, Radnor Lake is Tennessee's first State Natural Area. The park features a 85-acre lake surrounded by rolling hills and lush hardwood forests, providing a critical sanctuary for diverse wildlife including river otters, mink, and various migratory birds. The park is managed primarily for nature observation and hiking, prohibiting jogging, pets, and bicycles on the trails to maintain the tranquility of the ecosystem.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, gravel path that circles the lake, offering excellent opportunities for spotting waterfowl and deer.

hikingTrails.name: Ganier Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging ridge-top trail that provides panoramic views of the lake and the surrounding Nashville hills.

tennessee.campingInfo: There is no camping available at Radnor Lake State Park as it is a protected State Natural Area.
tennessee.fishingBoating: Fishing and boating are not permitted on Radnor Lake to protect the water quality and wildlife habitat.

visitorCenter.name: Barbara J. Mapp Aviary Education Center
visitorCenter.info: Features educational exhibits about local raptors and the park's history, along with a viewing deck for bird watching.

tennessee.hours: 6:00 AM until dark daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Radnor Lake State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and fall for vibrant foliage.
tips: Parking is limited; arrive early on weekends to secure a spot.
Pets are strictly prohibited on all trails to protect the wildlife.
Bring binoculars for the best bird-watching experience near the lake.

tennessee.name: Tims Ford State Park
tennessee.shortDescription: Located on the picturesque Tims Ford Reservoir, this park is a premier destination for bass fishing, boating, and outdoor recreation in Middle Tennessee.
tennessee.fullDescription: Tims Ford State Park encompasses 3,546 acres on the Tims Ford Reservoir, one of the most beautiful and productive fishing lakes in Tennessee. The park features a diverse landscape of rolling hills and hardwood forests, offering visitors a serene escape. Established in the 1970s following the construction of the Tims Ford Dam by the Tennessee Valley Authority, the park has become a hub for water sports, hiking, and golf, centered around the expansive 10,700-acre lake.
thingsToDo: Golfing at the Bear Trace at Tims Ford

hikingTrails.name: Marble Plains Loop
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds through hardwood forests and offers beautiful views of the lake shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Blue Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: An accessible path perfect for families, featuring gentle terrain and opportunities to spot local wildlife.

tennessee.campingInfo: The park offers 52 campsites with water and electric hookups, as well as 20 deluxe cabins available for rent year-round.
tennessee.fishingBoating: The park features multiple boat ramps and a full-service marina offering boat rentals, fuel, and bait.

visitorCenter.name: Tims Ford State Park Main Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with cabin and campsite reservations.

tennessee.hours: 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
tennessee.entranceFees: There is no daily entrance fee for Tims Ford State Park.
tennessee.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and optimal fishing conditions.
tips: Book your cabin or campsite well in advance, especially for summer weekends.
Bring your own fishing gear as the lake is famous for its smallmouth and largemouth bass.
Check the park website for current water levels and boat ramp accessibility.
nearbyAttractions: Sewanee: The University of the South
Old Stone Fort State Archaeological Park

texas.name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park
texas.shortDescription: Texas Panhandle park in Palo Duro Canyon, the second-largest canyon in the US, home of the Lighthouse rock.
texas.fullDescription: Palo Duro Canyon State Park covers about 28,000 acres in Randall and Armstrong counties near Canyon and opened in 1934. The canyon is billed as the second-largest in the country. Sixteen trails for hiking, cycling and horseback riding include the hike to the Lighthouse formation, and the outdoor musical TEXAS plays in the canyon in summer.

hikingTrails.name: CCC Trail
hikingTrails.description: TPWD lists the CCC trail as 1.4 miles one-way, taking about 1.5 hours, and rates it Difficult.

hikingTrails.name: Capitol Peak Trail
hikingTrails.description: TPWD lists Capitol Peak as a 3.5-mile loop that takes about 1.5 hours and rates it Moderate.

hikingTrails.name: Lighthouse Trail
hikingTrails.description: The official park page says you can hike to the Lighthouse, but it's not easy, so plan ahead for a safe hike.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers campsites with water and electricity, tent sites, equestrian sites, backpack camping areas, cabins on the rim and canyon floor, and glamping sites.
texas.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

texas.hours: Open daily. Office 7:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; gate 7:30 a.m.–10 p.m.
texas.entranceFees: $8 daily per adult (13+); children 12 and under free
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall are the most comfortable times to visit, since summer is the busy season with July highs averaging 92°F and trails may close for excessive heat, while January lows average 19°F.
tips: The park often reaches capacity, so reserve day passes or campsites online or at (512) 389-8900 to guarantee entry.
Trails can be challenging, so bring plenty of water and hike with a partner.
Trails may close because of wet weather or excessive heat, and flash flooding is a serious danger, so check trail status with the park or on its Facebook page before you go.

texas.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area
texas.shortDescription: Texas Hill Country natural area known for bigtooth maples that turn red and gold in late fall.
texas.fullDescription: Lost Maples State Natural Area protects 2,906 acres of hills and canyons on the upper Sabinal River near Vanderpool. It is named for its stands of bigtooth maple, and is busiest when fall colors peak in late October and early November. It is managed mainly for protection, with 11 miles of hiking trails, two small lakes on Can Creek and 30 campsites.

hikingTrails.name: East Trail
hikingTrails.description: A visitor reported that hiking the East Trail together with the East-West trail was a hard climb over a steep rocky hill, about 4.6 miles in total.

texas.campingInfo: The park has 30 campsites with water and electricity, plus primitive campsites you can backpack to.
texas.fishingBoating: You can fish in the Sabinal River or Can Creek, no license is needed to fish from shore or pier, and the park loans fishing gear.

visitorCenter.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

texas.hours: Open daily, 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.
texas.entranceFees: Adult $6 daily; children 12 and under free
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Fall brings the famous bigtooth maple colors, with foliage reports starting mid-October and October–November the busiest time, while spring (March–May) offers wildflowers and milder weather than the hot summers (July average high 94°F).
tips: In October and November the park reaches capacity daily, so reserve day passes online or by phone at (512) 389-8900 to guarantee entry.
There is no cell phone service in the natural area, so download maps and plans beforehand.
Stay on designated trails, because the terrain is steep and rugged and the bigtooth maples' shallow roots are easily damaged.

texas.name: Pedernales Falls State Park
texas.shortDescription: Texas Hill Country park where the Pedernales River tumbles over tilted 300-million-year-old limestone.
texas.fullDescription: Pedernales Falls State Park covers about 5,212 acres along the Pedernales River, 10 miles east of Johnson City and about 25 miles west of Austin. The falls run over limestone about 300 million years old. The river is used for swimming, tubing and fishing, though flash floods can rise within minutes. The park has nearly 20 miles of hiking and biking trails.

hikingTrails.name: Twin Falls Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short trail with a stop at the scenic overlook over the falls.

hikingTrails.name: Wolf Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging trail that wraps around Tobacco and Wolf mountains and winds along small canyons created by Mescal and Tobacco creeks.

hikingTrails.name: Pedernales Falls Trail System
hikingTrails.description: Take an hour or spend all day hiking around the falls area, following some of the many offshoot trails.

texas.campingInfo: Campers can choose a site with water and electricity or hike to a primitive site, and groups can use the Youth Group Camp or Equestrian Group Camp.
texas.fishingBoating: Visitors can fish, tube, canoe or kayak the Pedernales River, putting in at the swimming area or Trammell's Crossing Trail; put-ins and take-outs are not allowed in the Pedernales Falls area.

visitorCenter.name: Pedernales Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

texas.hours: Open daily; office 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; park gates closed 10 p.m.–8 a.m.
texas.entranceFees: $6 daily per person 13 and older; children 12 and under free
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall offer milder weather than summer, when highs average about 94°F, but these are busy seasons, so reserve ahead and watch for flash floods in the wettest months of May, August and September.
tips: The park often reaches capacity and closes to visitors without permits, so reserve day passes or campsites online or by phone at (512) 389-8900 to guarantee entry.
Leave the river area immediately if the water rises or turns muddy, because flash flooding is common. Swimming access is a strenuous 1/4-mile or longer hike with steep rock stairs and no handrail.
Campers with reservations who may arrive after 10 p.m. must call the park before 4:30 p.m. to get the gate code.
nearbyAttractions: Lyndon B. Johnson National Historical Park
Lyndon B. Johnson State Park & Historic Site

texas.name: Garner State Park
texas.shortDescription: Garner State Park is a beloved Texas destination famous for its scenic Frio River frontage and iconic summer evening dances.
texas.fullDescription: Located in the Texas Hill Country, Garner State Park spans 1,774 acres of scenic land along the Frio River. Established in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park features rugged limestone bluffs, dense woodlands, and crystal-clear waters. It is a premier destination for outdoor recreation, offering a unique blend of geological beauty and cultural history, including the tradition of jukebox dances that have been held at the park's pavilion since the 1940s.

hikingTrails.name: Old Baldy Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep, rocky climb that rewards hikers with panoramic views of the Frio River canyon.

hikingTrails.name: Crystal Cave Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but challenging hike leading to a small cave entrance nestled in the hillside.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options including campsites with water and electricity, screened shelters, and historic cabins built by the CCC.
texas.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Frio River with no license required while fishing from the shore within the park boundaries; kayaks and tubes are available for rent seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Garner State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the local ecosystem.

texas.hours: Daily: 8:00 AM - 10:00 PM
texas.entranceFees: $8.00 per person daily for adults 13 and older; children 12 and under are free.
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild weather, or Summer for swimming and river activities.
tips: Make reservations well in advance as the park reaches capacity quickly, especially on summer weekends.
Bring water shoes for the rocky riverbed of the Frio River.
Visit during the week to avoid the heavy weekend crowds.

texas.name: Colorado Bend State Park
texas.shortDescription: Discover the rugged beauty of the Texas Hill Country at Colorado Bend, home to the stunning Gorman Falls and miles of scenic river frontage.
texas.fullDescription: Colorado Bend State Park encompasses over 5,300 acres of diverse terrain, including limestone canyons, oak woodlands, and the pristine Colorado River. The park is geologically significant for its karst topography, featuring numerous caves and the spectacular 70-foot Gorman Falls, which is fed by a spring-fed creek. Historically used for ranching, the land was acquired by the state in 1984 to preserve its unique natural resources and provide recreational access to the river.

hikingTrails.name: Gorman Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A rocky trail that leads to the base of the breathtaking 70-foot Gorman Falls, featuring lush vegetation and limestone formations.

hikingTrails.name: Spicewood Springs Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows a spring-fed creek with numerous small waterfalls and swimming holes, perfect for cooling off on hot days.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers primitive hike-in campsites, drive-up campsites with water, and sites with water and electricity. No full RV hookups are available.
texas.fishingBoating: The Colorado River offers excellent fishing for bass and catfish. There is a boat ramp available, though water levels can fluctuate significantly.

visitorCenter.name: Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, park information, cave tour bookings, and basic supplies.

texas.hours: Open daily 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM
texas.entranceFees: $5.00 per person daily for adults 13 and older.
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming wildflowers.
tips: Book cave tours well in advance as they sell out quickly.
Bring plenty of water, as the trails can be hot and exposed.
Check the park website for river flow conditions before planning water activities.

texas.name: Caprock Canyons State Park & Trailway
texas.shortDescription: Home to the official Texas State Bison Herd, this rugged park features dramatic red canyons and expansive vistas in the Texas Panhandle.
texas.fullDescription: Caprock Canyons State Park is located along the Caprock Escarpment, a geological transition zone between the High Plains and the Rolling Plains. The park is renowned for its deep, colorful canyons, diverse wildlife, and the historic Texas State Bison Herd, which are descendants of animals saved by Charles Goodnight in the late 1800s. Visitors can explore over 90 miles of trails, including the 64-mile Caprock Canyons Trailway, which follows a former railroad line through tunnels and over trestles.

hikingTrails.name: Eagle Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers stunning panoramic views of the canyon floor and is a prime spot for spotting the bison herd.

hikingTrails.name: Upper Canyon Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging trek that winds through rugged terrain and provides intimate access to the park's unique geological formations.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options including sites with water and electricity, primitive hike-in sites, and equestrian campsites.
texas.fishingBoating: Lake Theo offers fishing for bass, catfish, and sunfish; non-motorized boating is permitted.

visitorCenter.name: Caprock Canyons Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the history of the bison herd, local geology, and information on trail conditions.

texas.hours: Open daily, 24 hours for campers; day use from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM.
texas.entranceFees: $5.00 per person, per day for ages 13 and older.
texas.address: 850 Caprock Canyon Park Rd, Quitaque, TX 79255
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming wildflowers.
tips: Always maintain a distance of at least 50 yards from the bison.
Bring plenty of water, as the canyon heat can be intense even in cooler months.
Check the park website for trail closures due to rain, as the red clay soil becomes very slick.

texas.name: Inks Lake State Park
texas.shortDescription: Located in the heart of the Texas Hill Country, Inks Lake State Park offers sparkling blue water and colorful rock outcrops perfect for outdoor recreation.
texas.fullDescription: Inks Lake State Park is situated on the banks of Inks Lake, one of the Highland Lakes on the Colorado River. The park features rugged, pink granite hills and a diverse landscape of cedar and oak forests. Formed by the construction of Inks Dam in 1938, the lake provides a constant-level water source that supports a variety of aquatic life and recreational activities. Visitors can explore the unique geology of the Llano Uplift, characterized by ancient Precambrian rock formations that have been exposed over millions of years.

hikingTrails.name: Pecan Flats Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds through diverse terrain, offering beautiful views of the lake and surrounding hills.

hikingTrails.name: Devil's Waterhole Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular path leading to a stunning swimming hole surrounded by dramatic rock cliffs.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers nearly 200 campsites, ranging from primitive hike-in sites to full-hookup RV sites, as well as several climate-controlled cabins.
texas.fishingBoating: The park features a boat ramp and a fishing pier. No fishing license is required when fishing from the shore within the state park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Inks Lake Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: The headquarters provides park maps, information on local flora and fauna, and assistance with camping reservations.

texas.hours: Open daily from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM
texas.entranceFees: $7.00 per person, per day for adults 13 and older.
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and blooming wildflowers.
tips: Make camping reservations well in advance as the park is very popular on weekends.
Bring water shoes for the rocky shoreline and swimming areas.
Visit during the week to avoid heavy crowds at the Devil's Waterhole.

texas.name: Mustang Island State Park
texas.shortDescription: Mustang Island State Park offers five miles of pristine coastline on the Gulf of Mexico, perfect for beachcombing, swimming, and coastal camping.
texas.fullDescription: Located on a barrier island along the Texas Gulf Coast, Mustang Island State Park protects 3,954 acres of dunes, marshes, and sandy beaches. The park was established in 1979 and serves as a vital habitat for coastal wildlife. Visitors can explore the diverse ecosystem of the island, which features a complex network of tidal flats and salt marshes that support a wide variety of migratory birds and marine life.

hikingTrails.name: Mustang Island Paddling Trail
hikingTrails.description: A series of shallow water trails through the coastal marshes that offer excellent opportunities for birding and observing marine life.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Walk
hikingTrails.description: A scenic walk along the shoreline of the Gulf of Mexico, perfect for finding shells and enjoying the ocean breeze.

texas.campingInfo: The park offers 48 campsites with water and electricity hookups, as well as 10 miles of primitive beach camping where you can pitch a tent right on the sand.
texas.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Gulf and the bay side of the park; no fishing license is required when fishing from the shore within the state park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Mustang Island State Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: The headquarters provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping reservations and park permits.

texas.hours: Open 24 hours daily for day-use and camping.
texas.entranceFees: $5.00 per person, per day for ages 13 and older.
texas.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild temperatures and peak bird migration.
tips: Bring plenty of sunscreen and insect repellent for the beach and marsh areas.
Check the tide charts before setting up a primitive campsite on the beach.
Visit during the early morning hours to see the most active bird life.

virginia.name: Grayson Highlands State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Virginia highland park near Mount Rogers known for open balds, wild ponies and Appalachian Trail access.
virginia.fullDescription: Grayson Highlands State Park covers 4,502 acres in Grayson County, next to the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. Its high mountain meadows, or balds, have wide views and are home to a herd of wild ponies introduced in the 1970s. Trails connect to the Appalachian Trail, and the park hosts a fall festival and folk music jam sessions.

hikingTrails.name: Appalachian Trail
hikingTrails.description: The park provides year-round access to the Appalachian Trail.

hikingTrails.name: Wilburn Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: Hikers can park in the state park's backpacker lot and take the Wilburn Ridge trail to the Appalachian Trail.

virginia.campingInfo: Full-service camping is offered May through October with reservations strongly recommended, and primitive camping is allowed in Chestnut Hollow campground in March, April and November.
virginia.fishingBoating: All streams in the park are Special Regulation Wild Trout Streams, which require single hooks and artificial lures.

visitorCenter.name: Grayson Highlands State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

virginia.hours: Park open daily 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; park office Mon–Fri 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; Visitor Center daily 10 a.m.–5 p.m. in season
virginia.entranceFees: Parking fee $7–$10 per vehicle (official parking-fee page lists $7 and $10; park Facebook cites $10/vehicle, $5/motorcycle, $20/bus)
virginia.address: 829 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through October is best, when full-service camping and the Visitor Center are open on these 5,000-foot-plus highlands. Winter brings closures, and there is no camping from early December to early March.
tips: Do not approach, feed or pet the wild ponies. They bite and kick when threatened, and human food is bad for them.
During primitive camping season at Chestnut Hollow there are porta-johns only and no water at the site. Drinking water is available at the park office.
Country Store hours vary, so call the park office at 276-579-7092 to confirm before you go.

virginia.name: Shenandoah River State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Virginia park along the South Fork of the Shenandoah River near Bentonville, with river access and overlooks.
virginia.fullDescription: Shenandoah River State Park, officially named for Delegate Raymond R. 'Andy' Guest Jr., was established in 1994 near Bentonville. It covers 1,619 acres along the South Fork of the Shenandoah River, with river access for canoeing and fishing, trails, and views of Massanutten Mountain.
virginia.campingInfo: Riverfront primitive tent campsites, a campground with water and electric sites, yurts, cabins, camping cabins and a group campground are available year-round; reserve online or call 1-800-933-PARK (7275).
virginia.fishingBoating: A car-top boat launch gives access to the South Fork of the Shenandoah River, and the "fish trap" access area near Shelter 3 is suitable for wade fishing with a Virginia freshwater license.

visitorCenter.name: Shenandoah River State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

virginia.hours: Park open daily 8 a.m. to dusk; visitor center 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. (may close when staff are not available)
virginia.entranceFees: $10 parking fee (DCR parking fee table); charged year-round
virginia.address: 350 Daughter of Stars Dr., Bentonville, VA 22610
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: The park is open year-round, but spring and fall offer milder weather and fewer crowds than busy summer weekends, when parking and picnic shelters fill up.
tips: Cabin, lodge and other overnight guests must bring their own linens because none are provided.
There are no designated swimming areas at the park.
Picnic shelters cannot be reserved on Saturdays or Sundays from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. They are first come, first served then, so arrive early.

virginia.name: First Landing State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Virginia's most visited state park, on Cape Henry in Virginia Beach near the 1607 colonists' first landing.
virginia.fullDescription: First Landing State Park, Virginia's first planned state park, sits at Cape Henry in Virginia Beach near where the Jamestown colonists first landed on April 26, 1607. It has a Chesapeake Bay beach, bald cypress swamps, over 19 miles of hiking and biking trails, cabins and campsites, and draws over a million visitors a year.

hikingTrails.name: Cape Henry Trail
hikingTrails.description: Komoot describes a hike on the Cape Henry Trail through diverse ecosystems in the park.

hikingTrails.name: Bald Cypress Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists the Bald Cypress Trail among the park's popular trails.

hikingTrails.name: Long Creek
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists Long Creek among the park's popular trails.

virginia.campingInfo: The park has cabins, yurts, water and electric hook-up campsites and tent campsites, reservable online or at (800) 933-PARK.
virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing and crabbing are popular, and a valid Virginia saltwater fishing license is required; the park has boat ramps.

visitorCenter.name: First Landing State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

virginia.hours: Day-use areas 7 a.m.-dusk; Office/Visitor Center daily 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; Trail Center daily 8 a.m.-4 p.m.; overnight areas accessible 24 hours when open
virginia.entranceFees: Parking fee $7 or $10 per vehicle (official DCR fee table; conditions for each rate not shown in excerpt)
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and fall offer milder coastal weather, and weekdays are best because weekends are very high-visitation days at Virginia's most-visited state park.
tips: Arrive early on weekends; once parking capacity is reached, guests are turned away.
There are no lifeguards, so bay swimming is at your own risk. Pets are allowed on the beach on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
Bring a valid Virginia saltwater fishing license if you plan to fish or crab.
nearbyAttractions: Virginia Aquarium and Marine Science Center

virginia.name: Douthat State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the Allegheny Mountains, Douthat State Park is one of Virginia's original six state parks and offers a stunning 50-acre lake for recreation.
virginia.fullDescription: Douthat State Park is a historic gem located in the Blue Ridge Mountains, originally developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in the 1930s. The park features a 50-acre lake, over 43 miles of hiking and mountain biking trails, and a rich history of mountain recreation. Its geology is defined by rugged ridges and deep valleys, providing a scenic backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts seeking both adventure and tranquility.
thingsToDo: Trout fishing in the lake and Wilson Creek
Swimming at the designated beach area
Mountain biking on extensive trail networks

hikingTrails.name: Blue Suck Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular trail that leads hikers to a beautiful waterfall, especially impressive after rainfall.

hikingTrails.name: Mountain Top Trail
hikingTrails.description: Offers challenging elevation gains and rewarding panoramic views of the surrounding Allegheny Mountains.

virginia.campingInfo: The park offers multiple campgrounds with sites for tents and RVs, including electric and water hookups. Additionally, there are 32 historic CCC-era cabins available for rent.
virginia.fishingBoating: The park is famous for its trout fishing program. Boat rentals including pedal boats, rowboats, and canoes are available at the lake during the summer season.

visitorCenter.name: Douthat State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and educational exhibits about the CCC.

virginia.hours: 8:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
virginia.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle parking fee for Virginia residents; $10.00 for non-residents.
virginia.address: 14239 Douthat State Park Rd, Millboro, VA 24460
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for wildflowers and fall for spectacular foliage.
tips: Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular year-round.
Bring a valid Virginia fishing license if you plan to fish in the lake or creek.
Check the park website for trail closures during hunting season.

virginia.name: Hungry Mother State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the mountains of Southwest Virginia, this park is famous for its beautiful 108-acre lake and rich Civilian Conservation Corps history.
virginia.fullDescription: Hungry Mother State Park is one of the original six Virginia State Parks opened in 1936. The park is named after a local legend involving a pioneer woman and her child who were captured by Native Americans, escaped, and were later found near the mountain stream. The park features a stunning lake, sandy beach, and rugged mountain trails that offer panoramic views of the surrounding Appalachian landscape.
thingsToDo: Boating and fishing on the lake

hikingTrails.name: Molly's Knob Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb to the highest point in the park, offering breathtaking views of the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that circles the entire lake, providing excellent opportunities for bird watching and wildlife viewing.

virginia.campingInfo: The park offers multiple campgrounds with water and electric hookups, as well as several historic cabins built by the CCC available for rent.
virginia.fishingBoating: The lake is well-stocked with trout, bass, and crappie. Boat rentals including kayaks, canoes, and paddleboats are available seasonally at the boat house.

visitorCenter.name: Hungry Mother Discovery Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's history, local geology, and the legacy of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

virginia.hours: 8:00 AM - Sunset daily
virginia.entranceFees: Parking fees vary by season and vehicle type, typically ranging from $5 to $10 per vehicle.
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities and fall foliage.
tips: Rent a paddleboat or kayak to explore the lake from the water.
Visit the Restaurant at Hungry Mother for local mountain cuisine.
Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular during summer months.

virginia.name: Smith Mountain Lake State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Located on the shores of the second-largest freshwater lake in Virginia, this park offers extensive water-based recreation and scenic mountain views.
virginia.fullDescription: Smith Mountain Lake State Park is situated on the north shore of the 20,600-acre Smith Mountain Lake. The park features a diverse landscape of rolling hills and wooded shorelines, providing a perfect backdrop for outdoor enthusiasts. Established to provide public access to the lake, the park serves as a hub for boating, fishing, and swimming, while also preserving significant natural habitats for local wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Turtle Island Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail that winds through the forest and offers beautiful views of the lake shoreline.

hikingTrails.name: Chestnut Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses the ridge line, providing hikers with elevated perspectives of the surrounding mountain landscape.

virginia.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options, including full-service RV sites with water and electric hookups, as well as primitive tent sites and several rental cabins.
virginia.fishingBoating: The park features a public boat ramp and a fishing pier, with the lake being famous for its trophy-sized striped bass and largemouth bass populations.

visitorCenter.name: Smith Mountain Lake State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, local ecology, and current recreational programs.

virginia.hours: 8:00 AM - Dusk daily
virginia.entranceFees: Daily parking fees range from $5 to $10 depending on the day of the week and vehicle type.
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water activities.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the beach parking lot can reach capacity quickly.
Bring your own watercraft or rent one from the nearby marina for the best lake experience.
Check the park website for seasonal swimming beach hours before planning your trip.

virginia.name: Claytor Lake State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the Blue Ridge Mountains, Claytor Lake State Park offers a premier destination for water sports, fishing, and family-friendly outdoor recreation.
virginia.fullDescription: Claytor Lake State Park is situated on the shores of a 4,500-acre reservoir created by the damming of the New River. The park features a historic 19th-century home, the Howe House, which serves as an educational center. The surrounding landscape is characterized by rolling hills and dense forests, providing a scenic backdrop for boating, swimming, and hiking. The park is renowned for its diverse aquatic life and is a popular spot for sport fishing, particularly for striped bass and muskie.
thingsToDo: Fishing for striped bass and muskie

hikingTrails.name: Claytor Lake Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds along the shoreline, offering beautiful views of the lake and opportunities for bird watching.

hikingTrails.name: Poplar Leaf Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers through lush hardwood forests and provides a more challenging terrain with slight elevation changes.

virginia.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options, including full-hookup RV sites, tent-only sites, and several climate-controlled cabins available for rent year-round.
virginia.fishingBoating: The park features a full-service marina with boat slips, fuel, and boat rentals. Fishing is excellent from both the shore and by boat, with the lake being a well-known destination for trophy-sized fish.

visitorCenter.name: Howe House Education Center
visitorCenter.info: The center provides exhibits on the history of the lake, local geology, and the diverse wildlife found within the park.

virginia.hours: 8:00 AM - Dusk daily
virginia.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle parking fee for Virginia residents; $10.00 for non-residents.
virginia.address: 6620 Ben H. Bolen Dr, Dublin, VA 24084
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for optimal water activities and pleasant hiking weather.
tips: Rent a boat at the marina early in the day during summer weekends as they tend to sell out quickly.
Visit the Howe House to learn about the unique history of the New River valley.
Bring insect repellent if you plan on hiking the wooded trails during the warmer months.

virginia.name: Fairy Stone State Park
virginia.shortDescription: Famous for its unique fairy stones and rich history, this park offers a peaceful retreat in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
virginia.fullDescription: Fairy Stone State Park is one of the original six Virginia state parks opened in 1936. It is named for the rare staurolite crystals, known as 'fairy stones,' found in the area. The park features a 168-acre lake, rugged mountain terrain, and a variety of historic structures built by the Civilian Conservation Corps during the Great Depression.

hikingTrails.name: Little Mountain Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers through lush forests and past a beautiful waterfall.

hikingTrails.name: Lake Shore Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that follows the perimeter of the lake, offering excellent views of the water and local wildlife.

virginia.campingInfo: The park offers a variety of camping options, including full-service cabins, a lodge, and multiple campgrounds with water and electric hookups for RVs and tents.
virginia.fishingBoating: The 168-acre lake is open for fishing (bass, bluegill, catfish) and boating. Boat rentals, including kayaks and paddleboats, are available seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Fairy Stone State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on the park's history, geology, and the famous fairy stones, along with educational exhibits.

virginia.hours: 8:00 AM - Dusk daily
virginia.entranceFees: $7.00 daily vehicle parking fee for Virginia residents; $10.00 for non-residents.
virginia.address: 967 Fairy Stone Park Dr, Stuart, VA 24171
virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and beautiful foliage.
tips: Bring a small shovel or sifter to help search for fairy stones in the designated hunting areas.
Visit during the week to avoid weekend crowds at the lake.
Check the park website for seasonal programs and guided nature walks.

west virginia.name: Blackwater Falls State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: West Virginia park named for 62-foot Blackwater Falls, where the river drops into Blackwater Canyon.
west virginia.fullDescription: Blackwater Falls State Park lies in the Allegheny Mountains of Tucker County near Davis. Its centerpiece is 62-foot Blackwater Falls, where the Blackwater River leaves Canaan Valley and plunges into Blackwater Canyon; it is among the most photographed spots in the state. The park has a 51-room lodge, cabins, a campground and a summer nature center.

hikingTrails.name: Red Spruce Trail
hikingTrails.description: The Red Spruce Trail is a 1.25-mile trail listed on the park's official trails page.

hikingTrails.name: Gentle Trail
hikingTrails.description: A featured review on the official park page describes the Gentle Trail, above the falls, as offering ease of access for all.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park has a campground with a season of April 28 – October 31.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Anglers can catch bass, bluegill, catfish and trout at Pendleton Lake in the park.

visitorCenter.name: Blackwater Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free (no entrance fees across West Virginia state parks)
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through fall is ideal because the campground is open April 28 – October 31, and autumn brings fall color to this Allegheny Mountains park.
tips: Expect lots of stairs on the way down to the main falls, though there are places to stop and rest.
A boardwalk leads down to the bottom of the falls for the main view, and the Gentle Trail above offers easier access.
In sledding season, dogs are not permitted on sleds or on the sled hill, and sled tickets are available online.

west virginia.name: Babcock State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: New River Gorge park in West Virginia, known for the much-photographed Glade Creek Grist Mill.
west virginia.fullDescription: Babcock State Park covers 4,127 wooded acres along the New River Gorge in Fayette County, about 20 miles from the New River Gorge Bridge. Near headquarters stands the Glade Creek Grist Mill, built in 1976 from parts of three old mills, which grinds cornmeal sold at the park. It has more than 20 miles of trails, 19-acre Boley Lake, cabins and campsites.
west virginia.campingInfo: The park has 52 campground sites, and the campground is open spring through fall, weather permitting.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Largemouth bass, bluegill, trout and channel catfish live in Boley Lake and Glade Creek, and the New River is within a 20-minute drive.

visitorCenter.name: Babcock State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free – no entrance fees across the West Virginia State Park system
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring through fall is best, when the campground is open (weather permitting) and the park's 20+ miles of trails are most accessible.
tips: There is no entrance fee, so day visits to see the Glade Creek Grist Mill and trails are free.
The campground is seasonal (spring through fall, weather permitting), so check dates before planning an off-season camping trip; 28 cabins are also available.
One trail leaves the park and enters New River Gorge National Park & Preserve. It is 5.5 miles one way, with an estimated 1.5 to 2 hours walking time one way, so plan for the return trip.
nearbyAttractions: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

west virginia.name: Pipestem Resort State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Southern West Virginia resort park above the Bluestone River gorge, with an aerial tram and two golf courses.
west virginia.fullDescription: Pipestem Resort State Park covers 4,050 acres in the Bluestone River gorge on the Mercer-Summers county line and opened in 1970. It has two hotels, one reached only by aerial tramway to the bottom of the gorge, 26 cabins, a regular and a par-3 golf course, and restaurants.

hikingTrails.name: Lower Indian Branch Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that includes waterfall views.

hikingTrails.name: Canyon Rim Trail
hikingTrails.description: Descends 500 feet to Heritage Point, a massive sandstone outcropping with a scenic overlook.

hikingTrails.name: Bluestone River Trail
hikingTrails.description: According to AllTrails, this is the longest trail in Pipestem Resort State Park.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park's campground is open year-round, weather permitting.
west virginia.fishingBoating: The park offers boating and fishing, including some of the best trout and smallmouth bass fishing in West Virginia, and a fishing license is required.

visitorCenter.name: Pipestem Resort State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free (no entrance fees across West Virginia state parks)
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring through fall is ideal, with autumn especially scenic for fall color along the Bluestone River Gorge rim.
tips: A fishing license is required to fish in the park.
Activity operating days and hours may vary, so call the park at (304) 466-1800 before you go.
Ride the new aerial tramway for the park's most scenic views.

west virginia.name: Hawks Nest State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Perched high above the New River, this 270-acre park offers breathtaking views of the rugged New River Gorge and historic industrial history.
west virginia.fullDescription: Hawks Nest State Park is named for the nesting ospreys that once inhabited the cliffs overlooking the New River. The park is famous for its dramatic overlook, which provides a stunning vista of the New River Gorge, a deep canyon carved by the ancient New River. The area is rich in history, including the tragic Hawks Nest Tunnel disaster of the 1930s, and offers a unique blend of geological wonder and recreational opportunity.
thingsToDo: Jet boat tours on the New River

hikingTrails.name: Cliffside Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short but scenic trail that follows the edge of the gorge, offering multiple vantage points of the river below.

hikingTrails.name: Hawks Nest Rail Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, gravel-surfaced trail that follows the old railroad grade along the river, perfect for a leisurely walk or bike ride.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park does not offer traditional tent or RV camping, but it features the historic Hawks Nest Lodge which provides 31 guest rooms with modern amenities and scenic views.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the New River shoreline within the park boundaries; valid West Virginia fishing license required.

visitorCenter.name: Hawks Nest Lodge and Gift Shop
visitorCenter.info: The lodge serves as the primary visitor hub, featuring a gift shop, information desk, and access to the aerial tramway.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds.
west virginia.address: 49 Hawks Nest Park Rd, Ansted, WV 25812
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for the spectacular fall foliage or spring for blooming wildflowers.
tips: Take the aerial tramway down to the river level for a unique perspective of the gorge.
Visit the overlook early in the morning to avoid crowds and catch the best light for photography.
Check the official website for seasonal tramway and jet boat operating schedules before arriving.
nearbyAttractions: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

west virginia.name: Canaan Valley Resort State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the highest mountain valley east of the Rockies, this four-season resort offers breathtaking scenery and endless outdoor recreation.
west virginia.fullDescription: Canaan Valley Resort State Park is located in a high-elevation valley in the Allegheny Mountains of Tucker County, West Virginia. The park encompasses over 6,000 acres and is renowned for its diverse ecosystem, including wetlands and high-altitude forests. It serves as a premier destination for skiing in the winter and hiking, golfing, and mountain biking during the warmer months, providing a unique alpine experience in the heart of the Mountain State.

hikingTrails.name: Bald Knob Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads to one of the highest points in the valley, offering panoramic views of the surrounding mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Middle Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A relatively flat trail that winds through lush forests and provides excellent opportunities for spotting local wildlife.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park features a modern campground with 34 sites, including full hookups for RVs, as well as a lodge with 160 guest rooms and various cabin rentals.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in the park's ponds and nearby streams; no major boating facilities are on-site.

visitorCenter.name: Canaan Valley Resort Main Lodge
visitorCenter.info: The main lodge serves as the central hub for guest services, equipment rentals, and park information.

west virginia.hours: Open 24 hours daily for resort guests; park grounds accessible year-round.
west virginia.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; fees apply for specific activities like skiing, golf, and chairlift rides.
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Year-round; winter for skiing and summer for hiking and golf.
tips: Check the weather forecast as mountain temperatures can be significantly cooler than the surrounding lowlands.
Book your lodge room or campsite well in advance during peak ski season or fall foliage.
Bring binoculars for bird watching, as the valley is a major stopover for migratory species.

west virginia.name: Lost River State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the mountains of Hardy County, Lost River State Park offers a serene escape with historic cabins and panoramic views from Cranny Crow Overlook.
west virginia.fullDescription: Lost River State Park encompasses 3,750 acres of rugged mountain terrain in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle. Originally established in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park preserves the historic Lee Sulphur Springs site. The park is renowned for its diverse hardwood forests, abundant wildlife, and the famous Cranny Crow Overlook, which provides a breathtaking vista of five counties.

hikingTrails.name: Cranny Crow Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep climb that rewards hikers with one of the most spectacular panoramic views in the state.

hikingTrails.name: White Oak Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path winding through mature hardwood forests, perfect for birdwatching and observing local flora.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park features 24 historic cabins available for rent, ranging from rustic to modern, but does not offer traditional tent or RV camping sites.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in nearby streams, though the park itself does not feature a lake for boating.

visitorCenter.name: Lost River State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with cabin rentals and recreational activities.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds.
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Mid-October for peak fall foliage or late spring for blooming wildflowers.
tips: Bring binoculars for the Cranny Crow Overlook to spot distant mountain ranges.
Book cabins well in advance as they are highly popular during the summer and autumn months.
Check the official website for seasonal pool operating dates before planning a swim.

west virginia.name: Twin Falls Resort State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the rolling hills of southern West Virginia, this park features a unique lodge, championship golf, and two scenic waterfalls.
west virginia.fullDescription: Twin Falls Resort State Park is a 3,776-acre destination known for its diverse landscape, including lush forests and the namesake waterfalls, Black Fork Falls and Marsh Fork Falls. The park is home to a full-service lodge, a challenging 18-hole golf course, and a historic pioneer farm that offers a glimpse into 19th-century Appalachian life.
thingsToDo: Swimming in the seasonal outdoor pool

hikingTrails.name: Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that leads visitors to the base of the park's two beautiful waterfalls.

hikingTrails.name: Buck Run Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, wooded trail perfect for families and those looking for a quick nature walk.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park offers 50 campsites, including 25 with full hookups, as well as 14 cozy cabins available for year-round rental.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the park's ponds, which are stocked with trout seasonally.

visitorCenter.name: Twin Falls Resort Lodge
visitorCenter.info: The lodge serves as the central hub for guest services, park information, and dining.

west virginia.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds.
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for waterfall flow or Autumn for vibrant foliage.
tips: Visit the Pioneer Farm during summer months to see live demonstrations.
Book your tee time in advance if you plan to play the golf course.
Wear sturdy hiking boots as trails can be muddy near the waterfalls.

west virginia.name: Chief Logan State Park
west virginia.shortDescription: Nestled in the mountains of southwestern West Virginia, Chief Logan State Park offers a serene escape with extensive recreational facilities and beautiful woodland scenery.
west virginia.fullDescription: Chief Logan State Park is a 4,000-acre park located in Logan County, West Virginia. Named after the Mingo Chief Logan, the park features a rich history and diverse landscape. It is well-known for its modern facilities, including a lodge, conference center, and an outdoor amphitheater that hosts the popular 'Aracoma Story' historical drama. The park's rugged terrain provides a habitat for various wildlife and offers visitors a peaceful retreat into nature.
thingsToDo: Attending live theater at the amphitheater

hikingTrails.name: Cliffside Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that winds along the ridge, offering elevated views of the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, family-friendly path that meanders through the lush forest canopy.

west virginia.campingInfo: The park features a modern campground with 26 sites, including full hookups for RVs, as well as a 75-room lodge for those seeking more comfortable accommodations.
west virginia.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the park's stocked ponds; valid West Virginia fishing license required.

visitorCenter.name: Chief Logan State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with lodge and campsite reservations.

west virginia.address: 376 Little Buffalo Creek Rd, Logan, WV 25601
west virginia.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Check the schedule for the 'Aracoma Story' outdoor drama before visiting in the summer.
Bring comfortable walking shoes as the terrain can be hilly.
Visit during the holiday season to experience the park's famous Christmas light display.

connecticut.name: Sleeping Giant State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Connecticut traprock ridge north of New Haven shaped like a sleeping figure, with clifftop views.
connecticut.fullDescription: Sleeping Giant is a traprock mountain topping out at 739 feet, eight miles north of New Haven, named for its resemblance to a reclining figure. Its trails lead to clifftop views over New Haven County and, on clear days, across Long Island Sound. The park is open until sunset year-round.

hikingTrails.name: Tower Trail (Gray Blaze)
hikingTrails.description: The easiest route up the Giant, this wide gravel out-and-back climbs gently graded switchbacks to a stone observation tower on Mount Carmel with 360-degree views of Long Island Sound and the Greater New Haven area.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail (Pine Tree Blazed)
hikingTrails.description: A roughly one-hour loop with forty numbered trees and rocks keyed to a trail guide on the park's natural history; it starts fairly level and becomes rougher, steeper and rocky around station #13.

hikingTrails.name: Quinnipiac Trail to Tower (Blue Blaze)
hikingTrails.description: The park's most difficult trail starts at the Mill River and climbs steep switchbacks through a former quarry and a rock scramble to the 400-foot cliffs of the 'chin' before reaching the tower.

connecticut.campingInfo: Camping is limited to one youth group site for up to 40 campers, open only to qualified youth groups with advance reservations required.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Anglers can wade the Mill River or fish from the banks of Axel Shop Pond for striped bass and stocked rainbow, brook, brown and tiger trout.

visitorCenter.name: Sleeping Giant State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

connecticut.entranceFees: Free for in-state registered vehicles; out-of-state vehicles $15 weekends/holidays ($6 weekends after 4 p.m.), $10 weekdays, $112 season pass
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: The park is beautiful year-round but especially comes alive in fall, when the deciduous forest colors the Giant and raptor migration passes through; arrive early because the park often fills to capacity.
tips: The park is one of the state's most popular and often fills to capacity, so arrive early, especially on fall weekends.
Bus permits are required for mid-size and full-size buses seating 30 or more passengers.

The picnic shelter can be reserved April 14 - October 31 through Reserve America or 1-877-668-2267 ($220 plus $9 processing fee, parking not included); outside that window it is first come, first served.

connecticut.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Connecticut's largest shoreline park: two miles of Long Island Sound beach in Madison.
connecticut.fullDescription: Hammonasset Beach State Park has two miles of beach on Long Island Sound in Madison and is Connecticut's largest shoreline park, drawing about a million visitors a year. It has a large campground with 550 sites and a nature center.

hikingTrails.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park Walk
hikingTrails.description: The park's most popular trail is a paved and boardwalk out-and-back route that hugs the coastline from the nature center to the western section of the beach and is accessible to all.

hikingTrails.name: Meigs Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: This out-and-back trail runs along the rocky, sandy shoreline around Meigs Point, with views of the Sound on one side and protected marshland on the other.

hikingTrails.name: Willard's Island Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: This paved loop heads inland for a closer look at the park's salt marshes and is a birdwatching hotspot.

connecticut.campingInfo: The seasonal campground has 558 grassy campsites, including eight rustic cabins, but the 2026 season closed October 12 at noon and the 2027 season opens Friday, May 28.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Saltwater fishing is permitted at the Meigs Point and West Beach jetties during the day, with night fishing along the entire beach in peak season, and a car-top boat launch for canoes and kayaks is on the east side of the Meigs Point jetty.

visitorCenter.name: Hammonasset Beach State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

connecticut.hours: Open daily 8:00 a.m. to sunset; open 24 hours for camping or fishing Memorial Day to Columbus Day
connecticut.entranceFees: Free for in-state registered vehicles; out-of-state vehicles $22 weekends/holidays, $15 weekdays, $7 after 4:00 pm, $112 season pass
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is best for swimming on the two-mile beach and for camping, while spring and fall suit birding in the salt marshes and saltwater fishing, which runs from spring to fall.
tips: Out-of-state vehicles pay only $7 after 4:00 pm, compared with $15 on weekdays and $22 on weekends and holidays. Connecticut-registered vehicles enter free.
Life jackets are mandatory for paddlers from October 1 to May 31, and children under 12 must wear one year-round.
Leashed pets are allowed on the beach only from September 30 to April 1, and paved trails get very hot for dog paws on summer days.

connecticut.name: Kent Falls State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Litchfield Hills park where Kent Falls drops 250 feet in a series of cascades on Falls Brook.
connecticut.fullDescription: Kent Falls State Park in Kent, Connecticut, is home to a series of waterfalls on Falls Brook, a Housatonic River tributary, that drop 250 feet in under a quarter mile. The largest cascade falls more than 70 feet into a pool. A replica covered bridge crosses the brook to the falls.

hikingTrails.name: Kent Falls Steps Trail
hikingTrails.description: From the parking lot, a paved path passes through the covered bridge and picnic area to stone stairs that climb steeply along the falls, with viewing platforms along the way.

hikingTrails.name: Kent Falls Red and Yellow Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails lists this loop up and around Kent Falls, and the official page notes the red-blazed trail across the brook avoids the stairs but misses the views.

connecticut.campingInfo: The official page does not list camping in the park, but it names Macedonia Brook State Park Campground about 4 miles away as a nearby option.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Kent Falls is one of Connecticut's thirteen state trout parks, with brook, brown and rainbow trout and the best fishing spots below the base of the falls, but no entry into the water or swimming is allowed.

visitorCenter.name: Kent Falls State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

connecticut.entranceFees: Free for in-state registered vehicles; out-of-state vehicles $15 weekends/holidays, $10 weekdays, $112 season pass
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Visit in spring when snowmelt makes the falls flow heaviest, or in winter to see the falls without the crowds.
tips: No entry into the water or swimming is allowed, and visitors should stay on the hiking trails.
Parking is free for Connecticut-registered vehicles, but out-of-state vehicles pay $10 on weekdays and $15 on weekends and holidays.
An alcohol ban is in place, drones are prohibited, and bus permits are required for buses seating 30 or more passengers.
nearbyAttractions: Eric Sloane Museum and Kent Furnace

connecticut.name: Gillette Castle State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Perched high above the Connecticut River, this unique stone castle was the eccentric home of actor William Gillette, famous for his portrayal of Sherlock Holmes.
connecticut.fullDescription: Gillette Castle was built between 1914 and 1919 by William Gillette, an American actor, playwright, and stage manager. The castle, designed by Gillette himself, features 24 rooms and is constructed of local fieldstone. It is filled with intricate woodwork, secret doors, and unique architectural details that reflect Gillette's creative and theatrical personality. The surrounding park offers stunning views of the Connecticut River and extensive woodland trails.

hikingTrails.name: Castle Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that winds around the base of the castle and offers beautiful views of the Connecticut River.

hikingTrails.name: River View Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes hikers through dense forest and provides elevated vantage points overlooking the river valley.

connecticut.campingInfo: There is no public camping available within Gillette Castle State Park.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Connecticut River, but there are no boat ramps located directly within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Gillette Castle Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on tour tickets, park history, and local maps.

connecticut.hours: Grounds: 8:00 AM to sunset daily; Castle tours: Seasonal
connecticut.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park grounds; fees apply for castle tours.
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through autumn for foliage and pleasant weather.
tips: Book your castle tour tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly.
Wear comfortable walking shoes for the uneven terrain on the trails.
Visit during the fall season to experience the spectacular Connecticut River foliage.

connecticut.name: Rocky Neck State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Rocky Neck State Park is a premier coastal destination in Connecticut, featuring a beautiful sandy beach, tidal marshes, and historic stone structures.
connecticut.fullDescription: Located in East Lyme, Rocky Neck State Park offers a diverse landscape that includes a broad, crescent-shaped beach, salt marshes, and rocky shores. The park is well-known for its historic stone pavilion, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps during the Great Depression. Visitors can explore the diverse ecosystem, which supports a variety of coastal wildlife, or enjoy the calm waters of Long Island Sound.
thingsToDo: Bird watching in the salt marshes

hikingTrails.name: White Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers through wooded areas and offers views of the salt marsh and coastal landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Red Trail
hikingTrails.description: A shorter, accessible trail perfect for families that winds through the park's interior forest.

connecticut.campingInfo: The park features 160 wooded campsites available for tent and RV camping, with facilities including restrooms, showers, and a dump station.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Saltwater fishing is permitted along the rocky shoreline; no boat launch is available for motorized vessels.

visitorCenter.name: Rocky Neck Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park history, trail maps, and camping registration assistance.

connecticut.entranceFees: Parking fees apply for non-residents during the summer season, typically ranging from $15 to $22 depending on the day.
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities and hiking.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lot often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Bring binoculars to spot the nesting ospreys in the salt marsh area.
Check the official website for seasonal parking fee changes and beach water quality updates.

connecticut.name: Devil's Hopyard State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Famous for its spectacular Chapman Falls and mysterious potholes, this park offers a rugged landscape perfect for hiking and nature photography.
connecticut.fullDescription: Devil's Hopyard State Park is a 1,000-acre park located in East Haddam, Connecticut. It is renowned for the 60-foot Chapman Falls, which cascades over a series of metamorphic rock formations. The park's name is steeped in local folklore, with legends suggesting the devil himself created the unique circular potholes in the rock bed while pacing back and forth. The area features diverse geological formations, lush forests, and the Eightmile River, which provides a scenic backdrop for outdoor recreation.

hikingTrails.name: Chapman Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible path that leads directly to the base of the stunning Chapman Falls.

hikingTrails.name: Blue Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that traverses the higher elevations of the park, offering panoramic views of the surrounding valley.

connecticut.campingInfo: The park offers 21 rustic campsites available for reservation from mid-April through September, featuring fire rings and picnic tables.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Eightmile River, which is stocked with trout by the state.

visitorCenter.name: Devil's Hopyard Ranger Station
visitorCenter.info: Provides park maps, trail information, and assistance with camping permits.

connecticut.entranceFees: Free entrance for Connecticut residents; non-residents may be charged a parking fee during peak season.
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for foliage or Spring for peak waterfall flow.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain near the falls can be slippery.
Visit during the weekday to avoid heavy crowds at the waterfall.
Bring insect repellent during the summer months as the wooded areas can be buggy.

connecticut.name: Talcott Mountain State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Talcott Mountain State Park is home to the iconic Heublein Tower, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Farmington River Valley.
connecticut.fullDescription: Talcott Mountain State Park is a prominent geological feature in central Connecticut, characterized by its dramatic trap rock ridge. The park is most famous for the Heublein Tower, a historic landmark built in 1914 by Gilbert Heublein. The ridge provides a unique vantage point for observing the surrounding landscape, which was shaped by volcanic activity millions of years ago. Visitors can explore the extensive trail network that winds through hardwood forests and rocky outcrops, leading to the summit where the tower stands as a testament to the region's rich history.

hikingTrails.name: Heublein Tower Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steady climb through the forest that leads directly to the historic Heublein Tower and spectacular valley views.

hikingTrails.name: Talcott Mountain Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the scenic trap rock ridge, offering multiple overlooks and diverse woodland scenery.

connecticut.campingInfo: There is no camping available at Talcott Mountain State Park.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Fishing and boating are not available at this park.

visitorCenter.name: Heublein Tower Museum
visitorCenter.info: The tower serves as a museum featuring exhibits on the history of the Heublein family and the local environment.
visitorCenter.hours: Open seasonally, typically Friday through Sunday, 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM

connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for the spectacular fall foliage or late spring for blooming wildflowers.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails can be rocky and uneven.
Bring plenty of water, especially during the summer months, as there are no water stations on the trail.
Check the official website for tower operating hours before planning your visit to ensure you can go inside.

connecticut.name: Sherwood Island State Park
connecticut.shortDescription: Connecticut's first state park, offering expansive sandy beaches and scenic views of the Long Island Sound.
connecticut.fullDescription: Sherwood Island State Park is a 238-acre public recreation area located in Westport, Connecticut. Established in 1914, it holds the distinction of being the state's first state park. The park features a wide sandy beach, a nature center, and extensive picnic areas. Its unique geography includes salt marshes and open fields, providing a diverse habitat for coastal wildlife and a peaceful retreat for visitors looking to enjoy the Long Island Sound.
thingsToDo: Swimming in the Long Island Sound
Bird watching in the salt marshes

hikingTrails.name: Park Perimeter Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, scenic loop that takes visitors around the perimeter of the park, offering views of the beach and the marshlands.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Center Loop
hikingTrails.description: A short, educational trail near the nature center that winds through coastal vegetation and provides excellent bird-watching opportunities.

connecticut.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available at Sherwood Island State Park.
connecticut.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park. There is no boat launch facility for motorized vessels.

visitorCenter.name: Sherwood Island Nature Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features exhibits on the local ecology, marine life of the Long Island Sound, and the history of the park.
visitorCenter.hours: Seasonal: Wednesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM

connecticut.entranceFees: Free for Connecticut registered vehicles; non-resident fees apply during the summer season.
connecticut.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities and nature observation.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lot often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Bring binoculars to the nature center area for excellent bird watching.
Check the official website for seasonal beach water quality updates before swimming.

maine.name: Camden Hills State Park
maine.shortDescription: Maine park overlooking Penobscot Bay, with a road and trails up Mount Battie and Mount Megunticook.
maine.fullDescription: Camden Hills State Park covers 5,710 acres above Penobscot Bay in Camden. An auto road climbs nearly to the top of Mount Battie, and a trail leads up 1,385-foot Mount Megunticook, the park's tallest peak. The mile-long Maiden Cliff Trail ends at a monument to 12-year-old Elenora French.

hikingTrails.name: Megunticook Trail
hikingTrails.description: Maine Trail Finder calls it the most direct route to the park's finest views, and the official page describes Mt. Megunticook, the highest of the Camden Hills, as a moderate climb by foot trail.

hikingTrails.name: Maiden Cliff Trail
hikingTrails.description: This mile-long trail ends at a monument to 12-year-old Elenora French, whose misadventure in 1864 gave the site its name.

hikingTrails.name: Carriage Road Trail
hikingTrails.description: The park's trail conditions page lists this trail as open to hiking and snowshoeing.

maine.campingInfo: The park has a campground whose comfort stations have hot showers, and the official page lists RV hookups (electric and water) and an RV dumping station.
maine.fishingBoating: Check the official park website for current boating and fishing details.

visitorCenter.name: Camden Hills State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.
