maine.hours: Open all year, 8:00 a.m. to sunset daily unless otherwise posted at the gate; Mt. Battie Road closes at 4:00 p.m. daily and closes for the winter on December 1 or when blocked by snow
maine.entranceFees: Day-use fee charged year-round: Maine resident adults $4, nonresident adults $6, nonresident seniors $2, children 5-11 $1
maine.bestTimeToVisit: Early fall is a highlight, when visitors drive the Mt. Battie Auto Road to see the fall foliage before the road closes for the winter on December 1, while summer is popular for camping.
tips: Mt. Battie Road closes at 4:00 p.m. daily and shuts for the winter on December 1 or when blocked by snow, so plan any summit drive early.
Text CAMDEN to 888-514-7527 to subscribe to the park's condition alerts, and read the Browntail Moth Alert before visiting.
Don't bring firewood from home; buy it from a local source to avoid spreading exotic insects and diseases.

maine.name: Popham Beach State Park
maine.shortDescription: Maine's busiest day-use state park: a broad Atlantic beach between the Morse and Kennebec rivers.
maine.fullDescription: Popham Beach State Park covers 605 acres on the Atlantic in Phippsburg, on a shifting peninsula between the mouth of the Morse River and the Kennebec River's Atkins Bay. It is Maine's highest-volume day-use state park. The peninsula is also the site of historic Fort Popham, Fort Baldwin and remnants of the 1607 Popham Colony.

hikingTrails.name: Perkins Farm Trail
hikingTrails.description: AllTrails users rate Perkins Farm Trail as the best hike in Popham Beach State Park, with a 4.4-star rating from 44 reviews.

maine.campingInfo: Check the official park website for current camping details.
maine.fishingBoating: Surf casting is popular, with striper the most commonly caught species, and the closest trailerable boat launch is a hard-topped 150-ft all-tide ramp on the Kennebec River in Phippsburg.

visitorCenter.name: Popham Beach State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

maine.hours: Open daily 9:00 a.m. to sunset, unless otherwise posted; temporary pre-sunset gate closures may occur in all seasons
maine.entranceFees: $6 Maine resident adult, $8 non-resident adult, $2 non-resident senior (per person, per day)
maine.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is the classic beach season, with lifeguards on duty mid-June to mid-August. October through March brings quieter visits when leashed pets are allowed on the beach, and experienced surfers especially enjoy winter surfing.
tips: Come early on busy days, because Popham often fills all its parking spaces. If vehicle access is closed, you may park legally outside the gates and walk in, but do not block gates or roadways.
Check the tides before exploring. Islands and sandbars are tidal and become inaccessible within 1-2 hours after low tide, and reaching Fox Island now requires crossing the mouth of the Morse River.
Pets are not allowed on the beach from April 1 to September 30. From October 1 through March 31 they are welcome if leashed at all times.

maine.name: Two Lights State Park
maine.shortDescription: Cape Elizabeth headland park with rocky ledges, ocean views and a World War II bunker and tower.
maine.fullDescription: Two Lights State Park occupies 41 acres of headland on Cape Elizabeth with views of Casco Bay and the Atlantic. Opened in 1961, it is named for the nearby twin Cape Elizabeth Lights, though the lighthouses are not in the park. It includes a World War II seacoast battery bunker and fire control tower, and nearly two miles of paths along the rock ledges.

hikingTrails.name: Two Lights State Park (Maine Trail Finder network)
hikingTrails.description: The park's trail network, linked from the official page via Maine Trail Finder, crosses dirt, gravel, rock ledge and grass surfaces along the rocky headland.

hikingTrails.name: Two Lights Loop Trail
hikingTrails.description: A loop in Cape Elizabeth with coastline views and remains of old military fortifications.

maine.campingInfo: Check the official park website for current camping details.
maine.fishingBoating: Fishing is a listed activity at the park, which is known for excellent saltwater fishing along its rocky coastline.

visitorCenter.name: Two Lights State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

maine.hours: Open all year; 9:00 a.m. to sunset daily unless otherwise posted at the gate
maine.entranceFees: $5.00 Maine resident adult, $7.00 non-resident adult (per person, per day); children 5–11 $1.00; children under 5 free
maine.bestTimeToVisit: The park is open year-round, but summer and early fall are best for picnicking and walking the shoreline paths, keeping in mind that ocean breezes can cool even summer afternoons.
tips: When walking on the rocks by the ocean, stand at least 20 feet back from the surf and keep a close eye on children.
Bring warm clothing, because ocean breezes can cool off a summer afternoon.
Text TKC to 888-514-7527 to subscribe to the park's Condition Alerts before your visit.
nearbyAttractions: Cape Elizabeth Lights (twin lighthouses, viewable from the turnaround at the end of Two Lights Road)

maine.name: Baxter State Park
maine.shortDescription: A vast, rugged wilderness area in northern Maine featuring the iconic Mount Katahdin and pristine backcountry landscapes.
maine.fullDescription: Baxter State Park was established through the vision and generosity of former Maine Governor Percival P. Baxter, who purchased the land and donated it to the state with the stipulation that it be kept forever wild. The park encompasses over 200,000 acres of mountains, forests, and lakes, including the northern terminus of the Appalachian Trail. Its geology is defined by the dramatic glacial cirques of the Katahdin massif, offering some of the most challenging and rewarding terrain in the northeastern United States.

hikingTrails.name: Hunt Trail
hikingTrails.description: This challenging trail serves as the northern terminus of the Appalachian Trail, leading hikers to the summit of Mount Katahdin.

hikingTrails.name: Sandy Stream Pond Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that offers excellent opportunities for viewing moose and other wildlife near the water.

maine.campingInfo: The park offers numerous remote campgrounds accessible by vehicle or foot, including sites at Roaring Brook, Katahdin Stream, and Abol. Reservations are highly recommended and often required months in advance.
maine.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in many ponds and streams with a valid Maine fishing license; non-motorized boating is allowed on designated waters.

visitorCenter.name: Togue Pond Gatehouse
visitorCenter.info: The primary entrance station where visitors receive orientation, parking permits, and current trail condition updates.

maine.entranceFees: Entrance is free, but parking fees apply for day-use vehicles and camping fees vary by site.
maine.bestTimeToVisit: July through September for optimal weather and trail access.
tips: Always check the park website for parking reservations before arriving, as they are strictly enforced.
Be prepared for rapidly changing weather conditions, especially at higher elevations.
Pack out all trash and follow Leave No Trace principles to preserve the wilderness.
nearbyAttractions: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument

maine.name: Reid State Park
maine.shortDescription: Reid State Park features Maine's first state-owned saltwater beach and offers stunning views of rocky headlands and offshore islands.
maine.fullDescription: Located in Georgetown, Reid State Park was donated to the state by Walter E. Reid in 1946. The park is renowned for its expansive sandy beaches, including Mile Beach and Half Mile Beach, which are rare in this region of Maine. The park's geology is defined by rugged granite headlands, salt marshes, and tidal pools that provide a diverse habitat for coastal wildlife. Visitors can explore the dunes, walk along the rocky coastline, or observe the migratory birds that frequent the area.
thingsToDo: Bird watching in the salt marshes

hikingTrails.name: Little River Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that winds through the woods and offers beautiful views of the Little River salt marsh.

hikingTrails.name: Griffith Head Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads to a rocky headland providing panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean and nearby islands.

maine.campingInfo: Reid State Park does not offer camping facilities. Nearby private campgrounds are available in the surrounding Georgetown and Bath areas.
maine.fishingBoating: Saltwater fishing is permitted from the rocky shorelines, though swimming areas are restricted during peak hours. No boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Reid State Park Entrance Station
visitorCenter.info: The entrance station provides park information, maps, and guidance on current beach conditions and tide times.

maine.hours: 9:00 AM to sunset daily, from mid-April through mid-October.
maine.entranceFees: Maine residents: $6.00; Non-residents: $8.00; Non-resident seniors: $3.00; Children 5-11: $1.00.
maine.bestTimeToVisit: Summer months for swimming, or early autumn for bird watching and cooler hiking temperatures.
tips: Check the tide charts before visiting to ensure you can explore the tidal pools safely.
The ocean water is quite cold even in summer, so be prepared if you plan to swim.
Arrive early on sunny weekends as the parking lots can fill up quickly.

maine.name: Grafton Notch State Park
maine.shortDescription: Grafton Notch State Park is a rugged mountain pass in western Maine, famous for its dramatic gorges, waterfalls, and access to the Appalachian Trail.
maine.fullDescription: Located in the Mahoosuc Range, Grafton Notch State Park offers some of the most spectacular mountain scenery in Maine. The park is defined by the deep, glacier-carved notch that separates Old Speck Mountain from Baldpate Mountain. Visitors can explore unique geological features like Mother Walker Falls, Screw Auger Falls, and Moose Cave, which were formed by the erosive power of water over thousands of years. The park serves as a critical corridor for the Appalachian Trail and provides challenging terrain for experienced hikers and nature enthusiasts.

hikingTrails.name: Old Speck Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb to the third-highest peak in Maine, featuring an observation tower with panoramic views of the White Mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Screw Auger Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, accessible walk leading to a series of stunning waterfalls and deep, narrow rock chasms.

maine.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within the boundaries of Grafton Notch State Park. Nearby private campgrounds and lodging are available in the town of Newry.
maine.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Bear River, though the park is primarily focused on hiking and geological sightseeing rather than boating.

visitorCenter.name: Grafton Notch Information Kiosk
visitorCenter.info: The park features informational kiosks at major trailheads providing maps and safety information for hikers.

maine.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to mid-October for fall foliage, or July to August for hiking.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the terrain is rocky and can be slippery near waterfalls.
Always carry a physical map, as cell service is extremely limited or non-existent in the notch.
Check the weather forecast specifically for the mountain peaks, as conditions change rapidly compared to the valley floor.

maine.name: Sebago Lake State Park
maine.shortDescription: Located on the shores of Maine's deepest and second-largest lake, this park offers pristine sandy beaches and extensive forested trails.
maine.fullDescription: Sebago Lake State Park was one of the original five state parks in Maine, established in 1938. The park encompasses 1,400 acres of forested land, sandy beaches, and rocky shorelines along the northern basin of Sebago Lake. The area is geologically significant for its glacial history, which left behind the sandy deposits that form the park's famous beaches. It serves as a vital recreational hub for swimming, boating, and camping in the Lakes Region.

hikingTrails.name: Sebago Lake Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop that winds through the pine and hardwood forests, offering glimpses of local flora and fauna.

hikingTrails.name: Hidden Pond Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail leads hikers through diverse terrain to a quiet, secluded pond area perfect for birdwatching.

maine.campingInfo: The park features 250 wooded campsites suitable for tents and RVs, equipped with fire rings and picnic tables. Reservations are highly recommended during the summer season.
maine.fishingBoating: The park features a public boat launch for access to Sebago Lake, which is renowned for landlocked salmon and lake trout fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Sebago Lake State Park Entrance Station
visitorCenter.info: The entrance station provides park maps, camping registration, and information on current water conditions and safety regulations.

maine.hours: 9:00 AM to sunset daily from mid-May through mid-October
maine.entranceFees: Maine residents: $6.00; Non-residents: $10.00; Children 5-11: $1.00; Seniors (Maine residents): Free.
maine.bestTimeToVisit: July through August for swimming, or late September for fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the park often reaches capacity by mid-morning.
Bring insect repellent, especially if hiking the wooded trails in early summer.
Check the official website for current water quality alerts before planning a swim.

maine.name: Rangeley Lake State Park
maine.shortDescription: Nestled on the shore of the pristine Rangeley Lake, this park offers breathtaking views of the western mountains and exceptional outdoor recreation.
maine.fullDescription: Rangeley Lake State Park is situated on the southern shore of Rangeley Lake, a large, deep, and cold-water lake famous for its landlocked salmon and trout fishing. The park encompasses 869 acres of forested land, providing a tranquil setting for camping, picnicking, and hiking. The area is geologically significant for its glacial history and serves as a gateway to the rugged beauty of Maine's western mountain region.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, short loop perfect for families that winds through the wooded areas near the campground.

hikingTrails.name: Mountain View Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail offers elevated vantage points providing stunning panoramic views of Rangeley Lake and the surrounding peaks.

maine.campingInfo: The park features 50 wooded campsites suitable for tents and small trailers, with access to hot showers, flush toilets, and a dump station.
maine.fishingBoating: The park features a concrete boat ramp and a large parking area for boat trailers, providing excellent access to the lake for fishing and recreational boating.

visitorCenter.name: Rangeley Lake State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, fishing regulations, and local area maps.

maine.hours: 9:00 AM to sunset daily (mid-May through mid-October)
maine.entranceFees: Maine residents: $6.00; Non-residents: $8.00; Children 5-11: $1.00; Seniors (Maine residents 65+): Free.
maine.bestTimeToVisit: Late June through early September for water activities, or late September for fall foliage.
tips: Make camping reservations well in advance as sites fill up quickly during the summer months.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the early summer season.
Check the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife for current fishing license requirements.

massachusetts.name: Walden Pond State Reservation
massachusetts.shortDescription: Concord kettle pond made famous by Henry David Thoreau, with a summer swimming beach and a cabin replica.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Walden Pond is a glacial kettle pond in Concord, protected within the 335-acre Walden Pond State Reservation. It became a National Historic Landmark in 1962 for its association with Henry David Thoreau, who lived beside it and wrote Walden. A replica of his cabin stands near the visitor center, opened in 2016. The reservation is day-use only; no camping.

hikingTrails.name: Walden Pond Path
hikingTrails.description: A popular path around the famous pond with about 88 feet of elevation gain, typically taking 0.5–1 hour to complete.

hikingTrails.name: Thoreau House Site Trail
hikingTrails.description: A universally-designed trail leading to the site of Thoreau's cabin, which is marked by a series of granite posts north of the pond.

hikingTrails.name: Walden Pond via Emerson-Thoreau Amble
hikingTrails.description: An out-and-back forest trail near Concord that reaches Walden Pond.

massachusetts.campingInfo: No camping in the park.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Fishing and non-motorized boating are allowed, with a boat ramp open seasonally from April 1 to December 1 (weather permitting); gasoline engines are prohibited.

visitorCenter.name: Walden Pond State Reservation Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

massachusetts.hours: 7:00 am-5:30 pm daily (park hours vary seasonally); Visitor Center 10:00 am-4:00 pm daily
massachusetts.entranceFees: Daily parking: $8 for vehicles with MA plates; $30 for out-of-state vehicles (charged year-round; cash not accepted)
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Summer is the popular season for swimming at this famous kettle pond, but arrive early because the lot closes at capacity; spring and fall offer quieter walks around the pond and to Thoreau's cabin site.
tips: The parking lot closes once the park reaches capacity. Check mass.gov/parkalerts or call (978) 369-3254 for closure status. Annual passes do not grant admission during capacity closures.
Cash is not accepted. Buy a daily parking pass on the Mass DCR YODEL Portal or at the credit card machines in the lot. Annual and senior passes are not sold in the park.

Dogs and pets, bikes on trails, grilling, inflatable water toys, drones and street parking are not allowed. Open water swimmers must use a safety apparatus and follow designated hours and entry points.

massachusetts.name: Blue Hills Reservation
massachusetts.shortDescription: 7,000-acre wooded hill range ten miles south of Boston, topped by the historic Blue Hill Observatory.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Blue Hills Reservation covers 7,000 acres across Milton, Quincy, Braintree, Canton, Randolph and Dedham, about ten miles south of downtown Boston. Its highest point, Great Blue Hill, holds the Blue Hill Meteorological Observatory, founded in 1885. The reservation also has Houghton's Pond for swimming and the Mass Audubon Trailside Museum.

hikingTrails.name: Summit Road
hikingTrails.description: A paved trail listed by DCR as steep, with an average slope of 9% and a maximum slope of 20%; the length is one way.

hikingTrails.name: Old Route 128 by Houghton's Pond
hikingTrails.description: A flat paved trail with slopes under 5% and dirt for the first 100 yards; the length is one way.

hikingTrails.name: Skyline Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steep, scenic trail that crosses the Blue Hills, with some rocky scrambles.

massachusetts.campingInfo: Camping is listed among the activities at Blue Hills Reservation on the official DCR page.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Non-motorized boating is allowed only on Ponkapoag Pond in Canton, and Houghton's Pond offers summer swimming and fishing.

visitorCenter.name: Blue Hills Reservation Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

massachusetts.hours: Dawn to dusk
massachusetts.entranceFees: Free (no entrance fee; parking is free)
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: The reservation offers year-round recreation: hiking from spring through fall, swimming at Houghton's Pond in summer, and skiing on Great Blue Hill from roughly December to March.
tips: Hikers may not park at the Donovan School lot (123 Reed Street, Randolph) during school hours (7:00 AM-3:00 PM); use Fisherman's Beach near 1060 Randolph Street in Canton or the Randolph Little League Fields on High Street instead.
Dogs must stay on-leash and are not allowed on the beach at Houghton's Pond.
Pick up maps and information at park headquarters, where parking is limited to 10 minutes.

massachusetts.name: Halibut Point State Park
massachusetts.shortDescription: Cape Ann park on a former granite quarry, with tidepools, ocean ledges and quarry history.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Halibut Point State Park in Rockport occupies the former Babson Farm granite quarry on Cape Ann, next to The Trustees' Halibut Point Reservation. Trails lead to tidepools and ledges with views reaching the Isles of Shoals and southern Maine. A former WWII fire control tower holds a small museum on Cape Ann granite quarrying, and a self-guided tour circles the quarry.

hikingTrails.name: Halibut Point Trail
hikingTrails.description: A very popular loop trail near Rockport, generally considered easy, that takes an average of about 37 minutes to complete.

massachusetts.campingInfo: No camping in the park.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Fishing is a listed activity at the park, but swimming in or entering the quarry for any reason is prohibited; boating is not mentioned in the material.

visitorCenter.name: Halibut Point State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Check the official park website for visitor center details.

massachusetts.hours: 8:00 a.m. to sunset, open year-round
massachusetts.entranceFees: Parking fee May 23 through October 12: $5 per vehicle with MA plates, $20 per vehicle with non-MA plates; no parking fees November through April
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Visit on clear days from late spring through fall to explore the tide pools and see views reaching to the Isles of Shoals and Mount Agamenticus, or come in winter to watch loons, grebes and ducks feeding offshore, when no parking fee is charged.
tips: Swimming in or entering the water-filled quarry is not allowed for any reason, and alcohol, fires, grills, bicycles and drones are also prohibited.
The parking fee is charged May 23 through October 12 and is based on your license plate ($5 MA, $20 out of state). Mobile payment is accepted through the YODEL app.
Leave tide-pool creatures, plants and rocks where you find them, because removing park resources is prohibited and throwing rocks is not allowed.

massachusetts.name: Mount Greylock State Reservation
massachusetts.shortDescription: Mount Greylock is the highest point in Massachusetts, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Berkshires and beyond from its iconic summit.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Established in 1898 as Massachusetts' first state park, Mount Greylock State Reservation encompasses over 12,500 acres of protected wilderness. The mountain is a prominent geological feature of the Taconic Range, rising to an elevation of 3,491 feet. It is home to the historic Veterans War Memorial Tower and the Bascom Lodge, providing visitors with a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural history.

hikingTrails.name: Bellows Pipe Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads hikers through lush forests and offers a steady climb toward the summit.

hikingTrails.name: Hopper Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging ascent through the famous 'Hopper' glacial cirque, providing dramatic views of the mountain's rugged face.

massachusetts.campingInfo: The park offers the Sperry Campground, which features primitive tent sites and lean-tos available by reservation during the summer season.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas; no major boating facilities are available on the mountain.

visitorCenter.name: Mount Greylock Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides educational exhibits on the park's natural history, trail maps, and information on current conditions.

massachusetts.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily; summit road is closed in winter.
massachusetts.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; parking fees apply for non-Massachusetts residents at the summit.
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to mid-October for peak fall foliage.
tips: Check the summit road status before driving, as it closes during winter months.
Bring layers, as temperatures at the summit are significantly cooler than at the base.
Pack plenty of water, as there are limited potable water sources on the trails.

massachusetts.name: Nickerson State Park
massachusetts.shortDescription: Nickerson State Park is a sprawling woodland oasis on Cape Cod, famous for its crystal-clear kettle ponds and extensive pine forest trails.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Located in Brewster, Massachusetts, Nickerson State Park encompasses over 1,900 acres of pine and oak forests. The park is geologically significant for its numerous kettle ponds, which were formed by retreating glaciers thousands of years ago. Visitors can enjoy a diverse landscape that includes sandy beaches, dense forests, and miles of paved bike paths that connect to the Cape Cod Rail Trail.
thingsToDo: Biking on the extensive trail network

hikingTrails.name: Little Cliff Pond Loop
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that circles the perimeter of Little Cliff Pond, offering beautiful water views and shaded forest paths.

hikingTrails.name: Big Cliff Pond Trail
hikingTrails.description: A relatively flat and accessible trail perfect for families, winding through the pine woods surrounding the pond.

massachusetts.campingInfo: The park features over 400 campsites nestled within the forest, including sites suitable for tents and RVs, with access to restrooms and showers.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: The park's kettle ponds are stocked with trout, and non-motorized boating is permitted with boat ramps available at several ponds.

visitorCenter.name: Nickerson State Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: Provides park maps, camping registration assistance, and information on local conservation efforts.

massachusetts.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
massachusetts.entranceFees: $8.00 for Massachusetts residents and $30.00 for non-residents per vehicle.
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for swimming and camping.
tips: Book campsites well in advance as they fill up quickly during summer months.
Bring a bicycle to take advantage of the direct connection to the Cape Cod Rail Trail.
Check the water quality reports for the ponds before swimming during peak summer heat.
nearbyAttractions: Cape Cod Museum of Natural History

massachusetts.name: Bash Bish Falls State Park
massachusetts.shortDescription: Home to the highest single-drop waterfall in Massachusetts, this park offers stunning scenic views and rugged terrain in the Berkshires.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Bash Bish Falls State Park is located in the southwestern corner of Massachusetts, nestled within the Taconic Mountains. The park is famous for the Bash Bish Falls, which cascade 80 feet into a crystal-clear pool. The area is geologically significant, featuring dramatic rock formations and deep gorges carved by glacial activity. It is a popular destination for hikers and nature enthusiasts seeking to experience the raw beauty of the Berkshire landscape.

hikingTrails.name: Bash Bish Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular path that leads visitors down to the base of the spectacular waterfall.

hikingTrails.name: South Taconic Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging ridge trail offering expansive views of the surrounding valley and mountain ranges.

massachusetts.campingInfo: There is no camping available within the immediate boundaries of Bash Bish Falls State Park; however, nearby Mount Washington State Forest offers camping facilities.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park in accordance with state regulations; no boating facilities are available.

visitorCenter.name: Mount Washington State Forest Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, safety information, and guidance for exploring the surrounding state forest and falls area.

massachusetts.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Spring for peak water flow or Autumn for vibrant foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trail to the falls can be steep and rocky.
Swimming and climbing on the rocks near the falls are strictly prohibited for safety.
Arrive early on weekends, as the parking area fills up very quickly.

massachusetts.name: Salisbury Beach State Reservation
massachusetts.shortDescription: A premier coastal destination featuring 3.8 miles of sandy beach along the Atlantic Ocean and the Merrimack River.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Salisbury Beach State Reservation is one of the most popular ocean beaches in Massachusetts. Stretching along the Atlantic Ocean and the mouth of the Merrimack River, the park offers expansive sandy shores, a large campground, and excellent opportunities for swimming, fishing, and boating. The area has a rich history as a summer resort destination and remains a vital habitat for coastal wildlife.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Walk
hikingTrails.description: A scenic walk along the entire length of the sandy shoreline with views of the Atlantic Ocean.

hikingTrails.name: Dune Boardwalk
hikingTrails.description: A short, elevated path that allows visitors to view the protected dune ecosystem without disturbing the vegetation.

massachusetts.campingInfo: The reservation features a large campground with 481 sites, many of which offer electric and water hookups, suitable for tents and RVs.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: The park features a boat ramp on the Merrimack River and excellent surf fishing opportunities along the jetty.

visitorCenter.name: Salisbury Beach State Reservation Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping reservations.

massachusetts.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
massachusetts.entranceFees: $14.00 for Massachusetts residents and $40.00 for non-residents per vehicle.
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Summer months for swimming and beach activities.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly.
Check the tide charts before planning your beach day.
Bring bug spray if you are camping, as coastal areas can have mosquitoes.

massachusetts.name: Skinner State Park
massachusetts.shortDescription: Home to the historic Summit House, Skinner State Park offers breathtaking panoramic views of the Connecticut River Valley from the top of Mount Holyoke.
massachusetts.fullDescription: Skinner State Park is situated on the summit of Mount Holyoke, the westernmost peak of the Holyoke Range. The park is famous for the historic Summit House, which has served as a destination for visitors since the 19th century. The geology of the area is defined by the traprock ridges of the Metacomet Ridge, providing a unique ecosystem and dramatic cliffs that overlook the winding Connecticut River below.
thingsToDo: Photography of the Connecticut River Valley

hikingTrails.name: Summit Road Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steady climb up the paved access road that offers consistent views and leads directly to the historic Summit House.

hikingTrails.name: Metacomet-Monadnock Trail
hikingTrails.description: A rugged, rocky trail that traverses the ridgeline of the Holyoke Range, providing challenging terrain and spectacular vistas.

massachusetts.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available at Skinner State Park.
massachusetts.fishingBoating: Fishing and boating are not available within the park boundaries, though the nearby Connecticut River offers extensive water recreation.

visitorCenter.name: Summit House
visitorCenter.info: The historic Summit House serves as the primary visitor center, offering exhibits on the history of the mountain and the surrounding region.
visitorCenter.hours: Open seasonally from Memorial Day through late October

massachusetts.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily; Summit House open seasonally
massachusetts.entranceFees: Free entrance to the park; parking fees may apply during peak season.
massachusetts.address: 100 Skinner State Park Rd, Hadley, MA 01035
massachusetts.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for peak fall foliage or late spring for blooming mountain laurel.
tips: Bring binoculars to take full advantage of the expansive views from the summit.
The summit road is steep; ensure your vehicle is in good condition if driving up during open hours.
Check the official website for seasonal road closure dates before planning your trip.
nearbyAttractions: Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art

new hampshire.name: Franconia Notch State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: A spectacular mountain pass in the White Mountains featuring iconic natural landmarks and diverse outdoor recreation.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Franconia Notch State Park is located in the heart of the White Mountain National Forest. This pass is traversed by the scenic Franconia Notch Parkway and is home to the famous Flume Gorge, Echo Lake, and the Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway. The park's geology is defined by dramatic granite cliffs and glacial features formed during the last ice age.
thingsToDo: Ride the Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway
Bike the Franconia Notch Recreation Trail
Visit the New England Ski Museum

hikingTrails.name: Flume Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop featuring a natural gorge with 80-foot granite walls, waterfalls, and covered bridges.

hikingTrails.name: Artist's Bluff Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular hike offering panoramic views of Echo Lake and the surrounding mountain peaks.

new hampshire.campingInfo: Lafayette Place Campground offers 97 wooded campsites suitable for tents and small RVs, located centrally within the park.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Echo Lake offers excellent trout fishing and non-motorized boating opportunities.

visitorCenter.name: Hiker Information Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides trail maps, weather updates, and information on park history and safety.

new hampshire.hours: Open daily year-round, though specific attractions operate seasonally.
new hampshire.entranceFees: Fees vary by attraction; Flume Gorge requires a paid ticket, while general park access is free.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to early October for fall foliage, or summer for hiking and swimming.
tips: Book your Flume Gorge tickets online in advance to guarantee entry.
Arrive early in the morning during peak foliage season to avoid parking congestion.
Bring layers as temperatures can drop significantly at higher elevations.

new hampshire.name: Crawford Notch State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: A spectacular mountain pass in the White Mountains featuring dramatic cliffs, cascading waterfalls, and miles of rugged hiking trails.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Crawford Notch State Park encompasses nearly 6,000 acres of the White Mountain National Forest. Historically significant as a vital transportation route through the mountains, the notch is defined by the Saco River and towering peaks like Mount Willey and Mount Webster. Visitors can explore the dramatic geology of the notch, including the famous Arethusa Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in New Hampshire.

hikingTrails.name: Arethusa Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A popular trail leading to the base of the impressive 140-foot Arethusa Falls, offering scenic forest views along the way.

hikingTrails.name: Mount Willard Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail provides one of the most rewarding views in the White Mountains, looking directly down into the heart of Crawford Notch.

new hampshire.campingInfo: The Dry River Campground offers 36 sites suitable for tents and small RVs, located near the Saco River with basic amenities.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Saco River and nearby streams; no boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Crawford Notch Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on trail conditions, park history, and local wildlife, along with a small gift shop.

new hampshire.entranceFees: Day-use fees are $4.00 per person for adults; children 5 and under are free.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late September to early October for fall foliage or June to August for hiking.
tips: Check the weather forecast before heading out as mountain conditions change rapidly.
Arrive early on weekends during peak foliage season as parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring sturdy hiking boots and plenty of water for the steep terrain.

new hampshire.name: Monadnock State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: Mount Monadnock is one of the most climbed mountains in the world, offering breathtaking panoramic views of New England from its rocky summit.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Mount Monadnock is a prominent 3,165-foot peak in southwestern New Hampshire, famous for its isolation and the extensive network of trails leading to its bare, rocky summit. The mountain has inspired writers like Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau, and its unique geology—a monadnock—has become a geological term for an isolated mountain rising above a surrounding plain. The park offers a challenging hiking experience with rewarding views that can extend to the Boston skyline on clear days.

hikingTrails.name: White Dot Trail
hikingTrails.description: The most direct and popular route to the summit, featuring steep, rocky sections that require careful footing.

hikingTrails.name: White Cross Trail
hikingTrails.description: Often used as an alternative to the White Dot, this trail offers slightly less steep terrain while still providing a challenging ascent.

new hampshire.campingInfo: The park features the Gilson Pond Campground, which offers 35 sites for tents and RVs, including some with electric and water hookups, available by reservation.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Fishing is not a primary activity at this park; there are no boat ramps or significant water bodies for boating.

visitorCenter.name: Monadnock State Park Headquarters
visitorCenter.info: The headquarters provides trail maps, educational exhibits about the mountain's ecology, and assistance from park rangers.

new hampshire.entranceFees: $15.00 per vehicle for day-use parking reservations.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking; winter for snowshoeing.
tips: Reservations are required for parking and are highly recommended during peak weekends.
Wear sturdy hiking boots with good ankle support as the trails are very rocky.
Bring plenty of water and layers, as the summit is often significantly windier and colder than the base.

new hampshire.name: Mount Sunapee State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: Mount Sunapee State Park offers a stunning landscape featuring a pristine beach on Lake Sunapee and rugged mountain trails.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Mount Sunapee State Park is a premier destination in the Dartmouth-Lake Sunapee region, encompassing over 2,900 acres. The park is famous for its diverse recreational opportunities, ranging from the sandy shores of Lake Sunapee to the challenging hiking trails that lead to the summit of Mount Sunapee. The area is rich in glacial history and provides a habitat for diverse flora and fauna, making it a favorite for nature enthusiasts and outdoor adventurers alike.

hikingTrails.name: Summit Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that rewards hikers with panoramic views of the surrounding lakes and mountains.

hikingTrails.name: Andrew Brook Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that follows a mountain stream, offering a peaceful ascent through lush forest terrain.

new hampshire.campingInfo: Mount Sunapee State Park does not offer overnight camping facilities; however, there are several private campgrounds located in the surrounding Newbury and Sunapee area.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: The park provides access to Lake Sunapee for boating and fishing, with a boat launch available nearby for public use.

visitorCenter.name: Mount Sunapee State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, trail maps, and assistance with day-use area inquiries.

new hampshire.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily during the summer season
new hampshire.entranceFees: $5.00 per person for adults, $2.00 for children ages 6-11, and free for children under 6.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for hiking and swimming.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the beach parking area fills up quickly.
Wear sturdy hiking boots if you plan to tackle the summit trails.
Check the official website for seasonal beach closures or parking capacity alerts.
nearbyAttractions: The Fells Historic Estate and Gardens

new hampshire.name: Odiorne Point State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: Located on the scenic New Hampshire coastline, Odiorne Point State Park offers stunning ocean views, rocky shores, and rich historical significance.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Odiorne Point State Park is the largest stretch of undeveloped coast in New Hampshire. The park features a diverse landscape of rocky shores, salt marshes, and woodlands. It is home to the Seacoast Science Center and contains the remnants of World War II coastal defense fortifications, providing visitors with a unique blend of natural beauty and military history.
thingsToDo: Tide pooling along the rocky shore

hikingTrails.name: Coastal Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic path that winds along the rocky coastline, offering excellent views of the Atlantic Ocean and local bird habitats.

hikingTrails.name: Woodland Loop
hikingTrails.description: A peaceful trail through the park's forested areas, perfect for spotting local wildlife and enjoying the shade.

new hampshire.campingInfo: There is no camping available at Odiorne Point State Park.

visitorCenter.name: Seacoast Science Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features interactive exhibits on marine life, local ecology, and the history of the Odiorne Point area.

new hampshire.entranceFees: $4.00 for adults, $2.00 for children ages 6-11, and children under 6 are free.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for the best weather and tide pooling conditions.
tips: Visit during low tide to explore the extensive tide pools along the rocky shore.
Bring binoculars for excellent bird watching opportunities throughout the year.
Check the Seacoast Science Center website for special educational programs and events.

new hampshire.name: Echo Lake State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: A picturesque destination in the White Mountains featuring a stunning glacial lake nestled beneath the towering Cathedral Ledge.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Echo Lake State Park is a scenic gem located in North Conway, New Hampshire. The park is centered around a beautiful, calm lake that offers spectacular views of the surrounding White Mountains. It is most famous for its proximity to Cathedral Ledge and White Horse Ledge, which are massive granite cliffs that draw rock climbers from across the country. The area was formed by glacial activity, leaving behind the deep, clear basin that now serves as a popular swimming and picnicking spot.

hikingTrails.name: Cathedral Ledge Trail
hikingTrails.description: A steady climb that leads hikers to the top of the massive granite cliff, offering panoramic views of the Saco River Valley.

hikingTrails.name: Echo Lake Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, flat path that circles the perimeter of the lake, providing excellent vantage points for viewing the cliffs above.

new hampshire.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within Echo Lake State Park. Nearby camping can be found in the White Mountain National Forest or private campgrounds in North Conway.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the lake, though it is primarily a swimming destination. No motorized boats are allowed on the water.

visitorCenter.name: Echo Lake Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides information on trail conditions, climbing safety, and park regulations.

new hampshire.hours: 9:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily during the summer season
new hampshire.entranceFees: $4.00 per adult, $2.00 for children ages 6-11, children 5 and under are free.
new hampshire.address: 68 Echo Lake Rd, North Conway, NH 03860
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: Late June through early October for swimming and fall foliage views.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lot fills up quickly and the park often reaches capacity.
Bring sturdy footwear if you plan to hike up to the top of Cathedral Ledge.
Check the official website for current parking reservation requirements before your visit.

new hampshire.name: Pawtuckaway State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: Pawtuckaway State Park is a premier destination in Nottingham, NH, offering a large lake, glacial boulders, and extensive hiking trails.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Located in Nottingham, New Hampshire, Pawtuckaway State Park spans over 5,000 acres. The park is famous for its large lake, which is popular for swimming and boating, and its unique geological features, including massive glacial erratics left behind during the last ice age. The park also features a fire tower on South Mountain that offers panoramic views of the surrounding region.
thingsToDo: Boating and kayaking on Pawtuckaway Lake

hikingTrails.name: South Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that leads hikers to the historic fire tower with expansive views of the park.

hikingTrails.name: Boulder Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle path that takes visitors through the forest to see the impressive glacial erratic boulders.

new hampshire.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 192 wooded sites, including options for tents and RVs, though no hookups are available.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Pawtuckaway Lake offers excellent fishing for bass and panfish, with a boat launch available for non-motorized and motorized watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: Pawtuckaway State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides park information, maps, and assistance with camping reservations.

new hampshire.entranceFees: $5.00 per adult, $2.00 per child (ages 6-11), children under 6 are free.
tips: Reservations are highly recommended for camping, especially on weekends.
The beach area fills up quickly on hot summer days, so arrive early.
Bring sturdy hiking boots if you plan to explore the boulder fields.
nearbyAttractions: Great Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve

new hampshire.name: Hampton Beach State Park
new hampshire.shortDescription: Hampton Beach State Park offers a premier coastal destination featuring a wide sandy beach, modern RV camping facilities, and stunning Atlantic Ocean views.
new hampshire.fullDescription: Located at the southern tip of Hampton Beach, this state park provides a unique opportunity to enjoy the Atlantic coastline. The park is situated on a barrier island and features a large RV campground, picnic areas, and direct access to the ocean. It is a popular destination for swimming, sunbathing, and coastal fishing, serving as a gateway to the vibrant Hampton Beach resort area.

hikingTrails.name: Hampton Beach Boardwalk
hikingTrails.description: A paved, scenic walk along the coastline offering views of the ocean and access to local shops and restaurants.

hikingTrails.name: Seacoast Greenway
hikingTrails.description: A flat, accessible path that runs parallel to the beach, perfect for walking or light cycling.

new hampshire.campingInfo: The park features 28 full-hookup RV campsites, which are highly popular and require reservations well in advance during the summer season.
new hampshire.fishingBoating: Surf fishing is permitted in designated areas of the beach; no boat ramps are available within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Hampton Beach State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on park regulations, camping reservations, and local coastal safety.

new hampshire.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily during peak season
new hampshire.entranceFees: Daily parking fees vary by season and demand, typically ranging from $10 to $20 per vehicle.
new hampshire.bestTimeToVisit: June through August for swimming and beach activities.
tips: Book your RV campsite months in advance as they fill up quickly.
Arrive early in the morning during weekends to secure parking.
Check the official website for current water quality and swimming advisories.

new jersey.name: Liberty State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: A historic urban oasis offering breathtaking views of the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, and the Manhattan skyline.
new jersey.fullDescription: Liberty State Park is a 1,212-acre park located on the Jersey City waterfront. It serves as a poignant reminder of America's immigrant history, housing the historic Central Railroad of New Jersey Terminal. The park features expansive green spaces, a two-mile promenade, and the Empty Sky Memorial, providing a serene escape from the surrounding urban landscape.
thingsToDo: Take the ferry to Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island

hikingTrails.name: Liberty Walk
hikingTrails.description: A paved waterfront promenade offering panoramic views of the New York City skyline and harbor.

hikingTrails.name: Nature Interpretive Center Loop
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail winding through the park's salt marsh habitat, perfect for birdwatching.

new jersey.campingInfo: Camping is not permitted at Liberty State Park.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas along the waterfront. There is a public boat launch available for small watercraft.

visitorCenter.name: CRRNJ Terminal
visitorCenter.info: The historic terminal serves as the main visitor information hub, featuring exhibits on the history of the railroad and immigration.

new jersey.hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM daily
new jersey.entranceFees: Admission to the park is free.
new jersey.address: 200 Morris Pesin Dr, Jersey City, NJ 07305
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for mild weather and optimal skyline visibility.
tips: Arrive early on weekends as parking lots fill up quickly.
Bring binoculars for birdwatching in the salt marsh area.
Check the ferry schedule in advance if planning to visit the Statue of Liberty.
nearbyAttractions: Ellis Island National Museum of Immigration

new jersey.name: High Point State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: High Point State Park offers breathtaking views from the highest elevation in New Jersey, featuring diverse landscapes and extensive recreational trails.
new jersey.fullDescription: Located along the Kittatinny Ridge, High Point State Park encompasses 16,000 acres of rolling hills, forests, and wetlands. The park is home to the High Point Monument, which sits at 1,803 feet above sea level, providing panoramic views of three states. The area is geologically significant for its quartzite ridges and glacial lakes, offering a rich habitat for diverse flora and fauna.

hikingTrails.name: Monument Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that takes hikers to the base of the High Point Monument with sweeping views of the surrounding valley.

hikingTrails.name: Appalachian Trail (High Point Section)
hikingTrails.description: A challenging segment of the famous long-distance trail that traverses the rugged ridgeline of the park.

new jersey.campingInfo: The park offers a family campground with 50 tent and trailer sites, as well as several rustic cabins available for seasonal rental.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Lake Marcia and Sawmill Lake; non-motorized boating is allowed on designated lakes.

visitorCenter.name: High Point State Park Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the park's natural history, geology, and the construction of the monument.

new jersey.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new jersey.entranceFees: $5.00 per vehicle for NJ residents and $10.00 for non-residents on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for wildflowers or autumn for spectacular fall foliage.
tips: Bring binoculars to take full advantage of the views from the monument.
Check the official website for seasonal swimming availability at Lake Marcia.
Be prepared for cooler temperatures at the summit compared to the base.

new jersey.name: Cape May Point State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: Located at the southernmost tip of New Jersey, this park is a premier destination for birdwatching and features a historic 1859 lighthouse.
new jersey.fullDescription: Cape May Point State Park is a vital stopover for migratory birds along the Atlantic Flyway. The park encompasses 244 acres of coastal dunes, freshwater marshes, and forested wetlands. Its centerpiece is the iconic Cape May Lighthouse, which has guided mariners since 1859. The area is rich in history, having served as a strategic defense location during World War II, with remnants of concrete bunkers still visible along the beach.

hikingTrails.name: Red Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, accessible trail that winds through the freshwater marsh and provides excellent views of the local bird population.

hikingTrails.name: Blue Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail takes visitors through the forested dunes and offers a quiet path for observing native flora and fauna.

new jersey.campingInfo: There is no camping available within Cape May Point State Park.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in designated areas of the park, but there are no boat ramps or rentals available.

visitorCenter.name: Cape May Point State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The visitor center features exhibits on the park's natural history, the Atlantic Flyway, and the history of the lighthouse.

new jersey.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new jersey.entranceFees: Admission to the park is free, though there is a fee to climb the lighthouse.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Fall for peak bird migration.
tips: Bring binoculars for birdwatching, especially during the fall migration season.
Check the lighthouse schedule in advance if you plan to climb to the top.
Wear comfortable walking shoes as the trails are primarily sand and gravel.

new jersey.name: Island Beach State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: Island Beach State Park is a preserved barrier island that protects one of the last remaining undeveloped stretches of the New Jersey coast.
new jersey.fullDescription: Island Beach State Park stretches for 10 miles between the Atlantic Ocean and Barnegat Bay. It is a narrow barrier island that remains in its natural state, featuring rolling sand dunes, maritime forests, and tidal marshes. The park serves as a vital habitat for diverse wildlife, including the state's largest osprey colony and various migratory birds. Visitors can explore the unique ecosystem that has been preserved from the intense development seen elsewhere on the Jersey Shore.
thingsToDo: Biking along the main park road

hikingTrails.name: Spizzle Creek Nature Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, scenic boardwalk trail that winds through the salt marsh and maritime forest, offering excellent bird-watching opportunities.

hikingTrails.name: Ocean Ridge Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail traverses the dune system, providing hikers with beautiful views of the Atlantic Ocean and the surrounding coastal vegetation.

new jersey.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within Island Beach State Park. Nearby private campgrounds are available in the surrounding communities of Seaside Park and Berkeley Township.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Surf fishing is permitted in designated areas. Kayak and canoe launches are available on the Barnegat Bay side of the park.

visitorCenter.name: Island Beach State Park Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features exhibits on the park's natural history, local marine life, and the importance of barrier island ecosystems.

new jersey.hours: 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (seasonal variations apply)
new jersey.entranceFees: $6.00 per vehicle for NJ residents and $12.00 per vehicle for non-residents on weekdays; $10.00 for NJ residents and $20.00 for non-residents on weekends and holidays.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for beach activities and bird migration.
tips: Arrive early during summer weekends as the park often reaches capacity and closes the entrance gate.
Bring plenty of sunscreen and water, as there is very little shade on the beach and trails.
Check the official website for current surf fishing regulations and permit requirements.

new jersey.name: Wawayanda State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: Wawayanda State Park offers a rugged wilderness experience in the New Jersey Highlands, featuring a pristine 255-acre lake and extensive forested trails.
new jersey.fullDescription: Located in Sussex and Passaic counties, Wawayanda State Park encompasses over 35,000 acres of diverse landscape. The park is defined by its glacial lake, Wawayanda Lake, and the surrounding Appalachian mountain terrain. It is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, offering a glimpse into the region's iron mining history and providing critical habitat for black bears, bobcats, and various migratory birds.

hikingTrails.name: Cedar Swamp Trail
hikingTrails.description: A flat, scenic loop that takes hikers through a unique Atlantic white cedar swamp on a well-maintained boardwalk.

hikingTrails.name: Wawayanda Mountain Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging climb that rewards hikers with panoramic views of the surrounding Highlands and the lake below.

new jersey.campingInfo: The park offers 40 wooded campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. There are no RV hookups available, and the sites are best suited for tent camping.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Wawayanda Lake is a popular spot for fishing, with species including largemouth bass, pickerel, and sunfish. Boat rentals are available seasonally, and private non-motorized boats are permitted with a launch fee.

visitorCenter.name: Wawayanda State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, trail information, and educational displays about the park's history and natural resources.

new jersey.hours: 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily
new jersey.entranceFees: $5.00 per vehicle for NJ residents and $10.00 per vehicle for non-residents on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for wildflowers or autumn for spectacular fall foliage.
tips: Arrive early on summer weekends as the parking lot for the beach area fills up quickly.
Bring insect repellent, especially during the warmer months when ticks and mosquitoes are active.
Check the official website for seasonal hunting closures on certain trails.

new jersey.name: Cheesequake State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: Located in the heart of the Raritan Bayshore, Cheesequake State Park offers a unique transition zone where northern hardwood forests meet southern pine barrens.
new jersey.fullDescription: Cheesequake State Park is a 1,610-acre park in Old Bridge and Sayreville, New Jersey. The park is geologically significant because it sits at the meeting point of two distinct ecosystems: the northern hardwood forest and the southern pine barrens. This unique convergence creates a diverse landscape featuring saltwater and freshwater marshes, pine barrens, cedar swamps, and open fields. The park's name is derived from the Lenape word 'Chesequaks,' meaning 'upland.'

hikingTrails.name: Green Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop that traverses the diverse ecosystems of the park, including hardwood forests and marshlands.

hikingTrails.name: Blue Trail
hikingTrails.description: A shorter, accessible trail that winds through the pine barrens and offers excellent bird-watching opportunities.

new jersey.campingInfo: The park features 53 tent and trailer campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Modern restrooms and showers are available nearby.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Hooks Creek Lake, which is stocked with trout. Canoes and kayaks can be launched from the designated area.

visitorCenter.name: Cheesequake State Park Interpretive Center
visitorCenter.info: The center provides educational exhibits on the park's unique geology, local history, and the diverse flora and fauna found within the transition zone.

new jersey.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new jersey.entranceFees: $5.00 per vehicle for NJ residents and $10.00 per vehicle for non-residents on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild temperatures and vibrant foliage.
tips: Bring insect repellent, especially during the summer months near the marsh areas.
Check the official website for seasonal swimming availability at Hooks Creek Lake.
Arrive early on weekends during the summer as the parking lots can reach capacity quickly.
nearbyAttractions: Sandy Hook Gateway National Recreation Area

new jersey.name: Hacklebarney State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: A scenic, rugged park known for its dramatic gorge, cascading waterfalls, and lush hemlock forests in the Black River valley.
new jersey.fullDescription: Hacklebarney State Park is a geological treasure located in Morris County, New Jersey. The park features a deep, rocky gorge carved by the Black River, which is fed by the Rinehart and Trout Brooks. Originally established as a mining site in the 19th century, the area was transformed into a state park in 1924. Visitors can explore the steep, boulder-strewn trails that wind through dense forests of hemlock, oak, and beech, offering spectacular views of the river and seasonal foliage.

hikingTrails.name: Black River Trail
hikingTrails.description: This trail follows the course of the Black River, offering beautiful views of the water and the surrounding gorge.

hikingTrails.name: Hacklebarney Loop
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that descends into the gorge and climbs back up, featuring steep stairs and rocky terrain.

new jersey.campingInfo: There is no camping available at Hacklebarney State Park. The park is strictly for day-use activities.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in the Black River, which is stocked with trout by the state. No boating is allowed due to the rocky and shallow nature of the river.

visitorCenter.name: Hacklebarney State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: The park office provides trail maps, safety information, and general assistance for visitors.

new jersey.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
new jersey.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Hacklebarney State Park.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Autumn for fall foliage or Spring for high water levels in the waterfalls.
tips: Wear sturdy hiking boots as the trails are rocky and can be slippery.
Arrive early on weekends, as the parking lots fill up quickly during peak season.
Pack out all trash to help preserve the natural beauty of the gorge.

new jersey.name: Washington Crossing State Park
new jersey.shortDescription: Commemorating the historic 1776 crossing of the Delaware River, this park offers a blend of Revolutionary War history and serene natural landscapes.
new jersey.fullDescription: Washington Crossing State Park marks the site where General George Washington and the Continental Army crossed the icy Delaware River on Christmas night in 1776. The park encompasses over 3,500 acres of rolling hills, woodlands, and fields. It features the Johnson Ferry House, a historic site dating back to the 18th century, and the Visitor Center Museum which houses an extensive collection of Revolutionary War artifacts and exhibits detailing the famous crossing.
thingsToDo: Visit the historic Johnson Ferry House
Attend outdoor theater performances at the Open Air Theatre
Bird watching along the Delaware River

hikingTrails.name: Sullivan's Way
hikingTrails.description: A gentle trail that winds through wooded areas and open fields, perfect for a casual nature walk.

hikingTrails.name: River Trail
hikingTrails.description: Follows the banks of the Delaware River, offering scenic water views and opportunities to spot local waterfowl.

new jersey.campingInfo: The park offers a family campground with 72 tent and trailer sites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Modern restrooms and showers are available on-site.
new jersey.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted along the Delaware River in accordance with New Jersey state regulations. There is no boat launch within the park boundaries.

visitorCenter.name: Washington Crossing Visitor Center Museum
visitorCenter.info: Features exhibits on the American Revolution, the crossing of the Delaware, and local history.

new jersey.hours: Daily: Sunrise to Sunset
new jersey.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for the park, though some specific programs or camping sites may require a fee.
new jersey.bestTimeToVisit: Spring and Autumn for mild weather and beautiful foliage.
tips: Visit the Visitor Center first to get a map and understand the historical context of the site.
Check the schedule for the Open Air Theatre if visiting during the summer months.
Bring binoculars if you plan to walk the River Trail for better bird watching.
nearbyAttractions: Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park

new york.name: Watkins Glen State Park
new york.shortDescription: Famed for its deep shale gorge featuring 19 spectacular cascading waterfalls in less than two miles.
new york.fullDescription: Watkins Glen State Park is the most famous of the Finger Lakes state parks, located at the southern tip of Seneca Lake in New York. The park's center is a spectacular, 400-foot-deep shale canyon carved out by Glen Creek. Guided stone-step paths wind through the gorge, passing under and behind 19 roaring waterfalls. It is a stunning display of natural hydraulic carving, historic CCC stone craftsmanship, and dense forest foliage.
thingsToDo: Walking the historic stone Gorge Trail
Viewing Rainbow Falls and Cavern Cascade
Camping under a dense hemlock canopy

hikingTrails.name: Gorge Trail
hikingTrails.description: Features 832 stone steps climbing through the deep shale gorge, passing under waterfalls (including Rainbow Falls) and crossing historic stone bridges.

hikingTrails.name: Indian Trail
hikingTrails.description: Runs along the high, forested rim of the gorge, offering dramatic overlook views of the canyon below.

new york.campingInfo: The park has 305 campsites nestled in the woods, with modern bathhouses, hot showers, and a dump station, plus 9 rustic rustic cabins available for reservation.
new york.fishingBoating: Seneca Lake (located 1 mile north) is famous for lake trout fishing and pleasure boating. No boating is available inside the gorge creek.

visitorCenter.name: Watkins Glen State Park Welcome Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides park trail maps, shuttle bus schedule, and interactive screens detailing the geologic formation of the Finger Lakes canyons.

new york.hours: Gorge Trail open late May to October; Rim Trails open year-round, Sunrise to Sunset.
new york.entranceFees: $10.00 daily vehicle parking fee (includes access to the swimming pool).
new york.address: 1009 N Franklin St, Watkins Glen, NY 14891
new york.bestTimeToVisit: June to August for roaring waterfall flows, and October for peak Finger Lakes fall foliage.
tips: The Gorge Trail can be wet and slippery; always wear supportive athletic shoes or boots with good tread.
Use the park shuttle bus ($6.00) to ride to the top of the gorge, then walk downhill for an easier hike.
Arrive before 9:00 AM to enjoy the magical atmosphere of the gorge before the tour buses and crowds arrive.

pennsylvania.name: Ricketts Glen State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: Ricketts Glen State Park is a premier Pennsylvania destination famous for its spectacular series of 22 named waterfalls along the Falls Trail.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Spanning over 13,000 acres across Luzerne, Sullivan, and Columbia counties, Ricketts Glen State Park is a National Natural Landmark. The park is defined by the Glens Natural Area, where Kitchen Creek carves through a deep gorge, creating a breathtaking series of waterfalls ranging from 11 to 94 feet in height. The area was once home to a massive logging operation in the late 19th century, but today it serves as a sanctuary for old-growth timber and diverse wildlife.
thingsToDo: Swimming at the beach on Lake Jean
Boating and fishing on Lake Jean
Winter ice fishing and cross-country skiing

hikingTrails.name: Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop that takes hikers past 22 stunning waterfalls through a rocky, scenic gorge.

hikingTrails.name: Beach Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle, flat path that connects the campground area to the swimming beach at Lake Jean.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: The park features a large campground with 120 sites, including modern electric hookups, as well as 10 rustic cabins available for rent year-round.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: Lake Jean offers a boat launch, boat rentals (seasonal), and excellent fishing for warm-water species like bass, perch, and sunfish.

visitorCenter.name: Ricketts Glen State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides maps, educational exhibits on the park's geology and history, and assistance from park rangers.

pennsylvania.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily
pennsylvania.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Ricketts Glen State Park.
pennsylvania.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for peak waterfall flow or autumn for vibrant fall foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy, waterproof hiking boots as the Falls Trail is rocky, steep, and often slippery.
Arrive early on weekends, as the parking lots for the Falls Trail fill up quickly by mid-morning.
Bring a camera and a waterproof bag to protect your gear near the waterfall spray.

pennsylvania.name: Ohiopyle State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: Ohiopyle State Park is a stunning 20,500-acre destination in the Laurel Highlands, famous for its whitewater rafting on the Youghiogheny River and breathtaking waterfalls.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Ohiopyle State Park encompasses the spectacular Youghiogheny River Gorge, which serves as the centerpiece for the park's outdoor recreation. The park is renowned for its world-class whitewater rafting, scenic hiking trails, and the iconic Ohiopyle Falls. Historically, the area was a hub for the lumber industry and the Western Maryland Railway, and today it preserves the natural beauty of the Laurel Highlands through extensive conservation efforts and diverse ecological habitats.
thingsToDo: Biking on the Great Allegheny Passage

hikingTrails.name: Ferncliff Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic loop trail that winds through a unique botanical area featuring diverse plant life and river views.

hikingTrails.name: Baughman Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging hike that leads to a spectacular overlook providing panoramic views of the Youghiogheny River Gorge.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: The park features the Kentuck Campground, which offers over 200 campsites including tent sites, RV sites with electric hookups, and rustic camping cottages.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: The Youghiogheny River is a premier destination for trout fishing and whitewater rafting, with multiple access points for kayaks and rafts.

visitorCenter.name: Ohiopyle State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: The center features interactive exhibits on the park's history, geology, and local wildlife, along with helpful ranger staff.

pennsylvania.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily
pennsylvania.entranceFees: There is no daily vehicle entrance fee for Ohiopyle State Park.
pennsylvania.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring through early autumn for water activities and fall foliage.
tips: Visit Cucumber Falls early in the morning to avoid large crowds.
Wear sturdy water shoes if you plan on exploring the natural rock slides at Meadow Run.
Check the river flow levels on the official website before planning any water-based activities.

pennsylvania.name: Cherry Springs State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: Renowned as one of the best places in the eastern United States for stargazing, this park offers exceptionally dark skies.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Located in the heart of the Susquehannock State Forest, Cherry Springs State Park is famous for its dark night skies, which are protected by the park's remote location and high elevation. The park is a designated International Dark Sky Park, attracting astronomers and stargazers from around the world to witness the Milky Way and celestial events in near-pristine conditions.

hikingTrails.name: Black Forest Trail
hikingTrails.description: A challenging loop trail that traverses rugged terrain and offers spectacular views of the surrounding state forest.

hikingTrails.name: Susquehannock Trail System
hikingTrails.description: A long-distance trail that passes through the park, providing access to deep woods and scenic vistas.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: The park features a rustic campground with 30 sites suitable for tents and small RVs, available by reservation.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: Fishing is available in nearby streams within the Susquehannock State Forest; no boating facilities on-site.

visitorCenter.name: Cherry Springs State Park Office
visitorCenter.info: Provides information on stargazing events, park maps, and educational materials about the night sky.

pennsylvania.hours: Open 24 hours for stargazing; day use areas open sunrise to sunset.
pennsylvania.entranceFees: No entrance fee; camping fees vary by site type and residency.
pennsylvania.bestTimeToVisit: Late summer and autumn for the clearest skies and comfortable temperatures.
tips: Bring a red-filtered flashlight to preserve your night vision.
Check the clear sky chart online before planning your trip.
Dress in layers as temperatures drop significantly at night even in summer.

pennsylvania.name: Presque Isle State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: A beautiful 3,200-acre sandy peninsula that arches into Lake Erie, offering miles of beaches and diverse recreational opportunities.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Presque Isle State Park is a National Natural Landmark that serves as Pennsylvania's only 'seashore.' Formed by glacial activity, this recurved sand spit provides a unique ecosystem that includes lagoons, marshes, and sandy beaches. It is a premier destination for bird migration, water sports, and cycling, featuring a rich history dating back to the War of 1812.

hikingTrails.name: Karl Boyes Multi-Purpose Trail
hikingTrails.description: A paved trail that loops around the entire park, offering scenic views of the lake and interior lagoons.

hikingTrails.name: Sidney Boardwalk
hikingTrails.description: A wooden boardwalk that winds through the marshy areas, providing excellent opportunities for wildlife observation.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: There is no overnight camping available within the boundaries of Presque Isle State Park.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: The park offers multiple boat launches and excellent fishing for perch, bass, and walleye in the lagoons and Lake Erie.

visitorCenter.name: Tom Ridge Environmental Center
visitorCenter.info: Features interactive exhibits about the park's ecology, a giant screen theater, and educational programs.

pennsylvania.hours: Sunrise to Sunset daily
pennsylvania.entranceFees: Admission to Presque Isle State Park is free.
pennsylvania.bestTimeToVisit: Summer for beach activities or Spring/Fall for bird migration.
tips: Visit the Tom Ridge Environmental Center first to get a map and current beach conditions.
The park can get very crowded on summer weekends; arrive early to secure parking.
Bring binoculars, as the park is a world-renowned birding hotspot.

pennsylvania.name: Hickory Run State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: Nestled in the western foothills of the Pocono Mountains, Hickory Run State Park is famous for its massive Boulder Field and miles of scenic trout streams.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Hickory Run State Park encompasses nearly 16,000 acres in Carbon County, Pennsylvania. The park is defined by its unique geological history, most notably the Boulder Field, a National Natural Landmark consisting of a vast expanse of sandstone boulders deposited during the last ice age. The park features over 40 miles of hiking trails, beautiful waterfalls like Hawk Falls, and diverse ecosystems ranging from hardwood forests to rhododendron-filled ravines.

hikingTrails.name: Boulder Field Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trek that leads visitors through dense forest directly to the famous, expansive Boulder Field.

hikingTrails.name: Hawk Falls Trail
hikingTrails.description: A short, popular path that descends through a rhododendron forest to a stunning 25-foot waterfall.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: The park offers a large campground with 381 sites, including options for tents, trailers, and RVs, as well as several rustic cabins available for rent.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Hickory Run, Sand Spring Run, and Mud Run, which are stocked with trout. Swimming is available at the designated Sand Spring Day Use Area beach.

visitorCenter.name: Hickory Run State Park Visitor Center
visitorCenter.info: Provides educational exhibits on the park's geology, history, and local wildlife, along with maps and ranger assistance.

pennsylvania.hours: Sunrise to sunset daily
pennsylvania.entranceFees: There is no entrance fee for Hickory Run State Park.
pennsylvania.bestTimeToVisit: Late spring for rhododendron blooms or autumn for peak fall foliage.
tips: Wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes if you plan to walk across the Boulder Field as the rocks can be unstable.
Arrive early on summer weekends as the swimming area and parking lots fill up quickly.
Check the park website for seasonal hunting regulations before planning your hike.

pennsylvania.name: Kinzua Bridge State Park
pennsylvania.shortDescription: Home to the historic Kinzua Viaduct, this park offers breathtaking views from a skywalk built upon the remains of a massive railroad bridge.
pennsylvania.fullDescription: Kinzua Bridge State Park features the remains of the Kinzua Viaduct, once the highest and longest railroad bridge in the world. After a tornado destroyed much of the structure in 2003, the remaining towers were converted into a pedestrian skywalk that extends 600 feet into the Kinzua Gorge, offering spectacular views of the surrounding Allegheny National Forest.

hikingTrails.name: Kinzua Creek Trail
hikingTrails.description: A scenic trail that descends into the valley floor, allowing visitors to view the massive bridge towers from below.

hikingTrails.name: General Kane Trail
hikingTrails.description: A gentle loop trail that winds through the forest and provides historical context about the area.

pennsylvania.campingInfo: There is no camping available within Kinzua Bridge State Park, but several private campgrounds are located in the surrounding McKean County area.
pennsylvania.fishingBoating: Fishing is permitted in Kinzua Creek, which is stocked with trout, but there are no boat ramps or boating facilities within the park.

visitorCenter.name: Kinzua Bridge State Park Visitor Center
